These three states are also devoid of a sense of dignity or regard for others.[27] Such beings do not really have any possibility of practicing Dharma because the above conditions render their general way of existing inappropriate for it.

d.div: [27] The Tibetan ngo tsha signifies a personal sense of dignity that makes you ashamed of yourself for committing unworthy actions, whereas a respect for others (khrel) signifies being concerned about what others will think or say.

f.d: lha tshe ring po zhes bya ba ni/ 'du shes med pa ste/ der 'jug pa'i rnam shes 'khor dang bcas pa rgyun chad pa'i phyir chos nyams su len pa'i go skabs med pa yin no/ / yang na 'dod khams kyi lha rang yang yin te/ mi la ltos na lha tshe ring ba'i phyir ro/ / yang na lha thams cad kyang mi khom pa yin te/ gnas skabs kyi bde ba la chags nas dge ba la mi 'bad pa mi khom pas so/[45] / de bas na da lta mi'i sdug bsngal bag tsam pa 'di la yon tan yod pa yin te/ 'khor ba la skyo ba skye bar 'gyur/ rang gi nga rgyal zhi bar 'gyur/ sems can la snying rje skye bar 'gyur/ sdig pa'i las la 'dzem zhing dge ba la dga' bar 'gyur ro/ /

The “long-living” gods are those without cognition. Because their stream of consciousness, along with its related mental activities, is in a state of suspension, they do not have the possibility of practicing Dharma: their mind is incapable of applying itself to it. Apart from these particular gods, all desire-realm gods live long compared to humans, and so could also be included in this category. In fact, all the gods are in an unfavorable condition due to their attachment to the well-being of their situation. This makes them unsuited because they are unable to strive for virtue.[28] /53/ In this respect, the relatively limited degree of manifest suffering present in human life is a [helpful] quality, inasmuch as it fosters rejection of samsara, quells pride, gives rise to compassion for other beings, and makes us shun unwholesome action and appreciate virtue.

d.div: [45] dge ba la 'bad pa mi khom pas so/ /dpal spungs dang mi rigs dpe skrun khang /
[28] The Palpung and Beijing editions say, “This makes them unsuited for a vigorous quest for virtue.”

f.d:
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug pa las kyang /
gzhan yang sdug bsngal yon tan ni/ / skyo bas dregs pa sel bar byed/ / 'khor ba pa la snying rje skye/ / sdig la 'dzem zhing dge ba dga'/[46] / zhes gsungs so/ /

This is also mentioned in Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life:
There are further virtues to suffering: World-weariness helps dispel your arrogance, you experience compassion for those in samsara, and you shun nonvirtue and delight in virtue.[29]

d.div: [46] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_spyod 'jug_le'u/ 6_sh+loka_21_shog_15_na7_dge la dga'/
[29] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 6:21, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 14a7.

f.d: de ltar na 'gro ba rigs bzhi la dal ba med par bshad pa yin no/ / mi yin du zin yang / kla klo ni skyes bu dam pa dang phrad par dka' ba'i phyir ro// log lta can ni dge ba la mtho ris dang thar pa'i rgyur ma mthong ba'i phyir ro/ / sangs rgyas kyis stongs pa'i 'jig rten du skyes pa ni/[47] bya ba dang bya ba ma yin pa ston par byed pa med pa'i phyir ro/ / lkugs pa ni legs par bshad pa dang nyes par bshad pa'i chos rang nyid kyis shes par mi nus pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar brgyad po de dag dang bral ba ni dal ba phun sum tshogs pa zhes bya ba'o//

The above explains why those four [nonhuman] sorts of existence simply do not have the freedom to work toward enlightenment. But neither do some forms of human existence: barbarians, because of the improbability of their interacting with spiritual teachers; those with fixed aberrant views, because of the difficulty they have in understanding virtue to be the cause of rebirth into better states and of liberation; those born in a world without a Buddha, because of the absence of teachings on what is and what is not to be done; and those with severe impediments, because these make them unable to understand the Dharma teachings explaining which things are worthwhile and which things are harmful. The “very best freedom” is to be free from the above eight.

d.div: [47] stong / dpal spungs/

f.d:
'byor ba ni/[48] rang gi 'byor ba lnga dang / gzhan gyi 'byor ba lnga ste bcu'o/ / de la rang gi 'byor pa lnga ni/ ji skad du/
mi nyid dbus skyes dbang po tshang / / las mtha' ma log gnas la dad/[49] / ces pa rnams so/ /

There are ten assets: five are personal and five are other-related. The five personal assets are described as:
To be human, born in a central land, with complete faculties, free from having committed the worst of actions, and having appropriate trust.[30]

d.div: [48] 'byor ba la/ mi rigs dpe skrun khang /
[49] sde dge_4036_bstan/ sems tsam/ dzi_slob dpon dbyig gnyen/ nyan thos kyi sa/ le'u/ 1_shog_3_ba4
[30] Asaṅga, Śrāvaka Levels (Śrāvakabhūmi), Toh 4036 Tengyur, sems tsam, dzi, 3b4.

f.d: de la mi nyid ni/ mi rnams dang skal pa mnyam par skyes pa dang bud med kyi dbang po dang ldan pa'o/[50] / yul dbus su skyes pa ni/ skyes bu dam pa rnams la bsten du yod pa'i sar skyes pa'o/[51] / dbang po tshang ba ni/ glen pa dang lkugs pa ma yin pa ste/ dge ba'i chos bsgrub pa'i skal pa yod pa'o/ / gnas la dad pa ni/ ston pas gsungs pa'i dam pa'i chos 'dul ba dkar po'i chos thams cad kyi gnas su gyur ba la dad pa'o/ / las kyi mtha' ma log pa ni/ tshe 'di la mtshams med pa'i las ma byas pa'o/ /

“To be human” means to have been born the same as other humans, with male or female organs. To have been born in a “central land” means birth in a place with accessible holy beings. To have “complete faculties” means that you have the intellectual faculties needed for the actual practice of virtue, suffering from neither a severe learning difficulty nor a severe communication impediment. “Free from having committed the worst of actions” means you have not committed the actions of immediate consequence[31] in this life. “Appropriate trust” means confidence in all those wholesome things that truly merit trust—the noble teachings declared by the Buddha as a way of taming the mind.

d.div: [50] mnyam pa/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun khang /
[51] brten/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

[31] The “actions of immediate consequence” are so called because they cause you to be reborn immediately in the lower realms after death, without passing through the intermediate state (bardo) as most people do.

f.d: gzhan gyi 'byor pa lnga ni/ sangs rgyas 'jig rten du byon pa dang / dam pa'i chos bstan pa dang / chos bstan pa rnams gnas pa dang / chos gnas pa rnams kyi rjes su 'jug pa dang / gzhan gyi phyir snying brtse bar byed pa yod pa'o/ / de ltar rang gzhan gnyis kyi bcu po de dag dang ldan pa ni 'byor ba phun sum tshogs pa dang ldan pa zhes bya'o// de ltar dal 'byor rnam gnyis 'dzom pa de mi lus rin po che yin no/[52] / ci'i phyir de la rin po che zhes bya zhe na/ yid bzhin gyi nor bu rin po che dang chos mthun pa ste/ rnyed par dka' bas na rin po che zhes bya'o/ / phan 'dogs che bas na rin po che zhes bya'o/ /

The five other-related assets are: (6) a Buddha has manifested in the world, (7) the noble Dharma has been taught, (8) the teachings of noble Dharma are still extant, (9) there are those who follow them, and (10) loving kindness can be developed due to others.[32] Someone possessing these ten personal and situational factors is called “a person with the very best assets.” Where these two—the freedoms and the assets—are complete, that is the precious human existence. Why is it called “precious”? /54/ It is so termed because, being rarely encountered and exceedingly beneficial and useful, its qualities are comparable to those of a wish-fulfilling gem.

d.div: [52] 'dzoms/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[32] “Others” here implies benefactors who help create appropriate material circumstances.

f.d:
de la rnyed par dka' ba ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod las/
mir gyur ba ni dka' ba ste/ / mi srog thob pa'ang dka' ba yin/ / dam pa'i chos thob dka' ba ste/ / sangs rgyas 'byung ba'ang dka' ba yin/[53] / zhes gsungs pa dang /

It is rarely encountered: It says in the Bodhisattva Collection:
It is difficult to be born human, and then difficult to stay alive. The noble Dharma is a rare thing to obtain, and it is also rare for a buddha to manifest.[33]

d.div: [53] sde dge_56_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ga_byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod/ le'u/ 7_shog_67_ba5
[33] Bodhisattvapiṭaka, Toh 56 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ga, 67b5.

f.d:
snying rje pad+ma dkar po'i mdo las kyang /
mir skye ba ni rnyed par dka'/ dal ba phun sum tshogs pa'ang rnyed par dka'/ sangs rgyas 'jig rten du 'byung ba'ang rnyed par dka'/ dge ba'i chos la 'dun pa'ang rnyed par dka'/ yang dag pa'i smon lam yang rnyed par dka' ba lags so/[54] / zhes gsungs pa dang /

Furthermore, it says in the White Lotus of Compassion Sutra:
It is not easy to come by a human existence. A person possessing the finest freedoms is also rarely encountered, and it is difficult, too, to find a world in which a Buddha has appeared. Further, it is not at all easy to aspire to what is virtuous, nor is it easy to find most perfect aspiration.[34]

d.div: [54] sde dge_111_bka'/ mdo sde/ cha_snying rje chen po pad+ma dkar po'i mdo/ le'u/ 2_shog_69_na2
[34] Mahākaruṇāpuṇḍarīkasūtra, Toh 111 Kangyur, mdo sde, cha, 69a2.

f.d:
'phags pa sdong po bkod pa'i mdo las kyang /
mi khom pa brgyad las bzlog pa'ang rnyed par dka'/ mir gyur pa'ang rnyed par dka'/ dal ba phun sum tshogs pa rnam par dag pa'ang rnyed par dka'/ sangs rgyas 'byung ba'ang rnyed par dka'/ dbang po ma tshang ba med pa'ang rnyed par dka'/ sangs rgyas kyi chos nyan pa'ang rnyed par dka'/ skyes bu dam pa dang 'grogs pa'ang rnyed pa dka'/ yang dag pa'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams kyang rnyed par dka'/ yang dag pa'i tshul rjes su bstan pa nye bar bsgrub pa'ang rnyed par dka'/ yang dag pa'i 'tsho ba'ang rnyed par dka'/ mi'i 'jig rten na chos dang rjes su mthun pa'i chos la nan tan byed pa'ang rnyed par dka'/[55] zhes gsungs pa dang /

It also says, in the Marvelous Array Sutra:
It is rare to encounter that which is free from the eight unfavorable circumstances. It is rare, too, to be born human. It is also rare to obtain the very best form of freedom, in its plenitude. It is rare, too, for a Buddha to manifest. It is also rare not to have deficient faculties. It is rare, too, to be able to study the Buddhadharma. It is also rare to be in the company of holy beings. It is rare, too, to find truly qualified spiritual teachers. It is also rare to be able to practice properly that which has been taught so purely. It is rare, too, to maintain a truly right livelihood, and rare, in the human world, to earnestly do what is in accord with Dharma.[35]

d.div: [55] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ ga_le'u/ 45_sdong po bkod pa'i mdo/ shog_381_na7
[35] Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra, Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, ga, 381a7.

f.d:
byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug pa las kyang /
dal 'byor 'di ni shin tu rnyed par dka'/[56] / zhes gsungs so//

Furthermore, it says in Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life:
These freedoms and assets are exceedingly rare.[36]

d.div: [56] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_spyod 'jug_le'u/ 1_sh+loka_4_shog_1_na5
[36] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 1:4a, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 1a5.

f.d:
de yang dpe ji ltar rnyed par dka'/ gang zag gang gis rnyed par dka'/ rgyu mtshan ci'i phyir rnyed par dka' zhe na/ de la dpe ni byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug pa las/
de nyid phyir na bcom ldan gyis/ / rgya mtsho cher g.yengs gnya' shing gi / bu gar rus sbal mgrin chud ltar// mi nyid shin tu thob dka' gsungs/[57] / zhes pa ltar ro/ /

What could exemplify this rarity, for whom is it so rare, and just why it is such a rare thing? Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life gives an analogy:
On account of it being like that, the Buddha has said that to be human is as rare as a turtle putting its neck through the hole of a wooden yoke floating on a turbulent ocean.[37]

d.div: [57] gong mtshungs/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 4_sh+loka_20_shog_8_ba6

f.d:
gang nas gsungs na yang dag pa'i lung las te/ ji skad du/
sa chen po 'di chu 'ba' zhig tu gyur la/ der mi zhig gis gnya' shing bu ga gcig pa zhig bor ba rlung gis phyogs bzhir 'phyo'o/ / de na rus sbal zhar ba lo stong phrag du ma thub pa zhig[58] / ces bya ba la sogs pa gsungs so/ /

Where does this quotation come from? In the most excellent scripture it says, among other things:
Were this vast land to be transformed into water, and were someone to set afloat a single one-holed wooden yoke to be driven in the four directions by the winds, a poor-sighted turtle might take thousands of years [to surface and put its head through it].[38] /55/

d.div: [58] sde dge_266_bka'/ mdo sde/ 'a_'phags pa me tog gi tshogs zhes bya ba'i mdo/ shog_302_na7
[38] Host of Flowers Sutra (Kusumasaṃcayasūtra), Toh 266 Kangyur, mdo sde, ’a, 302a7.

f.d: gang zag ni ngan song gsum du skyes pa rnams kyis rnyed par dka' ba yin no/ / des rgyu rkyen ci'i phyir rnyed par dka' na dal 'byor gyi lus ni rgyu dge ba bsags pas thob pa yin la/ ngan song gsum du skyes pas ni dge ba'i las gsog mi shes par rtag tu sdig pa 'ba' zhig la spyod pa'i phyir ro/ / des na ngan song gsum du skyes kyang sdig pa shas chung ba dang / lan grangs gzhan la myong bar 'gyur ba'i las bsags pa zhig gis rnyed pa yin no//

For those born in the lower states of existence, this [precious human existence] is very hard to obtain. The rarity is due to causality, since the principal cause for obtaining an existence with freedoms and assets is a prior accumulation of merit in the continuum of lives. Once born into the lower realms, a being constantly does nothing but wrong and does not know how to develop virtue. For this reason the only ones born in the three lower realms who can attain a human existence are those who have built up relatively little evil, or those who have created karma that will have to be experienced but in some later life.

phan 'dogs pa che ba ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug pa las/
skyes bu'i don sgrub thob par gyur pa la/[59] / zhes gsungs te/

It is exceedingly beneficial and useful. It says in Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life:
Concerning the attainment of making an able human life meaningful.[39]

d.div: [59] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_rgyal sras zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 1_sh+loka_4_shog_1_na5
[39] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 1:4b, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 1a5.

f.d:
de la skyes bu ni rgya gar gyi skad du na/ pu ru Sha bya ba yin la/ pu ru Sha'i sgra ni stobs sam nus pa la 'jug ste/ dal 'byor gyi lus la mngon mtho dang nges legs sgrub pa'i stobs sam nus pa yod pas skyes bu zhes bya ba yin no/[60] / de yang nus pa rab 'bring gsum yod pas/[61] skyes bu yang rab 'bring gsum yod pa yin no/ / de ltar yang byang chub lam gyi sgron ma las/
chung ngu 'bring dang mchog gyur pa'i/ / skyes bu gsum du shes par bya/[62] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The “able human life” renders the Sanskrit term puruṣa,[40] a word [for a human life] connoting power or ability. A human existence endowed with the freedoms and assets is this “able human life,” because it has the strength or ability to attain higher rebirth and ultimate good. Further, since there are three levels of this ability, there will be three corresponding categories of powerful human potential. Thus it says in Lamp for the Path to Awakening:
One should know there to be three types of human ability: lesser, middling, and best.[41]

d.div: [60] bsgrub/ dpal spungs/
[61] de la/ dpal spungs/
[62] sde dge_3947_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_dpal mar me mdzad ye shes/ lam sgron/ sh+loka_2_shog_238_na7
[40] The term puruṣa had great significance in the other religions of India and was therefore a loaded term. This is the Buddhist way of appropriating it.
[41] Atiśa, Bodhipathapradīpa verse 2ab, Toh 3947 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 238b1.

f.d:
de yang skyes bu chung ngu la rang nyid ngan song du mi ltung bar lha mi thob pa'i nus pa yod pa yin no/ / de ltar yang /
gang zhig thabs ni gang dag gis/ / 'khor ba'i bde ba tsam dag la/ / rang nyid don du gnyer byed pa/ / skyes bu de ni tha mar bshad/[63] / ces gsungs so/ /

Those with the lesser type of powerful human potential have the ability to achieve human or divine rebirth by avoiding descent into the lower states. Thus it says:
He who through whatever means strives for personal welfare and aspires merely worldly well-being, that person is described as someone with lesser ability.[42]

d.div: [63] gong mtshungs/ lam sgron/ sh+loka_3_shog_238_ba1
[42] Ibid. verse 3, 238b1.

f.d:
skyes bu 'bring la rang nyid 'khor ba las grol nas zhi bde'i go 'phang thob pa'i nus pa yod pa yin no/ / de ltar yang /
srid pa'i bde la rgyab phyogs shing / / sdig pa'i las las bzlog bdag nyid/[64] / gang zhig rang zhi tsam don gnyer/ / skyes bu de ni 'bring zhes bya/[65] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Those with the middling human ability are able to attain a state of peace and well-being by liberating themselves from samsara:
Someone who turns away from worldly happiness, turns away from unwholesome action, and strives for their own peace alone, that person is refered to as the “middling” type.[43]

d.div: [64] zlog_dpal spungs/
[65] sde dge_3947_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_dpal mar me mdzad ye shes/ lam sgron/ sh+loka_4_shog_238_ba1
[43] Ibid. verse 4, 238b1.

f.d:
skyes bu rab la sems can gyi don du sangs rgyas thob pa'i nus pa yod pa yin no/ / de ltar yang /
rang rgyud rtogs pa'i sdug bsngal gyis/ / gang zhig gzhan gyi sdug bsngal kun/ / yang dag zad par kun nas 'dod/ / skyes bu de ni mchog yin no/[66] / zhes gsungs so//

Those with the highest human ability are capable of attaining buddhahood for the benefit of sentient beings:
Someone who, on the basis of his own suffering, aspires to totally eradicate the entire suffering all beings, that person is most excellent.[44]

d.div: [66] gong mtshungs/ lam sgron/ sh+loka_5_shog_238_ba2
[44] Ibid. verse 5, 238b2.

f.d:
yang phan 'dogs pa che bar slob dpon tsan+d+ra go mI+i'i zhal nas kyang /
gang zhig thob nas skye ba'i rgya mtsho mthar 'byin zhing / / byang chub mchog gi sa bon dge ba'ang 'debs byed pa/ / yid bzhin nor bu bas kyang yon tan ches lhag pa'i/ / mi nyid de ni su zhig 'bras bu med par byed/ / sems kyi stobs chen mi yis rnyed pa gang yin pa'i/ / lam de lha dang klu yis mi rnyed lha min dang / / mkha' lding rig 'dzin mi'am ci dang lto 'phyes min/[67] / zhes gsungs te/

Master Candragomin has also commented on the great benefit and use of a precious human existence, saying:
There are those who would reach the end of the ocean of rebirth and, further, plant the virtuous seed of supreme enlightenment. /56/ Such people, whose qualities far excel a wish-fulfilling gem, how would they engage in fruitless tasks? The path found by a human with such great strength of mind cannot be attained by gods, nāgas, demigods, garuḍas, knowledge holders, kiṃnaras, and uragas.[45]

d.div: [67] sde dge_4183_bstan/ spring yig_nge _slob dpon tsan+d+ra go mi/ slob spring / sh+loka_63_nas _64_shog_50_na2

[45] Candragomin, Letter to a Student (Śiṣyalekha) verse 64, Toh 4183 Tengyur, spring yig, nge, 50a2. Nāgas are generally of serpentine form but possess powers that ordinary snakes do not. Kiṃnaras are half-human, half-horse beings. Uragas—literally, those that “slide on their bellies”—are one of the eight classes of spirits.

f.d: dal 'byor gyi mi lus 'dis mi dge ba spong nus pa/ dge ba bsgrub nus pa/ 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho las brgal nus pa/ byang chub kyi lam la bsgrod nus pa/ rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas thob nus pa yin no/[68] / des na lha dang klu la sogs pa 'gro ba gzhan las khyad par du 'phags pa/ yid bzhin gyi nor bu rin po che bas kyang lhag par gyur pa yin no/ / de ltar na dal 'byor gyi mi lus 'di rnyed par dka' zhing phan 'dogs che bas rin po che zhes bya'o/ /

This human existence endowed with freedom and assets gives the ability to relinquish nonvirtue, cross samsara’s ocean, tread the path of enlightenment, and attain perfect buddhahood. Therefore such an existence is far superior to those of gods, nāgas, and the like. It is something even better than a most precious wish-fulfilling gem. Because this human existence endowed with freedoms and assets is hard to obtain and of such great benefit, it is called “most precious.”

d.div: [68] bgrod/ dpal spungs/

f.d:
de ltar rnyed par dka' zhing phan 'dogs pa che yang 'jig par shin tu sla ste/ tshe srog la gsos ma 'debs mkhan ni med/ 'chi ba'i rkyen ni mang / dus skad cig ma ni mi sdod pa'i phyir ro/ / de ltar yang byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug pa las/
de ring kho na mi 'chi zhes/ / bde bar 'dug pa rigs ma yin/ / bdag ni med par 'gyur ba'i dus/ / de ni gdon mi za bar 'byung /[69]/ zhes gsungs so/ /

Although it is so hard to obtain and of such tremendous benefit, it is very easily destroyed. This is because there is nothing that can perpetuate the life force, there are many causes of death, and the flow of moments never ceases. Thus it says in Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life:
It is not right to contentedly think, “At least I won’t die today.” It is without doubt that at one time or another I will be annihilated.[46]

d.div: [69] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_rgyal sras zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 2_sh+loka_59_shog_6_na6
[46] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 2:58, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 6a6.

f.d:
des na rnyed par dka' tshod dam/ 'jig par sla tshod dam/ phan 'dogs che tshod de ltar lags pas/ lus la gru'i 'du shes bzhag la 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho las ci sgrol byed dgos so/ / de ltar yang /
mi yi gru la brten nas ni/ sdug bsngal chu bo che las sgrol/ / gru 'di phyis nas rnyed dka' bas/ / rmongs pa dus su gnyid ma log[70] / ces gsungs so/ /

Thus, through its rarity, fragility, and real purpose, this physical existence should be considered a boat for doing whatever is needed to find a haven from the ocean of samsara. Thus it says:
Making use of this vessel of able human life, get free from the mighty river of suffering. Since such a craft will be hard to come across in the future, don’t fall into confusion: There is no time for sleep![47]

d.div: [70] gong mtshungs/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 7_sh+loka_14_shog_20_ba4

f.d:
lus la 'og rta'i 'du shes bzhag la/ 'khor ba sdug bsngal gyi 'phrang las ci thar bya'o/ / de ltar yang /
mi lus gtsang ma'i rta zhon nas/ / 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal phrang las bros/[71] [72] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Considering this existence as a steed to be ridden, do whatever must be done to get free from the hazardous path of samsara and suffering. Thus it says:
Having mounted the steed of a pure human existence, gallop away from the hazardous paths of samsara’s suffering.[48]

d.div: [71] 'phrang / dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun khang /
[72] tshigs bcad 'di gzhung gang nas drangs gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[48] The source of this quote has not been identified.

f.d:
lus la g.yog gi 'du shes bzhag la dge ba'i las la bkol bar bya'o/ / de ltar yang /
mi 'o cag gi lus 'di ni/[73] / bkol bar bya ba nyid du zad/[74] / ces gsungs so//

Considering this physical existence as a servant, make it do wholesome tasks. Thus it says:
This human existence should be employed in service [of others].[49]

d.div: [73] mi 'o cog_dpal spungs/
[74] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_spyod 'jug_le'u/ 5_sh+loka_66_shog_12_ba6
[49] Śāntideva, Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life (Bodhicaryāvatāra) 5:66, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 12b6.

f.d:
de ltar byed pa la yang dad pa dgos te/ dad pa med na dkar po'i chos rgyud la mi skye gsung / de ltar yang 'phags pa chos bcu pa'i mdo las/
dad pa med pa'i mi rnams la/ / dkar po'i chos rnams mi skye ste/ / sa bon me yis tshig pa la/ / myu gu sngon po ji bzhin no/[75] / zhes gsungs pa dang /

The three types of faith: In order to act in such a way, faith is needed. It is said that without faith, noble qualities will not develop in a person. Thus the Ten Dharmas Sutra says:
The noble qualities will not arise in someone without faith, /57/ just as a green shoot will not emerge from a scorched seed.[50]

d.div: [75] sde dge_53_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ kha_chos bcu pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 9_shog_166_na3
[50] Daśadharmakasūtra, Toh 53 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, kha, 166a3.

f.d:
sangs rgyas phal po che'i mdo las kyang /
srid pa'i gnas can dad pa chung ba yis/ / sangs rgyas byang chub shes par mi nus so/[76] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Flower Ornament Sutra also says:
Those of worldly disposition with little faith will be unable to know the buddhas’ enlightenment.[51]

d.div: [76] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ ka_bam po bdun pa/ shog_90_ba5
[51] Avataṃsakasūtra, Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, ka, 90b5.

f.d:
des na dad pa bskyed par bya ste/[77] 'phags pa rgya che rol pa las kyang /
bka' stsal pa/ kun dga' bo/ dad pa la sbyor bar gyis shig / 'di ni de bzhin gshegs pas gsol ba 'debs pa'o/[78] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Therefore, you should cultivate faith. As the Buddha teaches in the Vast Manifestation Sutra:
Ānanda, cultivate faith; this is what the Tathāgata asks of you.[52]

d.div: [77] skyed/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[78] sde dge_95_bka'/ mdo sde/ kha_rgya cher rol pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 7_shog_49_ba5
[52] Lalitavistarasūtra, Toh 95 Kangyur, mdo sde, kha, 49b5.

f.d: 'o na dad pa zhes bya ba de ji lta bu zhig yin zhe na/ dad pa la dbye na gsum yod de/ yid ches pa'i dad pa dang / 'dod pa'i dad pa dang / dang ba'i dad pa'o/ /
What exactly does faith mean? When analyzed, it has three aspects: faith as conviction, faith as aspiration, and faith as admiration.

de la yid ches pa'i dad pa ni/ yul las dang 'bras bu dang sdug bsngal gyi bden pa dang kun 'byung gi bden pa la brten nas skye ba yin te/ de yang dge ba'i las kyi 'bras bus 'dod khams kyi bde ba 'byung bar yid ches/ mi dge ba'i las kyi 'bras bus 'dod khams kyi sdug bsngal 'byung bar yid ches/ mi g.yo ba'i las kyi 'bras bus khams gong ma gnyis kyi bde ba 'byung bar yid ches/ kun 'byung gi bden pa zhes bya ba las dang nyon mongs pa spyad pas/ sdug bsngal gyi bden pa zhes bya ba zag bcas kyi phung po lnga thob par yid ches pa'o//

Faith as conviction arises from contemplating actions and their consequences, the truth of suffering, and the truth of suffering’s origin. Conviction means being convinced that the consequence of virtuous action is to experience well-being in the desire realm,[53] the consequence of nonvirtuous action is to experience misery in the desire realm, and the consequence of unwavering karma is to experience well-being in the form and formless realms. It means being convinced that through the power of karma and afflictions, explained as the truth of all origination, you will obtain the five contaminated aggregates, explained as the truth of suffering.

d.div: [53] The desire realm (Skt. kamadhātu, Tib. ’dod khams) is one of the three realms of existence (see glossary). It is often translated literally as “desire realm,” on account of the Tibetan ’dod, and it can be explained in that way—as a domain where beings have much desire. However, there is another explanation in which ’dod is short for ’dod pa’i yon tan (“fields of the senses”), since its beings’ experiences are principally those of the five sense consciousnesses. Another translation would therefore be “sensorial realms.”

f.d: 'dod pa'i dad pa ni/ bla na med pa'i byang chub de nyid khyad par can du mthong nas/ de thob pa'i ched du gus pa dang ldan pas lam la slob pa'o/ /
Faith as aspiration is to consider highest enlightenment as something very special indeed and to ardently study how it can be attained.

dang ba'i dad pa ni/ yul dkon mchog gsum la brten nas skye ba yin te/ lam ston par byed pa sangs rgyas dkon mchog dang / lam du gyur pa chos dkon mchog dang / lam bsgrub pa'i grogs su gyur pa dge 'dun dkon mchog la mos shing gus la sems dang ba'o/[79] / de ltar yang chos mngon pa las/
dad pa gang zhe na/ las dang / 'bras bu dang / bden pa dang / dkon mchog la mngon par yid ches pa dang / 'dod pa dang / sems dad pa'o/[80] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Faith as admiration [54] is something stable that emerges with respect to its object, the Three Jewels—being a joyful clear mind that has devotion and respect for the most precious Buddha as teacher of the path, for the most precious Dharma as that which is the path itself, and for the most precious Sangha as the companions who practice the path. Thus it says, in the Treasury of Higher Knowledge:
What is faith? It is confidence in karma and its results, the [four] truths, and the most precious ones. It is aspiration and it is lucidity of mind.[55]

d.div: [79] sgrub/ dpal spungs/
[80] sde dge_4090_bstan/ mngon pa/ ku_mdzod rang 'grel/ gnas/ 2_shog_65_na1

[54] The Tibetan term translated here as “admiration” is dang ba. The term literally connotes “clarity” but can also mean “joy,” because a person has joyful confidence in the Three Jewels and so forth. When used in a more Vajrayana context of faith due to clear realization that confirms the value of the Three Jewels, the term can also mean “lucidity.”
[55] Vasubandhu, Abhidharmakośabhāṣyam, Toh 4090 Tengyur, mngon pa, ku, 64a1.

f.d:
yang rin chen phreng ba las/
'dun dang zhe sdang 'jigs pa dang / / rmongs pas gang zhig chos mi 'da'/ / de ni dad pa can zhes bya/ / nges par legs pa'i snod mchog yin/[81] / zhes gsungs te/

Further, it says in the Precious Garland:
Whoever, despite temptation, anger, fear, or confusion, never strays from Dharma is said to possess faith. Such a person is a wonderful vessel for the highest good.[56]

d.div: [81] sde dge_4158_bstan/ spring yig_ge_mgon po klu sgrub/ rin chen phreng ba/ le'u/ 1_sh+loka_6_shog_107_na5
[56] Nāgārjuna, Ratnāvalī 1:6, Toh 4158 Tengyur, spring yig, ge, 107a5.

f.d: de la 'dun pas chos las mi 'da' ba ni/ 'dod chags kyi phyogs nas chos mi gtong ba ste/ dper na gzhan zhig na re/ khyod la zas nor ram/ bud med dam/ rgyal srid la sogs pa'i bya dga' chen po ster gyi chos thong zer yang mi gtong ba'o/[82] /

“Not to stray from Dharma despite temptation” means not to abandon Dharma out of craving. /58/ You would not renounce it despite temptations of food, wealth, consorts, kingdoms, or any enticement intended to persuade you to give up the Dharma.

d.div: [82] thongs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: zhe sdang gis chos las mi 'da' ba ni/ khong khro ba'i phyogs nas chos mi gtong ba ste/ dper na gzhan zhig gis bdag la sngar yang gnod pa chen po byas la/ da rung yang gnod pa chen po byed du byung yang chos mi gtong ba'o/ /

“Not to stray from Dharma despite anger” means not to abandon Dharma out of aggression. For example, you would not relinquish a Dharma way of life for the sake of [fighting] someone who had not only harmed you greatly in the past but is also harming your greatly in the present.

'jigs pas chos las mi 'da' ba ni/ bred pa'i phyogs nas chos mi gtong ba ste/ dper na 'ga' zhig na re/ khyod chos mi gtong na dpa' bo sum brgya bkral nas/ nyin re bzhin khyod kyi lus las sha srang lnga lnga gcod zer yang chos mi gtong ba'o/[83] /

“Not to stray from Dharma despite fear” means not to abandon Dharma out of fear. For instance, even faced with the threat that, were you not to abandon Dharma, three hundred fierce warriors would cut five ounces of flesh from your body every day, you would still not relinquish it.

d.div: [83] brgya bsgrel/ dpal spungs/

f.d: rmongs pas chos las mi 'da' ba ni/ mi shes pa'i phyogs nas chos mi gtong ba ste/ dper na 'ga' zhig na re/ las mi bden/ 'bras bu mi bden/ dkon mchog gsum mi bden/ khyod chos byas nas ci byed/ chos zhog zer yang chos mi gtong ba'o/ /

“Not to stray from Dharma despite confusion” means not to abandon Dharma out of ignorance. For instance, even though people might argue convincingly that cause and effect, the Three Jewels, and so forth are false, and thereby throw your Dharma into question, still you would not relinquish it.

de ltar rnam pa bzhi dang ldan pa de dad pa can yin/ nges legs bsgrub pa'i snod mchog yin no// de ltar dad pa de dag yod na phan yon dpag tu med de/ skyes bu mchog gi sems skye ba yin/ mi khom pa rnams spong ba yin/ dbang po rno zhing gsal ba yin/ tshul khrims mi nyams pa yin/ nyon mongs pa 'jil ba yin/[84] bdud kyi spyod yul las 'da' ba yin/ thar pa'i lam rnyed par 'gyur ba yin/ dge ba rgya chen po gsog pa yin/ sangs rgyas mang po mthong ba yin/ sangs rgyas kyis byin gyis rlobs pa yin/[85] de la sogs pa yon tan bsam gyis mi khyab pa 'byung ngo / /

Someone who can maintain conviction when faced with these four types of situations is a person with faith. Such faith makes you ideally suited to achieving liberation. Such faith will create countless benefits, including giving rise to the mentality of the best of beings, eliminating the unfavorable, sharpening and brightening the faculties, ensuring the nondegradation of moral discipline, removing afflictions, taking one beyond domains of experience marred by evil, enabling one to encounter the way of liberation, gathering a vast store of virtue, making one see many buddhas, and causing the buddhas’ blessing to be received.

d.div: [84] 'jil bo/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[85] rlob/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d:
de ltar yang dkon mchog ta la'i gzungs las/
rgyal dang rgyal ba'i chos la dad gyur zhing / / sangs rgyas sras kyi spyod la dad byed pa/ / byang chub bla na med la dad gyur na/ / skyes bu chen po rnams kyi sems skye'o/[86] / zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs so/ /

As it says in the Jewel Lamp Dhāraṇī Sutra:
If, through faith in the enlightened beings and their teachings and trust in the activity of the bodhisattvas, one comes to have faith in the peerless enlightenment, the mental attitude of a great being arises.[57]

d.div: [86] sde dge_145_bka'/ mdo sde/ pa_dkon mchog ta la'i gzungs/ le'u tha ma/ shog_63_ba5
[57] Ratnolkānāmadhāraṇīsūtra, Toh 145 Kangyur, mdo sde, pa, 63b5.

f.d:
yang dad pa yod na sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das rnams kyang de'i drung du byon nas chos bston par byed do/[87] / de ltar yang byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod las/
de ltar dad pa la gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpa' ni/ sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das rnams kyis sangs rgyas kyi chos rnams kyi snod du rig nas/ de'i drung du gshegs te/ byang chub sems dpa'i lam yang dag par ston to/[88] / zhes so/ /

This and more is said. Further, it is taught that all the buddhas, the blessed ones, will appear before a person of faith. The Bodhisattva Collection says:
Thus the buddhas, the blessed ones, having recognized them as being worthy vessels of the Buddhadharma, will appear before them and will most properly teach them the way of the bodhisattva.[58]

d.div: [87] chos ston/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[88] sde dge_56_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ga_byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod/ le'u/ 11_shog_186_na1
[58] Bodhisattvapiṭaka, Toh 56 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ga, 186a1.

f.d: de ltar na mi lus rin po che zhes bya ba lus dal 'byor rnam pa gnyis dang ldan pa/ sems dad pa rnam pa gsum dang ldan pa de/[89] bla med kyi byang chub sgrub pa'i rten gyi gang zag yin no/[90] /

Thus a “most precious human existence,” /59/ having two sets of qualities (the freedoms and assets) as well as three mental qualities (the aspects of faith), is the proper basis for achieving peerless enlightenment.

d.div: [89] ldan te/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[90] bsgrub/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: dam pa'i chos yid bzhin gyi nor bu thar pa rin po che'i rgyan las rten gyi le'u ste gnyis pa'o// //
This concludes the second chapter, concerning the basis, of this Ornament of Precious Liberation, a Wish-Fulfilling Gem of Sublime Dharma.
(spyi don gsum pa bla med byang chub sgrub pa'i rkyen bshad pa/)
III. The Condition
le'u gsum pa/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsten pa/
3. Relying on the Spiritual Teacher

rkyen ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen yin/ / zhes pa la/ de ltar rten phun sum tshogs pa dang ldan yang / rkyen dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis ma bskul na/ sngar gyi bya ba ngan pa la goms shing /[91] bag chags brtas pa'i stobs kyis byang chub kyi lam la 'jug par dka'o/ / des na dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsten par bya ste/

Now to explain the line, “The special condition is the Dharma master.” Even with the very best basis, it will be very difficult to progress along the path to enlightenment without the encouragement of a good Dharma master, who represents the condition [for enlightenment]. The difficulty is due to the strength of ingrained habits—unwholesome tendencies fashioned by former harmful actions. Therefore one needs to rely on Dharma teachers.

d.div: [91] sngar byas kyi/ dpal spungs/

f.d:
sdom ni/
'thad pa dang ni dbye ba dang / / phye ba so so'i mtshan nyid dang / / bsten pa'i thabs dang phan yon te/ / lnga yis bshes gnyen bsten pa bsdus/ / zhes pa'o//

The synopsis is:
Relying on Dharma masters is treated through five points: justification, the different kinds, the specific characteristics of each kind, how to rely, and its benefits.
de la dang po dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsten dgos pa'i 'thad pa ni gsum ste/ lung dang / rigs pa dang /[92] dpe'o/ /
The necessity of relying on Dharma masters is justified in three ways: scripturally, logically, and through analogy.

d.div: [92] ma dper/ rig pa dang / zhes yang 'jug sa med par byung yang / dpal spungs dpar ma dang mi rigs dpe skrun khang bzhin bcos/

f.d:
de la lung ni/ 'phags pa sdud pa las/
slob ma bzang pos bla mar gus ldan de dag gis/ / bla ma mkhas pa dag la rtag tu bsten par bya/ / ci yi phyir na mkhas pa'i yon tan de las 'byung /[93] / zhes gsungs so/ /

For the scriptural justification, it says in the Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom:
Good disciples devoted to their teachers should always rely on wise and skillful Dharma masters. Why? Because from this will emerge the qualities of the wise.[59]

d.div: [93] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ shog_9_na6
[59] Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā, Toh 13 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 9a6.

f.d:
'phags pa brgyad stong pa las kyang /
'di ltar byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya bar 'dod pas/ dang po nyid du dge ba'i bshes gnyen dag la bsnyen par bya/ bsten par bya/ bsnyen bkur bar bya'o/[94] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In the Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines it says:
Thus realized bodhisattvas who wish to genuinely and totally awaken to peerless, utterly pure, and perfect enlightenment should from the very outset seek out, rely on, and serve Dharma masters.[60]

d.div: [94] sde dge_12_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_brgyad stong pa/ le'u/ 22_shog_216_ba1
[60] Aṣṭasāhasrikāprajñāpāramitā, Toh 12 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 216b1.

f.d: rigs pa ni/ thams cad mkhyen pa thob par 'dod pa'i gang zag de chos can/ khyod kyis dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsten dgos par dam bca'/ rang nyid kyis tshogs gsog pa dang /[95] sgrib pa sbyong mi shes pa'i phyir/ zhes pa ni gtan tshigs so/ / mthun pa'i dpe dus gsum gyi sangs rgyas bzhin no/ / bzlog pa'i dpe rang sangs rgyas bzhin no/ /

For the logical justification, the reasoning is: Given that you wish to attain omniscience [subject], you need to rely on Dharma masters [predicate], because by yourself you do not know how to accrue spiritual wealth or how to dispel your obscurations [reason]. The buddhas of the three times are an example substantiating this assertion. The pratyekabuddhas are an example of the contrary.

d.div: [95] sog pa/ dpal spungs/

f.d: de'i don bshad na/ bdag cag rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas thob par byed pa la bsod nams dang ye shes kyis bsdus pa'i tshogs thams cad gsog dgos shing / de gsog pa'i thabs dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rag las pa'i phyir dang / nyon mongs pa dang / shes byas bsdus pa'i sgrib pa thams cad spong dgos la/ de spong ba'i thabs dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rag lus pa'i phyir ro/ /

The above is explained as follows. For us to achieve perfect buddhahood, /60/ all forms of spiritual wealth will need to be accrued, and that accrual depends on Dharma masters. Furthermore, we will need to rid ourselves of all the obscurations, summarized in terms of the afflictions obscuration and the knowledge obscuration. Their removal is also dependent on Dharma masters.

dpe ni/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni lam rgyus med la 'gro dus kyi lam mkhan lta bu'am/ 'jigs pa'i sa phyogs la 'gro dus kyi skyel ma lta bu'am/ chu bo chen po las brgal dus kyi mnyan pa lta bu yin no/[96]/
The justification by analogy is that a Dharma master is like a guide when traveling an unknown path, like an escort when in a dangerous land, and like a ferryman when crossing a mighty river.

d.div: [96] chen po la brgal/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: de la dpe dang po bshad na/ lam rgyus med la 'gro ba'i tshe lam mkhan med na/ lam nor dogs dang / gol dogs dang / 'khyar dogs yod do/ / lam mkhan dang 'grogs na lam nor dogs dang / gol dogs dang / 'khyar dogs med de gom pa chud ma zos par bsdis sar phyin par 'gyur ro/[97] / de bzhin du bla na med pa'i byang chub kyi lam la zhugs nas rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi sar 'gro ba la/ lam mkhan dang 'dra ba'i theg pa chen po'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen med na/ gal te mu stegs pa'i lam du nor dogs yod/ gal te nyan thos kyi lam du gol dogs yod/ gal te rang sangs rgyas kyi lam du 'khyar dogs yod/ lam mkhan dang 'dra ba'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang 'grogs na/[98] lam la nor dogs dang / gol dogs dang / 'khyar dogs med par thams cad mkhyen pa'i grong khyer du phyin par 'gyur ro/ /

The first example is that of a guide. Traveling in unfamiliar lands without a guide, you risk going in the wrong direction or making a longer or shorter detour. But if there is a companion guide, there are none of these risks, and the destination can be attained without a single wasted step. Like this, if there is no good Mahayana Dharma teacher when setting out on the path to peerless enlightenment and heading for that state, then there is the danger of mistakenly taking an aberrant path or, even without straying that gravely, of making the greater detour of the śrāvakas or the lesser detour of the pratyekabuddhas. When accompanied by good Dharma teachers, who are like guides, there is no longer this danger of taking a completely wrong path, or of a large or small detour, and the citadel of omniscience will be reached.

d.div: [97] bsdig_mi rigs dpe skrun/
[98] 'dra ba'i theg pa chen po'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen/ dpal spungs/

f.d:
de ltar yang dpal 'byung gi rnam thar las/
dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni pha rol tu phyin pa'i lam du 'dzud pa'i lam mkhan lta bu'o/[99] /[100] zhes gsungs so//

Thus it says in the Instructions for Liberation of Śrī Saṃbhava:
Leading you along the path that reaches the farther shore, a good master is like a guide.[61]

d.div: [99] 'dzud pas/ dpal spungs/
[100] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_dpal 'byung gi rnam thar/ shog_286_na5
[61] The Instructions for Liberation of Śrī Saṃbhava is found in the Flower Ornament Sutra (Avataṃsakasūtra), Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, ā, 286a5.

f.d: dpe gnyis pa bshad na/ 'jigs pa'i sa phyogs ni chom rkun nam/ gcan gzan la sogs pa'i 'tshe ba dang bcas pa yin no/ / de la 'gro ba'i tshe skyel ma med na/ lus sam srog gam longs spyod la nye zho byung dogs yod la/ skyel ma btsan po dang 'grogs na nye zho med par phyin par 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du byang chub kyi lam du zhugs nas bsod nams dang ye shes kyi tshogs gsog cing thams cad mkhyen pa'i grong khyer du 'gro ba la skyel ma dang 'dra ba'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen med na/ chom rkun dang 'dra ba'i rang gi rnam rtog gam nyon mongs pa dang /[101] phyi'i bdud dang log 'dren la sogs pas dge ba'i nor 'phrog dogs yod/ bde 'gro'i srog gcod dogs yod do/ /

The second example is that of the escort. In dreaded places there are harmful things such as bandits, thieves, wild animals, and the like. Going to such places without an escort is dangerous for possessions, for physical safety, and even for life itself. When accompanied by a powerful escort, however, we pass through without mishap. Similarly, without a Dharma master to act as an escort on the path to enlightenment, accruing spiritual wealth, and heading for the citadel of omniscience, /61/ we risk having our wealth of virtue plundered by that band of thieves [that consists of] ideas and mental afflictions within and harmful forces and misleading influences without. There is even the risk of our life in the happier realms being cut short.

d.div: [101] nang gi/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d:
de ltar yang /
nyon mongs chom rkun tshogs 'di ni/ / glags rnyed gyur na dge 'phrog cing / / bde 'gro'i srog kyang gcod par byed/[102] / ces gsungs so/ /

Therefore, it is said:
As soon as that gang of robbers and thieves, the afflictions, find the opportunity, they will steal virtue and put an end to life in the higher states.[62]

d.div: [102] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_rgyal sras zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 5_sh+loka_28_shog_11_na6
[62] Śāntideva, Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life (Bodhicaryāvatāra) 5:28, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 11a6.

f.d:
skyel ma dang 'dra ba'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang ma bral na dge ba'i nor mi 'chor/ bde 'gro'i srog mi chad par thams cad mkhyen pa'i grong khyer du phyin par 'gyur ro/ / de ltar yang dpal 'byung gi rnam thar las/
byang chub sems dpa'i bsod nams thams cad ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis bsrung ba'o/[103] /[104] zhes gsungs pa dang /

Never straying from the Dharma master who is like an escort, the wealth of virtue will not be lost, existence as a being in the higher realms will not be cut short, and the citadel of omniscience will be attained. Therefore it says in the Instructions for Liberation of Śrī Saṃbhava:
All the merit of a bodhisattva is protected by the Dharma master.[63]

d.div: [103] bsrungs/ dpal spungs/
[104] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_dpal 'byung gi rnam thar/ shog_284_ba3
[63] Flower Ornament Sutra (Avataṃsakasūtra), Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, ā, 284b3.

f.d:
dge bsnyen ma mi g.yo ba'i rnam thar las kyang /
dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni bdag cag thams cad mkhyen pa'i gnas su phyin par skyel ba'i skyel ma lta bu'o/[105] / zhes gsungs so//

One also reads, in the Instructions for Liberation of Upāsikā Acalā:
Good Dharma masters are like an escort because they ensure our safe passage to the state of omniscience.[64]

d.div: [105] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_dpal 'byung gi rnam thar/ shog_36_ba3_skyel bas skyel ma lta bu'o/ /dpal spungs/ skyel ma lta bu'o/ /mi rigs dpe skrun khang /
[64] The Instructions for Liberation of Upāsikā Acalā is found in the Flower Ornament Sutra (Avataṃsakasūtra), Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, ā, 36b3.

f.d: dpe gsum pa bshad na/ chu bo chen po rgal ba'i tshe mnyan pa med par gru'am gzings su zhugs kyang /[106] phar kar mi phyin par chu nyid du bying ba'am/[107] chu nyid kyis khyer bar 'gyur la/ mnyan pa yod na de'i 'bad rtsol gyis phar kar phyin par 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho las brgal ba'i tshe/ mnyan pa dang 'dra ba'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen med na/ dam pa'i chos kyi gru gzings la zhugs nas phyin yang / 'khor ba nyid du bying zhing 'khor ba'i rgyun gyis khyer ro//

The third example is that of a ferryman. Crossing a mighty river, you may be securely aboard the boat, but if there is no ferryman, you cannot reach the other shore, and the boat may sink or be swept away by the currents. With a ferryman and through his striving, however, the other shore will be reached. Likewise, when trying to traverse the ocean of samsara without Dharma masters who are like ferrymen, you may well be aboard the ship of Dharma yet drown in samsara or be carried off by its currents.

d.div: [106] brgal/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[107] pha gir/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d:
de ltar yang /
skya ba 'dzin pa med par ni/ / gru yis pha rol phyin mi 'gyur/ / yon tan thams cad rab rdzogs kyang / / bla ma med na srid mthar min/[108] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Thus it is said:
When there is no oarsman, the vessel will not reach the other shore. Even if one may be accomplished in all, yet without a master, existence will be endless.[65]

d.div: [108] sde dge_2219_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ wi_in+d+ra b+hU ti/ ye shes grub pa/ le'u/ 14_sh+loka_5_shog_51_na2
[65] Indrabhūti, Achieving Pristine Awareness (Jñānasiddhisādhanopāyikā), Toh 2219 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, wi, 51a2.

f.d:
des na mnyan pa dang 'dra ba'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsten par byas na 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho'i pha rol mya ngan las 'das pa'i skam sar phyin par 'gyur ro/[109] / de ltar yang sdong po bkod pa'i mdo las/
dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni 'khor ba'i chu bo chen po las sgrol bas na mnyan pa lta bu'o/[110] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Staying on board with the ferryman-like Dharma master, nirvana—the dry land of the far shore of samsara—will be attained. Therefore it says in the Marvelous Array Sutra:
Delivering us from the ocean of samsara, the Dharma master is like a ferryman.[66]

d.div: [109] bsten byas na/ dpal spungs dang mi rigs dpe skrun khang /
[110] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_dpal 'byung gi rnam thar/ shog_286_na7
[66] Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra, Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, a, 286a7.

f.d: de bas na lam mkhan nam skyel ma'am/ mnyan pa lta bu'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsten par bya'o//
Thus one really needs to rely on Dharma masters, who are like guides, escorts, and ferrymen.

dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi dbye ba ni bzhi ste/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen so so skye bo dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen sa chen po la gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpa' dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen sangs rgyas sprul pa'i sku dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku'o/ /

The second point examines the different kinds of Dharma master. There are four: (1) the Dharma master as a specific individual, (2) the Dharma master as a bodhisattva who has attained the levels (bhūmi), (3) the Dharma master /62/ as an emanation body (nirmāṇakāya) of a buddha, (4) the Dharma master as an enjoyment body (saṃbhogakāya) of a buddha.

de dag kyang rang gi gnas skabs dang sbyar te/ rang las dang po pa'i dus su sangs rgyas dang sa chen po la gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams la bsten pa'i nus pa med pas/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen so so'i skye bo la bsten pa'o/ / rang las kyi sgrib pa phal cher dag tsa na/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen sa chen po la gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpa' la bsten par nus pa'o/ / rang tshogs lam chen po yan chad la gnas tsa na/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen sangs rgyas sprul pa'i sku la bsten par nus pa'o/ / rang sa chen po la gnas tsa na/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku la bsten par nus pa'o/ /

These correspond to the personal situation. Since one is totally unable to rely on buddhas or bodhisattvas while still a beginner in the Dharma, a Dharma master in the form of a specific individual is relied upon. When most of the action-related obscurations have been purified, one is able to rely on a Dharma master who is a bodhisattva on the levels. From the top-most stage of the path of accumulation onward, one can rely on a Dharma master in the nirmāṇakāya form of a buddha. Once the bodhisattva levels are attained, it is possible to rely on a Dharma master in the saṃbhogakāya form of a buddha.

de ltar bzhi las rang la drin gang che na/ bdag cag dang po las dang nyon mongs pa'i mun khang na 'dug pa'i tshe/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gong ma rnams bsten pa bas/ zhal mthong ba tsam yang med pa las/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen so so skye bo dang mjal bas/ de'i gsung gi sgron mes lam snang bar byas nas/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen gong ma rnams dang mjal bar 'gyur te/ des na dngos kyis drin che ba ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen so so skye bo yin no/[111] /

Which of these four types is kindest to us? At the outset, when still in the dark pit of action and affliction, were we to try to rely on Dharma masters of the three latter types, we would not even be capable of seeing their faces; it is only due to our path being illuminated by the lamp held aloft by teachers who are specific individuals that we will eventually encounter them. Therefore, masters in the form of specific individuals are the kindest.

d.div: [111] des na nangs kyi/ dpal spungs/ des na nang gi/ mi rigs dpe skrun khang /

f.d: dge ba'i bshes gnyen bzhi po de'i mtshan nyid 'chad pa la/
The third point concerns the specific characteristics of each of these four kinds of Dharma masters.
sangs rgyas ni sgrib pa rnam pa gnyis spangs pas ni spangs pa phun sum tshogs pa yin/ mkhyen pa rnam pa gnyis mnga' bas na ye shes phun sum tshogs pa yin no/[112] /

Buddhas embody the highest, most complete form of purification because they have eliminated both sorts of obscuration. They also embody the highest, most complete form of pristine awareness because they possess the two forms of knowledge.

d.div: [112] pas na/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: dge ba'i bshes gnyen sa chen po la gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams la yang / sa dang po nas sa bcu pa'i bar gyi spangs pa dang ye shes ci rigs su mnga'o/ / khyad par du yang sa brgyad pa yan chad la gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpa' ni/ gzhan rjes su 'dzin pa'i dbang bcu la mnga' brnyes pa yin te/ tshe la dbang ba dang / de bzhin du sems dang / yo byad dang / las dang / skye ba dang / mos pa dang / smon lam dang / rdzu 'phrul dang / ye shes dang / chos la dbang ba'o/ /

Dharma masters as bodhisattvas on the levels will have whichever degree of purification and pristine awareness is appropriate to their particular level, from the first to the tenth. Of particular import are bodhisattvas of the eighth to tenth levels, for they have ten powers enabling them to nurture others: powers related to life, mind, requisites, karma, birth, aspiration, prayers, miracles, pristine awareness, and Dharma:
de la tshe la dbang ba ni ji srid 'dod pa de srid du gnas par nus so/ /
1. Power over life is the ability to stay in a world as long as wished.
sems la dbang ba ni bdag nyid ji ltar 'dod pa bzhin du ting nge 'dzin la mnyam par 'jog nus pa'o/ /
2. Power over mind is the ability to enter stably into meditative absorption, just as is wished.
yo byad la dbang ba ni sems can rnams la yo byad rin po che dpag tu med pa'i char 'bebs nus pa'o/ /
3. Power over requisites is the ability to shower an immeasurable rain of precious objects on beings. /63/
las la dbang ba ni khams dang / sa dang / 'gro ba dang / skye gnas dang / gnas skabs gzhan du myong bar 'gyur ba'i las rnams gzhan du sbyor nus pa'o/ /
4. Power over karma is the ability to rearrange karmic results in terms of dimension, state, type of existence, and mode of birth that might otherwise be experienced in other states.
skye ba la dbang ba ni/ bsam gtan la gnas shing yongs su ma nyams bzhin du 'dod pa'i khams su skye bar nus la/ der skyes nas kyang de'i nyes pas mi gos pa'o/ /

5. Power over birth is the ability to take birth in the desire realm yet to always maintain profound meditative concentration and not experience any sort of degeneration, remaining completely unsullied by the evils of that state.
mos pa la dbang ba ni sa la sogs pa chu la sogs par mos na'ang bsgyur nus pa'o/ /
6. Power over aspiration is the ability to transform the elements—earth, water, and so forth—into one another, as wished.
smon lam la dbang ba ni ji ltar 'dod pa bzhin du bdag dang gzhan gyi don phun sum tshogs par byed pa'i smon lam 'debs shing / de mngon par 'grub pa'o/ /
7. Power of prayer is the ability to pray or compose prayers in a way that will most properly accomplish the well-being of oneself and others; also the power to make prayers become realities.
rdzu 'phrul la dbang ba ni sems can 'dun par bya ba'i phyir rdzu 'phrul gyi cho 'phrul dpag tu med pa ni ston nus pa'o/ /
8. Power over miracles is the ability to demonstrate countless miracles and supernatural feats in order to kindle aspiration in beings.
ye shes la dbang ba ni chos dang don dang nges pa'i tshig dang spobs pa rnams rab kyi mthar phyin par mkhyen pa'o/[113] /
9. Power of pristine awareness is knowledge that encompasses, in the best possible way, the ultimate meaning of Dharma, of key points, of the true sense of words, and of bodhisattva prowess.

d.div: [113] rab ni/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: chos la dbang ba ni ci rigs par ci tsam du sems can thams cad la/ ming dang tshig dang yi ge'i tshogs gzhan dang gzhan dag gis mdo la sogs pa'i chos rnam par bzhag nas/ cig char gsung gcig gis so so'i skad dang mthun pa'i sems yongs su tshims par byed nus pa'o/[114] /

10. Power of Dharma is the ability to teach beings that which is suited to them, in just the right amount. This is achieved by presenting all the different nouns, terms, and characters of Dharma, in the various sutras and other teachings, in such a way that their sole speech is understood by each in his or her own language and in a totally satisfying way that makes sense.

d.div: [114] tshim/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: dge ba'i bshes gnyen so so skye bo'i mtshan nyid kyang yon tan brgyad dang ldan pa'am/ yang na bzhi dang ldan pa'am/ yang na gnyis dang ldan pa'o/ /
Dharma masters as specific individuals have as their characteristics qualities described sometimes as eightfold, fourfold, or twofold.

de la dang po/ byang chub sems dpa'i sa las/
de la rnam pa brgyad dang ldan na byang chub sems dpa' dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnam pa thams cad rdzogs pa yin par rig par bya ste/ brgyad gang zhe na/ byang chub sems dpa'i tshul khrims dang ldan pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod mang du thos pa dang / rtogs pa dang ldan pa dang / rjes su snying brtse ba dang ldan pa dang / mi 'jigs pa dang ldan pa dang / bzod pa dang ldan pa dang / yid yongs su mi skyo ba yin pa dang / tshig gi bya ba dang ldan pa'o/[115] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Of those with eight qualities, Bodhisattva Levels says:
Concerning the above, if one has eight things, then one should be known as a bodhisattva who is completely qualified as a Dharma master. What are the eight? They are: (1) to have a bodhisattva’s moral discipline, (2) to be learned in the bodhisattva scriptures, (3) to have realization, (4) to be kind and loving to one’s followers, (5) to be fearless, (6) to be patient, (7) to be of untiring mind, and (8) to know how to use words.[67]

d.div: [115] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 16_shog_127_na3
[67] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 127a3.

f.d:
gnyis pa ni/ mdo sde rgyan las/
rgya che the tshom spong ba dang / / gzung 'os de nyid gnyis ston pa/ / 'di ni byang chub sems dpa' yi/ / ston pa phun tshogs yin zhes bya/[116] / zhes gsungs te/ mang du thos pas ston pa rgya che ba dang / shes rab che bas gzhan gyi the tshom gcod pa dang / skyes bu dam pa'i las byed pas tshig gzung bar 'os pa dang / kun nas nyon mongs pa dang / rnam par byang ba gnyis kyi mtshan nyid kyi de kho na nyid ston pa'o/[117] /

Of those with four qualities, the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
Broad based, eliminators of doubt, worthy of recollecting, and teaching the two natures: such are the very best of bodhisattva teachers.[68] This means that: (1) Their teaching is very broad based because they have studied many things; (2) they can remove others’ doubts because they themselves have superb discerning awareness; (3) their speech is worthy of recollection because their deeds are those of holy beings; /64/ and (4) they teach the two natures: the characteristics of the completely defiled and of the utterly pure.

d.div: [116] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 13_sh+loka_5_shog_16_ba6
[117] nyid kyis/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[68] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 15:5, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 16b6.

f.d:
gsum pa ni byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug pa las/
rtag par dge ba'i bshes gnyen ni/ / theg chen don la mkhas pa dang / / byang chub sems dpa'i brtul zhugs mchog / srog gi phyir yang mi gtong ngo /[118] / zhes gsungs te/ theg pa chen po'i don la mkhas pa dang / byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa dang ldan pa'o/ /

Of those with twofold qualities, Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life says:
Even should it cost your life, never forsake a qualified Dharma master, who is skilled in the meaning of Mahayana and maintains the noble bodhisattva discipline.[69]

d.div: [118] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 5_sh+loka_102_shog_14_na5
[69] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 5:102, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 14a5.

f.d: de lta bu'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnyed nas bsten pa'i thabs la gsum ste/ bkur sti dang rim gro'i sgo nas ji ltar bsten pa dang / mos pa dang gus pa'i sgo nas ji ltar bsten pa dang / bsgrub pa dang nan tan gyi sgo nas ji ltar bsten pa'o/[119] /

The fourth point is how to rely on the Dharma master skillfully. Once someone has connected with such Dharma masters, there are three ways of relying on them: (1) by showing respect and rendering service, (2) by cultivating the relevant reverence and devotion, and (3) by personal Dharma practice and earnestness.

d.div: [119] sgrub/ dpal spungs/

f.d: dang po la gnyis las/ bkur stis ji ltar bsten pa ni/ phyag 'tshal ba dang / myur du ldang ba dang / lus 'dud pa dang / bskor ba bya ba dang / gdung ba'i sems kyis dus su smra ba dang / ngoms pa med pa'i sems kyis yang dang yang du blta ba la sogs pa ste/[120] dper na tshong dpon gyi bu nor bzang gis dge ba'i bshes gnyen ji ltar bsten pa bzhin no/[121] /

The first of these [has two parts]. Showing respect is accomplished by prostrating to them, rising quickly [when they enter], bowing to them, circumambulating them, speaking at the appropriate time with a loving mind, looking at them again and again with an insatiable mind, and so forth. This was exemplified by the way that Maṇibhadra, a powerful merchant’s son, related to his teacher.

d.div: [120] ngom/ dpal spungs/
[121] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_sdong po bkod pa'i mdo/ shog_305_na3

f.d:
'phags pa sdong po bkod pa'i mdo las kyang /
dge ba'i bshes gnyen blta ba la ngoms pa med par gyis shig /de ci'i phyir zhe na/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen rnams ni mthong bar dka'o/ /'byung bar dka'o/ /mjal bar dka'o/[122] / zhes gsungs so/ /

It says in the Marvelous Array Sutra:
Gaze insatiably at your Dharma master. Why? Dharma masters are rarely seen, rarely manifest, and seldom met with.[70]

d.div: [122] gong mtshungs/ sdong po bkod pa'i mdo/ shog_343_na2
[70] Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra, Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, a, 305a3.

f.d: rim gros ji ltar bsten pa ni/ chos dang mthun pa'i zas dang / gos dang / mal cha dang / stan dang / bsnyun gyi gso sman dang / nor la sogs pa'i yo byad kyis lus dang srog la mi lta bar dge ba'i bshes gnyen la bsnyen bkur byed pa ste/ dper na 'phags pa rtag tu ngus dge ba'i bshes gnyen ji ltar bsten pa bzhin no/[123] /[124]

Relying on Dharma masters by serving them is accomplished by catering to their needs. This means providing them with food, clothing, bedding, seating, medicines when they are unwell, funds, and the like, in a way that accords with the Buddhist teaching. This is to be done without heed for one’s own life or physical well-being, as exemplified by the realized being Sadāprarudita.

d.div: [123] srog la yang / dpal spungs/
[124] sde dge_12_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_brgyad stong pa/ le'u/ 30_shog_261_na3

f.d:
dpal 'byung gi rnam thar las kyang /
sangs rgyas kyi byang chub ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen la rim gro byas pas thob bo/[125] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In the Instructions for Liberation of Śrī Saṃbhava we read:
A buddha’s enlightenment is attained by serving Dharma masters.[71]

d.div: [125] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_sdong po bkod pa'i mdo/ dpal 'byung gi le'u/ shog_284_ba5

f.d: mos pa dang / gus pas ji ltar bsten pa ni/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen la sangs rgyas kyi 'du shes bzhag la/ ji skad gsungs pa'i bka' mi gcog pa dang /[126] mos pa dang / gus pa dang / dang ba bskyed pa ste/[127] dper na paN chen nA ro pas dge ba'i bshes gnyen ji ltar bsten pa bzhin no/[128] /

The second way is to rely on them by [cultivating] reverence and devotion. Having established the concept that the teacher is a buddha, whatever the teacher says is taken to be instruction, never to be transgressed, to be followed in constancy and with the cultivation of reverence, devotion, and joyous trust. /65/ This was exemplified by the way master scholar Nāropa relied on his guru.

d.div: [126] bcog pa/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[127] dad pa/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[128] paN chen nA ro pas dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsten tshul skor bka' brgyud pa'i rnam thar pod dang po/ dpal nA ro pa'i rnam thar dri med legs bshad bde chen 'brug sgra/ shog_77_nas _213

f.d:
rgyal ba'i yum las kyang /
khyod kyis dge ba'i bshes gnyen la nan tan du gus pa bskyed par bya'o/ / phangs par bya'o/ / rab tu dad par bya'o/[129] / zhes gsungs so/ /

It says, in the Mother of the Conquerors:
Earnestly cultivate reverence for Dharma masters, follow them, and have joyous trust.[72]

[72] Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines (Aṣṭasāhasrikāprajñāpāramitā), Toh 12 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 261a3.

f.d: gzhan yang dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi thabs mkhas pa'i spyod pa la yang / log par rtog pa spong zhing lhag par yang gus pa bskyed pa ste/[130] dper na rgyal po me'i rnam thar bzhin no/[131] /

Besides this, wrong ways of thinking about the personal conduct of masters should be abandoned, because their conduct is in fact their skillful technique at work. Instead, cultivate the noblest devotion for it. This was exemplified in the biography of King Anala.[73]

d.div: [130] log par rtog pa spong zhing lhag par yang gus pa bskyed pa ste/ zhes pa'i tshig 'di dag ma dper mi byung yang / mtsho sngon mi rigs dpe skrun khang nas dpar du btab pa/ bod kyi bcu phrag rig mdzod chen mo/ bka' brgyud gsung rab pod brgyad pa'i thar rgyan du gsal bas 'dir bcug pa yin/
[131] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_sdong po bkod pa'i mdo/ shog_22_na7

[73] The bodhisattva Sudhana was sent to King Anala to learn compassion, but when he arrived, he saw what seemed to be the king judging and punishing evildoers mercilessly. Thus he initially doubted the king’s bodhisattva qualities. However, he listened to his inner voice and went to the king, who then took him to wonderful paradises and explained that he could manifest visions of the worst punishments or the greatest rewards in order to instill confidence in moral discipline in his subjects.

f.d: bsgrub pa dang nan tan gyi sgo nas ji ltar bsten pa ni/[132] dge ba'i bshes gnyen de'i chos la thos pa dang / bsam pa dang / sgom pa gsum gyi sgo nas bsgrub pa dang / nan tan du byed pa ste/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen mchog tu mnyes par 'dis 'gyur ba yin no/ /

The third way to rely on masters is by Dharma practice and earnestness. There are three steps to Dharma practice in this respect: first to study Dharma under the masters’ guidance, then to contemplate its significance, and finally to make it a reality in practice. Do these earnestly; that is what will be most satisfying for the teacher.

d.div: [132] bsgrub/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

Thus the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
The firm one who practices just as instructed will surely make their minds most pleased.[74]

d.div: [133] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 18_sh+loka_12_shog_25_ba4
[74] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 25b4.

dge ba'i bshes gnyen mgu na sangs rgyas thob par 'gyur te/ dpal 'byung gi rnam thar las kyang /
dge ba'i bshes gnyen mgu bar byas na sangs rgyas thams cad kyi byang chub thob bo/[134] / zhes gsungs so/ /

When someone’s Dharma master is satisfied, that person will attain buddhahood. It says in the Instructions for Liberation of Śrī Saṃbhava:
By satisfying the master, the enlightenment of all the buddhas will be attained.[75]

d.div: [134] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_sdong po bkod pa'i mdo/ dpal 'byung gi le'u/ shog_288_ba1
[75] Flower Ornament Sutra (Avataṃsakasūtra), Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, ā, 288b1.

f.d: dge ba'i bshes gnyen la chos zhu ba de yang / sbyor ba dang dngos gzhi mjug gsum 'dzom pa'i tshul gyis zhu ba ste/ de yang sbyor ba la ni byang chub kyi sems dang ldan pas zhu'o/ / dngos gzhi la rang la nad pa'i 'du shes dang / chos la sman gyi 'du shes dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen la sman pa'i 'du shes dang / chos la nan tan du nyams su len pa ni nad nye bar 'tsho ba'i 'du shes bskyed pas zhu'o/ / mjug tu ni snod kha sbubs lta bu dang /[135] snod zhabs rdol lta bu dang / snod dug can lta bu'i skyon spang bar bya'o/ /

As far as requesting Dharma teachings from one’s Dharma masters is concerned, there are three phases: the preparation, the actual instruction, and the conclusion. The preparation is to have the bodhisattva motivation when requesting the teachings. During the actual instruction, consider yourself to be like a patient, the Dharma to be like medicine, the teacher to be like the physician, and the earnest practice of Dharma to be the best and quickest way to recovery. The conclusion is to avoid the three mistakes of being like an upturned container, a leaky container, or a filthy container.[76]

d.div: [135] sbub/ dpal spungs/
[76] These three “faults of the container” refer respectively to being unreceptive, nonretentive, or soiled by the afflictions.

f.d:
dge ba'i bshes gnyen bsten pa'i phan yon ni/ dpal 'byung gi rnam thar las kyang /
rigs kyi bu dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis yang dag par zin pa'i byang chub sems dpa' ni/ ngan song du mi ltung ngo / / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis yongs su bsrung ba'i byang chub sems dpa' ni/ sdig pa'i grogs po'i lag tu mi 'gro'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis yongs su bskyangs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' ni/ theg pa chen po'i chos las mi ldog go / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis yang dag par zin pa'i byang chub sems dpa' ni/ so so skye bo'i sa las yongs su 'da'o/[136] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The fifth point is about the benefits of relying on Dharma masters. In the Instructions for Liberation of Śrī Saṃbhava we read:
Child of noble descent! A bodhisattva who is most properly nurtured by a good Dharma master will not fall into the lower states. A bodhisattva who is totally protected by a Dharma master will not be swayed by corrupting friends. A bodhisattva who is perfectly trained by a Dharma master will not abandon the bodhisattva way. A bodhisattva who is most excellently sustained will completely transcend the activities of ordinary people.[77] /66/

rgyal ba'i yum las kyang /

The Perfection of Wisdom [in Eight Thousand Lines] also says:
A realized bodhisattva who is most properly nurtured will swiftly attain peerless, totally pure, and perfect enlightenment.[78]
