(3) Having taken refuge in the Sangha, trust should not be placed in the misguided (tīrthika).[223] The sutra says:
Those who have taken refuge in the Sangha will not side with the tīrthikas.[224]

d.div: [416] brten/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[417] sde dge_119_bka'/ mdo sde/ nya_mya ngan las 'das pa chen po'i mdo/ le'u/ 4_shog_120_na6

[223] I have translated the Tibetan mu stega pa as “the misguided,” following the Kagyü-lineage explanation for this term, which is far from the oft-used “heretic,” as they are truly devoted to a spiritual path that has many beneficial elements. In Buddhist scriptures, the term refers to the proponents of the non-Buddhist philosophical schools.
[224] Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra, Toh 119 Kangyur, mdo sde, nya, 120a6.

f.d: cha mthun pa'i bslab bya gsum las/ sangs rgyas dkon mchog gi rten de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku gzugs tha na sA ts+tsha'i chag dum yan chad la gus par bya ba dang /[418] chos dkon mchog gi rten dam chos kyi po ti dang glegs bam/ tha na de'i yi ge 'bru re yan chad la gus par bya ba dang / dge 'dun dkon mchog gi rten ston pa'i cha lugs dang / tha na ser po'i lhan pa btab pa yan chad la gus par bya'o/ /

The three specific instructions are: (1) Respect should be shown for images of the Tathāgata, whatever they may be, from a small image molded in clay upward, because they represent the real, most precious Buddha. (2) Respect should be shown for the volumes and collected works of scripture, from a mere letter of scripture upward, because they represent the most precious Dharma. (3) Respect should be shown for Buddhist garb, from a simple patch of yellow cloth upward, because it represents the most precious Sangha.

d.div: [418] tshwa tshwa'i/ dpal spungs/

f.d: skyabs su song ba'i phan yon la brgyad de/ nang pa sangs rgyas par tshud pa dang / sdom pa thams cad kyi rten du 'gyur ba dang / sngar byas kyi sdig pa thams cad zad par 'gyur ba dang / mi dang mi ma yin pa'i bar chad kyis mi tshugs pa dang / bsam pa'i dngos po thams cad 'grub pa dang / rgyu bsod nams chen po dang ldan par 'gyur ba dang / ngan song du mi ltung ba dang / myur du mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas bar 'gyur ba'o//

Ninth, eight [principal] benefits come from taking refuge: (1) A person becomes a Buddhist. (2) It is the basis for all the [other] precepts. (3) All evils formerly committed will be consumed. (4) Hindrances created by humans or nonhumans can no longer overwhelm [the person]. (5) All that is wished for will be achieved. (6) Great causal merit is accrued.[225] (7) The person will not fall into the lower states and (8) will soon become truly and perfectly enlightened.

d.div: [225] In itself, and as the basis for all the other precepts, taking refuge is a cause of great merit, since the karmic power of a vow such as refuge acts continuously, even in sleep.

f.d: The first point in this overall section on the persons whose lives constitute a basis for bodhicitta discussed the necessity of [having] Mahayana potential, [that is, belonging to the Mahayana fold]. The second concerned the need to have taken refuge, as explained above. The third point deals with the need to have taken one of the prātimokṣa commitments.
don gsum pa

so so thar pa'i sdom pa ni/ rdzas su ni bzhi/ rten du ni brgyad yod pa las/ 'dir bsnyen gnas ma gtogs pa'i ris bdun po gang rung gcig blang ba'o/[419] / de la so so thar pa ris bdun ni/ dge slong pha ma gnyis/ dge slob ma dang gsum/ dge tshul pha ma gnyis te lnga/ dge bsnyen pha ma gnyis te bdun no/ /

There are four main types of prātimokṣa vows, which, when considered through the individuals [males and females] who take them, make eight categories. Of these, if you disregard the temporary precepts observed when fasting,[226] there are seven types. Whichever one of these seven is appropriate is adopted. The seven classes of prātimokṣa commitment are those of the monk, nun, novice monk, trainee nun, novice nun, ordained layman, and ordained laywoman.[227]

d.div: [419] blangs pa'o/ / mi rigs dpe skrun/

[226] The temporary lay precepts (bsnyen gnas, upavāsatha) are eight precepts observed for twenty-four-hour periods on special occasions: not to kill, steal, lie, have sex, take intoxicants, eat after the appointed time (usually noon), wear adornments, sing or dance, or use high seats or beds.
[227] The names of these seven levels in Sanskrit are respectively bhikṣu, bhikṣuṇī, śrāmaṇera, śikṣamāṇā, śrāmaṇerikā, upāsaka, and upāsikā.

f.d:
de ltar yang byang chub sems dpa'i sa las/
so so thar pa'i sdom pa yang dag par blangs pa'i ris bdun po de/ dge slong dang / dge slong ma dang / dge slob ma dang / dge tshul dang / /dge tshul ma dang / dge bsnyen dang / dge bsnyen ma'i tshul khrims gang yin pa ste/ de yang khyim pa dang / rab tu byung ba'i phyogs la ci rigs par rig par bya'o/[420] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Bodhisattva Levels says of these:
The seven categories of those who have most properly adopted the precepts of prātimokṣa are these: those [observing] the moral discipline of the monk, nun, novice monk, trainee nun, novice nun, ordained layman, and ordained laywoman. According to their content, these precepts are those of laypersons or renunciates, as appropriate.[228]

d.div: [420] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 10_shog_74_ba7
[228] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 74b7.

f.d: 'o na 'jug pa'i sems bskyed kyi don du so so thar pa'i sdom pa dgos pa ci zhe na/ dpe dang / lung dang / 'thad pa ste/ rgyu mtshan gsum gyi sgo nas rten du dgos par rig par bya'o/ /

Now, one might ask, “Why is it that one needs to have prātimokṣa vows as a prerequisite for generating the engaged bodhicitta?” They should understand this need for such vows as a basis [for engaged bodhicitta] in three ways: by simile, by scriptural authority, and by reason. /114/

de la dang po ni/ dper na 'khor los sgyur ba'i rgyal po chen po de spyan drangs shing bzhugs su gsol ba'i gnas ni/ lud dang ljan ljin la sogs pa mi gtsang bas khyab pa'i sa phyogs ma yin te/ khang bzang legs par byi dor byas pa rin po che la sogs pa'i rgyan du mas spras pa yid du 'ong ba cig yin pa ltar/ byang chub kyi sems kyi rgyal po de yang bskyed cing bzhugs su gsol ba'i gnas ni/ lus ngag yid gsum mi dge ba las mi sdom pa dang / sdig pa'i dri mas gos pa'i rgyud la ma yin te/ lus ngag yid gsum sdig pa'i dri ma dang bral ba/ sdom pa'i tshul khrims kyis legs par brgyan pa'i lus la bskyed cing bzhugs su gsol ba yin pa'o/ /

The first way is by simile. A place to which a great universal monarch is invited to come and stay should not be filled with impurities such as dung and rubbish. It should be an excellent dwelling place, spotlessly clean and decorated with many fine adornments made of precious substances and the like. It should be a pleasing place. Likewise, when someone is cultivating the great monarch bodhicitta and hoping for it to remain, the “place” where it can abide is not in a person who is not committed to avoiding wrong physical, verbal, and mental actions. It is not in one who is tarnished by the stains of evil. It is to be invited to reside in someone without the stains of physical, verbal, and mental evil, someone whose physical existence is properly adorned with the moral discipline of commitment.

lung ni/ mdo sde rgyan gyi sems bskyed pa'i skabs las/ sdom pa rgya chen de yi rten/[421] / zhes gsungs te/ de yang bsnyen gnas kyi sdom pa ni/ nyin zhag gcig pa'i sdom pa yin pas rgya chung la/ ris bdun po de ni de ltar ma yin pas sdom pa rgya chen po ste/ des na ris bdun ni sems bskyed kyi rten du gsungs pa yin no/ /

The second way is by scriptural authority. In the bodhicitta section of the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras, it says, “Its basis is extensive vows.”[229] The temporary lay vow are of limited extent because they only last for a day and a night. Unlike this, the other seven classes are extensive commitments, and this is why those seven are taught as constituting the foundation for bodhicitta.

d.div: [421] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 5_sh+loka_4_shog_4_ba4
[229] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 5:4, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 4b4.

f.d:
byang chub lam sgron las kyang /
so so thar pa ris bdun gyis/ / rtag tu sdom gzhan ldan pa la/ / byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa yi/ / skal pa yod kyi gzhan du min/[422] / zhes gsungs te/ so so thar pa ris bdun las gang rung gcig rten du bshad pa'o/ /

Further, Lamp for the Path to Awakening states:
Only those who have the lasting commitment in one of the seven classes of prātimokṣa vows are suitable for the bodhisattva vow; it is not so for others.[230] This is explained as meaning that you should observe whichever one of those seven types is appropriate.

d.div: [422] sde dge_3947_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_byang chub lam sgron/ sh+loka_21_shog_239_na4
[230] Atiśa, Bodhipathapradīpa verse 20, Toh 3947 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 239a4.

f.d: 'thad pa ni/ so so thar pa'i sdom pa ni gzhan la gnod pa gzhi dang bcas pa spong ba yin la/ byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa ni gzhan la phan 'dogs pa yin te/ gnod pa las ma log par phan gdags thabs med pa'i phyir ro/ /

The third way is by logical necessity. Through the prātimokṣa vows, you abandon harm to others along with its basis. Through the bodhisattva vows, you benefit others. There is no way in which you can benefit others without first renouncing harming them.

gal te gzhan dag na re/ so so thar pa'i sdom pa de/ byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa skye ba'i rten du mi 'thad de/ za ma dang / ma ning dang / lha la sogs pa la so so thar pa'i sdom pa mi skye ba la/ byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa skye bar bshad pa'i phyir ro/ / gnas pa'i rten du yang mi 'thad de/ so so thar pa ni shi 'phos pas gtong la/[423] byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa des mi gtong ba'i phyir ro zhe na/

However, according to some people, the prātimokṣa vows are not necessarily a prerequisite for giving rise to the bodhisattva vow because hermaphrodites, eunuchs, gods, and so on who are unable to take the prātimokṣa vows are able to give rise to bodhicitta. Some also assert that the prātimokṣa precepts cannot be a prerequisite because they expire at death, whereas the bodhisattva commitment does not. If you wonder about these points,

d.div: [423] so so thar pa'i sdom pa/ dpal spungs/

f.d: lan ni/ so so thar pa'i sdom pa la bsam pa'i khyad par gyi rigs gsum yod de/[424] rigs bdun po de khams gsum gyi bde bar 'dod pa'i bsam pas blangs nas legs smon gyi tshul khrims shes bya la/[425] rang gi sdug bsngal gtan du spang bar 'dod pa'i bsam pas blangs na/ nyan thos kyi nges par 'byung ba'i tshul khrims shes bya'o/ / byang chub chen po thob par 'dod pa'i bsam pas blangs na/ byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa'i tshul khrims shes bya'o/ /

understand that the prātimokṣa precepts fall into three categories, determined by the attitude with which they are taken: (1) When these vows are taken because of a motivation to reach happiness in the three dimensions of existence, they are called the moral discipline of vested interest. (2) When they are taken with the wish of being rid of suffering forever, they are known as the moral discipline of śrāvaka renunciation. /115/ (3) When they are taken through a wish to achieve great enlightenment, they are called the moral discipline of the bodhisattva vow.

d.div: [424] gyis/ dpal spungs/
[425] blangs na/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: de la snga ma gnyis po ni/ za ma dang / ma ning dang / lha la sogs pa la mi skye ba'i phyir dang / shi 'phos nas gtong ba'i phyir dang / nyams na slar gso mi rung ba'i phyir/ byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa'i rten ma yin la/ byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa'i tshul khrims ni/ za ma dang / ma ning dang / lha la sogs pa la yang yod pa dang / shi 'phos kyang mi gtong ba dang / nyams na slar gso rung ba'i phyir/ skye ba'i rten yang yin la gnas pa'i rten yang yin no/ /

The first two of the above cannot be taken by hermaphrodites, eunuchs, gods, and the like. They finish at death and cannot be restored if damaged, and so are not the foundation for the bodhisattva vow. The moral discipline of the bodhisattva vow can be taken by hermaphrodites, eunuchs, gods, and so on, is not lost at death, and can be restored if damaged. For these reasons it is the prerequisite for both taking and keeping the bodhisattva vow.

des na mdo sde rgyan gyi 'grel pa las kyang /
sems de'i rten gang zhe na/ byang chub sems dpa'i tshul khrims kyi sdom pa ni rten no/[426] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Thus it says in the commentary to the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras:
What is the foundation of that mentality? The vow of bodhisattva moral discipline is its foundation.[231]

d.div: [426] sde dge_4034_bstan/ sems tsam/ mi_blo gros brtan pa/ mdo sde rgyan gyi 'grel bshad/ le'u/ 1_shog_53_ba1
[231] Sthiramati, Detailed Exposition of the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras (Sūtrālaṃkāravṛttibhāṣya), Toh 4034 Tengyur, sems tsam, mi, 53b1.

f.d:
yang na skye ba'i rten du dgos la/ gnas pa'i rten du nges pa med de/
dper na zag pa med pa'i sdom pa skye ba'i rten du/ bsam gtan gyi sdom pa dgos kyang / gnas pa'i rten du nges pa med pa lta bu'o/[427] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Therefore prātimokṣa precepts are needed as a basis for giving rise to bodhicitta but are not necessarily required as a continuous basis for maintaining bodhicitta.
This is a similar case to the meditative concentration vow being a necessary basis for giving rise to the untainted vow but not necessarily required for the latter’s continuance.[232]

d.div: [427] gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/

[232] Ibid. The “meditative concentration vow” (dhyānasaṃvara) is the conceptual and artificial dedication of the mind needed to develop profound absorption. It requires discipline. When it bears fruit, the “untainted vow” (anāsravasaṃvara), natural to the state of meditative concentration itself, supplants the artifice, which need no longer be maintained.

f.d: byang chub sems dpa'i so so thar pa'i sdom pa de yang / len pa'i cho ga ni logs su mi dgos te/ sngar nyan thos kyi bslab pa nyid phyis bsam pa khyad par can gyi zin na/[428] gnas gyur nas byang chub sems dpa'i sdom par 'gyur ba yin te/[429] dman pa'i sems btang yang spong ba'i sems pa ma dor ba'i phyir ro/[430] / de ltar theg pa chen po'i rigs dang ldan pa/ dkon mchog gsum la skyabs su song ba/ so so thar pa'i sdom pa ris bdun las gang rung gcig dang ldan pa ste/ de nas byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i rten gyi gang zag yin no/ /

There is no need to take the bodhisattva prātimokṣa precepts through a special ceremony. If they have already been taken as part of śrāvaka training, they will still be extant when the mind has the special inspiration [of bodhicitta] and will automatically become the bodhisattva’s prātimokṣa commitment, since the lesser motivation will have been abandoned but not the spirit of renouncing harming others. Thus we have seen that someone who has Mahayana potential, who has taken refuge in the three most precious refuges, and who has taken whichever is appropriate of the seven classes of prātimokṣa vow is a suitable person for giving rise to bodhicitta.

d.div: [428] bslab pa blangs pa nyid phyis/ mi rigs dpe skrun/ bslab pa blangs pa nyid kyi/ dpal spungs/
[429] gnas 'gyur/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[430] mi rigs dpe skrun khang dpar mar dgag sgra mi byung /

f.d: dam chos yid bzhin gyi nor bu thar pa rin po che'i rgyan las/ skyabs su 'gro zhing sdom pa bzung ba'i le'u ste brgyad pa'o// //
This concludes the eighth chapter, concerning refuge and taking precepts, from this Ornament of Precious Liberation, a Wish-Fulfilling Gem of Sublime Dharma.
le'u dgu pa/ byang chub kyi sems yongs su gzungab/
9. The Proper Adoption of Bodhicitta

d.i: Second topic: The essential nature of bodhicitta development

f.d:
byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i ngo bo nyid ni/ gzhan gyi don du yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub 'dod pa ste/ mngon rtogs rgyan las/
sems bskyed pa ni gzhan don phyir/ / yang dag rdzogs pa'i byang chub 'dod/[431] / ces gsungs so/ /

Having explored the first point, the basis for bodhicitta, at length, the second point defines the essential nature of bodhicitta development, which is a wish for utterly pure and perfect enlightenment so as to be able to benefit others. This is clearly defined in the Ornament of Clear Realization:
Developing bodhicitta means wanting utterly perfect enlightenment for the sake of others.[233]

d.div: [431] sde dge_3786_bstan/ sher phyin/ ka_byams pa mgon po/ mngon rtogs rgyan/ skabs/ 1_sh+loka_19_shog_2_ba5
[233] Maitreya, Abhisamayālaṃkāra 1:18ab, Toh 3786 Tengyur, shes phyin, ka, 2b5.

f.d: byang chub kyi mchog tu sems bskyed pa la dbye na gsum ste/ dpe'i sgo nas dbye ba dang / sa mtshams kyi sgo nas dbye ba dang / mtshan nyid kyi sgo nas dbye ba'o/ /
The different types of supreme bodhicitta are described in three ways /116/: by simile, according to what demarcates levels, and according to their characteristics.

de la dang po ni/ byang chub kyi sems de nyid so so skye bo nas sangs rgyas kyi sa'i bar du dbye ba dpes bstan pa 'phags pa byams pas gsungs te/ ji skad du/ mngon rtogs rgyan las/
de yang sa gser zla ba me/ / gter dang rin chen 'byung gnas mtsho/ / rdo rje ri sman bshes gnyen dang / / yid bzhin nor bu nyi ma glu/ / rgyal po mdzod dang lam po che/ / bzhon pa bkod ma'i chu dang ni/ / sgra brnyan chu bo sprin rnams kyis/ / rnam pa nyi shu rtsa gnyis so/[432] / zhes gsungs so//[433]

The similes typifying bodhicitta, from that of an individual person through to that of a buddha, were taught by Ārya Maitreya in the Ornament of Clear Realization:
These are the twenty-two examples: earth, gold, the moon, fire, treasure, a jewel mine, an ocean, a vajra, a mountain, medicine, a virtuous friend, a wish-fulfilling gem, the sun, a song, a king, a treasury, a highway, a carriage, a reservoir, melodious sounds,[234] a river, and a cloud.[235]

d.div: [432] gong mtshungs/ mngon rtogs rgyan/ skabs/ 1_sh+loka_20_shog_2_ba5
[433] gsungs te/ dpal spungs/

[234] The text here lists this twentieth bodhicitta as resembling an “echo” (sgra brnyan), but in Gampopa’s explanation below, it is given as “melodious sound” (sgra snyan). The spellings in Tibetan are very close. As the Sanskrit here is ānandokti, sgra snyan is the better choice.
[235] Maitreya, Abhisamayālaṃkāra 1:19–20, Toh 3786 Tengyur, shes phyin, ka, 2b5.

f.d: dpe nyi shu rtsa gnyis po 'di dag ni/ don 'dun pa nas chos sku'i bar du yin te/ de yang lam lnga dang sbyar na/ 'dun pa dang ldan pa ni sa dang 'dra ste/ chos dkar po thams cad kyi gzhi'i dngos po byed pa'o/ /

These twenty-two similes cover bodhicitta from [initial] aspiration through to [final] dharmakāya. To relate these to the five phases of the path: (1) Bodhicitta endowed with aspiration is like the earth, for it serves as the foundation for all good qualities.
bsam pa dang ldan pa ni gser dang 'dra ste/ byang chub kyi bar du mi 'gyur ba'o//
(2) Bodhicitta endowed with commitment is like a gold, for it will not change until enlightenment is achieved.

lhag pa'i bsam pa dang ldan pa ni zla ba tshes pa dang 'dra ste/ dge ba'i chos mtha' dag rnam par 'phel bar 'gyur ba'o/ / de gsum ni tshogs lam chung ngu dang 'bring dang chen po nyid kyi las dang po pa'i sas bsdus pa'o/ /

(3) Bodhicitta endowed with profound commitment is like the waxing moon, for [with this] every virtuous quality will increase. These three constitute the beginner’s stage, that is, the lower, middle, and higher sections of the path of accumulation.
sbyor ba dang ldan pa ni me dang 'dra ste/ thams cad mkhyen pa nyid gsum la sgrib pa'i bud shing bsreg par byed pa'o/[434] / de ni sbyor ba'i lam gyis bsdus pa'o/ /
(4) Bodhicitta endowed with integration is like fire, for it burns away the fuel that is the obstacles to the threefold wisdom, such as omniscience. This is encompassed by the path of application.

d.div: [434] sreg_dpal spungs/

f.d: sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa dang ldan pa ni gter chen po dang 'dra ste/[435] sems can thams cad tshim par byed pa'o/ /
(5) Bodhicitta endowed with the perfection of generosity is like a great treasure, for it brings satisfaction to all beings.

d.div: [435] dpal spungs dang mi rigs dpe skrun khang gnyis su/ dang ldan pa/ zhes pa'i tshig mi byung /

f.d: tshul khrims dang ldan pa ni rin po che'i 'byung gnas dang 'dra ste/ yon tan rin po che'i rten gyi dngos po byed pa'o/ /
(6) Bodhicitta endowed with the perfection of moral discipline is like a jewel mine, for it acts as the supporting ground for precious qualities.
bzod pa dang ldan pa ni rgya mtsho chen po dang 'dra ste/ mi 'dod pa thams cad thog tu bab pas mi 'khrug pa'o/[436] /
(7) Bodhicitta endowed with the perfection of patience is like an ocean, for [with this] one remains untroubled by whatever unwanted thing turns up.

d.div: [436] 'khrugs/ dpal spungs/

f.d: brtson 'grus dang ldan pa ni rdo rje dang 'dra ste/ mi shigs pa nyid kyis na sra ba'o/ /
(8) Bodhicitta endowed with the perfection of diligence is like a vajra, for one remains indestructible.
bsam gtan dang ldan pa ni ri'i rgyal po dang 'dra ste/ dmigs pa'i rnam par g.yeng bas mi bskyod pa'o/ /
(9) Bodhicitta endowed with the perfection of meditative concentration is like a mountain, for one remains unshaken by distractions posed by the mind’s objects of attention.
shes rab dang ldan pa ni sman dang 'dra ste/ nyon mongs pa dang shes bya'i sgrib pa'i nad zhi bar byed pa'o/ /
(10) Bodhicitta endowed with the perfection of wisdom is like medicine, for it pacifies the sicknesses that are the affliction and knowledge obscurations.
thabs dang ldan pa ni dge ba'i bshes gnyen dang 'dra ste/ gnas skabs thams cad du sems can gyi don yongs su mi gtong ba'o/ /
(11) Bodhicitta endowed with the perfection of skillful means is like a virtuous friend, for [with this] one never relents from bringing benefit to beings, no matter what the circumstances.
smon lam dang ldan pa ni yid bzhin gyi nor bu dang 'dra ste/ ji ltar smon pa'i 'bras bu 'grub pa'o/ /
(12) Bodhicitta endowed with the perfection of aspiration is like a wish-fulfilling gem, for [with it] one achieves whatever result is wished.
stobs dang ldan pa ni nyi ma dang 'dra ste/ gdul bya yongs su smin par byed pa'o/ /
(13) Bodhicitta endowed with the perfection of powers /117/ is like the sun, for it helps bring disciples to full maturity.

ye shes kyi pha rol tu phyin pa ni chos kyi sgra dbyangs dang 'dra ste/ gdul bya 'dun par byed pa'i chos ston pa'o/ / de ltar bcu ni rim pa ltar rab tu dga' ba la sogs pa sa bcus bsdus te/ mthong ba'i lam dang / bsgom pa'i lam gyi spyod yul can yin no/ /

(14) Bodhicitta endowed with the perfection of pristine awareness is like the melody of Dharma songs, for [with it] one gives disciples Dharma teachings that inspire them. These ten, mentioned above, correspond in their respective order to the ten bodhisattva levels, from the Joyous [the first level] to the tenth. Thus they lie within the sphere the path of seeing and the path of cultivation.[236]

d.div: [236] The paths of seeing and cultivation are defined differently by Gampopa here than in the later chapters dedicated to the phases of the path (chapter 18) and the bodhisattva levels (chapter 19). The more usual allocation of the path of seeing to the first bodhisattva level alone is here extended up to the seventh level, while the path of cultivation is confined to the nondual eighth through tenth levels.

f.d: mngon par shes pa dang ldan pa ni rgyal po chen po dang 'dra ste/ mthu thogs pa med pas gzhan gyi don sgrub pa'o/[437] /
(15) Bodhicitta endowed with clear awareness is like a powerful king, for with it one benefits others with unimpeded power.

d.div: [437] bsgrub/ dpal spungs/

f.d: bsod nams dang ye shes dang ldan pa ni bang mdzod dang 'dra ste/ tshogs mang po'i mdzod du gyur pa'o/ /
(16) Bodhicitta endowed with the wealth of goodness and pristine awareness is like a treasury, for one becomes a storehouse of many accumulations.
byang chub kyi phyogs dang mthun pa'i chos dang ldan pa ni lam po che dang 'dra ste/ 'phags pa thams cad gshegs shing rjes su gshegs pas so/ /
(17) Bodhicitta endowed with the factors conducive to enlightenment is like a great highway, for with it one treads the way that all the noble ones have trod.
snying rje dang lhag mthong dang ldan pa ni bzhon pa dang 'dra ste/ 'khor 'das gang du yang mi btang bar bde blag tu 'gro ba'o/[438] /
(18) Bodhicitta endowed with great compassion and deeper insight is like a carriage, for with it one travels directly to one’s goal, straying into neither samsara nor the mere peace of nirvana.

d.div: [438] mi ltung par/ dpal spungs/

f.d: gzungs dang spobs pa dang ldan pa ni bkod ma'i chu dang 'dra ste/ thos pa dang ma thos pa'i chos 'dzin pas mi zad pa'o/ / de ltar lnga ni byang chub sems dpa'i khyad par gyis lam gyis bsdus pa'o/[439] /

(19) Bodhicitta endowed with dhāraṇī[237] and prowess is like a reservoir, for with it everything learned through study or otherwise is retained and not wasted. These five are encompassed by the special bodhisattva path.

d.div: [439] khyad par gyi/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

[237] Dhāraṇī (Tib. gzungs) here refers to the ability to associate many things to a key trigger, such as a syllable, and the way this leads to retention of knowledge and experience. In higher phases of the path, simply uttering, and remaining within, the key trigger can spontaneously activate one’s accumulated knowledge and experience.

f.d: chos kyi skyed mos tshal dang ldan pa ni sgra snyan pa thos pa dang 'dra ste/ thar pa 'dod pa'i gdul bya la snyan par sgrogs pa'o/ /
(20) Bodhicitta endowed with the “beautiful garden of Dharma” is like listening to a melodious sounds, for it makes those disciples keen on liberation eager to listen.
bgrod pa gcig pa'i lam dang ldan pa ni chu bo'i rgyun dang 'dra ste/ gzhan gyi don bya ba mi nyams pa'o/ /
(21) Bodhicitta endowed with the one and only way [traveled by all the buddhas] is like the flow of a great river, for with it one never deviates from the purpose of benefitting others.

chos kyi sku dang ldan pa ni sprin dang 'dra ste/ dga' ldan gyi gnas su bzhugs pa la sogs pa ston pa'i sgo nas/ sems can gyi don du bya ba rnams de la rag las pa'o/ / de ltar gsum ni sangs rgyas kyi sas bsdus pa ste/ de ltar na nyi shu rtsa gnyis po las dang po pa'i sa nas bzung ste/ sangs rgyas kyi sa'i bar gyis bsdus so/ /

(22) Bodhicitta endowed with the dharmakāya is like a rain cloud, for on it depends the bringing about of the welfare of sentient beings, such as through demonstrating the deed of residing in Tuṣita Paradise. These last three points are encompassed within the stage of buddhahood. Thus the twenty-two [aspects of bodhicitta presented by means of similes] cover the entire path from the beginner’s level through to the buddhahood.

sa mtshams kyi sgo nas dbye ba ni bzhi ste/ mos pa dang ldan pa'i sems bskyed dang / lhag pa'i bsam pa dang ldan pa'i sems bskyed dang / rnam par smin pa'i sems bskyed dang / sgrib pa spangs pa'i sems bskyed do/ / de la dang po ni/ mos pas spyod pa'i sas bsdus pa rnams so/ / gnyis pa ni/ sa dang po nas bdun pa'i bar dag go / gsum pa ni/ sa brgyad pa nas bcu pa'i bar dag go/ bzhi pa ni/ sangs rgyas kyi sa'o/ /

Classified in terms of what demarcates levels, bodhicitta is fourfold: (1) bodhictta endowed with aspiration, (2) bodhicitta endowed with extraordinary intention, (3) bodhicitta in its full maturity, and (4) bodhicitta with obscurations eliminated. The first of the above corresponds to the levels of practice motivated by aspiration; the second applies to the first seven great bodhisattva levels; the third, to the eighth through tenth levels; and the fourth, to the level of buddhahood.

de ltar yang mdo sde rgyan las/
sems bskyed de ni sa rnams la// mos dang lhag bsam dag pa dang / / rnam par smin pa gzhan du 'dod/ / de bzhin sgrib pa spangs pa'o/[440] / zhes gsungs so//

Thus the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
Bodhicitta on the various levels is held to be accompanied by aspiration, pure extraordinary intention, full maturity, and the elimination of all obscurations.[238] /118/

d.div: [440] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 5_sh+loka_2_shog_4_ba2
[238] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 5:2, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 4b2.

f.d:
mtshan nyid kyi sgo nas dbye na gnyis te/ don dam byang chub kyi sems dang / kun rdzob byang chub kyi sems so/ / de ltar yang dgongs pa nges par 'grel ba'i mdo las/
byang chub kyi sems de yang rnam pa gnyis te/ don dam pa byang chub kyi sems dang / kun rdzob byang chub kyi sems so/[441]/ zhes gsungs so/ /

Classified in terms of essential characteristics bodhicitta is twofold: the ultimate bodhicitta and the relative bodhicitta. As the Sutra Definitely Elucidating the Noble Intention says:
There are two aspects to bodhicitta: ultimate bodhicitta and relative bodhicitta.[239]

d.div: [441] sde dge_106_bka'/ mdo sde/ ca_mdo sde dgongs 'grel/ le'u/ 8_shog_34_ba7
[239] Saṃdhinirmocanasūtra, Toh 106 Kangyur, mdo sde, ca, 34b7.

f.d: 'o na don dam byang chub kyi sems de ci tsam zhig snyam na/ stong nyid snying rje'i snying po can gsal la mi g.yo ba spros pa'i mtha' dang bral ba'o/ /
What, then, is ultimate bodhicitta? It is emptiness having compassion as its very essence, an unvacillating state that is lucidity, free of the extremes of conceptual elaboration.

de ltar yang mdo sde de nyid las/
de la don dam byang chub kyi sems de ni 'jig rten las 'das pa/ spros pa'i mtha' dang bral ba/ shin tu gsal ba/ don dam pa'i yul can/ dri ma med pa/ mi g.yo ba/ rlung med pa'i mar me'i rgyun ltar shin tu gsal ba'o/[442] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Therefore the sutra says:
Of those, ultimate bodhicitta is that vivid clarity that transcends the world, without any extreme of conceptual elaboration, extremely clear, having the ultimate meaning as its object, unpolluted and unwavering, as still as a flame protected from the breeze.[240]

d.div: [442] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde dgongs 'grel/ le'u/ 8_shog_34_ba7
[240] Ibid.

f.d:
'o na kun rdzob byang chub kyi sems de ci tsam zhig yin snyam na/ yang mdo sde de nyid las/
kun rdzob byang chub kyi sems ni snying rjes sems can mtha' dag 'khor ba nas 'don par dam bcas pa'o/[443] / zhes gsungs so//

And what would relative bodhicitta be? Quoting the same sutra:
Relative bodhicitta is the commitment, through compassion, to lead all sentient beings out of samsara.[241]

d.div: [443] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde dgongs 'grel/ le'u/ 8_shog_34_ba7
[241] Ibid.

f.d: de la don dam byang chub kyi sems de ni chos nyid kyis thob pa yin la/ kun rdzob byang chub kyi sems ni yang dag par blangs pa brda las byung ba yin par mdo sde rgyan las bshad do/[444]/ don dam byang chub kyi sems de gnas skabs gang na yod ce na/ sa dang po rab tu dga' ba yan chad na yod do/ /

Of the two forms of bodhicitta mentioned above, it is stated in the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras that the ulimate bodhicitta is attained by means of realizing suchness, while the relative bodhicitta arises through language in the form of adopting it [in a valid ritual].[242]

d.div: [444] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 5_sh+loka_7_shog_4_ba6
[242] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 4b6.

f.d:
de ltar yang mdo sde rgyan gyi 'grel pa las/
don dam pa'i sems bskyed pa de yang sa dang po rab tu dga' ba la yin pas/[445] zhes gsungs so/ /

Furthermore the Detailed Exposition of the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
At what stage is there ultimate bodhicitta? From the first great bodhisattva level, the Joyous, onward.[243]

d.div: [445] sde dge_4034_bstan/ sems tsam/ mi_blo gros brtan pa/ mdo sde rgyan gyi 'grel bshad/ le'u/ 1_shog_54_na7
[243] Sthiramati, Sūtrālaṃkāravṛttibhāṣya, Toh 1034 Tengyur, sems tsam, mi, 54a7.

f.d:
kun rdzob byang chub kyi sems la dbye na gnyis te/ smon pa'i sems dang / 'jug pa'i sems so/ / de ltar yang spyod 'jug las/
byang chub sems de mdor bsdu na/ / rnam pa gnyis su shes bya ste/ / byang chub smon pa'i sems dang ni/ / byang chub 'jug pa nyid yin no/[446] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In terms of categories, relative bodhicitta has two aspects: aspiration bodhicitta and engaged bodhicitta. Thus Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life says:
Bodhicitta can be summed up as being known through two aspects: the mind aspiring to enlightenment and the mind proceeding to enlightenment.[244]

d.div: [446] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_rgyal sras zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 1_sh+loka_15_shog_2_ba4
[244] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 1:15, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 2b4.

f.d: smon 'jug gnyis kyi khyad par 'di la yang bzhed pa tha dad pa mang ste/ 'phags pa 'jam dpal nas/ slob dpon klu sgrub nas mar la brgyud pa'i slob dpon zhi ba lhas ni/[447] smon pa ni/ 'gro bar 'dod pa dang 'dra ste/ rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas thob par 'dod pa'i don bsam pa yin la/[448] 'jug pa ni 'gro ba dngos dang 'dra ste/ sangs rgyas bsgrub pa'i sbyor ba yin par bzhed do/[449] /

There are many different explanations of the particularities of these two aspects of relative bodhicitta—aspiration and engagement. According to Master Śāntideva, of the tradition stemming from Ārya Mañjuśrī through Master Nāgārjuna, aspiration is like a wish to go and comprises in reality all intentions longing for perfect buddhahood, whereas engagement is like the actual going /119/ and is in reality the practical application of all that will achieve buddhahood.

d.div: [447] ma la/ dpal spungs/
[448] mi rigs dpe skrun dpar mar don zhes pa mi byung /
[449] sgrub/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d:
de ltar yang spyod 'jug las/
'gro bar 'dod dang 'gro ba yi/ / bye brag ji bzhin shes pa ltar/ / de bzhin mkhas pas 'di gnyis kyi/ / bye brag rim bzhin shes par bya/[450] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Thus Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life says:
Just as wanting to go and actually going are known to be different, so should these two be respectively distinguished by the wise.[245]

d.div: [450] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_rgyal sras zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 2_sh+loka_16_shog_2_ba5

f.d: 'phags pa byams pa nas/ slob dpon thogs med nas mar la brgyud pa'i jo bo gser gling pa ni/[451] smon pa ni/ sems can thams cad kyi don du bdag gis rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas thob par bya'o snyam du 'bras bu la dam bca' len pa yin la/ 'jug pa ni sangs rgyas kyi rgyur pha rol tu phyin pa drug la bslab par bya'o snyam du rgyu la dam bca' len par bzhed pa'o/ /

According to the great Serlingpa, of the lineage stemming from Ārya Maitreya through Master Asaṅga, aspiration is to make a promise committing oneself to the result, thinking, “For the benefit of all sentient beings I will attain perfect buddhahood,” whereas engagement is to make a promise committing oneself to the cause, thinking, “I will train in the six perfections as the cause of buddhahood.”

d.div: [451] pas ni/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d:
don de dang mthun par chos mngon pa kun las btus pa las/
sems bskyed pa ni rnam pa gnyis te/ khyad par can ma yin pa dang / khyad par du 'phags pa'o/ / de la khyad par can ma yin pa ni/ kye ma'o bdag bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya bar shog cig snyam pa'o/ / khyad par du 'phags pa ni/ de ltar sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa yongs su rdzogs par shog cig snyam pa nas/ shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i bar du'o/[452] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In line with this interpretation, the Compendium of Higher Knowledge says:
Those who develop bodhicitta are of two types: those who are not special and those who are particularly excellent. Of these, those who are not special think, “Oh, if only I could become totally enlightened in unsurpassable, totally pure, and perfect buddhahood.” Those who are particularly excellent think, “May I totally accomplish the perfection of generosity . . . and so forth . . . through to the perfection of wisdom.”[246]

d.div: [452] sde dge_4049_bstan/ sems tsam/ ri_'phags pa thogs med/ mngon pa kun btus/ le'u/ 2_shog_95_ba4
[246] Asaṅga, Abhidharmasamuccaya, Toh 4049 Tengyur, sems tsam, ri, 95b4.

f.d: de ltar dpe dang / sa mtshams dang / mtshan nyid kyi sgo nas sems bskyed kyi dbye ba bshad zin to/ /

d.i: Fourth topic: The focus of bodhicitta

f.d:
byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i dmigs pa ni/ byang chub dang sems can gyi don la dmigs pa'o/ / de ltar yang byang chub sems dpa'i sa las/
de lta bas na/ sems bskyed pa de ni byang chub la dmigs pa dang / sems can la dmigs pa yin no/[453] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Fourth, the focus of bodhicitta encompasses both enlightenment and the welfare of sentient beings. It says of this, in Bodhisattva Levels:
Hence bodhicitta is something focused on enlightenment and focused on sentient beings.[247]

d.div: [453] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 1_shog_7_ba3
[247] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 7b3.

f.d:
de la byang chub la dmigs pa zhes bya ba ni/ theg pa chen po'i ye shes 'tshol bar dmigs pa ste/ mdo sde rgyan gyi sems bskyed kyi skabs nas kyang /
de bzhin de'i ye shes 'tshol bar dmigs pa'o/[454]/ zhes gsungs so/ /

Of these two, bodhicitta focused on enlightenment is that which is focused on striving for Mahayana pristine awareness. In the chapter in the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras concerning bodhicitta development, it says:
. . . likewise that which it is focused on is pristine awareness.[248]

d.div: [454] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 5_sh+loka_3_shog_4_ba3
[248] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 4b3.

f.d: sems can la dmigs pa zhes bya ba yang / sems can gcig gam/ gnyis sam/ 'ga' tsam ma yin te/ nam mkhas gar khyab na sems can gyis khyab/ des gar khyab pa na las dang nyon mongs pas khyab la/ des gang na khyab pa na sdug bsngal gyis khyab pas/ de rnams kyi sdug bsngal sel bar bya ba'i ched du sems bskyed pa'o/[455] /

That which is focused on sentient beings does not mean focused on just one, two, or several beings. Space is pervaded, for as far as it stretches, by conscious life forms, and they in turn are permeated by karma and affliction. Wherever the latter pervade, suffering pervades also. Bodhicitta is developed to remove those beings’ sufferings.

d.div: [455] bsal bar/ dpal spungs/

f.d:
de ltar yang bzang spyod smon lam las/
nam mkha'i mthas gtugs gyur pa ci tsam par/ / sems can ma lus mtha' yang de bzhin te/ / ji tsam las dang nyon mongs mthar gyur pa/ / bdag gis smon lam mtha' yang de tsam mo/[456] / zhes gsungs so//

Thus the Prayer of Excellent Conduct says: /120/
Whatever may be the limits of space, they are the limits of sentient beings. They are also the limits of karma and the afflictions, and they are the limits of my aspirations as well.[249]

d.div: [456] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_sdong po bkod pa'i mdo/ bzang spyod smon lam/ shog_361_na6
[249] In the Marvelous Array Sutra (Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra), in the Flower Ornament Sutra, Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, a, 361a6.

d.i: Fifth topic: The causes of bodhicitta

f.d:
byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i rgyu ni/ chos bcu pa'i mdo las/
rgyu bzhis sems de skye bar 'gyur te/ sems de nyid kyi phan yon mthong ba dang / de bzhin gshegs pa la dad pa dang / sems can gyi sdug bsngal mthong ba dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis yang dag par bskul ba'o/[457]/ zhes gsungs so/ /

Fifth, concerning the causes for bodhicitta development, the Ten Dharmas Sutra says:
Such a mind will arise on account of four causes: insight into the benefits and qualities of such a mentality, faith in the Buddha, recognition of the sufferings of sentient beings, and proper encouragement from a Dharma teacher.[250]

d.div: [457] sde dge_53_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ kha_chos bcu pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 1_shog_168_na1
[250] Daśadharmakasūtra, Toh 53 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, kha, 168a1.

f.d:
byang chub sems dpa'i sa las kyang rgyu bzhir gsungs te/ ji skad du/
de la rgyu bzhi gang zhe na/ rigs phun sum tshogs pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i sems skye ba'i rgyu dang po'o/ / sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' dang / dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyis yongs su zin pa ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i sems skye ba'i rgyu gnyis pa'o/ / sems can rnams la snying rje ba ni/ byang chub sems dpa'i sems skye ba'i rgyu gsum pa'o/ / 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal dang dka' ba spyad pa'i sdug bsngal yun ring ba rnam pa sna tshogs pa/ drag pa/ bar chad med pas kyang mi 'jigs pa 'di ni byang chub sems dpa'i sems skye ba'i rgyu bzhi pa'o/[458] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Further, Bodhisattva Levels says:
What are the four causes for that? (1) The first cause for the arising of the bodhisattva mind is that of possessing the very best potential. (2) The second cause for the arising of the bodhisattva mind is to be properly supported by the buddhas, bodhisattvas, and by spiritual teachers. (3) The third cause for the arising of the bodhisattva mind is to have compassion for sentient beings. (4) The fourth cause for the arising of the bodhisattva mind is fearlessness in the face of samsara’s suffering and the sufferings of undergoing hardships, even though these may be long enduring, manifold, difficult to cope with, and without respite.[251]

d.div: [458] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 1_shog_9_na3
[251] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 9a3.

f.d:
mdo sde rgyan las ni/ yang dag par blangs pa brda las byung ba'i sems bskyed pa dang / don dam pa'i sems bskyed pa gnyis rgyu so sor gsungs te/ de la dang po ni/
grogs stobs rgyu stobs rtsa ba'i stobs/ / thos stobs dge ba goms pa las/ / mi brtan pa dang brtan byung ba/ / gzhan gyis bstan pa'i sems bskyed bshad/[459] / ces gsungs te/

In the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras, separate causes are mentioned for the generation of the two aspects of bodhicitta: (1) generation of a verbally arisen bodhicitta on the basis of having received it through a perfect ritual, and (2) generation of ultimate bodhicitta. With respect to the first, it says:
Through the power of support, of the cause, and of the root, of learning, and of virtuous habits, it is taught that, respectively, stable and unstable bodhicitta, and bodhicitta taught by others will emerge.[252]

d.div: [459] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 5_sh+loka_7_shog_4_ba5
[252] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 5:7, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 4b5.

f.d: gzhan gyis bstan pa'i sems bskyed ces pa ni/ gzhan gyi rnam par rig byed las sems skye ba gang yin pa de ni yang dag par blangs pa brda las byung ba zhes kyang bya ste/ kun rdzob byang chub kyi sems so/ /

The generation of “bodhicitta taught by others” refers to that which has arisen on the basis of other’s revelatory speech (vijñapti) and is also known as “that which is properly received and occurs by means of words.” This is relative bodhicitta.

de yang grogs kyi stobs las te dge ba'i bshes gnyen gyi ngor skye ba yod do/ / rgyu'i stobs las te rigs kyi mthus skye ba yang yod do/ / dge ba'i rtsa ba'i stobs las te/ de'i rigs rgyas pa'i sgo nas skye ba yang yod do/ / thos pa'i stobs las te/ chos kyi rnam grangs de dang de bshad pa na skye ba yang yod do/ / dge ba la goms pa las te tshe 'di nyid la rtag tu nyan pa dang 'dzin pa dang 'chang ba la sogs pa las skye ba yang yod do/ / de yang grogs kyi stobs las mi brtan la/ rgyu la sogs pa'i stobs las ni brtan par 'byung ba'o/ /

Within this there are those that arise through the power of support—that is, through the presence of a spiritual teacher. Then there are those that arise through the power of cause, meaning by the force of our natural potential; those that arise through the power of the root of virtue, meaning the activation of that potential; those arising through the power of learning, when the varieties and meaning of the Dharma are explained; and those that arise through the power of virtuous habits, /121/ through whatever has been routinely studied, directly understood, firmly adhered to, and so forth in this life. Of the above, that which arose through the power of support is unstable, while those that arose through the power of the cause and the rest are stable.

don dam pa'i sems skye ba'i rgyu ni/
rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas rab mnyes byas/ / bsod nams ye shes tshogs rab bsags/ / chos la mi rtog ye shes ni/ / skye phyir de ni dam par 'dod/[460] / ces gsungs te/ lung dang / sgrub pa dang /[461] rtogs pa'i khyad par dag gis bskyed pa'o/ /

As to the cause for the arising of ultimate bodhicitta, it is said that:
Having pleased well the perfect buddhas, and having gathered perfectly merit and wisdom, nonconceptual pristine awareness of reality arises; this is held to be the ultimate bodhicitta.[253] That is, ultimate bodhicitta is generated through study of scriptures, practice, and realization.

d.div: [460] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 5_sh+loka_8_shog_4_ba6
[461] bsgrub pa dang / dpal spungs/

d.i: Sixth topic: The source from which the vow is taken

f.d: byang chub kyi sems de blang ba'i yul ni/ slob dpon yod pa'i lugs dang / med pa'i lugs gnyis yin te/ de yang slob dpon de'i spyan sngar 'gro ba la srog gam tshangs par spyod pa'i bar chad med na/ sa thag ring yang slob dpon yod pa yin pas de'i spyan sngar phyin la yul de las blang ba'o/ / slob dpon gyi mtshan nyid kyang / sdom pa 'bogs pa'i cho ga la mkhas pa dang / rang nyid sdom pa thob la ma nyams par gnas pa dang / lus ngag gi rig byed kyi don go bar nus pa dang / zang zing lhur mi byed par brtse bas slob ma skyong ba'o/ /

The sixth point concerns the source from which the bodhisattva vow is adopted. There are two ways [of taking the vow]: one involving a preceptor and one without a preceptor. If it poses no obstacle to life or practice of purity, the aspirant should go to a preceptor, if one is available, and take the commitment personally, even if the latter is far away. The characteristic qualities of such teachers are (1) skill in the ritual ceremony for administering the vow, (2) having received the vow themselves and kept it unimpaired, (3) the ability to convey the meaning of the ritual’s physical gestures and words, (4) a loving care for their disciples that is undefiled by the pursuit of material gain.

de ltar yang byang chub lam sgron las/
yang dag mtshan nyid ldan pa yi/ / bla ma bzang la sdom pa blang / / sdom pa'i cho ga la mkhas dang / / bdag nyid gang zhig sdom la gnas/ / sdom pa 'bogs bzod snying rjer ldan/ / bla ma bzang por shes par bya/[462] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Thus it says, in Lamp for the Path to Awakening:
Take the vow from a good master, possessing the very best characteristics. A good master should be known as someone skilled in the ceremony for taking the vow who has personally kept whatever the vow entails and gives the vow patiently and compassionately.[254]

d.div: [462] sde dge_3947_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_jo bo rje dpal ldan a ti sha_byang chub lam sgron/ sh+loka_23_shog_239_na5
[254] Atiśa, Bodhipathapradīpa verses 22cd–23, Toh 3947 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 239a5.

f.d:
byang chub sems dpa'i sa las kyang /
byang chub sems dpa' smon lam btab pa'i phyir/ chos mthun pa/ sdom pa blangs pa/ mkhas pa/ ngag gi rnam par rig byed kyi don 'dzin pa dang / go bar nus pa/[463] zhes gsungs so/ /

Bodhisattva Levels says:
To be able to give the bodhisattva wish, the preceptor should be in accord with Dharma, have taken the vow, be skilled, know how to communicate the meaning of the ritual words, and know how to make the disciple understand.[255]

d.div: [463] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 10_shog_82_na7
[255] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 82a7.

f.d: de lta bu'i bla ma de thag nye ba na bzhugs kyang de'i spyan sngar 'gro ba la srog gam/ tshangs par spyod pa la bar chad yod na/ bla ma med pa zhes bya ba yin te/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku gzugs kyi spyan sngar smon 'jug gang len pa'i tshig rnams snying thag pa nas lan gsum brjod pas smon pa'am 'jug pa de thob bo/ /

However, if such a lama resides close by but there is a possibility of some threat to life or to purity in going to him, then there is the “lama-less” method. For this, stand before an image of the Buddha and sincerely recite three times the words of the aspiration bodhicitta or the engaged bodhicitta vow, whichever is appropriate. Thereby you receive the aspiration or practice vow.

de ltar yang byang chub sems dpa'i sa las/
gal te yon tan de dag dang ldan pa'i gang zag med par gyur na/ byang chub sems dpas de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku gzugs kyi spyan sngar/ bdag nyid kyis byang chub sems dpa'i tshul khrims kyi sdom pa yang dag par blang bar bya ste/[464] zhes gsungs so/ /

Thus, Bodhisattva Levels says:
Should it happen that there is no such person with the requisite qualities, bodhisattvas properly go before an image of the Buddha and take the vow of bodhisattva moral discipline by themselves.[256]

d.div: [464] gong mtshungs/ byang sa/ le'u/ 10_shog_83_ba2

f.d:
bla ma dang sku gzugs gnyis ka ma rnyed na/ mdun gyi nam mkha' la sangs rgyas dang / byang chub sems dpa' rnams mngon sum bsgoms nas/ smon pa'am 'jug pa'i tshig rnams lan gsum brjod pas thob bo/ /de ltar yang bslab pa kun las btus pa las/
yang de lta bu'i dge ba'i bshes gnyen med na/ phyogs bcu na bzhugs pa'i sangs rgyas dang byang chub sems dpa' rnams mngon sum du bsgoms nas/ sdom pa bdag nyid kyi stobs dang sbyar la blang ste/[465] zhes gsungs so//

If neither a preceptor /122/ nor a Buddha image is available, the words of the aspiration or engaged bodhicitta vow are recited three times in front of buddhas and bodhisattvas visualized as truly present, assembled in space before the aspirant. The Compendium of Trainings says:
Further, should there be no such spiritual mentor, meditate that the buddhas and bodhisattvas dwelling in the ten directions are really present and take the vow through the strength of your own mind.[257]

d.div: [465] sde dge_3940_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_rgyal sras chen po zhi ba lha/ bslab btus/ le'u/ 1_shog_9_ba1
[257] Śāntideva, Śikṣāsamuccaya, Toh 3940 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 9b1.

f.d: byang chub kyi sems de blang ba'i cho ga ni/ bla ma mkhas pa dag gi brgyud pa'i man ngag las/ tshul lugs tha dad pa du ma snang ngo / / de ltar snang yang ni/ 'dir 'phags pa 'jam dpal nas slob dpon klu sgrub na mar la brgyud pa slob dpon zhi ba lha'i lugs dang / 'phags pa byams pa nas slob dpon thogs med na mar brgyud pa/ jo bo gser gling pa'i lugs dang gnyis su shes par bya'o/ / de yang 'phags pa 'jam dpal nas slob dpon klu sgrub na mar brgyud pa slob dpon zhi ba lha'i lugs ltar na gsum ste/ sbyor ba'i cho ga dang / dngos gzhi'i cho ga dang / rjes kyi cho ga'o/ /

The seventh point explains the ceremony for adopting bodhicitta. Many ways and traditions of taking the bodhisattva vow have emerged, evolving from the specific styles of instruction of lineages originating from the great learned masters. Though there are many, the subject matter here concerns the two [main] traditions: Master Śāntideva’s tradition, of the lineages passed down from Ārya Mañjuśrī to Master Nāgārjuna; and Master Serlingpa’s tradition, of the lineages passed down from Ārya Maitreya to Master Asaṅga. Master Śāntideva’s tradition. This is the lineage passed down from Ārya Mañjuśrī to Master Nāgārjuna; it has a ceremony in three stages: (1) a preparation, (2) the actual ceremony [generating bodhicitta], and (3) a conclusion.
[Preparation]

dang po la drug ste/ mchod pa 'bul ba dang / sdig pa bshags pa dang / dge ba la rjes su yi rang ba dang / chos kyi 'khor lo bskor bar bskul ba dang / mya ngan las mi 'da' bar gsol ba gdab pa dang / dge ba'i rtsa ba bsngo ba'o/ / de la dang po mchod pa 'bul ba 'di yang / yul dang mchod pa gnyis su shes par bya'o/ / de yang yul ni/ dkon mchog mngon sum na bzhugs pa la mchod pa dang / mngon sum na mi bzhugs pa la mchod pa gnyis bsod nams mnyam par bshad pas/ mngon sum du gyur pa dang / ma gyur pa thams cad yul du byas la mchod do/ /

The preparation is in six parts: (1) making offerings, (2) confessing past wrongs, (3) rejoicing in virtue, (4) requesting the buddhas to teach the Dharma, (5) supplicating the buddhas not to abandon the world, and (6) dedicating the roots of virtue. The first, making offerings, needs to be understood in terms of both recipients and the offerings themselves. The offerings are made to the most precious refuges. Since it is explained that making offerings to them creates the same merit whether or not you are actually in their presence, offerings are made both to those present and to those not actually present.

de ltar yang mdo sde rgyan las/
rab dang sems dang ldan pa yis/ / tshogs gnyis rdzogs par bya ba'i phyir/ / sangs rgyas rnams la gos la sogs/ / mngon sum mngon sum min par mchod/[466] / ces gsungs so/ /

Thus the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
With a mind filled with faith, offer robes and so forth to the buddhas, both in reality and with your imagination, in order to complete the two accumulations.[258]

d.div: [466] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 18_sh+loka_1_shog_25_na4
[258] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 18:1, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 25a4.

f.d: mchod pa la yang gnyis las/ bla na yod pa'i mchod pa dang / bla na med pa'i mchod pa'o/ /
As for the offerings, there are two types: surpassable and unsurpassable offerings.

dang po la gnyis te/ zang zing gi mchod pa dang / bsgrub pa'i mchod pa'o/ / dang po ni/ phyag gi mchod pa dang / bstod pa'i mchod pa dang / rdzas rim par bshams pa'i mchod pa dang / bdag pos yongs su ma gzung ba'i rdzas phul du byung ba'i mchod pa dang /[467] blos sprul pa'i mchod pa dang / lus dbul ba'i mchod pa ste/ de dag rgyas par shes par bya'o/ / sgrub pa'i mchod pa ni/[468] lha'i sku phyag rgya chen po sgom pa dang / byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyi ting nge 'dzin las byung ba'i bkod pas mchod pa'o/ /

The surpassable offerings are also twofold: material offerings and the offering of realization. Material offerings comprise prostrations, praises, /123/ material goods neatly and properly set out in the right order, and also the offering of things that belong to no one in particular. These can be actual things of good quality as well as creations of the imagination and the offering of your own body. Such offerings can be studied in detail in other works. Realization as an offering entails offering Mahāmudrā[259] meditation of the deities’ forms as well as the various arrays [of offerings] emerging from the profound meditative absorptions of the bodhisattvas.

d.div: [467] bzung / dpal spungs/
[468] bsgrub/ dpal spungs/

[259] Mahāmudrā (Tib. phyag rgya chen po), the central teaching and practice of the Kagyü tradition, is both meditation on and realization of the empty nature of the mind. The meditation can be done with tantric visualization practice, which is what “medition on the deities’ forms” refers to in this sentence.

f.d:
bla na med pa'i mchod pa ni/ dmigs pa dang bcas pa'i mchod pa dang / dmigs pa med pa'i mchod pa'o/ / de la dang po ni/ byang chub kyi sems sgom pa ste/ ji skad du/
mkhas pas byang chub sems bsgoms na/ / rgyal ba sras dang bcas pa la// mchod pa 'di ni dam pa ste/[469] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Unsurpassable offerings are twofold: those that take place within what appears to be objective reality and those beyond objective reality. The first of these is bodhicitta meditation. As it is said:
When a wise person cultivates bodhicitta, this is the highest offering he can make to the buddhas and their heirs.[260]

d.div: [469] mkhas pas byang chub sems bsgoms na/ /zhes sogs kyi gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[260] The source of this quote has not been identified.

f.d:
dmigs pa med pa'i mchod pa ni/ bdag med kyi don bsgom pa ste/ mchod pa'i mchog yin no/ / de ltar yang lha'i bu blo gros rab gnas kyis zhus pa'i le'u las/ byang chub 'dod pa'i byang chub sems dpa' yis/ /
bskal pa bye ba gang gA'i bye snyed du/ / me tog spos dang de bzhin zas skom dag / phul nas mi mchog sangs rgyas mchod pa bas/ / gang gis gang la bdag dang srog dang ni/ / gang zag ma mchis de 'dra'i chos 'di dag / thos nas de la 'od gsal bzod thob pa/ / de yis mi mchog dam pa mchod pa lags/[470] / zhes gsungs so//

The second, offering that is beyond objective reality, refers to meditation on the absence of self-entity, which is the supreme offering. Therefore it says in the Questions of the Devaputra Susthitamati Sutra:
Were a bodhisattva, desirous of enlightenment, to make offerings to the Buddha, the best of all humans, offering quantities of flowers, incense, food, and drink equal in number to the grains of sand on the banks of the river Ganges, so doing for ten million cosmic ages, and were another such bodhisattva to offer his training in the teachings on no-self, absence of life force, and absence of personality, along with the resulting achievement of being able to sustain clear lucidity, it would be the latter bodhisattva who made the better offering.[261]

d.div: [470] sde dge_80_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ca_lha'i bu blo gros rab gnas kyis zhus pa'i mdo/ bam po/ 2_shog_300_na3
[261] Susthitamatidevaputraparipṛcchāsūtra, Toh 80 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ca 300a3.

f.d:
seng ge sgra chen gyi mdo las kyang /
gang 'du shes dang mtshan ma skyed par mi byed pa de ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa mchod pa yin no/ / blang dor med pa dang / gnyis su med par 'jug pa de ni de bzhin gshegs pa mchod pa yin no/ / grogs po dag de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku ni dngos po med pa'i mtshan nyid yin pas/ de ni dngos po'i 'du shes la gnas pas mchod par slang ba ma yin no/[471]/ zhes gsungs so/ /

It also says, in the Lion’s Roar Sutra:
Not to create ideas or descriptions is to make offerings to the Tathāgata. To be without adopting or rejecting and to penetrate that which is nondual is to make offerings to the Tathāgata. Friends, since the very character of the body of the Tathāgata is insubstantial, do not make offerings while conceiving it to be substantial.[262]

d.div: [471] sde dge_67_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ca_seng ge sgra chen gyi mdo/ bam po/ 3_shog_103_ba6
[262] Siṃhanādasūtra, Toh 67 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ca, 103b6.

f.d: mchod pa 'bul ba bshad zin to//
This concludes the section on making offerings.

gnyis pa ni/ sdig pa bshags pa bshad na/ spyir dge sdig thams cad yid kyi kun slong la rag las te/ yid gtso bo yin/ lus ngag bran yin no/ / de ltar yang rin chen phreng ba las/
chos rnams yid ni sngon 'gro bas/ / yid ni gtso bo zhes grags pas/[472] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The second [of the six parts of the preparation] is confessing past wrongs. Generally speaking, good and evil depend on the mind’s motivation: mind is the master, and body and speech are its servants. The Precious Garland says:
Since mind precedes all things, it is often said, “Mind is master.”[263]

d.div: [472] sde dge_4158_bstan/ spring yig_ge_mgon po klu sgrub/ rin chen phreng ba/ le'u/ 4_sh+loka_73_shog_121_na1
[263] Nāgārjuna, Ratnāvalī 4:73, Toh 4158 Tengyur, spring yig, ge, 121a1.

f.d: des na yid chags sdang la sogs pa nyon mongs pa can gyis kun nas bslang nas/ mtshams med pa lnga'am/ / de dang nye ba lnga'am/ mi dge ba bcu'am/ sdom pa dang / dam tshig nyams pa la sogs pa rang gis byas pa dang / gzhan byed du bstsal pa dang /[473] byed pa la rjes su yi rang ba rnams sdig pa mi dge ba zhes bya ste/ der ma zad yid chags sdang dang / nyon mongs pa can gyis kun nas bslang nas dam pa'i chos la thos bsam sgom gsum byas pa yang mi dge ba yin no/[474] /

Hence when the mind is motivated by a defiled state—desire, anger, and the like—people may commit the five acts with an immediate consequence, the five like them, or the ten negative actions. They may break vows or profound commitments /124/ or perhaps incite others to do such things. Even if they do not do these things personally, they may delight in the fact that others are perpetrating such evils. All the preceding are what is meant by the terms “wrong” and “nonvirtue.” Not only those [manifestly wrong actions] but even Dharma activities such as study, contemplation, or practice that are motivated by a mind under the sway of passion, anger, and the afflictions also become nonvirtue.

d.div: [473] brtsal/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[474] bslangs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d:
de dag gi 'bras bu ni sdug bsngal 'byung ba yin te/ de ltar yang rin chen phreng ba las/
'dod chags zhe sdang gti mug gsum/ / des bskyed las ni mi dge ba/ / mi dge ba las sdug bsngal kun/ / de bzhin ngan 'gro thams cad de/[475]/zhes gsungs so/ /

Thus the Precious Garland says:
Attachment, anger, ignorance, and the actions to which they give rise are nonvirtue. Nonvirtue brings all the sufferings and hence all the lower states of existence.[264]

d.div: [475] sde dge_4158_bstan/ spring yig_ge_mgon po klu sgrub/ rin chen phreng ba/ le'u/ 1_sh+loka_20_shog_107_ba5
[264] Ibid. 1:20ab and 21ab, 107b5.

f.d:
spyod 'jug las kyang /
mi dge ba las sdug bsngal 'byung // 'di las ji ltar nges thar zhes/ / nyin mtshan kun tu bdag gis ni/ / 'di nyid 'ba' zhig bsam par rigs/[476] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Further, in Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life, it says:
From nonvirtue will arise suffering. The correct thing to do, day or night and in every circumstance, is to contemplate one thing and one thing alone: How can I attain definitive release from this?[265]

d.div: [476] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 2_sh+loka_63_shog_6_ba1
[265] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 2:63, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 6b1.

f.d:
des na sdig pa thams cad bshags par bya'o/[477] / bshags pas 'dag nges sam snyam na/ shin tu yang nges te/ mdo mya ngan 'das chen las/
sdig pa byas nas kyang phyis 'gyod de phyis 'chos na/ chu rnyogs pa can nor bu chu dwangs kyis dwangs pa'am sprin dang bral nas zla ba gsal ba dang 'dra'o/[478] / zhes pa dang /
de bas na sdig pa la 'gyod cing ma bcabs par bshags na ji lta bu yang byang bar 'gyur ro/[479] / zhes gsungs so/ /

This is the reason every wrong needs to be confessed. Will calling wrongs to mind actually purify them though? Most definitely! The Great [Passing into] Nirvana Sutra says:
Although a wrong may have been committed, subsequent remorse will put things right, in much the same way as cetain precious substances restore water’s clarity or as the moon retrieves her brilliance when emerging from clouds.[266] and
Hence it is by unburdening yourself of wrongdoings, with remorse and without dissimulation, that there will be purity.[267]

d.div: [477] de la/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[478] sde dge_119_bka'/ mdo sde/ nya_yongs su mya ngan las 'das pa'i mdo+o/ le'u/ 7_bam po/ 26_shog_305_ba1
[479] gong mtshungs/ yongs su mya ngan las 'das pa chen pa'i mdo+o/ le'u/ 7_bam po/ 26_shog_305_ba2
[266] Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra (longer version), Toh 119 Kangyur, mdo sde, nya, 305b1.

f.d:
bshags lugs ji ltar bshags na/ stobs rnam pa bzhi'i sgo nas bshags so/ / de ltar yang chos bzhi bstan pa'i mdo las/
byams pa byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po chos bzhi dang ldan na/ sdig pa byas shing bsags pa zil gyis gnon par 'gyur ro/ / bzhi gang zhe na/ 'di lta ste/ rnam par sun 'byin pa kun tu spyod pa dang / gnyen po kun tu spyod pa dang / nyes pa las zlog pa'i stobs dang / rten gyi stobs so/[480] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In what way exactly should you rid yourself of wrongdoings? By applying the four powers. Thus it says, in the Sutra Teaching the Four Qualities:
Maitreya! If bodhisattva mahāsattvas have these four things they will overcome evils that have been committed and established. What are these four? They are (1) the power of the thorough application of total remorse, (2) the power of thoroughly applying the remedy, (3) the power of renouncing harmful acts, and (4) the power of the support.[268]

d.div: [480] sde dge_249_bka'/ mdo sde/ za_chos bzhi bstan pa'i mdo/ shog_59_ba1
[268] Caturdharmanirdeśasūtra, Toh 249 Kangyur, mdo sde, za, 59b1.

f.d: de la rnam par sun 'byin pa kun tu spyod pa'i stobs ni/ sngar byas kyi sdig pa la 'gyod pa drag po bskyed nas yul gyi spyan sngar mthol bshags byed pa'o/[481] / de yang ji ltar 'gyod par bya zhe na/ 'gyod pa skyed lugs rnam pa gsum ste/[482] don med par brtags la 'gyod pa skyes pa dang / 'jigs par brtags la 'gyod pa skyes pa dang / myur du 'bral dgos par brtags la 'gyod pa skyes pa'o/ /

First is the power of the thorough application of total remorse. This is to disclose sincerely and with ardent regret, in the presence of the refuges, wrongs done in the past. How to stimulate remorse? There are three ways: (1) by considering the pointlessness of those wrongs, (2) by considering fear, and (3) by considering the urgent need for purification.

d.div: [481] skyes/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[482] skye lugs/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: de la dang po ni/ bdag gis byas pa'i sdig pa de yang res 'ga' dgra 'dul ba'i ched du byas/ res 'ga' gnyen bskyang ba'i ched du byas/ res 'ga' lus gnas pa'i ched du byas/ res 'ga' rdzas bsags pa'i ched du byas te/ bdag shi nas 'jig rten phyi mar skyes 'degs pa'i tshe/ dgra dang gnyen dang yul dang lus dang nor rdzas rnams bdag dang mi 'grogs par/ las ngan gyi sdig sgrib rnams bdag dang 'grogs nas gang du skyes pa der gshed mar ldang ba yin no/ /

[First,] remorse by considering their pointlessness is engendered by reflecting, “I have committed wrongs sometimes to subdue my enemies, sometimes to protect my friends, /125/ sometimes for the sustenance of my own body, and sometimes to accumulate material wealth. However, when I die and the time comes to move on to another life, my enemies and friends, my country and my body, and my wealth and possessions will not accompany me. Yet I shall be shadowed by the wrongs and obscurations created by my harmful actions; no matter where I am reborn these will rise up as my executioners.”

de ltar yang / khyim bdag dpal sbyin gyis zhus pa'i mdo las/
pha ma spun dang bu dang chung ma dang / / bran dang nor dang rtsa lag tshogs rnams kyang / / shi ba'i rjes phyir de dag 'gro ba med/ / las rnams rjes su 'brang zhing de dag 'gro/[483] / zhes dang /
shin tu sdug bsngal gyur pa de dus su/ / bu dang chung ma skyabs su 'gyur ma yin/ / bdag nyid gcig pus sdug bsngal myong bar 'ong / / de dag de tshe bdag gi skal mi len/[484] / zhes gsungs so/ /

This is why the Questions of the Layman Vīradatta Sutra says:
Father, mother, brothers, sisters, spouse, servants, wealth, and acquaintances cannot accompany those who die, but their actions do follow and trail after them.[269] It also says:
When great suffering comes, children and spouse offer no refuge. You experience the agony alone, and they cannot share your lot.[270]

d.div: [483] sde dge_72_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ca_dpal sbyin gyis zhus pa'i mdo/ shog_201_ba6
[484] gong mtshungs/ dkon brtsegs/ ca_dpal sbyin gyis zhus pa'i mdo/ shog_201_ba4
[269] Vīradattagṛhapatiparipṛcchāsūtra, Toh 72 Kangyur, dkon brstegs, ca, 201b6.

f.d:
spyod 'jug las kyang /
thams cad bor te chas dgos par/ / bdag gis de ltar ma shes nas/ / mdza' dang mi mdza' don gyi phyir/ / sdig pa rnam pa sna tshogs byas/ / mdza' ba rnams kyang med par 'gyur/ / mi mdza' rnams kyang med par 'gyur/ / bdag kyang med par 'gyur ba ste/ / de bzhin thams cad med par 'gyur/[485] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life says:
I must go, leaving everything behind. Unconscious of this, I commit various wrongs for the sake of the loved ones and those I dislike. However, those I love will cease to exist, those I dislike will cease to exist, and even I myself will cease to exist. In such a way, everything comes to the end of its existence.[271]

d.div: [485] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 2_sh+loka_36_shog_5_na6
[271] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 2:34–35, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma la, 5a6.

f.d: des na sdig pa ni dgra gnyen gnyis dang / lus longs spyod gnyis te de bzhi'i ched du byas pa la/ de bzhi dang bdag yun du 'grogs su med pas na/ sdig pa nyid tshegs che la don chung bar bsams nas 'gyod pa drag po bskyed do// gal te don med kyang des bdag la gnod par mi 'gyur snyam na/ don gnyis pa sdig pa'i 'bras bu des 'jigs par brtags la 'gyod par bya ste/ de yang sdig pa byas pa de 'chi ka'i tshe 'jigs pa dang / shi ba'i tshe 'jigs pa dang / shi ba'i 'og tu 'jigs pa dang gsum mo/ /

Thus we have committed wrongs for the sake of those four: friends, enemies, our body, and possessions. Those four will not accompany us for very long, yet on their account we have committed wrongs that bring much trouble and little benefit. Contemplating the reality of this, great remorse will arise. There are those who think that even if wrong actions are of little benefit, they will not really bring harm to their doer. They should contemplate the second point: remorse by considering fear. Reflecting, “The consequence of wrong is fear,” remorse will arise. Wrong actions result in three main times of fear: fear prior to death, fear when actually dying, and fear after death.

de la dang po ni sdig pa can rnams ni 'chi ka'i dus su yang / gnad gcod la sogs pa'i sdug bsngal mi bzad pa myong ste/[486] ji skad du/
bdag ni mal na 'dug bzhin du/ / gnyen bshes rnams kyis mtha' bskor yang / / srog gcod pa yi tshor ba dag /[487] bdag nyid gcig pus myong bar 'gyur/[488]/ zhes gsungs so/ /

Prior to death, those who have committed wrongs will experience unbearable sufferings, feeling struck to their very marrow and so forth. It is said:
As I lie on my bed, I may be surrounded by my friends and relatives, but it is I and I alone who will experience the feelings of life coming to its end.[272]

d.div: [486] gnod/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[487] srog chad/ dpal spungs/
[488] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 2_sh+loka_41_shog_5_ba2

f.d:
de nas shi ba'i tshe 'bras bu 'jigs pa ni/ gshin rje'i pho nya skyes bu nag po ma rungs pa zhags pa thogs pas ni mgul nas bcings shing dmyal ba'i gnas su khrid/ dbyug pa dang / shang lang la sogs pa mtshon cha thogs pa rnams kyis ni phyi nas gtses te/ gnod pa du ma 'byung ngo / / de ltar yang /
gshin rje'i pho nyas zin pa la/ / gnyen gyis ci phan bshes ci phan/ / de tshe bsod nams gcig skyabs na/ / de yang bdag gis ma bsten to/[489] / zhes gsungs so/ /

At the time of actual death, the result of wrongdoing is fear. The wrongdoer experiences the henchmen of the Lord of Death, black and horrible beings /126/ brandishing lassos, coming to place their lassos around his neck so as to lead him off to hell. Later others, bearing sticks, swords, and all sorts of weapons, torture and torment in many differing ways:
When grabbed by Yama’s henchmen, what use are relatives, what use are friends? At that time merit alone provides shelter, and merit have I not pursued![273]

d.div: [489] gong mtshungs/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 12_sh+loka_42_shog_5_ba3

f.d:
slob spring las kyang /
dus kyi zhags pas ske nas btags te gshin rje'i mi/ / gtum mo rnams kyis dbyug pas 'da' zhing khrid par 'gyur/[490] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Letter to a Student says:
Having locked time’s noose around our necks, Yama’s ferocious henchmen prod us with sticks and drag us along.[274]

d.div: [490] sde dge_4183_bstan/ spring yig_nge _slob dpon can+d+ra go mi/ slob spring / sh+loka_34_shog_48_na7
[274] Candragomin, Śiṣyalekha verse 34, Toh 4183 Tengyur, spring yig, nge, 48a7.

f.d:
gshin rje'i pho nya la bdag mi 'jigs so snyam na/ ji skad du/
skye bo yan lag gcod pa'i sar/ / de ring khrid pa'ang bred gyur te/ / kha skam mig rtsa ngan la sogs/ / sngar las gzhan du 'gyur snang na/ / gshin rje'i pho nya 'jigs 'jigs lta'i/ / sha tshugs can gyis bzung gyur cing / / 'jigs chen nad kyis thebs gyur pa/ / rab tu nyam thag smos ci dgos/[491] / zhes gsungs so/ /

A person who thinks “I shan’t be afraid of Yama’s henchmen” should reflect as follows:
Even those taken to a place where their limbs are to be hacked off become terror-stricken and dry-mouthed, their eyes bulging and bloodshot and the like. What need to mention my unspeakable horror when gripped by the fear that comes at the time of death and I am seized by the terrifying emissaries of the Lord of Death, vivid as if in flesh and blood?[275]

d.div: [491] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_spyod 'jug_le'u/ 2_sh+loka_44_shog_5_ba4
[275] Śāntideva, Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life (Bodhicaryāvatāra) 2:44–45, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 5b4.

f.d:
shi ba'i 'og rol du sdig pa'i 'bras bu 'jigs pa ni/ dmyal ba chen por lhung nas/ btso bsreg la sogs pa'i sdug bsngal mi bzad pa nyams su myong bar 'gyur ro/ / des na shin tu 'jigs te/ ji skad du/
dmyal ba bris pa mthong dang thos pa dang / / dran dang bklag dang gzugs su bgyis rnams kyang / / 'jigs pa skyed par 'gyur na mi bzod pa'i/ / rnam smin nyams su myong rnams smos ci 'tshal/[492] / zhes gsungs so/ /

There will also be fear beyond death as a consequence of wrongdoing. Having descended into the great hells, the unbearable sufferings of being boiled, burned, and so on are experienced, and this is quite terrifying:
Seeing hells depicted, hearing about them, thinking about them, reading about them, and seeing models— if these make people shudder with fear, what need is there to speak of those who actually experience the unbearable fruition of their acts [in the hells].[276]

d.div: [492] sde dge_4182_bstan/ spring yig_nge _mgon po klu sgrub/ bshes spring / shog_44_ba3
[276] Nāgārjuna, Letter to a Friend (Suhṛllekha) verse 84, Toh 4182 Tengyur, spring yig, nge, 44b3.

f.d: de ltar sdig pa'i 'bras bu de shin tu 'jigs pas na 'gyod pa bskyed par bya'o//
Thus wrongdoing will come to be regretted by understanding the terrible fears that result from it.

gsum pa bshad na/ sdig pa de yang dus phyis bshags pas chog gam snyam na/ mi chog ste myur du bshags dgos so/ / de ci'i phyir zhe na/ sdig pa ma byang ba'i 'og tu bdag 'chi dogs yod do/ / de ltar yang /
bdag ni sdig pa ma byang bar/ / sngon du 'gum par 'gyur du mchi/ / ji ltar 'di las nges thar bar/ / myur ba'i tshul gyis bskyab tu gsol/[493] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Third is remorse by realizing the urgent need for purification. If you think that it will probably be all right to rectify wrongdoings at some later time, realize that it will not be all right at all and that atonement is needed urgently. Why? Because there is a distinct possibility that death will come before wrongs have been purified. It says:
Before my wrongs are purified I may well come to die. Pray save me swiftly so that I am definitely released from my wrongdoings.[277]

d.div: [493] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 2_sh+loka_33_shog_5_na5
[277] Śāntideva, Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life (Bodhicaryāvatāra) 2:32, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 5a5.

f.d:
sdig pa ma byang bar bdag mi 'chi'o snyam na/ 'chi bdag gi bdud des bdag gi sdig pa byang ba dang mi byang ba'i tshis mi byed par/[494] glags rnyed kyis srog 'phrog pas nam 'chi nges pa med pa'o/[495] / de ltar yang /
yid brtan mi rung 'chi bdag 'dis/ / byas dang ma byas mi sdod pas/ / na dang mi na kun gyis kyang / / glo bur tshe la yid mi brtan/[496] / zhes gsungs so/ /

If you think that somehow you will not die before misdeeds have been purified, then consider this: the Lord of Death will not bother in the least about how many misdeeds have or have not been purified. He will steal life away whenever the opportunity presents itself; the time of death is uncertain. Thus it says:
It is wrong to feel so confident. My death will not wait for me to finish the things I have to do. As far as this ephemeral life is concerned, /127/ it matters not whether I am sick or healthy.[278]

d.div: [494] choms/ dpal spungs/
[495] glegs rnyed tshad kyi/ dpal spungs/
[496] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 2_sh+loka_34_shog_5_na5

f.d: des na tshe srog la blo ltos med de/[497] sdig pa ma byang bar 'chi dogs yod pas myur du sbyang dgos so/ / des na gyong kha de la thug pas na 'gyod par bya'o/ / de ltar rgyu mtshan gsum gyis sdig pa la 'gyod pa bskyed la/[498] yul khyad par can dang phal po che'i spyan sngar mthol zhing bshags par bgyi'o/ / de ltar rnam pa sun 'byin pa kun tu spyod pa'i stobs kyis sdig pa 'dag pa ni/ dper na kha drag po'i bu lon 'ong ba la ma 'khor nas zhu ba byas pa dang 'dra/[499] /zhes gsungs so/ /

Since those who do not realize the uncertainty of their lifespan are quite likely to die without having cleared up their misdeeds, all wrongs should be purified as quickly as possible. The risk is very real, so give rise to great remorse. When sincere remorse has been stimulated by the three contemplations described above, misdeeds should be admitted and purification requested in front of either the general or special sources of refuge. Thus, it has been taught, that the power of total repentance will purify misdeeds, just as a plea from someone who cannot afford to repay a debt to a rich man may persuade him to wipe out that debt.[279]

d.div: [497] med do/ dpal spungs/
[498] skyes/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[499] 'ong ba la 'jigs nas/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[279] In the Sage and Fool Sutra (Damamūkanāmasūtra), Toh 341 Kangyur, mdo sde, a, 253 b4.

f.d:
sngon mi gdung ba sor mo'i phreng ba can zhes bya ba mi dgu brgya dang dgu bcu rtsa dgu bsad pa'i mi sdig can zhig kyang / rnam par sun 'byin pa kun tu spyod pa'i stobs nyams su blangs pas/ sdig pa byang nas dgra bcom pa'i 'bras bu thob bo/[500] / de ltar yang /
gang zhig sngon chad bag med gyur pa la/ / phyi nas bag dang ldan par gyur de yang / / zla ba sprin bral lta bur rnam mdzes te/ / dga' bo sor phreng mthong ldan bde byed bzhin/[501] / zhes gsungs so/ /

There was once an evil person known as Aṅgulimāla. Even though he had committed grave misdeeds, killing 999 people, he managed to purify his evils and achieve the state of an arhat by practicing this power of the thorough application of total and utter remorse.[280] Thus, it is said:
Once someone who previously did not care later comes to learn to be heedful, he becomes beautified, like the moon breaking free from clouds, as was the case with Nanda, Aṅgulimāla, Ajātaśatru, and Udayana.[281]

d.div: [500] sde dge_341_bka'/ mdo sde/ a_mdzangs blun zhes bya ba'i mdo/ le'u/ 36_shog_253_ba4
[501] sde dge_4182_bstan/ spring yig_nge _mgon po klu sgrub/ bshes spring / sh+loka_14_shog_41_na7
[280] There are several versions of this well-known story. For a fuller account, see Gombrich’s “Who Was Aṅgulimāla?” in his How Buddhism Began (New Delhi: Munishiram Manoharlal, 2002), pp. 135ff.
[281] Nāgārjuna, Letter to a Friend (Suhṛllekha) verse 14, Toh 4182 Tengyur, spring yig, nge, 41a7. For more on Udayana, Nanda, and Ajātaśatru, see notes 293, 297, and 303 below.

f.d:
gnyen po kun tu spyod pa'i stobs ni/ sdig pa'i gnyen por dge ba spyod pa'o/ / des zag pa zad par byed de/[502] mngon pa kun las btus pa las kyang /
mi mthun pa'i phyogs kyi las ni/ gnyen po'i las stobs dang ldan par blta ste/ mi mthun pa'i phyogs kyi 'bras bu 'phangs su zin kyang / gnyen po'i stobs kyis gzhan du bsgyur ba'i phyir ro/[503] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Second [of the four powers] is the power of thoroughly applying the remedy. Virtuous actions are the remedy for misdeeds. They will consume impurities. Thus the Compendium of Higher Knowledge says:
Actions with remedial power will prevent corresponding misdeeds from coming to unwholesome fruition by transforming the consequence into something else.[282]

d.div: [502] sdig pa/ dpal spungs/
[503] sde dge_4049_bstan/ sems tsam/ ri_'phags pa thogs med/ mngon pa kun btus/ le'u/ 1_shog_19_ba4
[282] Asaṅga, Abhidharmasamuccaya chap. 1, Toh 4049 Tengyur, sems tsam, ri, 19b4.

f.d: de ltar yang de bzhin gshegs pa'i mdzod las ni/ stong pa nyid bsgoms pas sdig pa byang bar gsungs so/[504]/
In the Treasury of the Tathāgatas, it says that cultivating awareness of emptiness purifies misdeeds.[283]

d.div: [504] sde dge_3940_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_zhi ba lha/ bslab btus/ le'u/ 8_shog_96_na7_de bzhin gshegs pa mdzod kyi mdo bod skad du ma bzhugs pas bslab btus su drangs pa'i lung 'dir bkod/
[283] A Treasury of the Tathāgatas is not to be found in the Tibetan canon, but this quote appears in Śāntideva, Compendium of Trainings (Śikṣāsamuccaya), Toh 3940 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 96a7.
