f.d: rdo rje gcod pa las ni/ mdo sde zab mo bton pas sdig pa byang bar gsungs so/[505] /
In the Diamond Cutter Sutra, it says that misdeeds will be purified by reciting the profound scriptures.[284]

d.div: [505] sde dge_16_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_rdo rje gcod pa/ shog_226_ba7
[284] Kamalaśīla, Diamond Cutter Sutra Commentary, (Vajracchedikāṭīkā), Toh 3817 Kangyur, mdo ’grel, ma, 226b7.

f.d: dam tshig gsum bkod pa'i rgyal po dang / dpung bzang gis zhus pa'i mdo las ni/ gsang sngags kyi bzlas pa byas pas sdig pa byang bar gsungs so/[506] /
In the King for Establishing the Three Commitments Tantra and in Questions of Subāhu Tantra, it says that misdeeds will be purified by reciting mantras.[285]

d.div: [506] sde dge_805_bka'/ rgyud/ wa_dpung bzang gis zhus pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 5_shog_126_ba6
[285] Subāhuparipṛcchātantra, Toh 805 Kangyur, rgyud ’bum, wa, 126b6.

f.d: me tog brtsegs pa'i gzungs las ni/ de bzhin gshegs pa'i mchod rten la mchod pa byas pas sdig pa byang bar gsungs so/[507] / de bzhin gshegs pa'i sku gzugs kyi le'u las ni/ sku gzugs bzhengs pas sdig pa byang bar gsungs so/[508] /

In the Heap of Flowers Dhāraṇī, it says that faults are purified by making offerings to the stupas of the Buddha.[286] It also says, in the section on buddha images,[287] that making images of the Buddha will purify misdeeds.

d.div: [507] sde dge_886_bka'/ gzungs 'dus/ e_'phags pa me tog brtsegs pa zhes bya ba'i gzungs/ shog_160_ba2
[508] mdo lung 'di bka' 'gyur nas ma brnyed mod/ bslab btus su drangs/ sde dge_3940_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_rgyal sras chen po zhi ba lha/ bslab btus/ le'u/ 8_shog_97_na7
[286] Puṣpakūṭadhāraṇī, Toh 886 Kangyur, gzungs ’dus, e, 160b2.
[287] The chapter mentioned has not been identified, but this statement is found in Śāntideva’s Śikṣāsamuccaya, Toh 3940 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 97a7.

f.d: gzhan yang chos nyan pa dang / klog pa dang / bri ba la sogs pa dge ba'i las gang mos byed pa ste/ des sdig pa byang bar gsungs so/ /
Elsewhere it says that listening to teachings, reading or writing out the scriptures, and so forth— /128/ whichever one feels for the most—will also purify wrong actions.

de ltar yang 'dul ba lung las/
gang zhig sdig pa'i las byas pa/ / dge ba yis ni 'gog byed de/ / nyi zla sprin las byung ba bzhin/ / 'jig rten 'di der snang bar 'gyur/[509] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Basis of Vinaya says:
Whosoever has committed evil action but then annihilates it through virtue shines in this world like the sun or moon emerging from clouds.[288]

d.div: [509] sde dge_1_bka'/ 'dul ba/ ka_'dul ba gzhi/ shog_125_na2
[288] Vinayavastu, Toh 1 Kangyur, ’dul ba, ka, 125a2.

f.d:
'o na sdig pa'i gnyen por dge ba byed pa de yang sdig pa ji snyed byas pa de snyed kyi dge ba bya dgos sam zhe na/[510] ma yin te/ mya ngan 'das chen gyi mdo las/
dge ba gcig byas kyang sdig pa mang po 'joms te/[511] zhes dang /
rdo rje chung ngus ri rab bam/ me chung ngus rtswa shing ngam/ dug chung ngus sems can 'joms pa ltar/ dge ba chung ngus kyang sdig pa chen po 'joms pas na/ don du gnyer ba chen po nyid do/[512] / zhes gsungs so/ /

You may wonder, “If engaging in virtue is the antidote for evil, then do you have to do a quantity of good that is equivalent to the amount of bad previously done?” Not so. The Great [Passing into] Nirvana Sutra tells us:
Even a single virtuous act overcomes many evils.[289] And:
Just as a small vajra can destroy a mountain, a little fire can burn down a forest, or a minute amount of poison can kill beings, likewise a small beneficial action can overcome a great wrong. It is most efficacious![290]

d.div: [510] byas pa de nyid/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[511] sde dge_119_bka'/ mdo sde/ nya_yongs su mya ngan las 'das pa'i mdo+o/ le'u/ 7_bam po/ 26_shog_304_ba5
[512] gong mtshungs/ yongs su mya ngan las 'das pa chen pa'i mdo+o/ le'u/ 7_bam po/ 26_shog_305_ba5
[289] Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra (longer version), Toh 119 Kangyur, mdo sde, nya, 304b5.

f.d:
gser 'od dam pa'i mdo las kyang /
gang gis bskal pa stong rnams su/ / sdig pa shin tu mi bzad bgyis/ / lan gcig rab tu bshags pa yis/ / de dag thams cad byang bar 'gyur/[513] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Sutra of Golden Light explains:
Someone may have committed unbearable evils for a thousand ages, yet performing just one perfect purification will cleanse all their wrongs.[291]

d.div: [513] sde dge_555_bka'/ rgyud/ pa_gser 'od dam pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 4_shog_44_ba4
[291] Toh 555 Kangyur, rgyud, pa, 44b4.

f.d: de ltar gnyen po kun tu spyod pa'i stobs kyis sdig pa 'dag pa ni/ dper na ngan skyugs kyi 'dam rdzab tu chud pa'i gang zag gcig 'dam rdzab nas phyung nas khrus byas te bri bzang po byugs pa dang 'dra/[514] zhes gsungs so/ /

Thus it has been taught that misdeeds will be purified by the power of thoroughly applying remedies. It is like someone who has fallen into a putrid swamp and, once out of the swamp, bathes and is anointed with perfumed oils.[292]

d.div: [514] byung / dpal spungs/
[292] Sutra of Golden Light, Toh 555 Kangyur, rgyud, pa, 44b4.

f.d: sngon khye'u bde byed ces bya ba ma bsad pa'i sdig can zhig kyang gnyen po kun tu spyod pa'i stobs nyams su blangs pas sdig pa dag nas lhar skyes te/[515] 'phags pa rgyun zhugs kyi 'bras bu thob bo/ /

[For example] there was once a nobleman’s son called Udayana. Even though he had killed his own mother, he managed, through this power of thoroughly applying the remedy, to purify himself of his misdeeds. He was reborn as a god and obtained the Dharma result of a stream-enterer.[293]

d.div: [515] sde dge_1_bka'/ 'dul ba/ ka_'dul ba gzhi/ rab byung gi gzhi/ bam po / 10_shog_120_ba1

[293] Story from Basis of Vinaya (Vinayavastu) verse 14, Toh 1 Kangyur, ’dul ba, ka, 120b1. Udayana’s mother brought him up alone. To prevent his having an illicit liaison with a neighbor, she locked him in his room. Overcome by rage, he killed his mother. His overwhelming remorse eventually led him to become a Buddhist monk, though he was later expelled from the Sangha. By that time he had become very devout and learned. As a layman, he built and sponsored retreats for monks. At death he was reborn immediately in hell, but through his good deeds he swiftly migrated to the god realms, where he practiced well and progressed.

f.d:
de ltar yang /
gang zhig sngon chad bag med gyur pa las/ / phyis nas bag dang ldan par gyur de yang / / zla ba sprin bral lta bur rnam mdzes te/ / dga' bo sor phreng mthong ldan bde byed bzhin/[516] / zhes gsungs so//

[Thus, as already quoted:]
Once someone who previously did not care later comes to learn to be heedful, he becomes beautified, like the moon breaking free from clouds, as was the case with Nanda, Aṅgulimāla, Ajātaśatru, and Udayana.[294]

d.div: [516] sde dge_4182_bstan/ spring yig_nge _mgon po klu sgrub/ bshes spring / sh+loka_14_shog_41_na7
[294] Nāgārjuna, Letter to a Friend (Suhṛllekha), Toh 4182 Tengyur, spring yig, nge, 41a7.

f.d:
nyes pa las bzlog pa'i stobs ni/ rnam smin gyis 'jigs nas/ phyin chad sdig pa 'phro gcod de sdom pa'o/ / de ltar yang /
'dren pa rnams kyis bdag gi sdig / nongs pa lags par gzung du gsol/ / 'di ni bzang po ma lags pas/ / slan chad bdag ni yongs mi bgyid/[517] / ces gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

Third [of the four powers] is the power of renouncing harmful acts. In awe of the full consequences of karma, you desist from wrong henceforth, thinking,
Guides of humanity, please [help me] remove these evils I have committed. These misdeeds are indeed bad. Never will I do them again.[295]

d.div: [517] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 2_sh+loka_66_shog_6_ba3
[295] Śāntideva, Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life (Bodhicaryāvatāra) 2:65, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 6b3.

f.d: de ltar nyes pa las bzlog pa'i stobs kyis sdig pa 'dag pa ni/ dper na chu rgyun gnod pa can gyi 'ol bsgyur ba dang 'dra/ zhes gsungs so/ / sngon gcung dga' bo zhes bya ba bud med la chags pa'i sdig can zhig kyang nyes pa las zlog pa'i stobs nyams su blangs pas sdig pa dag nas dgra bcom pa'i 'bras bu thob bo/[518] /

Thus, it has been taught, that the power of renouncing evil will purify misdeeds, just as diverting a dangerous river removes the threat from a town.[296] [For example] once there was a person called Nanda who harbored much desire for women. Even though he had committed wrongs, through practicing this power of renouncing evil, his faults were purified /129/ and he attained the state of an arhat.[297]

d.div: [518] sde dge_57_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ga_dga' bo mngal na gnas pa bstan pa'i mdo/ shog_205_ba2
[296] Nanda’s Abiding in the Womb (Nandagarbhāvakrāntinirdeśa), Toh 57 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ga, 205b2.

[297] Nanda was the Buddha’s nephew and heir to a throne. He was enthralled with his wife’s beauty and talents and, more generally, was an extreme romantic. Even when he became a monk, his mind was constantly distracted by romantic thoughts and attachment. The Buddha took him to both heaven and hell, to show the future rebirths he would gain if he continued to think and act through passion and self-centeredness. Terrified by the prospect of his future, he deeply resolved to forsake his mind’s clinging. He eventually became an arhat. His story comprises one of the most celebrated works of Sanskrit literature: Aśvaghoṣa’s Saundarananda. See Linda Covill’s translation in Handsome Nanda (New York: New York University Press, 2007).

f.d:
de ltar yang /
gang zhig sngon chad bag med gyur pa las/ / phyis nas bag dang ldan par gyur de yang / / zla ba sprin bral lta bur rnam mdzes te/ / dga' bo sor phreng mthong ldan bde byed bzhin/[519] / zhes gsungs so//

[As already quoted:]
Once someone who previously did not care later comes to learn to be heedful, he becomes beautified, like the moon breaking free from clouds, as was the case with Nanda, Aṅgulimāla, Ajātaśatru, and Udayana.[298]

d.div: [519] sde dge_4182_bstan/ spring yig_nge _mgon po klu sgrub/ bshes spring / sh+loka_14_shog_41_na7
[298] Nāgārjuna, Letter to a Friend (Suhṛllekha) verse 14, Toh 4182 Tengyur, spring yig, nge, 41a7.

f.d:
rten gyi stobs ni/ dkon mchog gsum la skyabs su 'gro ba dang / byang chub mchog tu sems bskyed pa'o/ / de ltar yang dkon mchog la skyabs 'gro byas pas sdig pa 'dag pa ni/ phag mo'i rtogs pa brjod pa las/
gang dag sangs rgyas skyabs song ba/ / de dag ngan 'gror 'gro mi 'gyur/ / mi yi lus ni spangs nas su/ / de dag lha yi lus thob bo/[520] / zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs so/ /

Fourth [of the four powers] is the power of the support. This comes from taking refuge and developing bodhicitta. Seeking shelter in the three most precious refuges will purify misdeeds, as it says in the Story of the Sow:
Those who have taken refuge in the buddhas will not take birth in states of suffering. Having left their human bodies, they obtain celestial ones.[299]

d.div: [520] sde dge_345_bka'/ mdo sde/ aM_phag mo'i rtogs brjod/ shog_290_ba6

[299] Sūkarikāvadāna, Toh 345 Kangyur, mdo sde, aṃ, 290b6. In this story, a god who is nearing the end of his life is in agony, for he sees he is about to be reborn in the womb of a pig in the city of Rājagṛha. Śakra, king of the gods, comes upon him and encourages him to take refuge in Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. The god does so and is instead reborn in Tuṣita Paradise. See Rotman, Divine Stories, 325–28.

f.d:
mya ngan 'das chen gyi mdo las kyang /
dkon mchog gsum la skyabs song bas/ / 'jigs pa med pa thob par 'gyur/[521] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Great [Passing into] Nirvana Sutra says:
One who has sought refuge in the Three Jewels will attain fearlessness.[300]

d.div: [521] sde dge_119_bka'/ mdo sde/ nya_yongs su mya ngan las 'das pa chen pa'i mdo+o/ le'u/ 4_shog_120_na6
[300] Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra (longer version), Toh 119 Kangyur, mdo sde, nya, 120a6.

f.d:
byang chub mchog tu sems bskyed pas sdig pa 'dag pa ni/ 'phags pa sdong po bkod pa'i mdo las/
mi dge ba'i chos thams cad zad par byed pas sa'i 'og lta bu'o/ / nyes pa thams cad bsreg par byed pas bskal pa'i me lta bu'o/[522] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The development of bodhicitta will purify misdeeds. The Marvelous Array Sutra says:
It will put an end to all nonvirtuous actions, like burying them for good. It will burn up all evil, like the fire at the end of the eon.[301]

d.div: [522] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_sdong po bkod pa'i mdo/ shog_120_na6
[301] Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra, Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, a, 310a4 and 310a7.

f.d:
spyod 'jug las kyang /
sdig pa shin tu mi bzad byas na yang / / dpa' la brten nas 'jigs pa chen po ltar/ / gang la brten nas yud kyis sgrol 'gyur ba/ / de la bag can rnams kyis cis mi brten/[523] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life also tells us:
The support of someone strong and fearless can free us from fear. Likewise, if supported in this way we will be quickly liberated, even though we may have committed unbearable wrongs. How then could those who care not rely on such support?[302]

d.div: [523] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 1_sh+loka_13_shog_2_ba3
[302] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 1:13, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 2b3.

f.d: de ltar rten gyi stobs kyis sdig pa 'dag pa ni/ dper na (skyabs 'gro byas pa'i dpe/) kha nyen pos dbang po che la 'jus pa'am/ dug la (sems bskyed pa'i dpe/)sngags kyis btab pa dang 'dra/[524] zhes gsungs so/ / sngon rgyal bu mthong ldan zhes bya ba pha bsad pa'i sdig can zhig kyang rten gyi stobs nyams su blangs pas/ sdig pa dag nas byang chub sems dpar gyur to/[525] /

Thus the power of the support purifies faults. For example, the support of refuge could be compared, it has been stated, to that of a strong person helping weak followers. The support of bodhicitta development could be compared to the neutralization of a powerful poison by reciting the appropriate mantra. There was once a prince called Ajātaśatru who had committed the great evil of patricide.[303] Nevertheless he was purified through the power of support and became a bodhisattva.

d.div: [524] dper na kha nyes pos dbang po che la 'jus pa'am/ dug la sngags kyis btab pa dang 'dra/ dpal spungs/
[525] sde dge_119_bka'/ mdo sde/ ta_mya ngan las 'das pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 12_shog_199_ba4

[303] Ajātaśatru was monarch of a kingdom in central India. His father, Bimbisāra, was a patron of the Buddha and also a highly advanced Buddhist who had attained the state of stream-enterer. Ajātaśatru was drawn into several harmful actions by Devadatta, the Buddha’s jealous cousin. One of them was an assassination attempt on the Buddha. Another was the killing of Bimbisāra. Having committed two of the five “evils of no reprieve,” Ajātaśatru became covered with foul-smelling boils and was destined to go straight to hell at death. He sought refuge in the Buddha and managed to purify his misdeeds, mainly through the power of practicing bodhicitta. His story is in the longer Great Passing into Nirvana Sutra (Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra), Toh 119 Kangyur, mdo sde, ta, 199b4.

f.d:
de ltar yang /
gang zhig sngon chad bag med gyur pa las/ / phyis nas bag dang ldan par gyur de yang / / zla ba sprin bral lta bur rnam mdzes te/ / dga' bo sor phreng mthong ldan bde byed bzhin/[526] / zhes gsungs so/ /

[Thus, as quoted above:]
Once someone who previously did not care later comes to learn to be heedful, he becomes beautified, like the moon breaking free from clouds, as was the case with Nanda, Aṅgulimāla, Ajātaśatru, and Udayana.[304]

d.div: [526] sde dge_4182_bstan/ spring yig_nge _mgon po klu sgrub/ bshes spring / sh+loka_14_shog_41_na7
[304] Nāgārjuna, Letter to a Friend (Suhṛllekha) verse 14, Toh 4182 Tengyur, spring yig, nge, 41a7.

f.d:
de ltar stobs de dag re res kyang sdig pa 'dag par 'gyur na/ bzhi kas bshags na lta smos kyang ci dgos so/ / de ltar bshags pas sdig pa dag pa'i rtags rmi lam du yong ste/ skul byed kyi gzungs las/
rmi lam na zas ngan skyugs pa dang / zho dang 'o ma la sogs pa 'thung ba dang / nyi ma dang zla ba mthong ba dang / nam mkha' la 'gro ba dang / me 'bar ba dang / ma he dang / mi nag po thub pa dang / dge slong dang dge slong ma'i dge 'dun mthong ba dang / 'o ma 'byung ba'i shing dang / glang po dang / khyu mchog dang / ri dang seng ge'i khri dang / khang bzang gi steng du 'dzegs pa dang / chos nyan pa la sogs pa rmis na sdig pa dang bral bar 'gyur te/[527] zhes gsungs so/ /

Since each of the above four powers is capable of purifying misdeeds, there is no need even to mention how effective all four combined will be. In actual practice, those who do admit and repair their wrongs, in the ways explained above, experience signs of their purification in dreams. The Dhāraṇī of Encouragement explains:
Dreams of the following are signs of breaking free from fault: vomiting bad food, or drinking milk or yogurt or the like; /130/ seeing the sun and the moon; flying in the sky; seeing a blazing fire; seeing buffalo; seeing a dark, powerful person, or an assembly of monks or nuns; seeing a milk-producing tree; seeing elephants or mighty bulls; sitting on a mountain, a lion throne, or a mansion; listening to Dharma teachings; and so forth.[305]

d.div: [527] lung 'di bslab btus su drangs/ sde dge_3940_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_zhi ba lha/ bslab btus/ shog_97_na4
[305] Cited in Śāntideva, Śikṣāsamuccaya, Toh 3940, Tengyur, dbu ma khi, 97a4.

f.d: sdig pa bshags pa bshad zin to//
This concludes the explanation on confessing past wrongs.

dge ba la rjes su yi rang ba ni/ gzhan dag dus gsum gyis bsdus pa'i dge ba byed pa po thams cad kyi bsod nams la rjes su yi rang ba bsgom pa ste/ de yang
'das pa'i dus su phyogs thams cad du byon pa'i sangs rgyas dpag tu med pa/ bgrang ba las 'das pa/ bsam gyis mi khyab pa de dag thams cad kyis dang po byang chub mchog tu sems bskyed pa nas bzung ste tshogs rnam pa gnyis bsags shing / sgrib pa rnam gnyis sbyangs nas/ mngon par rdzogs par sangs ma rgyas kyi bar gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba gang lags pa dang / sangs rgyas nas kyang dam pa'i chos kyi 'khor lo bskor te/ gdul bya rnams smin par byas nas yongs su mya ngan las 'das kyi bar gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba gang lags pa dang / mya ngan las 'das nas kyang bstan pa ma zhig gi bar gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba gang lags pa dang / de dag gi bar skabs su byang chub sems dpa' ji snyed cig byon pa rnams kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba gang lags pa dang / 'phags pa rang sangs rgyas ji snyed cig byon pa rnams kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba gang lags pa dang / 'phags pa nyan thos ji snyed cig byon pa rnams kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba gang lags pa dang / so so skye bo rnams kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba bsags pa gang lags pa de dag thams cad la rjes su yi rang bar bgyi'osnyam du spro ba bsgom pa'o/ /

The third [of the six parts of the preparation] is rejoicing in virtue. This is about the need to cultivate a joyous appreciation of all the virtuous actions of sentient beings throughout the three times, thinking:
I delight in all the roots of virtue established by every one of the limitless, inconceivable enlightened beings who have appeared in the past, throughout the universe, from their first generating bodhicitta all the way through to their perfect awakening due to their amassing the two accumulations and purifying the two obscurations. I further delight in whatever roots of virtue have been produced subsequent to their enlightenment, from the time they turned the wheel of Dharma to bring to maturity those ready for instruction, until they manifested leaving the world of suffering. I also delight in the roots of virtue generated by their teachings between their parinirvāṇa and the eventual disappearance of their teaching, as well as in the virtue produced by whatever bodhisattvas have appeared in the interim before the manifestation of the following Buddha. I further delight in whatever roots of virtue have been produced by accomplished pratyekabuddhas and likewise in those of any śrāvakas who have appeared. Further, I delight in the roots of virtue generated by ordinary people. By contemplating joyfully in the above way, cultivate appreciation.
de bzhin du da ltar dang ma 'ongs pa'i de dag gi dge ba la yang de bzhin du sbyar la/ rjes su yi rang bsgom pa'o/ /

Likewise, nurture similar thoughts about virtuous actions being performed in the present moment and those that will be performed in the future. In each instance, the training is to cultivate joyous appreciation.

de ltar yang /
skyob pa rnams kyi byang chub dang / / rgyal sras sa la'ang yi rang ngo /[528] / zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs so/ /

As it is said:
I delight in the enlightenment of all the saviors, and in the levels of the conqueror’s heirs as well.[306]

d.div: [528] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 3_sh+loka_2_shog_6_ba5
[306] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 3:3, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 6b6.

f.d: rjes su yi rang ba bshad zin to/ /

chos kyi 'khor lo bskor bar bskul ba ni/ da ltar yang phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams na sangs rgyas dag_chos dkon mchog btsun par bya ba'i phyir ram/ gsol ba 'debs pa po'i bsod nams yongs su rdzogs par bya ba'i phyir chos mi gsung ba mang po yod do/ / de dag la dmigs pa chos gsung bar zhu ba 'bul ba'o/[529] /

The fourth [of the six parts of the preparation] is requesting that the wheel of Dharma be turned. Even at this moment in all the worlds of the ten directions, /131/ there are many buddhas not teaching Dharma. Addressing them mentally, offer requests to them to teach the Dharma.

d.div: [529] dmigs la/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d:
de ltar yang /
phyogs rnams kun gyi sangs rgyas la/ / thal mo sbyar te gsol ba ni/ / sems can sdug bsngal mun 'thoms la/ / chos kyi sgron me spar du gsol/[530] / zhes gsungs so//

Thus one reads:
With hands joined, I beseech the buddhas throughout the directions: Please light the torch of Dharma for all beings obscured in the darkness of suffering![307]

d.div: [530] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 3_sh+loka_4_shog_6_ba6

f.d:
mya ngan las mi 'da' bar gsol ba gdabs pa ni/ de ltar yang phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams na yang sangs rgyas dag_rtag par lta ba rnams sun dbyung ba'am/ le lo can rnams brtson 'grus bskyed pa'i phyir mya ngan las 'da' kha ma mang po yod de/ de dag la dmigs la mya ngan las mi 'da' bar gsol ba gdab pa'o/ / de ltar yang /
rgyal ba mya ngan 'da' bzhed la/ / thal mo sbyar te gsol ba ni/ / 'gro 'di ldongs par mi 'god phyir/ / bskal pa grangs med bzhugs par gsol/[531] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The fifth [of the six parts of the preparation] is supplicating the buddhas not to pass away from the suffering worlds. At present there are buddhas in the worlds of the ten directions who are at the point of entering into ultimate nirvana in order to stimulate those who believe in permanence to abandon their misconceptions and to inspire to diligence those who are wasting their time. With these buddhas in mind, supplication is made to them not to pass beyond the suffering worlds:
I pray with joined hands to those victors who are considering passing beyond to nirvana to remain for countless ages, so as not to leave all their beings in obscurity.[308]

d.div: [531] gong mtshungs/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 3_sh+loka_5_shog_6_ba6

f.d: bskul zhing gsol ba gdab pa bshad zin to//

dge ba'i rtsa ba bsngo ba ni/ sngar byas kyi dge ba'i rtsa ba de dag thams cad sems can thams cad kyi sdug bsngal bsal zhing bde ba sgrub pa'i rgyur gyur cig par bsngo ba'o/ / de ltar yang /
de ltar 'di dag kun byas te/ / dge ba bdag gis bsags pa gang / / des ni sems can thams cad kyi/ / sdug bsngal thams cad bsal bar shog[532] / ces pa la sogs pa gsungs so//

The sixth [and last part of the preparation] is dedicating the roots of virtue. All these previous roots of virtue are dedicated to removing the sufferings of all beings, and as a cause for their achieving happiness:
Having thus engaged in all such deeds, whatever virtues I may have gathered, May this help clear away the sufferings of all beings.[309]

d.div: [532] gong mtshungs/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 3_sh+loka_6_shog_6_ba7

f.d: de ltar bsngo ba bya ste/ de yan chad kyis sbyor ba'i cho ga bshad zin to/ /
This and what precedes it conclude the explanation of the preparatory stage of the bodhisattva vow ceremony.
[The actual ceremony for generating bodhicitta]

dngos gzhi'i cho ga ni/ dam bca' tshig tu brjod pa ste/ de ltar yang bslab btus nas gsungs pa ltar/ rje btsun 'jam dpal sngon rgyal po nam mkha' zhes bya ba gyur pa na/ sangs rgyas 'brug sgra'i dbyangs kyi rgyal po'i spyan sngar sems bskyed dang sdom pa stabs cig tu mnos pa bzhin du/ bdag cag gis kyang stabs cig tu nod par bya ste/ ji skad du/
'khor ba thog ma med pa yi/ / sngon gyi tha ma ji srid pa/ / de srid sems can phan don du/ / spyod pa dpag yas spyad par bgyi/ / 'jig rten mgon po'i spyan snga 'dir/ / byang chub mchog tu sems bskyed do/[533] / zhes pa la sogs pa lan gsum brjod pa'o/ /

The actual ceremony consists of uttering the pledge in words. As stated in in the Compendium of Trainings, just as when Ārya Mañjuśrī was King Amba he took the prātimokṣa and bodhisattva vows together from Buddha Megharava, likewise we too should receive [the two] simultaneously. Then recite such as the following three times:
For as long as this samsara without beginning endures, so long I will engage in limitless deeds to benefit all other beings. /132/ Before the Buddha, protector of the world, I generate the mind for supreme enlightenment.[310]

d.div: [533] sde dge_59_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ga_yon tan bkod pa'i mdo/ bam po/ 3_shog_278_ba6
[310] From the Sutra Describing the Qualities of the Buddhafield of Mañjuśrī (Mañjuśrībuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhasūtra), Toh 59 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ga, 279a7.

f.d:
yang na byang chub spyod 'jug nas gsungs pa ltar mdor bsdus pa'i tshig gis nod par bya ste/ ji skad du/
ji ltar sngon gyi bde gshegs kyis/ / byang chub thugs ni bskyed pa dang / / byang chub sems dpa'i bslab pa la/ / de dag rim bzhin gnas pa ltar/ / de bzhin 'gro la phan don du/ / byang chub sems ni bskyed bgyi zhing / / de bzhin du ni bslab pa la'ang / / rim pa bzhin du bslab par bgyi'o/[534] / zhes lan gsum brjod pa'o/ /

Alternatively, one could receive on the basis of a more consdensed formula, such as the following from the Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life:
Just as the sugatas of the past cultivated their minds toward supreme enlightenment and worked stage by stage through the bodhisattva training, so also will I, in order to benefit sentient beings, cultivate my mind toward enlightenment, and train stage by stage in the relevant disciplines.[311] This is repeated three times.

d.div: [534] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 3_sh+loka_22_shog_7_ba2
[311] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 3:23–24, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 7b2.

f.d: gal te sems bskyed dang sdom pa bzung ba gnyis so sor len par 'dod na/ gang len pa'i tshig de brjod pas blang ngo / /
Should someone wish to receive the bodhicitta and bodhisattva vows separately, the words relevant to whichever aspect is to be adopted should be recited.
dngos gzhi'i cho ga bshad zin to//
This concludes the actual ceremony.
[Conclusion of the ceremony]

rjes kyi cho ga ni/ dkon mchog la gtang rag gi mchod pa phul la/ don chen po'i bsam pas dga' ba dang spro ba rgya chen po bsgom par bya'o/ / de ltar yang /
de ltar blo dang ldan pa yis// rab dang byang chub sems bzung nas/ / mjug kyang rgyal par bya ba'i phyir/ / sems ni 'di ltar gzengs bstod do/[535] / zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs so/ /

As a conclusion of the ceremony, make offerings of thanksgiving to the most precious refuges and cultivate great joy and delight on the basis of contemplating the great purpose [of bringing about other’s welfare]. So one reads:
The wise, having seized with a clear confidence, the mind for enlightenment to be victorious at the conclusion as well, should uplift their minds in the following manner.[312] This and more is said.

d.div: [535] gong mtshungs/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 3_sh+loka_24_shog_7_ba3
[312] Ibid. 3:24, 7b3. The last line here varies in some canonical editions.

f.d: de ltar sbyor dngos rjes gsum gyis slob dpon zhi ba lha'i lugs bshad zin to//
This concludes the explanations on the preparation, actual ceremony, and conclusion for taking the bodhisattva commitment according to the tradition of Dharma Master Śāntideva.

'phags pa byams pa nas slob dpon thogs med na mar brgyud pa'i/ jo bo gser gling pa'i lugs ltar na gnyis te/ smon pa'i sems bskyed pa dang / 'jug pa'i sdom pa gzung ba'o/[536] / dang po la gsum ste/ sbyor ba dang / dngos gzhi dang / /rjes so/ /

According to this system of lineage, passed down from Ārya Maitreya to Dharma Master Asaṅga, there are two parts: generating the aspiring bodhicitta, and upholding to the engaged bodhicitta vow. The first has three parts: the preparation, the actual ceremony, and its conclusion.

d.div: [536] bzung / dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: sbyor ba la gsum ste/ gsol ba gdab pa dang / tshogs bsags pa dang / skyabs 'gro khyad par can bya ba'o/ /
First, the preparation also has three parts: supplication, establishing the accumulations, and taking the special form of refuge.

de la dang po ni/ sems bskyed par 'dod pa'i slob ma des/ dge ba'i bshes gnyen mtshan nyid dang ldan pa'i spyan sngar phyin la phyag bya'o/ / dge ba'i bshes gnyen des kyang slob ma de la gdams ngag byas la de 'khor ba la skyo ba bskyed/ sems can la snying rje bskyed/[537] sangs rgyas la 'dod pa bskyed/ dkon mchog la dad pa bskyed/ bla ma la gus pa bskyed par bya'o/ /

For the first, supplication, the person wishing to dedicate him or herself to enlightenment should go to a properly qualified spiritual mentor and pay homage. That spiritual mentor too, having given some instruction, helps engender revulsion for samsara in the supplicant, compassion for sentient beings, aspiration for enlightenment, faith in the Three Jewels, and respect for one’s gurus. /133/

d.div: [537] skye/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d:
de nas slob ma des slob dpon gyi rjes su 'di skad du/
slob dpon dgongs su gsol/ ji ltar sngon gyi de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das rnams dang / sa chen po la rab tu bzhugs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyis/ dang por bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub chen por thugs bskyed pa de bzhin du/ bdag ming 'di zhes bgyi ba yang / slob dpon gyis bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub chen por sems bskyed par mdzad du gsol/ / zhes lan gsum brjod do//

Next, repeating after the preceptor, the student recites:
Preceptor, pray attend to me. Just as the tathāgatas, defeaters of the enemy, the utterly pure and perfectly enlightened ones, the blessed ones of the past first raised an essential longing for the highest, utterly pure and perfect highest enlightenment—as did the bodhisattvas who are now actually established in the bodhisattva levels—so also I, [such-and-such] by name, pray to you, the teacher, to awaken in me the essential force for unsurpassable, utterly pure and perfect, highest enlightenment. Recite this three times.

gnyis pa tshogs bsags pa ni/ dang por bla ma dkon mchog la phyag bya'o/ / de nas dngos su bshams pa'i mchod pa dang / mchod pa 'byor tshad du blos sprul pa la sogs pa 'bul lo/ / de yang dge tshul gyi sdom pa ni mkhan slob las thob/ dge slong gi sdom pa ni dge 'dun las thob/ byang chub kyi sems rnam pa gnyis ni/ bsod nams kyi tshogs bsags pa las thob pa yin gsungs/[538] de ltar yang rang la 'byor ba che bar yod na dngos su chung bas mi 'ong ste/ che bar btang dgos pa yin no/ / sngon gyi byang chub sems dpa' 'byor ba che ba rnams kyis kyang cher btang ste/ gtsug lag khang bye ba tsam phul nas sems bskyed pa yang yod do/ /

For [the second,] establishing the accumulations, the supplicant first prostrates to the rare and precious refuges and to the preceptor. Then material offerings prepared for the occasion are offered, along with any amount of visualized and other offerings. It is taught that the novice vow is received from an abbot (upādhyāya) together with a preceptor (ācārya), that the full vow is received from the Sangha, and that the two types of bodhicitta are attained through the accumulation of merit. It would be inappropriate for wealthy people to make meager offerings; they should offer on a grand scale. Extremely wealthy bodhisattvas of the past made such vast offerings. Some even, when they gave rise to bodhicitta, took their vow making offerings as extensive as ten million monastic residences (vihāra).

d.div: [538] gsung / dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d:
de ltar yang bskal pa bzang po'i mdo las/
bde gshegs grags sbyin 'dzam gling rgyal po'i tshe/ / de bzhin gshegs pa zla ba'i tog de la/ / gtsug lag khang ni bye ba phul nas kyang / / dang por byang chub tu ni sems bskyed do/[539]/zhes gsungs so/ /

The Good Eon Sutra[313] tells us:
Sugata Yaśodatta first gave rise to bodhicitta when, as king of Jambudvīpa, he offered of ten million monastic residences to Tathāgata Śaśiketu.[314]

d.div: [539] sde dge_94_bka'/ mdo sde/ ka_mdo sde bskal bzang / le'u/ 2_shog_316_ba5
[313] The following readings of the Bhadrakalpikasūtra owe a particular debt to Peter Skilling for his careful analysis and suggestions.
[314] Bhadrakalpikasūtra, Toh 94 Kangyur, mdo sde, ka, 316b5.

f.d:
yang 'byor ba chung na dngos po nyung zad tsam cig phul bas chog pa yin no/ / sngon gyi byang chub sems dpa' 'byor pa chung ba rnams kyis dngos po cung zad tsam btang ba yin te/ rtswa nyag ma gcig gi sgron me phul nas sems bskyed pa yod do/ / de ltar yang /
bde gshegs 'od 'phro grong khyer rten pa'i tshe/ / de bzhin gshegs pa mtha' yas 'od de la/ / rtsa yi sgron me dag ni phul nas kyang / / dang por byang chub tu ni sems bskyed do/[540] / zhes gsungs so/ /

However, it suffices for someone who is not rich to make only modest offerings. In the past, poor bodhisattvas made very simple gifts; some even gave rise to bodhicitta offering the light of a burning twist of straw.
Sugata Arciṣmant first gave rise to bodhicitta when, as a poor city dweller, he offered grass “candles” to Tathāgata Anantaprabha.[315]

d.div: [540] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde bskal bzang / le'u/ 2_shog_289_na4

f.d:
yang 'byor ba med par gyur na thabs chag mi dgos te/ phyag lan gsum 'tshal ba tsam gyis kyang chog go / sngon gyi byang chub sems dpa' 'byor ba med pa dag gis kyang thal mo lan gsum sbyar nas sems bskyed pa yang yod do/ / de ltar yang /
de bzhin gshegs pa yon tan phreng ldan gyis/ / de bzhin gshegs pa bsgyings ldan bzhud de la/ / sangs rgyas phyag 'tshal thal mo lan gsum sbyar/ / dang por byang chub tu ni sems bskyed do/[541] / zhes gsungs so/ /

For one who possesses nothing at all, it suffices to make three prostrations. In the past there were certain bodhisattvas who had nothing and who awakened their bodhicitta joining their hands in homage three times: /134/
Tathāgata Guṇamālin first gave rise to bodhicitta when he joined his hands in homage and three times said “Praise to the Awakened One” to Tathāgata Vijṛmbhitagāmī.[316]

d.div: [541] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde bskal bzang / le'u/ 3_shog_296_na6
[316] Ibid., 296a6. The Sanskrit Vijṛmbhitagāmī for bsgyings ldan bzhud is speculative.

f.d: gsum pa skyabs 'gro khyad par can ni/[542] gong du bshad pa bzhin 'dir bya'o/ /
The third, taking the special form of refuge, is to be done as explained in the previous chapter.

d.div: [542] can bya ba ni/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d:
dngos gzhi la/ slob dpon gyis slob ma la gdams ngag 'di ltar bya ste/
spyir nam mkha'i khams kyis gar khyab na/ sems can gyis khyab nas yod pa yin/ sems can gyis gar khyab na nyon mongs kyis khyab nas yod pa yin/ nyon mongs kyi gar khyab na las ngan gyis khyab nas yod pa yin/ las ngan gyis gar khyab na sdug bsngal gyis khyab nas yod pa yin/ sdug bsngal can gyi sems can de dag thams cad bdag gi pha ma sha stag yin/ pha ma thams cad drin can kho na yin/ des na bdag gi pha ma drin can 'di rnams 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho chen por ni bying / sdug bsngal dpag tu med pas ni gzir/ mgon skyabs byed mkhan ni med/ shin tu 'o re brgyal/ nyon re mongs/ 'di rnams bde ba dang phrad na ci ma rung na/ sdug bsngal dang bral na ci ma rung na snyam du byams snying rje dar gcig sems su gzhug go / de nas yang da lta bdag gis 'di rnams kyi don bya bar mi nus pas/ da 'di rnams kyi don bya ba'i ched du yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas zhes bya ba/ nyes pa thams cad zad pa/ yon tan thams cad rdzogs pa/ 'gro ba mtha' dag gi don bya bar nus pa/ de bdag gis thob par bya'o snyam du sems su gzhug go /

For the actual ceremony, the preceptor should instruct the student as follows and help him contemplate thus:
Wherever there is space, there are sentient beings. Wherever there are beings, there are afflictions. Wherever there are afflictions, there is harmful karma, and whenever there is harmful karma, there will be suffering. All those beings beset by suffering are actually our parents; all our parents have been exceedingly kind to us. All those former parents who were so kind in the past are presently plunged into this powerful ocean of samsara, enduring immeasurable sufferings. With no one to protect them and be their refuge, they undergo terrible hardships and great pain. Thinking, “Oh, if only they could find happiness; if only they could get free from suffering,” rest your mind in loving kindness and compassion for a while. Now think, “At present, I have no power to help these beings. Therefore, to be able to come to their aid, I will achieve what is known as pure and perfect enlightenment—the ending of all that is wrong, the perfection of every quality, the power to accomplish the benefit of all beings, however many they may be.” Rest your mind in these thoughts for a while.

de nas slob ma des slob dpon gyi rjes su 'di skad du/
phyogs bcu na bzhugs pa'i sangs rgyas dang / byang chub sems dpa' thams cad bdag la dgongs su gsol/ slob dpon bdag la dgongs su gsol/ bdag ming 'di zhes bgyi ba skye ba 'di dang skye ba gzhan dag tu sbyin pa las byung ba dang / tshul khrims las byung ba dang / sgom pa las byung ba'i dge ba'i rtsa ba bgyis pa dang / bgyid du stsal ba dang / bgyis pa la rjes su yi rang ba des/ ji ltar sngon gyi de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das rnams dang / sa chen po la rab tu bzhugs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po rnams kyis/ dang por bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub chen por thugs bskyed pa de bzhin du/ bdag ming 'di zhes bgyi bas kyang / dus 'di nas bzung ste/ ji srid byang chub snying po la mchis kyi bar du/ sems can ma bsgral ba rnams bsgral ba dang / ma grol ba rnams dgrol ba dang / dbugs ma phyin pa rnams dbugs dbyung ba dang / yongs su mya ngan las ma 'das pa rnams yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba'i slad du/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub chen por sems bskyed par bgyi'o/ / zhes lan gsum brjod pas blangs bar 'gyur ro/ /

Then, repeating after the preceptor, the supplicant should recite the following formula three times:
All buddhas and bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions, pray heed me. I, [such-and-such] by name, do now—by the power of the roots of virtue that I gathered in former lives through the practice of generosity, moral discipline, and meditation, through the roots of virtue that I have encouraged others to establish, and through those that I have joyously appreciated—take the commitment to reach unsurpassable, pure, and perfect enlightenment, in the same way as in the past the tathāgatas, the victorious ones, the pure and perfect buddhas, the perfectly gifted and liberated victors first took the commitment to reach pure and perfect great enlightenment, /135/ and as did those bodhisattvas of the bodhisattva levels. Like them, I, [such-and-such] by name, will, from this moment until I reach the essence of enlightenment, awaken the force of unsurpassable, pure, and perfect highest enlightenment in order to rescue beings who are to be carried over, liberate those who are not free, let release their breath those who have not let out their breath, and take completely beyond suffering those who have not yet completely gone beyond it. Through repeating these words after the teacher, the vow is taken.

de yang sems can ma brgal ba rnams zhes pa ni/ dmyal ba yi dwags dud 'gro rnams te ngan song gi sdug bsngal rgya mtsho lta bu las ma brgal ba'i phyir ro/ / bsgral ba zhes pa ni/ de dag mngon mtho'i lam la bkod nas ngan song gi sdug bsngal las bsgral te/ lha mo'i go 'phang thob par bya ba'o/ / ma grol ba rnams zhes pa ni/ lha dang mi'i 'gro ba rnams te/ nyon mongs pa'i 'ching ba lcags sgrog lta bu las ma grol ba'i phyir ro/ / grol ba zhes pa ni/[543] de dag nges legs kyi lam la bkod nas nyon mongs pa'i 'ching ba las grol te thar pa'i go 'phang thob par bya ba'o/ / dbugs ma phyin pa zhes pa ni/ nyan thos dang / rang sangs rgyas rnams te theg pa chen por dbugs ma phyin pa'i phyir ro/ / dbugs dbyung ba dang zhes pa ni/ de dag byang chub mchog tu sems bskyed nas theg pa chen po'i lta spyod du dbugs phyung ste sa bcu go 'phang thob par bya ba'o/[544] / yongs su mya ngan las ma 'das pa zhes pa ni/[545] byang chub sems dpa' rnams te mi gnas pa'i mya ngan las 'das pa ma thob pa'i phyir ro/ / yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba zhes pa ni/ de dag sa lam rnams la rim par bkod nas yongs su mya ngan las 'da' ba ste sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang thob par bya ba'o/ / slad du zhes pa ni/ dgos ched kyi don de rnams grub par bya ba'i phyir sangs rgya bar dam bca' ba'o//

The meaning of these words is as follows: Those “who are to be carried over” are hell beings, hungry spirits, and animals, since they have yet to cross the ocean-like sufferings of samsara. “To rescue” them means to free them from the sufferings of the three lower states and establish them in the higher states so that they can continue in human or divine existences. “Those who are not free” are the humans and gods, since they are not yet free from the bondage of the afflictions, which are like shackles. “To liberate” means to help free them from the bondage of the afflictions by setting them on the path of liberation so that they can attain liberation. “Those who have not yet let out their breath” are the śrāvakas and the pratyekabuddhas, because they have not yet relaxed into the Mahayana path. “Those who have not yet gone completely beyond suffering” are the bodhisattvas, because they have yet to achieve the nirvana that is rooted in neither samsara nor peace. “In order to” is the commitment to achieve buddhahood in order to be able to accomplish all the above aims.

d.div: [543] dpal spungs dang mi rigs dpe skrun dpar mar dgrol zhes da sngon 'jug 'og tu'ang byung /
[544] bcu'i/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[545] 'das pa rnams/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: rjes ni don chen po grub pa'i bsam pas dga' ba dang / spro ba rgya chen po yang bsgom du gzhug / bslab bya rnams kyang brjod do/ /

As for the conclusion, make the students generate great joy and delight on the basis of thinking that a tremendous and useful thing has just been achieved. The preceptor should also pronounce the precepts as well.

de ltar sems bskyed pa de ni byang chub sems dpa' zhes bya ste/ sems can gyi ched du byang chub 'dod pa dang / byang chub thob nas sems can bsgral bar 'dod pa dang / byang chub dang sems can la dmigs pa dang / de dag gi don du dpa' zhing snying stobs ldan par mthong ba'o/[546] /

Someone who has thus developed the initial commitment of bodhicitta is called a bodhisattva, /136/ because they have the wish to achieve enlightenment for the sake of other sentient beings, because they focus on enlightenment as well as the sentient beings, and because they remain heroic for the sake [of beings] and are endowed with courageous determination.

d.div: [546] snying stobs lhag par mtho ba'o/ dpal spungs/

f.d: smon pa byang chub mchog tu sems bskyed pa'i cho ga bshad zin to//
This concludes the traditional ceremony for giving rise to the aspiration for supreme enlightenment.
[Taking the vow of engaged bodhicitta]
'jug pa'i sdom pa gzung ba la yang gsum ste/ sbyor ba dang / dngos gzhi dang / rjes so//
Taking the vow of engaged bodhicitta too has three three parts: preparation, actual ceremony, and conclusion.

dang po la bcu ste/ gsol ba gdab pa dang / bar chad thun mong ba dri ba dang / ltung ba'i lci yang brjod pa dang / nyams pa'i nyes dmigs dang / blangs pa'i phan yon dang / tshogs bsags pa dang / bar chad thun mong ma yin pa dri ba dang / bskul ba dang / bsam pa khyad par can bskyed pa dang / bslab pa mdor brjod pa'o/ /

First is the preparation. It is in ten parts, in which the preceptor: (1) [leads with the formal] supplication, (2) enquires about any general obstacles there may be to taking it, (3) explains the gravity of breaking the commitment, (4) [outlines] the harmful consequences of letting it degrade, (5) [outlines] the benefits of adopting it, (6) [helps the supplicant] establish the accumulations, (7) inquires about any specific obstacles, (8) encourages the supplicant, (9) inspires a special motivation in the supplicant, and (10) gives some summarized instruction.

dngos gzhi ni/ slob mas sdom pa len pa'i sems bskyed la/ slob dpon gyis
rigs kyi bu ming 'di zhes bya ba khyod/ bdag byang chub sems dpa' ming 'di zhes bya ba las/ 'das pa'i byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi bslab pa'i gzhi gang dag dang / tshul khrims gang dag dang / ma 'ongs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi bslab pa'i gzhi gang dag dang / tshul khrims gang dag dang / da lta phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams na bzhugs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi bslab pa'i gzhi gang dag dang / tshul khrims gang dag la/ 'das pa'i byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyis bslabs par gyur pa dang /[547] ma 'ongs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' thams cad slob par 'gyur ba dang / da ltar phyogs bcu'i 'jig rten gyi khams thams cad na bzhugs pa'i byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyi bslab pa'i gzhi thams cad dang / byang chub sems dpa'i tshul khrims thams cad de sdom pa'i tshul khrims dang / dge ba'i chos sdud pa'i tshul khrims dang / sems can gyi don bya ba'i tshul khrims len par 'dod dam/ zhes lan gsum dris la/ slob mas kyang 'tshal lags/ zhes lan gsum brjod do/ /

Second, with respect to the actual ceremony, the student should generate the intention to take the vow. Then, the preceptor says:
Child of good family, known as [such-and-such], do you wish to receive from me, bodhisattva [such-and-such], the following commitments to follow whatever was the basis of training and moral discipline of all the bodhisattvas of the past, to follow whatever will be the basis of training and moral discipline of all the bodhisattvas of the future, and to follow whatever is the basis of training and moral discipline of all the bodhisattvas presently throughout the universe in the ten directions? Such moral discipline was what the bodhisattvas of the past trained, is what the bodhisattvas of the future will train, and remains what the bodhisattvas in throughout the universe in the ten directions at present are training. That basis of training and way of right action are all founded in the moral discipline of restraint, the moral discipline of accumulating virtue, and the moral discipline of working for the welfare of sentient beings. Do you wish to receive these from me?[317] This is asked three times of the supplicant, who assents “Yes, I do” each time.

d.div: [547] bslab/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

[317] This entire passage of the actual ceremony of conferring the bodhisattva vows is from the moral discipline chapter of Asaṅga’s Bodhisattva Levels (Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 83a4). For an alternative translation, see Mark Tatz, Asaṅga’s Chapter on Ethics, 61.

f.d: rjes la chos drug ste/ mkhyen par gsol ba dang / ye shes gzigs par 'jug pa'i phan yon dang / sdom pa gya tshoms su mi bsgrag pa dang /[548] bslab pa mdor bsdus nas go bar bya ba dang / bka' drin dran pa'i mchod pa dang / dge ba'i rtsa ba bsngo ba'o/ /

Third, the conclusion [of the ceremony] has six parts. (1) The supplicant requests the preceptor’s kind attention, (2) the preceptor gives an explanation of the benefits of gaining insight into pristine awareness, /137/ (3) he explains the importance of not speaking about the vows to others casually for no reason, (4) he gives a summary instruction to help understand the precepts, (5) the supplicant makes offerings in recognition of the [preceptor’s] kindness, and (6) he dedicates the roots of virtue.

d.div: [548] sgrag_dpal spungs/

f.d: 'jug pa'i sdom pa bzung bshad zin to/ /
de dag gis jo bo gser gling pa'i lugs bshad pa'o//
This concludes the explanation of the tradition of the illustrious Serlingpa.

d.i: Eighth topic: The benefits of bodhicitta

f.d: byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i phan yon gnyis te/ grangs su chad pa dang / grangs ma chad pa'o/[549] /
The eighth point concerns the benefits of developing bodhicitta. These are of two types: enumerated and unenumerated.

d.div: [549] grangs su/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: dang po la gnyis te/ smon pa'i sems bskyed pa'i phan yon dang / 'jug pa'i sems bskyed pa'i phan yon no/ / dang po la brgyad de/ theg pa chen por chud par 'gyur ba dang / byang chub sems dpa'i bslab pa thams cad kyi rten du 'gyur ba dang / sdig pa thams cad rtsad nas gcod par 'gyur ba dang / bla na med pa'i byang chub kyi rtsa ba tshugs par 'gyur ba dang / bsod nams dpag tu med pa thob par 'gyur ba dang / sangs rgyas thams cad mnyes par 'gyur ba dang / sems can thams cad la phan par 'gyur ba dang / myur du mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ba'o/ /

First, the enumerated benefits are themselves of two types: those arising from aspiration bodhicitta, and those arising from engaged bodhicitta. The first [those arising from aspiration bodhicitta] are eightfold: (1) You enter the Mahayana, (2) it serves as the basis for all the other aspects of bodhisattva training, (3) it helps you eradicate all evils, (4) it helps you plant the root of unsurpassable enlightenment, (5) it helps you gain unsurpassable merit, (6) all the buddhas are pleased, (7) all beings are benefitted, and (8) perfect buddhahood is swiftly attained.

de la dang po bshad na/ gang la byang chub mchog gi sems cig ma skyes na/[550] / de ltar spyod pa phun sum tshogs pa dang ldan yang theg pa chen po'i khongs su mi tshud la/ theg pa chen por ma tshud na rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas mi thob bo/ / gang la byang chub mchog gi sems bskyed pa dang theg pa chen po par tshud pa yin no/ / byang sa las kyang /
sems de bskyed ma thag tu bla na med pa'i byang chub theg pa chen po la zhugs pa yin te/[551] zhes gsungs so//

The first of these points is explained as follows. People’s conduct may be the very best possible, but if they have not given birth to bodhicitta, then they have not yet entered the Mahayana. Without entering the Mahayana, buddhahood cannot be attained. A person who has awakened the bodhisattva mind becomes a Mahayanist. Thus it says in Bodhisattva Levels:
As soon as one has generated this mind, one has entered the Great Vehicle to unsurpassable enlightenment.[318]

d.div: [550] gcig_dpal spungs/ zhig_mi rigs dpe skrun/
[551] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 1_shog_7_ba6
[318] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 7b6.

f.d: gnyis pa'i don bshad na/ smon pa'i sems zhes bya ba sangs rgyas thob par 'dod pa'i blo med na/ byang chub sems dpa'i bslab pa zhes bya ba tshul khrims gsum po skye ba'am gnas pa'i don med la/ sangs rgyas thob par 'dod pa'i blo de yod na tshul khrims gsum po de skye zhing gnas pa yin pas sems de bslab pa'i rten yin no/ /

The second point is explained as follows. If you do not have aspiration bodhicitta—the longing to achieve enlightenment—you cannot generate and sustain the bodhisattva’s training consisting of the threefold moral discipline. However, if you do so aspire, you lay the very foundation for what is achieved by first adopting the threefold moral discipline and then training in it.

byang sa las kyang /
sems bskyed pa de ni byang chub sems dpa'i bslab pa rnams kyi rten yin te/[552] zhes gsungs so/ /

Bodhisattva Levels says:
Giving rise to this attitude is the basis for all the bodhisattvas’ training.[319]

d.div: [552] gong mtshungs/ 'phags pa thogs med/ byang chub sems dpa'i sa/ le'u/ 1_shog_8_na3

f.d:
gsum pa'i don bshad na/ sdig pa'i gnyen po dge ba yin la/ dge ba'i nang nas mchog tu gyur pa byang chub kyi sems yin te/ des na gnyen po skyes na mi mthun pa'i phyogs zad par gyur pa chos nyid yin no/[553] / de ltar yang /
des ni dus mtha'i mes bzhin sdig chen rnams/ / skad cig gcig gis nges par bsreg par byed/[554] / ces gsungs so/ /

The third point is that virtue is the remedy for former wrongs. The best of all virtues is the bodhisattva mind. By bringing this remedy into play, all adverse factors will be annihilated. Thus one reads: /138/
Blazing like the fire at the age’s end, instantly it will definitely burn away the great wrongs.[320]

d.div: [553] 'gyur pa/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[554] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 1_sh+loka_14_shog_2_ba4

[320] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 1:14ab, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 2b4. Some Buddhist texts describe the end of our universe through destruction by various waves of elements, including seven successive burnings. This is the disintegration of the fire element, i.e., the release of its remaining latent energy.

f.d:
bzhi pa'i don bshad na/ sems can gyi rgyud sa gzhi lta bu la byams snying rje'i rlan dang 'brel zhing / byang chub kyi sems rtsa ba lta bu 'di tshugs na/ byang chub kyi phyogs kyi chos sum cu rtsa bdun gyi yal 'dab rgyas shing / rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi 'bras bu smin nas sems can gyi phan bde 'byung ba yin te/ des na byang sems 'di skyes na sangs rgyas kyi rtsa ba tshugs pa yin no/ / byang sa las kyang /
sems bskyed pa de ni bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub kyi rtsa ba yin no/[555] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The fourth point is that when the moisture of loving kindness and compassion saturates the ground that is the mind of a being, into which the root—the mind set on enlightenment—has been well and firmly planted, then the branches full of leaves—the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening—are developed. Once the fruit—perfect buddhahood—has ripened, great benefit and happiness will arise from it for all beings. Thus when the bodhisattva mind has arisen, the root of buddhahood is firmly planted. Bodhisattva Levels says:
The awakening of the bodhisattva mind is the root of unsurpassable, pure, and perfect enlightenment.[321]

d.div: [555] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 1_shog_8_ba1
[321] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 8a1.

f.d:
lnga pa bsod nams dpag tu med pa thob par 'gyur ba ni/ dpa' sbyin gyis zhus pa'i mdo las/
byang chub sems kyi bsod nams gang / / gal te de la gzugs mchis na/ / nam mkha'i khams ni kun bkang ste/ / de ni de bas lhag par 'gyur/[556] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The fifth point is that immeasurable merit is obtained. The Questions of the Layman Vīradatta Sutra says:
Whatever merit there is of bodhicitta, if it were to posssess a form, it would fill up the whole expanse of space and extend well beyond its bounds.[322]

d.div: [556] sde dge_72_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ca_khyim bdag dpas byin gyis zhus pa'i mdo/ shog_202_ba6
[322] Vīradattagṛhapatiparipṛcchāsūtra, Toh 72 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ca, 202b6.

f.d:
drug pa sangs rgyas thams cad mnyes par 'gyur ba ni/ dpa' sbyin gyis zhus pa'i mdo las/
gang+gA'i bye ma'i grangs snyed kyi/ / sangs rgyas zhing rnams mi gang gis/ / rin chen dag gis yongs bkang ste/ / bde gshegs rnams la phul ba bas/ / gang gis thal mo sbyar bgyis te/ / byang chub tu ni sems btud na/ / mchod pa 'di ni khyad par 'phags/ / de la mtha' ni ma mchis so/[557]/ zhes gsungs so/ /

The sixth point is that it pleases all the buddhas. The same sutra says:
Were one person to fill as many buddhafields as there are grains of sand on the banks of the Ganges with gems and most precious substances and offer them to all the buddhas, and were another person, through compassion, to join his hands and incline the mind to enlightenment, then it would be the latter who made the superior offering. For this has no limits.[323]

d.div: [557] gong mtshungs/ dkon brtsegs/ ca_khyim bdag dpas byin gyis zhus pa'i mdo/ shog_202_ba6
[323] Ibid.

f.d:
bdun pa sems can thams cad la phan par 'gyur ba ni/ ji skad du/
'phags pa sdong po bkod pa'i mdo las/ 'jig rten pa thams cad la phan pas brten lta bu'o/[558] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The seventh point is that it will benefit all beings. The Marvelous Array Sutra says:
It is like a foundation because it brings benefit to all beings.[324]

d.div: [558] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_sdong po bkod pa'i mdo/ shog_309_ba6
[324] Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra, Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, a, 309b6.

f.d:
brgyad pa myur du mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ba ni/ byang sa las/
sems de skyes na mtha' gnyis la mi gnas te/ myur du mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ro/[559] / zhes gsungs so//

The last of the eight points is that one will quickly become a genuinely perfect buddha. It says, in Bodhisattva Levels:
Once this mentality has arisen, one will dwell in neither of the two extremes but quickly achieve really perfect buddhahood.[325]

d.div: [559] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 1_shog_7_ba7

[325] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 7b7. The “two extremes” here are the extremes of samsara and nirvana—being imprisoned within samsaric existence controlled by karma and affliction or falling into the meditative absorption of a solitary peace of personal nirvana.

f.d: 'jug pa'i sems bskyed pa'i phan yon ni bcu ste/ snga ma brgyad po'i steng du/ rang don rgyun chags su 'byung ba dang / gzhan don sna tshogs su 'byung ba'o/ /

The enumerated benefits arising through the engaged bodhisattva are tenfold. These are the eight mentioned above along with (9) you derive constant benefit and (10) it accomplishes the welfare of others, in all kinds of ways.

de la dang po ni/ 'jug pa'i sems de bskyed nas sngar dang mi 'dra ste/ rang nyid gnyid kyis log gam/ brgyal bar gyur tam/ bag med par spyod dam/ de la sogs pa'i dus thams cad du yang bsod nams kyi shugs rgyun mi chad par 'byung ba yin no/ / de ltar yang spyod 'jug las/
sems de yang dag blangs gyur pa/ / de nas bzung ste gnyid log gam/ / bag med gyur kyang bsod nams shugs/ / rgyun mi chad pa du ma zhig / nam mkha' mnyam par rab tu 'byung /[560] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The ninth point is that once this commitment to bodhisattva practice has been undertaken, unlike previously, the flow of merit will be uninterrupted in all circumstances, even when asleep, unconscious, not being especially conscientious, and so forth. /139/ Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life says:
The moment this mind is adopted then on, whether the person is asleep or remains idle, a multitude of merits equal to the expanse of space will befall him with their force uninterrupted.[326]

d.div: [560] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 1_sh+loka_19_shog_2_ba7
[326] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 1:19, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 2b7.

f.d:
gzhan don sna tshogs 'byung ba ni/ sems can rnams kyi sdug bsngal ni sel/ bde ba ni sgrub/ nyon mongs pa ni gcod pa ste/ de ltar yang spyod 'jug las/
gang zhig bde bas 'phongs pa dang / / sdug bsngal mang ldan de dag la/ / bde ba kun gyis tshim pa dang / / sdug bsngal thams cad gcod byed cing / / gti mug kyang ni sel byed dang / / de dang dge mtshungs ga la yod/ / de 'dra'i bshes kyang ga la yod/ / bsod nams de 'dra ga la yod/[561] / ces gsungs so/ /

The tenth benefit is that it will dispel the sufferings of beings, bring them happiness, and sever their afflictions. Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life says:
To those who are deprived of happiness and who experience many sufferings, it brings the satisfaction of many forms of happiness, it eradicates sufferings, and, moreover, it dispels ignorance. Is there any virtue that can match this? Is there anywhere such a friend or merit in such measure?[327]

d.div: [561] gong mtshungs/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 1_sh+loka_29_shog_3_na6

f.d: grangs su ma chad pa ni/ 'di nas bzung nas sangs rgyas kyi bar gyi yon tan thams cad 'byung ba yin te/ bgrang gis mi lang ngo //
The unenumerated benefits consist of all the qualities that emerge between its [initial] adoption and [the attainment of final] enlightenment. They remain beyond calculation.

d.i: Ninth topic: The consequences of abandoning bodhicitta

f.d: byang chub kyi sems dor ba'i nyes dmigs ni gsum ste/[562] nyes pas ngan 'gror 'gro ba dang / nyes pas gzhan don las nyams pa dang / nyes pas sa thob pa la yun ring du thogs pa'o/ /

The ninth point describes the harmful consequences of abandoning bodhicitta. This is a damaging thing, because those who abandon it will (1) be reborn in states of suffering, (2) impair their capacity to help others, and (3) delay considerably any achievement of the bodhisattva levels.

d.div: [562] sems de/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d:
de la dang po ni/ dam bca' ma sgrub ste sems bskyed shor na sems can bslus par song bas/ de'i rnam smin ngan song du skye ba'o/ / de ltar yang spyod 'jug las/
gal te de ltar dam bcas nas/ / las kyis bsgrub par ma byas na/ / sems can de dag kun bslus pas/ / bdag gi 'gro ba ci 'drar 'gyur/[563] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The first of these is that by not fulfilling the bodhisattva promise and abandoning the commitment to enlightenment, a person is effectively cheating all beings. Rebirth in states of suffering is the consequence of such deception. Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life says of this:
Should it happen that, having made the pledge, I do not do the work that needs to be accomplished, what sort of a being will I become, after having thus deceived all those beings?[328]

d.div: [563] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 4_sh+loka_4_shog_8_na4

f.d:
nyes pas gzhan don mi nus pa ni/ ji skad du/
'di ltar de ni byung gyur na/ / sems can kun gyi don las dman/[564] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The second point is that the capacity to help others is impaired:
If such a thing should happen, the welfare of all beings is diminished.[329]

d.div: [564] gong mtshungs/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 4_sh+loka_8_shog_8_na7

f.d:
sa thob pa la yun ring du thogs pa ni/ ji skad du/
de ltar ltung ba stobs ldan dang / / byang chub sems stobs ldan pa dag/ 'khor bar res kyis 'dre byed na/ / sa thob pa la yun ring thogs/[565] / zhes gsungs so//

The third point is the delay in achieving the [sublime bodhisattva] levels. It says:
Those who alternate between strong lapses and strong bodhicitta will continue cycling in samsara and experience serious delay in attaining the bodhisattva levels.[330]

d.div: [565] gong mtshungs/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 4_sh+loka_11_shog_8_ba1

d.i: Tenth topic: The causes for losing the cultivated bodhicitta

f.d: byang chub kyi sems bskyed 'chor ba'i rgyu ni gnyis te/ smon pa 'chor ba'i rgyu dang / 'jug pa 'chor ba'i rgyu'o/ / de la dang po ni/ sems can blos spangs pa dang / nag po'i chos bzhi bsten pa dang / mi mthun pa'i sems bskyed pas 'chor ro/ /

The tenth point concerns the causes of losing the cultivated bodhicitta. These are considered in two areas: the causes for losing the aspiration, and the causes for losing the practice. The aspiring vow will be lost by abandoning any sentient being from your intention, by adhering to the four dark actions, or by adopting an attitude incompatible with the aspiration.

'jug pa'i sdom pa 'chor ba'i rgyu ni/ byang sa las/
pham pa'i gnas lta bu'i chos bzhi kun nas dkris pa chen po spyad na 'chor bar bshad do/ / kun nas dkris pa 'bring dang / chung ngu spyad pa ni na smad tsam du bshad do/[566] /

The engaging vow will be lost according to Bodhisattva Levels, as follows:
If you have committed the four great offences analogous to the grounds of defeat with great involvement—this is described as losing [the generated mind]. /140/ It is further stated that the commitment with a medium or a lesser involvement will injure [the generated mind].[331]

d.div: [566] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 10_shog_97_ba4

[331] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 97b4. A defeat ( pham pa, pārājika) is a complete breakage by a monk or nun of one of the four root prātimokṣa precepts (no killing, lying, stealing, or sexual intercourse). Great involvement is committing any of the four offenses analogous to the grounds of defeat wherein (a) the bodhisattva makes a regular practice of it, (b) generates not the slightest sense of shame and embarassment, (c) is pleased with and glad of it, and (d) has a view for its good qualities. If one or more of these are missing, then the degree of involvement is characterized as being lesser or medium. For Asaṅga’s discussion of these points, see Tatz, Asanga’s Chapter on Ethics, pp. 64–65.

f.d: sdom pa nyi shu pa las/ de'i steng du smon pa'i sems bskyed shor bas kyang 'chor bar bshad do/[567] / rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba las/ byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa gtong ba'i rgyu bzhi gsungs so/[568] / snga ma gnyis po dang / bslab pa phul ba dang / log lta skyes pa'o/ / slob dpon zhi ba lha'i zhal nas kyang mi mthun pa'i sems skyes pas kyang sdom pa gtong ngo /[569] /zhes gsungs so/ /

In the Twenty Verses on the Vows it states that the loss of aspiration bodhicitta also brings the loss of engaged bodhicitta. In Establishing Summaries of the Levels of Yogic Practice, it is stated that there are four causes for relinquishing the bodhisattva vow.[332] These are the two mentioned above [abandoning any sentient being from one’s intention and indulging in the four dark actions] and third, renouncing the bodhisattva training, and fourth, giving rise to aberrant views. Master Śāntideva, too, says that engendering an incompatible mental attitude will break the vow.[333]

d.div: [567] sde dge_4082_bstan/ sems tsam/ hi_zhi ba 'tsho/ sdom pa nyi shu pa'i 'grel pa/ shog_17_ba
[568] sde dge_4038_bstan/ sems tsam/ zhi_'phags pa thogs med/ rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba/ shog_38_ba6
[569] sde dge_3940_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_zhi ba lha/ bslab btus/ le'u/ 8_shog_99_na7
[332] Asaṅga, Yogācārabhūmiviniścayasaṃgrahaṇī, Toh 4038 Tengyur, sems tsam, zhi, 38b6.
[333] Śāntideva, Śikṣāsamuccaya, Toh 3940 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 99a7.

d.i: Eleventh topic: How, if lost, to restore the bodhisattva vow

f.d: shor na phyir bcos pa'i thabs ni/ smon pa'i sems bskyed shor na slar blangs pas sor chud do/ / 'jug pa'i sdom pa shor ba la yang / smon pa'i sems shor bas 'jug pa shor ba de ni/ smon pa sor chud pas 'jug pa yang rang bzhin gyis sor chud do/ / rgyu gzhan gyis sdom pa shor ba ni/ slar len dgos so/ / pham pa'i gnas lta bu bzhi la kun nas dkris pa 'bring dang chung ngu spyad pa ni bshags pas chog go /

As for how, if lost, to restore the vow, if it is the aspiration vow that has been broken, it can be restored by taking it again. In the loss of the engaging vow by virtue of having lost the aspiration vow, then rectifying the aspiration bodhicitta brings about automatic restoration of the engaged bodhicitta vow. If the engaging vow has been broken due to some other cause, it will have to be taken again. If it is lost due to commiting the four offenses analogous to the grounds of defeat with a medium or lesser involvement, this can be rectified through declaration and purification.[334]

d.div: [334] See note 331 above for these offenses and involvements.

f.d:
de ltar yang sdom pa nyi shu pa las/
sdom pa slar yang blang bar bya/ / zag pa 'bring ni gsum la bshags/ / gcig gi mdun du lhag ma rnams/ / nyon mongs mi mongs bdag sems bzhin/[570] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Twenty Verses on the Bodhisattva Vows says:
One needs to retake the vow. [If commited] with middling pollutant, confess it to three [or more], and in the presence of one for the rest. For those with [lesser] afflictions or none, purify them in your own mind.[335]

d.div: [570] sde dge_4081_bstan/ sems tsam/ hi_slob dpon tsan+d+ra go mi/ sdom pa nyi shu pa/ shog_166_ba5

[335] Candragomin, Twenty Verses on the Bodhisattva Vow (Bodhisattvasaṃvaraviṃśaka) verse 8, Toh 4081 Tengyur, sems tsam, hi, 166b5. This verse lists four different ways of dealing with infraction of the bodhisattva vow. If the vow has been broken due to either the loss of the aspiration bodhicitta or through the commitment of any of the four offences with great involvement, one then needs to retake the vow afresh. If the infraction consists of committing any of the four offences with a medium involvement, one then needs to declare it and purify it in the presence of at least three people. For the rest, by which the author means the commitment of any of the four offences with a lesser involvement, one then needs to rectify this by purifying it in the presence of a single person. Finally, if the infraction consists of violating any of the secondary precepts with or without manifest afflictions present in one’s mind, one can then purify it within one’s own mind, as if taking one’s own mind as the witness.

f.d: dam chos yid bzhin gyi nor bu thar pa rin po che'i rgyan las/ byang chub kyi sems yongs su bzung ba'i le'u ste dgu pa'o// //
This then concludes the ninth chapter, discussing the proper adoption of bodhicitta, from this Ornament of Precious Liberation, a Wish-Fulfilling Gem of Sublime Dharma.
(byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i bslab bya/)
le'u bcu pa/ smon pa sems bskyed kyi bslab bya/
10. Precepts for Generating Aspiring Bodhicitta

d.i: Twelfth topic: Precepts related to generating bodhicitta

f.d: byang chub tu sems bskyed kyi bslab bya ni gnyis te/[571] smon pa byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i bslab bya dang / 'jug pa byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i bslab bya'o/ /
The precepts related to the generation of bodhicitta is twofold: (1) the precepts related to the aspiring bodhicitta and (2) the precepts related to the engaging bodhicitta.

d.div: [571] sems bskyed nas bslab bya/ dpal spungs/ sems bskyed pa'i bslab bya/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d:
de la dang po 'chad pa la/ sdom ni/
sems can blos mi btang ba dang / / sems de'i phan yon dran bya dang / / tshogs gnyis bsag par bya ba dang / / yang yang byang sems sbyang ba dang / / dkar nag chos brgyad blang dor te/ / lnga pos smon pa'i bslab bya bsdus/ / zhes pa'o//

To present the first, the synopsis is the following:
The precepts of aspiration are summed up in five points: to never mentally abandon sentient beings, to remain mindful of the benefits of that mind, to gather the two accumulations, to repeatedly train in bodhicitta, and to nurture the four bright modes of action while abandoning the four dark ones.

de dag kyang dang po ni/[572] byang chub kyi sems de mi 'chor ba'i thabs so/ / gnyis pa ni/ byang chub kyi sems de mi nyams pa'i thabs so/ / gsum pa ni/ byang chub kyi sems de'i stobs bskyed pa'i thabs so/ / bzhi pa ni/ byang chub kyi sems de 'phel ba'i thabs so/ / lnga pa ni/ byang chub kyi sems de mi brjed pa'i thabs so/ /

Of these five points, the first consists of the means for not abandoning bodhicitta; /141/ the second the means for preventing bodhicitta from degrading; the third the means for strengthening bodhicitta; the fourth the means to increase bodhicitta; and the fifth consists of the means for not forgetting bodhicitta.

d.div: [572] de dag las/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d:
de la dang po sems can blos mi btang ba la bslab pa zhes bya ba byang chub kyi sems de mi 'chor ba'i thabs bshad na/ ma dros pas zhus pa'i mdo las kyang /
byang chub sems dpa' chos gcig dang ldan na/ rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa'i sangs rgyas kyi chos rnams yongs su 'dzin to/ / chos gcig po gang zhe na/ sems can blos yongs su mi btang ba'i sems so/[573] / zhes gsungs te/ de yang sems can gang dag gis bdag la mi rigs pa zhig byas pas/ bdag de la sems rgyang bsrings nas/ sha tsha ba dang bral te phyin chad khyod la phan thogs pa'i dus byung yang mi gdags/ gnod pa bzlog pa'i dus byung yang mi bzlog snyam pa'i sems bskyed pa ni sems can blos btang ba yin no/ /

To explain the first, namely to never abandon any sentient being from your intention, which constitutes the means of ensuring that your bodhicitta does not get lost, the Questions of [Nāga King] Anavatapta Sutra says:
What one thing could bodhisattvas possess that would embrace fully every quality of the Enlightened One, endowed with the best of everything? It is the aspiration to never abandon any being from their intentions.[336] To abandon beings from your intentions means, for example, no longer feeling any sympathy for a person who has treated you unfairly, thinking, “Even if I could help you, I wouldn’t; were I able to save you from harm, I wouldn’t.” If you think like this, you have excluded someone from your compassionate intentions.

d.div: [573] sde dge_156_bka'/ mdo sde/ pha_klu'i rgyal po ma dros pas zhus pa'i mdo/ shog_208_ba4
[336] Anavataptanāgarājaparipṛcchāsūtra, Toh 156 Kangyur, mdo sde, pha, 208b4.

f.d: de yang sems can thams cad blos btang ba la zer ram/ gcig tsam blos btang ba la yang zer zhe na/ sems can thams cad blos spangs pa ni nyan rang rnam gnyis ma yin pa/ khra dang spyang ki la yang mi 'ong ste/ des na sems can gcig tsam blos btang bas kyang thun tshod kyi nang khongs su gnyen pos ma sleb na byang sems 'chor ro/ / de ltar sems can blos spong zhing bslab bya gzhan la gnas nas byang chub sems dpar khas len pa ni shin tu mi 'thad de/ dper na bu gcig pu bsad nas bu'i rdzas gsog pa dang 'dra'o/ / de bas na sems can bdag la phan 'dogs pa rnams la byang chub kyi sems ga na 'chor te/[574] gnod pa byed pa la 'chor dogs yod pas/ de la khyad par du snying rje bskyed pas phan bde bsgrub par bya'o/ /

Does “abandon beings from your intentions” mean all beings or even just one being? Except for śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas,[337] no one abandons all beings from the mind—not even birds of prey or wolves [do this]. Thus, someone who has mentally abandoned just one being and not rectified that within one watch of the day [i.e., four hours] has lost bodhicitta. This means that those who exclude beings from their intentions while engaging in bodhisattva conduct yet still think of themselves as bodhisattvas are completely mistaken. That would be like clinging to your only child’s belongings after having killed him. Since it is quite possible to drop the bodhisattva attitude even toward those who have been helpful, the risk of losing it toward those who are harmful is indeed high. Therefore, paying special attention to practicing compassion toward the latter, you should try to help them and make them happy.

d.div: [574] sems gnas/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

[337] This seemingly shocking statement probably refers to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas who are deeply absorbed in the bliss of meditative concentrations, where the sense gates are oblivious to input and the mind is so absorbed in its own peace that it is oblivious to everything else.

f.d:
'di ni dam pa rnams kyi chos lugs yin te/ ji skad du/
phan btags lan du gnod byas na/ / yang lan snying rje chen pos bslan/ / 'dzam bu'i gling gi skyes mchog ni/ / nyes pa'i lan yang legs pas ldon/[575] / zhes gsungs so//

This is the way of the sublime beings, for it is said:
Even if your kindness is repaid with harm, cultivate compassion in return. The most excellent beings of the world respond to even the negative with goodness.[338]

d.div: [575] blo sbyong brgya rtsar bzhugs pa 'chad ka ba'i tshigs brgyad ma'i 'grel par yang sh+lauka 'di byung der 'di ltar drangs/ phan btags lan du gnod byed na'ang / /lan la snying rje chen po bsgom/ /'dzam bu gling gi skyes mchog ni/ /nyes pa'i lan ni legs pas 'don/ /gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[338] The source for this quote has not been identified.

f.d:
gnyis pa sems bskyed pa'i phan yon dran par bya ba la bslab pa zhes bya ba/ byang chub kyi sems mi nyams pa'i thabs de bshad na/ byang chub lam sgron las kyang /
de ltar smon pa'i sems dag ni/ / bskyed pa'i yon tan gang yin pa/ / de ni sdong po bkod pa yi/ / mdo las byams pas rab tu bshad/[576] / ces pa la sogs pa gsungs te/ de yang mdo de las sems bskyed pa'i phan yon dpe nyis brgya sum cu tsam gyi sgo nas gsungs pa la/ de dag thams cad phan yon gyi sgo chen po bzhir 'dus pa yin gsung /

To explain the second point, to train in remaining mindful of the benefits of bodhicitta, which constitutes the means of guarding against its degradation, there are statements such as the following from the Lamp for the Path to Awakening: /142/
Whatever benefits there be in developing the aspiration for enlightenment have been explained by Maitreya, through the Marvelous Array [Sutra], and in similar texts.[339] In that sutra, the benefits of bodhicitta are presented through two hundred and thirty similes, and it states that that all of these benefits can be subsumed into four main categories.

d.div: [576] sde dge_3947_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_dpal mar me mdzad ye shes/ lam sgron/ sh+loka_12_shog_238_ba6
[339] Atiśa, Bodhipathapradīpa verse 12, Toh 3947 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 238b6.

f.d: de yang / rigs kyi bu byang chub sems ni sangs rgyas kyi chos thams cad kyi sa bon lta bu'o/ / dbul ba thams cad sel bar byed pa'i rnam thos kyi bu lta bu'o/[577] /zhes pa la sogs pa ni rang don 'byung ba'i phan yon no/[578] /

The sutra states, “Child of good family! This bodhicitta is like the seed of all the buddhas’ qualities. Because it dispels spiritual poverty, it is like the god of wealth.”[340] This and other similes concern the benefits for oneself.

d.div: [577] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_sdong po bkod pa'i mdo/ shog_309_ba1
[578] byung / mi rigs dpe skrun/
[340] Marvelous Array Sutra (Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra), in Flower Ornament Sutra (Avataṃsakasūtra), Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, a, 309b1.

f.d: 'gro ba thams cad yongs su skyob pas na gnas lta bu'o/ / 'gro ba thams cad brten pas rten lta bu'o/[579] /zhes pa la sogs pa ni gzhan don 'byung ba'i phan yon no/ /

Then it says, “Because it provides excellent protection for all beings, it is like a refuge,” and “Because it sustains all beings, it is like the supporting earth.”[341] This statement and others illustrate the benefit for others.

d.div: [579] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_sdong po bkod pa'i mdo/ shog_311_ba2_ba

f.d: nyon mongs pa'i dpung gis rgyal bar byed pa'i mdung lta bu'o/[580]/ sdug bsngal gyi ljon shing rab tu gcod par byed pa'i sta re lta bu'o/[581] /zhes pa la sogs pa ni mi mthun pa'i phyogs thams cad gcod pa'i phan yon no/ /

Next, it says, “Because it defeats the enemy, the afflictions, it is like a spear. . . Because it fells the mighty tree of suffering, it is like an axe.”[342] These statements and others illustrate the benefit it brings in cutting away wrong views.

d.div: [580] gong mtshungs/ shog_310_ba4
[581] gong mtshungs/ shog_310_ba5

f.d: bsam pa thams cad yongs su rdzogs par byed pa'i bum pa bzang po lta bu'o/ / 'dod pa thams cad yongs su sgrub par byed pa'i yid bzhin gyi nor bu rin po che lta bu'o/[582] /zhes pa la sogs pa ni mthun pa'i phyogs thams cad 'grub pa'i phan yon no/ /

Then it says, “Because it completely fulfills all intentions, it is like the enchanted vase. . . Because it makes all wishes come true, it is like a wish-fulfilling gem.”[343] These statements illustrate its benefit in causing the accomplishment of everything that goes in the right direction.

d.div: [582] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ a_sdong po bkod pa'i mdo/ shog_310_ba2

f.d: de lta bu'i phan yon de dag thams cad dran par byas pas phan yon can gyi byang chub kyi sems de la rtsis che zhing mchog tu 'dzin par 'gyur/ / de ltar gyur pas nyams su blangs nas sems de ma nyams par skyong bar 'gyur ba yin no/ / des na phan yon ni de dag rtag tu dran par bya zhing / tha na thun tshod kyi nang khongs su yang lan re dran par bya'o/ /

Through being mindful of the above benefits, you will come to greatly value the bodhisattva mind and appreciate its excellence. When this has been first achieved and then maintained through practice, it protects bodhicitta from degradation.
