Therefore always be mindful of bodhicitta’s benefits, even should it be just for a short while in every watch of the day.

gsum pa tshogs gnyis bsag par bya ba la bslab pa zhes bya ba/[583] byang chub kyi sems kyi stobs bskyed pa'i thabs de bshad na/ byang chub lam sgron las kyang /
bsod nams ye shes rang bzhin gyi/ / tshogs ni yongs su rdzogs pa'i rgyu/[584] / zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs te/ de yang bsod nams kyi tshogs na chos spyod bcu dang / bsdu ba'i dngos po bzhi la sogs pa thabs kyi cha 'di dag yin la/ ye shes kyi tshogs ni de dag 'khor gsum yongs dag tu zhes pa la sogs pa shes rab kyi cha 'di dag yin te/ de ltar tshogs gnyis bsags pas rang gi rgyud la byang chub kyi sems kyi stobs skye ba yin no/ /

To explain third point, training in gathering the two accumulations, which constitutes the means of strengthening bodhicitta, the Lamp for the Path to Awakening, for instance, states the following:
The accumulations, consisting of virtue and pristine awareness, are the cause for perfect [enlightenment].[344] Of these, the accumulation of merit consists of the skillful means aspect, comprising the ten activities pertaining to Dharma practice and the four means of gathering beings[345] and so on. The accumulation of pristine awareness consists of the profound wisdom aspect, such as the awareness of the total purity of the three spheres. Thus, it is through gathering the two accumulations that the force of bodhicitta arises within your mental continuum. /143/

d.div: [583] bsags/ dpal spungs/
[584] sde dge_3947_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_dpal mar me mdzad ye shes/ lam sgron/ sh+loka_35_shog_239_ba5
[344] Atiśa, Bodhipathapradīpa verse 34, Toh 3947 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 239b5.

[345] The four means of gathering beings are four ways a Dharma master gathers a following: through generosity (especially of Dharma), pleasing speech, appropriate conduct, and actions consistent with the teachings.

f.d:
des na tshogs gnyis po de rtag tu bsag cing / tha na sngags thung gcig bzlas pa yang tshogs gnyis tshang du btub pas thun tshod kyi nang khongs su yang lan re bsag par bya'o/[585] / tshogs kyi gtam las kyang /
de ring bdag gis bsod nams dang / / ye shes tshogs ni gang bya dang / / sems can phan par gang bya zhes/ / byang chub sems dpas rtag tu bsam/[586] / zhes gsungs so//

Therefore always gather the two accumulations. Since even a simple recition of a brief mantra once during each watch of the day can lead to completion of the two accumulations, even if it is only for a brief moment, you should gather the accumulations. A Discussion of Accumulation says of this:
“What will I do today to gather the accumulations of merit or of wisdom?” “What will I do today to help sentient beings?” So a bodhisattva constantly contemplates.[346]

d.div: [585] cig bzlos/ dpal spungs/
[586] sde dge_4166_bstan/ spring yig_ge_slob dpon dbyig gnyen/ tshogs kyi gtam/ sh+loka_12_shog_173_ba2
[346] Vasubhandhu, Sambhāraparikathā, Toh 4166 Tengyur, spring yig, ge, 173b2.

f.d:
bzhi pa yang dang yang du byang chub kyi sems sbyang ba la bslab pa zhes bya ba/ byang chub kyi sems de 'phel ba'i thabs de bshad na/ byang chub lam sgron las kyang /
byang chub smon pa'i sems dag bskyed nas ni/ / 'bad pa mang pos kun tu 'phel bya zhing /[587] / zhes gsungs so/ /

To explain the fourth point, training repeatedly in bodhicitta, which constitutes the means to increase bodhicitta, Lamp for the Path to Awakening says:
Having given rise to bodhicitta as an aspiration, strive to increase it in every way.[347]

d.div: [587] sde dge_3947_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_dpal mar me mdzad ye shes/ lam sgron/ sh+loka_18_shog_239_na2
[347] Atiśa, Bodhipathapradīpa verse 18ab, Toh 3947 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 239a2.

f.d: de yang byang chub rgyu'i sems sbyang ba dang / byang chub dngos kyi sems sbyang ba dang / byang chub spyod pa'i sems sbyang ba dang gsum du shes par bya'o/ / de gsum la sbyangs pas byang chub kyi sems de 'phel ba yin no//

This striving should be understood as applying to three areas of activity: (1) training in the attitude that gives rise to bodhicitta, (2) training in bodhicitta itself, and (3) training in the attitude related to bodhisattva conduct.
de la dang po ni/ sems can rnams la byams pa dang snying rje'i sems rtag tu bsam pa'am/ tha na yang thun tshod kyi nang du lan re bsam pa'o/ /
The attitude that gives rise to bodhicitta is to always be disposed to loving kindness and compassion toward sentient beings, or at least to engender such a thought once every watch of the day.

byang chub dngos kyi sems sbyang ba ni/ sems can gyi don du sangs rgyas thob par 'dod pa'i blos/ nyin lan gsum mtshan lan gsum du bsam pa'am/ sems bskyed kyi cho ga rgyas par bya ba'am/ tha na thun tshod kyi nang khongs su/ jo bos mdzad pa'i sems bskyed cho ga las gsungs pa/
sangs rgyas chos dang tshogs kyi mchog rnams la/ / byang chub bar du bdag ni skyabs su mchi/ / bdag gis sbyin sogs bgyis pa 'di dag gis/ / 'gro la phan phyir sangs rgyas 'grub par shog[588] / ces brjod pa'o/ /

Training in bodhicitta itself is to nurture an intention longing to attain enlightenment so as to be able to benefit beings. This should be the subject of contemplation during the three periods of the day and the three periods of the night. Alternatively, the longer bodhisattva ritual can be performed; or else, at a minimum, the following prayer, [recommended by] the great Atiśa, can be recited once every watch of the day:
To the buddhas, the Dharma, and the supreme community, I go for refuge until attainment of enlightenment. Through my engagement in generosity and so forth, may I achieve buddhahood for the benefit of all sentient beings.[348]

d.div: [588] sde dge_3969_bstan/ dbu ma/ gi_mar me mdzad/ sems bskyed pa dang sdom pa'i cho ga'i rim pa/ shog_246_na3_ma dper phyag dpe'i mtshan 'di sangs rgyas chos tshogs ma'i tshigs bcad kyi 'og tu byung yang dpar ma gzhan ltar 'gor bkod/

[348] Atiśa, Ritual Order for Bodhicitta and Vows (Cittotpādasaṃvaravidhikrama), Toh 3969 Tengyur, dbu ma, gi, 246a3. Many contemporary masters attribute these words to Buddha Śākyamuni three cosmic eons ago, when he first gave rise to bodhicitta.

f.d: byang chub spyod pa'i sems sbyang ba la gnyis te/ gzhan la phan btags pa'i sems sbyang ba dang / rang gi rgyud dag pa'i sems sbyang ba'o// de la dang po ni/ rang gi lus dang longs spyod dang dus gsum gyi dge ba thams cad gzhan gyi phan bde'i don du bsngo zhing btang ba'i sems bskyed pa'o/ / rang gi rgyud dag pa'i sems sbyang ba ni/ rtag tu tshul khrims la bsngo bgrang bya zhing sdig pa dang nyon mongs pa la 'dzem pa'o//

Training in the attittude related to bodhisattva conduct is twofold: developing the willingness to work for the benefit of others and developing the intention to purify the mind. The first of these means dedicating body, possessions, and whatever virtues have been established in the three times to the service of others and their happiness; it implies cultivating a willingness to give. Developing the intention to purify the mind involves constant examination of personal conduct as well as the elimination of afflictions and harmful actions.

lnga pa nag po'i chos bzhi spang zhing dkar po'i chos bzhi brten pa la bslab pa zhes bya ba/[589] byang chub kyi sems de mi brjed pa'i thabs de bshad na/ byang chub lam sgron las kyang /
'id ni skye ba gzhan du'ang dran don du/ / ji skad brjod pa'i bslab pa yongs su bsrung /[590] / zhes gsungs so/ /

To explain the fifth point, abandoning the four dark actions and nurturing the four bright ones, which constitutes the means for not forgetting bodhicitta, Lamp for the Path to Awakening says:
To remember this in other lives as well, carefully observe the precepts thus explained.[349]

d.div: [589] bsten/ dpal spungs/
[590] sde dge_3947_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_dpal mar me mdzad ye shes/ lam sgron/ sh+loka_18_shog_239_na3
[349] Atiśa, Bodhipathapradīpa verse 18cd, Toh 3947 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 239a3.

f.d:
bslab pa gang nas bshad na/ 'od srungs kyis zhus pa'i mdo las/[591] de yang nag po'i chos bzhi ni/ ji skad du/
'od srungs byang chub sems dpa' chos bzhi dang ldan na byang chub kyi sems brjed par 'gyur te/ bzhi gang zhe na/ 'di lta ste/[592] zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs so/ /

Where are these precepts explained? The Kāśyapa Chapter Sutra states the following, with respect to the four dark actions, for instance:
Kāśyapa! A bodhisattva possessing these four things will forget his bodhicitta. What are these four? They are. [350]

d.div: [591] mdo las te/ dpal spungs/
[592] sde dge_87_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ cha_'od srung gis zhus pa'i le'u/ shog_120_na6
[350] Kāśyapaparivartasūtra, Toh 87 Kangyur, dkon brtseg, cha, 120a6.

f.d:
de dag gi don bsdu na/ bla ma dang mchod par 'os pa bslus pa dang / gzhan 'gyod pa'i gnas ma yin pa la 'gyod pa skyes pa dang /[593] sems bskyed pa'i byang chub sems dpa' la zhe sdang gis tshigs su bcad pa ma yin pa brjod pa dang / sems can la g.yo sgyus spyod pa'o/ / dkar po'i chos bzhi yang / ji skad du/
'od srung byang chub sems dpa' chos bzhi dang ldan na/ skye ba thams cad du skyes ma thag tu byang chub kyi sems mngon du 'gyur te/ byang chub kyi snying po la thug gi bar du bar ma dor brjed par mi 'gyur ro/ / bzhi gang zhe na/[594] zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs so/[595] /

To summarize them, the four dark actions are: (1) to deceive a guru or person worthy of receiving offerings, (2) to cause others to regret actions that should not be regretted, (3) to speak improperly to a bodhisattva who has generated the mind, and (4) to engage with sentient being through pretense and deceit. With respect to the four bright actions as well, that same sutra states:
Kāśyapa! Should a bodhisattva possess these four, then in all future lives bodhicitta will definitely manifest from birth onward. Without any interruption, that bodhicitta will never be forgotten until enlightenment is attained. What are these four? They are. [351]

d.div: [593] bskyed/ dpal spungs/
[594] sde dge_87_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ cha_'od srung gis zhus pa'i le'u/ shog_120_ba3
[595] 'di lta ste/ zhes pa la sogs/ dpal spungs/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: de dag gi don bsdu na/ shes bzhin du srog gi phyir yang rdzun mi smra ba dang / sems can thams cad dge ba la 'god cing de yang theg pa chen po'i dge ba la 'god pa dang / sems bskyed pa'i byang chub sems dpa' la ston pa sangs rgyas kyi 'du shes bskyed cing de'i yon tan phyogs bcur brjod pa dang / sems can thams cad la g.yo sgyus ma yin par lhag pa'i bsam pas gnas par bya'o/ /[596]

To summarize the four, they are: (1) never knowingly to tell lies,[352] even should it cost your life; (2) to establish all beings in virtue and, further, to establish them in Mahayana virtue; (3) to consider a bodhisattva, meaning one who has taken the vow, as being the Teacher, the Enlightened One, and to proclaim that person’s qualities in every quarter; and (4) to constantly abide within a noble disposition of mind, free of pretense and deceipt toward any sentient being.

d.div: [596] bya ba'o// dpal spungs/

[352] This means telling lies for self-interest. Lies that may save others from harm, and lies in other altruistic instances, may be the most appropriate thing a bodhisattva could do (Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoché).

f.d: de la nag po'i chos dang po de'i don bshad na/[597] bla ma dang / mkhan po dang / slob dpon dang / sbyin gnas la sogs pa mchod 'os dag la bslu sems kyis brdzun smras te mgo bskor na/ de dag gis tshor rung ma tshor rung / dgyes rung ma dgyes rung / kham che rung chung rung / mgo 'khor rung ma 'khor rung / thun tshod las 'das par gnyen pos ma sleb na byang sems 'chor ro/ / de'i gnyen por dkar po'i chos dang po/ shes bzhin du srog gi phyir yang rdzun mi smra ba de la gnas par bya'o/ /

I will now explain the first dark action [and its opposite, bright action]. If, with an intention to deceive, you have actually been deceitful toward anyone “worthy of offerings”—meaning a guru, an abbot, a preceptor, or a person who is an object of your giving—the bodhisattva vow is broken, unless you do something to remedy the fault within a single watch of the day. It does not matter whether or not the person knew he [or she] was being deceived, whether or not the deception caused displeasure, whether it was a major or minor deception, or whether or not the deceit actually worked. Whatever the case, the vow is broken. The remedy to this is the first bright action, which is, in all circumstances, to avoid the intentional telling of untruths, even should that put your life at risk.

d.div: [597] chos dang de'i don/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: nag po'i chos gnyis pa de bshad na/ gzhan dag gis dge ba'i las byas pa la (spyan snga ba dang bya yul ba'i zhal nas theg chen gyi las gsungs/ rgya yon bdag gis theg pa che chung gang yang 'dra gsung / sbyin pa'i dbang du byas na/ sbyin pa byas pa de la bya byed ni bzang ste/)[598] 'gyod pa bskyed du gzhug pa'i bsam pas 'gyod pa bskyed pa ste/(sang gnang ltogs par song nas/ sprang dgos par mchi yi zer ba la sogs pa lta bu'o/)[599] / kho 'gyod pa skyes rung ma skyes rung / thun tshod kyi nang khongs su gnyen pos ma sleb na byang sems 'chor ro/ / de'i gnyen por dkar po'i chos gnyis pa sems can thams cad dge ba la 'god cing / de yang theg pa chen po'i dge ba la 'god pa la 'bad par bya'o/ /

The second dark action occurs in relation to the virtuous actions of others.[353] /145/ It involves trying to make them feel remorseful by stirring up notions of regret [for the good they have done]. In the case of generosity, we could take the giver as an example. Although that person did a good deed, someone else may try to stir up regret by saying that in days to come the loss of resources caused by the generosity will leave the giver hungry and a beggar—and then what will he do? If this dark action is not remedied within a watch of the day, the bodhisattva vow has been broken, whether or not the person actually does regret the deed. The remedy for this is the second bright action: to establish all beings in virtue, and in particular in Mahayana virtue.

d.div: [598] dpal spungs dpar mar gong gi gzhan dag gi dge ba'i las zhes pa nas bya byed ni bzang ste/ zhes pa'i bar gyi tshig rnams mi byung la/ ma dper tshig 'di rnams gzhung dkyus la bkod mod/ 'on kyang mi rigs dpe skrun khang gi dpar mar/ spyan snga pa zhes pa nas bzang ste/ zhes pa'i bar yig chung du bkod 'dug pa legs par snang bas 'dir de bzhin du byas yod/
[599] ma dper tshig 'di rnams gzhung dkyus la bkod 'dug mod/ mi rigs dpe skrun khang bzhin yig chung du byed na legs par snang bas de bzhin du byas yod/

[353] In the Tibetan original, there is a parenthetical sentence immediately following this sentence that reads: “Chengawa and Jayulwa speak of Mahayana virtuous actions, while Gya Yöndak says that it is the same for any virtuous action, be it that of the Mahayana or the Hinayana. In the case of engaging in giving, for example, the act as well as the agent becomes good if one has been engaged in a giving. . . ” It is unclear whether this annotation is part of the original or was added on by a subsequent editor.

f.d: nag po'i chos gsum pa de bshad na/ sems bskyed pa'i gang zag gcig la zhe sdang pas de'i skyon brjod pa ste/ de yang tha mal gyi skyon nas brjod kyang rung / chos kyi skyon nas brjod kyang rung / ngor yang rung / lkog tu yang rung / dmigs kyis phyes kyang rung / ma phyes kyang rung / 'jam pos kyang rung / rtsub pos kyang rung / thos kyang rung / ma thos kyang rung / dga' yang rung / ma dga' yang rung ste/ thun tshod kyi nang khongs su gnyen pos ma sleb na byang sems 'chor ro/ / de'i gnyen por dkar po'i chos gsum pa/ sems bskyed pa'i byang chub sems dpa' la sangs rgyas kyi 'du shes bskyed cing / de'i yon tan phyogs bcur brjod pa de la 'bad par bya'o/ /

The third dark action occurs through anger or hatred and involves talking about the faults of someone who has taken the bodhisattva vow. They may be ordinary faults or Dharma failings, addressed directly to that person or indirectly, and it could be done in a pleasant or unpleasant way. Whether or not the bodhisattva concerned is disturbed by what has been said, the bodhisattva vow is broken unless this is remedied within a watch of the day. The remedy is the third bright action: to conceive of anyone who has taken the bodhisattva vow just as you would conceive of a buddha and to let their qualities be known everywhere.

nag po'i chos bzhi pa de bshad na/ sems can gang yang rung ba la g.yo sgyu'i bsam pas zol zog gcig byas pa ste/ khos tshor rung / ma tshor rung / kho la gnod rung ma gnod rung / thun tshod kyi nang khongs su gnyen pos ma sleb na/ byang sems 'chor ba'o/ / de'i gnyen por dkar po'i chos bzhi pa/ sems can la lhag pa'i bsam pas gnas par bya ba zhes pa rang don la ma 'khris par phan gdags par 'dod pa'i bsam pa de bya'o/[600] /

The fourth dark action entails intentionally trying to deceive anyone at all. Unless remedied within a watch of the day, this will break the bodhisattva vow, whether or not the person is aware of the deception and whether or not any actual harm is done. The remedy is the fourth bright action: to act always with the noblest intentions toward beings. This means intending to benefit them without self-interest.

d.div: [600] ma mkhris/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: dam chos yid bzhin gyi nor bu thar pa rin po che'i rgyan las/ smon pa byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i bslab bya bstan pa'i le'u ste bcu pa'o// //
This then concludes the tenth chapter, on how to develop aspiration bodhicitta, of this Ornament of Precious Liberation, a Wish-Fulfilling Gem of Sublime Dharma.
('jug pa byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i bslab bya bshad pa/)
le'u bcu gcig pa/ pha rol tu phyin pa drug gi rnam gzhag bstan pa/
11. Presentation of the Six Perfections

'jug pa byang chub tu sems bskyed pa'i bslab bya ni rnam pa gsum yin te/ lhag pa tshul khrims kyi bslab pa dang / lhag pa sems kyi bslab pa dang / lhag pa shes rab kyi bslab pa'o/ / de ltar yang byang chub lam sgron las/
'jug pa'i sems kyi bdag nyid sdom gnas pas/ / tshul khrims bslab pa gsum la legs bslabs nas/ / tshul khrims bslab pa gsum la gus cher 'gyur/[601]/ zhes gsungs so/ /

The precepts related to engaged bodhicitta is threefold: (1) higher training in moral discipline, (2) higher training in [applying] the mind [i.e., meditation], and (3) higher training in wisdom. In this respect, Lamp for the Path to Awakening says:
Those who abide within the vow of engaged bodhicitta, having correctly trained in the three aspects of moral discipline, will greatly deepen their appreciation of those three trainings.[354]

d.div: [601] sde dge_3947_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_dpal mar me mdzad ye shes/ lam sgron/ sh+loka_33_shog_239_ba3
[354] Atiśa, Bodhipathapradīpa verse 32a–c, Toh 3947 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 239b3.

f.d: de la lhag pa tshul khrims kyi bslab pa ni/ sbyin pa dang / tshul khrims dang / bzod pa dang gsum yin no/ / lhag pa sems kyi bslab pa ni bsam gtan yin no/ / lhag pa shes rab kyi bslab pa ni shes rab yin no/ / brtson 'grus ni gsum char gyi grogs yin no/ /

The higher training in moral discipline consists of three: generosity, discipline, and patience; the higher training in mind consists of meditative concentration; and the higher training in wisdom consists of profound wisdom. As for diligence it serves as a complementary factor to all three [trainings].

de ltar yang mdo sde rgyan las/
bslab gsum dbang du mdzad nas ni/ / rgyal bas pha rol phyin pa drug / yang dag bshad de dang po gsum/ / tha ma gnyis kyis rnam pa gnyis/ / gcig ni gsum char la yang gtogs/[602]/ zhes gsungs so/ /

The Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
The Victorious One has most perfectly explained the six perfections in terms of the three trainings: the first three are the first training, the last two are the last two, while one [diligence] applies to all three.[355]

d.div: [602] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 16_sh+loka_7_shog_21_ba2
[355] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 16:7, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 21b2.

f.d:
de'i phyir na/ sdom ni/
sbyin dang tshul khrims bzod pa dang / / brtson 'grus bsam gtan shes rab ste/ / de ltar rnam pa drug po 'dis/ / 'jug pa'i sems bskyed bslab bya bsdus/ / zhes par bya'o/ /

Thus the synopsis for this chapter is the following:
Training in engaged bodhicitta can be summarized as sixfold: generosity, moral discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

lag bzangs kyis zhus pa'i mdo las kyang /
lag bzangs byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po myur du mngon par rdzogs par byang chub par bya ba'i phyir/ pha rol tu phyin pa drug po 'di dag la rtag par rgyun du yongs su rdzogs par bya'o/ / drug gang zhe na/ 'di lta ste/ sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa dang / tshul khrims kyi pha rol tu phyin pa dang / bzod pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa dang / brtson 'grus kyi pha rol tu phyin pa dang / bsam gtan gyi pha rol tu phyin pa dang / drug pa shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa ste/[603] zhes gsungs so/ /

In the Questions of Subāhu Sutra, too, it says:
Subāhu! For a great bodhisattva to quickly achieve real and perfect enlightenment, the six perfections must be applied constantly and in all circumstances until their utter completion. What are those six? They are the perfection of generosity, the perfection of moral discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, and sixth, the perfection of wisdom.[356]

d.div: [603] sde dge_70_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ca_lag bzangs kyis zhus pa'i mdo/ shog_154_na6
[356] Subāhuparipṛcchāsūtra, Toh 70 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ca 154a6.

f.d: pha rol tu phyin pa drug po 'di dag kyang bsdus don rnam par bzhag pa dang / yan lag rgyas par bshad pa la gnyis kyis shes par bya'o/ /

One should understand these six perfections in two ways: (1) through a summarized explanation or an overview, treating them as a group, /147/ and (2) through a detailed explanation of the individual perfections.

dang po bsdus don rnam par gzhag pa la/ sdoms ni/
grangs nges go rim nges pa dang / / mtshan nyid dang ni nges tshig dang / rab tu dbye dang bsdu ba ste/ / drug gis pha rol phyin drug bsdus/ / zhes pa'o//

First to present the summary, the synopsis is this:
The six perfections are summarized through six topics: their definite number, definite order, essential characteristics, etymology, subdivisions, and groupings.

de la pha rol tu phyin pa drug tu grangs nges pa ni/ mngon mtho dang nges legs kyi dbang du byas pa ste/ mngon mtho'i don gsum dang / nges legs kyi don gsum mo/ / de la mngon mtho'i don gsum ni/ longs spyod kyi don du sbyin pa'o/ / lus kyi don du tshul khrims so/ / 'khor gyi don du bzod pa'o/ / nges legs kyi don gsum ni/ yon tan 'phel bar byed pa'i don du brtson 'grus so/ / zhi gnas kyi don du bsam gtan no/ / lhag mthong gi don du shes rab bo/ /

First, their definite number is six. In terms of higher states of rebirth and liberation, there are three conducive to higher rebirth and three conducive to liberation. Of the three that lead to higher states, the perfection of generosity nurtures material prosperity, the perfection of moral discipline nurtures a good physical existence, and the perfection of patience nurtures a favorable environment.[357] Of the three that lead to liberation, the perfection of diligence nurtures increase of qualities, the perfection of meditative concentration nurtures tranquility (śamatha), and the perfection of wisdom—the prajñāpāramitā—nurtures deep insight (vipaśyanā).

d.div: [357] “Environment” is to be taken here in the widest sense of people, life circumstances, and places.

f.d:
de ltar yang mdo sde rgyan las/
longs spyod dang lus phun sum tshogs pa dang / 'khor ni phun sum tshogs pa mngon mtho dang /[604] / zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs so/ /

The Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
Higher states—the best possible prosperity, body, and retinue. [358]

d.div: [604] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 17_sh+loka_2_shog_21_na6
[358] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 17:2, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 21a6.

f.d: go rim nges pa ni/ rgyud la skye ba'i go rim ste/ sbyin pas longs spyod la mi blta bar tshul khrims yang dag par len no/ / tshul khrims dang ldan na bzod par 'gyur ro/ / bzod pa dang ldan pas brtson 'grus rtsom nus so/[605] / brtson 'grus brtsams na ting nge 'dzin skye bar 'gyur ro/ / ting nge 'dzin la mnyam par bzhag na yang dag pa ji lta ba bzhin du rab tu shes so/ / yang na dman pa dang mchog gi go rim ste/ gang dman pa ni sngon du bstan la mchog tu gnas pa ni phyis bstan pa'o// yang na phra ba dang rags pa'i go rim ste/ gang rags rags su gyur pa 'jug sla sla ni sngon du bstan la/ gang phra phrar gyur pa 'jug dka' dka' ni phyis bstan pa'o/ /

Second, the perfections occur in a definite order. First, there is the order in which they develop within the mental continuum of a person. Generosity enables proper conduct without concern for material well-being. Possessing moral discipline, patience can be cultivated. Through patience, diligence is enabled. Through diligence, meditative concentration can be developed. The mind that rests skillfully in meditative concentration will know properly the true nature of phenomena, just as it is. Alternatively, the order of sequence could be considered in terms of the gradual progression from lesser to higher. The lesser are those explained first, and those founded in what is nobler are explained subsequently. Or the order of sequence relates to the gradual progression from the grosser to the subtler. That which is grosser is easier to engage in and is thus presented earlier, while those that are subtler, because of their being more difficult to engage in, are presented later.

d.div: [605] brtsom/ dpal spungs/

f.d:
de ltar yang mdo sde rgyan las/
snga ma la brten phyi ma skye/ / dman dang mchog tu gnas phyir dang / / rags pa dang ni phra ba'i phyir/ / de dag rim pas gnas pa yin/[606] / zhes gsungs so//

In this regard, the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
The latter arises on the basis of what comes before; and since some are inferior and others superior, some grosser and others subtler, they abide in their respective sequence.[359]

d.div: [606] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 17_sh+loka_14_shog_21_ba7

f.d: byang chub sems dpa'i sbyin pa la sogs pa pha rol tu phyin pa rnams kyi mtshan nyid ni rnam pa bzhi ldan yin te/ mi mthun pa'i phyogs nyams dman par byed pa dang /[607] rnam par mi rtog pa'i ye shes bskyed pa dang / 'dod pa thams cad rdzogs par byed pa dang / sems can rnams yongs su smin par byed pa rnam pa gsum mo/ /

The third point concerns the four essential characteristics of bodhisattva generosity and the other perfections: (1) They diminish the strength of the unfavorable forces; (2) they enable the arising of pristine awareness, utterly free of concepts; (3) they bring perfect accomplishment of aspirations; /148/ and (4) they bring sentient beings to their full maturity in three ways [of the vehicles].

d.div: [607] nyams dmas/ dpal spungs/

f.d:
de ltar yang mdo sde rgyan las/
sbyin pa mi mthun phyogs nyams dang / / rnam par mi rtog ye shes ldan/ / 'dod pa thams cad yongs rdzogs byed/ / sems can rnam smin byed rnam gsum/[608] / zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs so//

The Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says of this:
Generosity curtails unfavorable forces, brings nonconceptual pristine awareness, perfectly fulfils all wishes, and brings beings to maturity in three ways.[360]

d.div: [608] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 17_sh+loka_8_shog_21_ba3

f.d: nges tshig ni/ dbul ba 'dor bar byed pas na sbyin pa'o/ / bsil ba thob par byed pas na tshul khrims so/ / khro ba bzod par byed pas na bzod pa'o/ / mchog la sbyor bar byed pas na brtson 'grus so/ / yid nang du 'dzin par byed pas na bsam gtan no/ / 'dis don dam pa shes pas na shes rab bo/ / 'di rnams kyis 'khor ba'i pha rol mya ngan las 'das par byed pas na pha rol tu phyin pa'o/[609] /

The fourth point relates to the etymology of the perfections. Since it clears away suffering, it is generosity;[361] since it is the attainment of coolness, it is moral discipline; since it copes with [what would cause] anger, it is patience; since it is application to that which is sublime, it is diligence; since it keeps the mind turned inward, it is meditative concentration; and since it causes awareness of that which is ultimate and meaningful, it is wisdom. Since all of them transport one to the far shore of samsara—namely, to nirvana—they are referred to as “what lead to the other shore” ( pāramitā).

d.div: [609] 'das par phyin par/ dpal spungs/

[361] This, and the following etymologies, are those of the Sanskrit terms for the perfections. Dāna, the Sanskrit for generosity, comes from a root meaning “to sweep away,” the implication being that it sweeps away greed and clinging. Coolness was a sought-after quality in hot India, and the relief of śīla (moral discipline) is compared to the shade of a cool tree in contrast to the searing summer heat of the passions. There is not a precise match in English for the broad uses of the word kṣānti (patience) as understood in Buddhism. Patience here is not a static waiting but refers to an ability to dynamically cope with situations that may otherwise trigger anger. Similarly, no single English term seems to translate the various implications of the Sanskrit vīrya, which means “energetic,” “efficient,” or “courageous”—all relevant meanings (see chapter 15 on diligence below). The Tibetan brtson ’grus means “industrious diligence.” The etymology of “diligence” takes us to the Latin diligere, denoting a sense of joy (the same root as “delight”), and to find joy in Dharma lies at the heart of this perfection and leads automatically to industrious perseverance.

f.d:
de ltar yang / mdo sde rgyan las/
dbul ba 'dor bar byed pa dang / / bsil ba thob dang khro bzod dang / / mchog sbyor ba dang yid 'dzin dang / / don dam shes pa'i phyir bshad do/[610] / zhes gsungs so//

In this regard the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras states:
Since through them one eliminates poverty, obtains coolness, forbears wrath, connects with supreme goal, retains the mind, and knows the ultimate, they’re thus termed.[362]

d.div: [610] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 17_sh+loka_15_shog_21_ba7
[362] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 17:15, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 21b7.

f.d:
rab tu dbye ba ni/ sbyin pa'i sbyin pa/ sbyin pa'i tshul khrims la sogs pa pha rol tu phyin pa re re la yang drug drug tu dbye ste/ de ltar sum cu rtsa drug go / de ltar yang mngon rtogs rgyan las/
sbyin pa la sogs rnam drug la/ / de dag so sor bsdus pa yis/ / go cha'i sgrub pa gang yin de/ / drug tshan drug gis ji bzhin bshad/[611] / ces gsungs so//

The fifth point concerns the six subdivisions within each of the perfections—the generosity of generosity, the moral discipline of generosity, and so forth, thus giving rise to thirty-six subdivisions. The Ornament of Clear Realization says:
With respect to the six perfections, generosity and so forth, each encompassing a sixfold division, this armor-like complete means of attainment is explained exactly in terms of six sets of six.[363]

d.div: [611] sde dge_3786_bstan/ sher phyin/ ka_byams pa mgon po/ mngon rtogs rgyan/ skabs/ 1_sh+loka_43_shog_3_ba4
[363] Maitreya, Abhisamayālaṃkāra 1:43, Toh 3786 Tengyur, shes phyin, ka, 3b4.

f.d: bsdu ba ni tshogs rnam pa gnyis su bsdus pa ste/ sbyin pa dang tshul khrims bsod nams kyi tshogs yin/ shes rab ye shes kyi tshogs yin/ bzod pa dang / brtson 'grus dang / bsam gtan gsum tshogs gnyis kar gtogs pa yin no/ /

The sixth point examines their groupings. They fall into two groups based on the two accumulations. Generosity and moral discipline belong to the accumulation of merit. Wisdom belongs to the accumulation of pristine awareness. Patience, diligence, and meditative concentration belong to both.

de ltar mdo sde rgyan las/
sbyin dang tshul khrims bsod nams kyi/ / tshogs yin shes rab ye shes kyi/ / gsum po gzhan ni gnyis ka'i ste/[612] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Thus the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
Generosity and moral discipline belong to the accumulation of merit, while wisdom belongs to the accumulation of pristine awareness, and the remaining three belong to both.[364]

d.div: [612] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 19_sh+loka_39_shog_30_na1
[364] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 19:39, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 30a1.

f.d: dam chos yid bzhin gyi nor bu thar pa rin po che'i rgyan las/ pha rol tu phyin pa drug gi rnam gzhag bstan pa'i le'u ste bcu gcig pa'o// //
This then concludes the presentation of the six perfections, the eleventh chapter of the Ornament of Precious Liberation, a Wish-Fulfilling Gem of Sublime Dharma. /149/
(pha rol tu phyin pa drug rgyas par bshad pa/)
le'u bcu gnyis pa/ sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa/
12. The Perfection of Generosity

yan lag rgyas par bshad pa la drug las/ dang po sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa la/ sdom ni/
skyon yon rnam gnyis bsam pa dang / / ngo bo dang ni dbye ba dang / / phye ba so so'i mtshan nyid dang / / spel dang dag par bya ba dang / / 'bras bu dang ni don bdun gyis/ / sbyin pa'i pha rol phyin bsdus so/ / zhes pa'o/ /

de la dang po bshad na/ gang zhig sbyin pa dang mi ldan na rang yang rtag tu bkren pas sdug bsngal te/ phal cher yi dwags su skye la/ gal te mi la sogs par skyes na yang / dbul zhing 'phongs nas nyam thag par 'gyur ba'o/ / de ltar yang 'phags pa sdud pa las/
ser sna can ni yi dwags gnas su skye bar 'gyur/ / ci ste mir skyes na yang de tshe dbul por 'gyur/[613] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The first point is reflections on the drawbacks of its absence and the benefits of its practice. A person lacking generosity will constantly suffer from poverty. Rebirth among hungry spirits is most likely, but should there be human rebirth, the person will be poverty-stricken. The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom says of this:
The miserly will be reborn among hungry spirits. Even if reborn human, they will be poor.[365]

d.div: [613] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ le'u/ 31_sh+loka_11_shog_19_na1
[365] Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā, Toh 13 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 19a1.

f.d:
'dul ba lung las kyang / gro bzhin skyes la yi dwags kyis lan btab pa/
bdag cag ser snas 'jungs pa can/ / sbyin pa cung zad ma btang ste/ / bdag cag yi dwags 'jig rten lhags/[614] / zhes 'byung ngo / /

Also in the Basis of Vinaya, we also find the following where a hungry spirit responds to the questions of Śroṇa:
“We who are ridden with miserliness never practiced giving even the slightest. Thus we are condemned to this hungry spirit state.”[366]

d.div: [614] sde dge_1_bka'/ 'dul ba/ ka_'dul ba/ ko lpags gyi gzhi/ shog_256_na6
[366] Vinayavastu, Toh 1 Kangyur, ’dul ba, ka, 256a6. See the summary of Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa’s story in note 133 above.

f.d:
yang sbyin pa dang mi ldan na/ gzhan don yang mi nus la/ byang chub kyang mi thob bo/ / de ltar yang /
sbyin gtong ma myong longs spyod med/ / sems can bsdu bar yongs mi nus/ / byang chub thob pa lta ci smos/[615] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Furthermore, without generosity, a person can neither help others nor achieve budddhahood. So it is said:
Those unaccustomed to giving are without wealth and have no power at all to gather beings to them, so what need is there even to consider their chances of reaching enlightenment?[367]

d.div: [615] gong mtshungs/ ko lpags gyi gzhi/ shog_256_ba7

f.d:
de las bzlog ste sbyin pa dang ldan na rang yang skye ba thams cad du longs spyod dang ldan nas bde ba thob pa yin no/ / de ltar yang 'phags pa sdud pa las/
byang chub sems dpa'i sbyin pas yi dwags 'gro ba gcod/ / dbul ba dang ni de bzhin nyon mongs thams cad gcod/ / spyod tshe longs spyod mtha' yas rgyas pa thob par 'gyur/[616] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The opposite of this is that generous people will be happy due to having plentiful possessions throughout all their existences. The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom says:
Bodhisattva generosity severs the possibilities of rebirth as a hungry spirit. It will abolish poverty and destroy all afflictions. Giving will bring limitless and tremendous wealth.[368]

d.div: [616] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ le'u/ 32_sh+loka_1_shog_19_ba1
[368] Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā, Toh 13 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 19b1.

f.d:
bshes spring las kyang /
sbyin pa tshul bzhin brtsal gyis pha rol tu/ / sbyin las gzhan pa'i gnyen mchog ma mchis so/[617] / zhes gsungs so/ /

d.div: [617] sde dge_4182_bstan/ spring yig_nge _mgon po klu sgrub/ bshes spring / sh+loka_6_shog_41_na2
[369] Nāgārjuna, Suhṛllekha verse 6cd, Toh 4182 Tengyur, spring yig, nge, 41a2.

f.d:
dbu ma 'jug pa las kyang /
skye bo 'di kun bde ba mngon 'dod cing / mi rnams bde ba'ang longs spyod med min la/ / longs spyod kyang ni sbyin las 'byung mkhyen nas/ / thub pas dang por sbyin pa'i gtam mdzad do/[618] / zhes gsungs so//

d.div: [618] sde dge_3861_bstan/ dbu ma/ 'a_zla ba grags pa/ dbu ma 'jug pa/ sems bskyed/ 1_sh+loka_10_shog_202_na2
[370] Candrakīrti, Madhyamakāvatāra 1:10, Toh 3861 Tengyur, dbu ma, ’a, 202a2.

f.d:
yang sbyin pa dang ldan na gzhan don bya ba yang nus te/ sbyin pas bsdus nas dam chos la dgod du yod do/ / de ltar yang /
sbyin pas sdug bsngal gyur pa'i sems can yongs smin byed/[619]/ ces gsungs so/ /

Generosity also brings the ability to help others. Those drawn to someone through generosity can then be established in sublime Dharma. So it is said:
It is through generosity that suffering beings are brought to full maturity.[371]

d.div: [619] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ le'u/ 32_sh+loka_1_shog_19_ba1
[371] Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā, Toh 13 Kangyur, sher spyin, ka, 19b1.

f.d:
yang sbyin pa dang ldan na bla med kyi byang chub kyang bsgrub par sla ba yin no/ / de ltar yang byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod las/
sbyin pa gtong la byang chub rnyed mi dka'/[620] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Furthermore, being generous makes it easier to achieve enlightenment. The Bodhisattva Collection says:
Enlightenment is not hard to find for those who have been generous.[372]

d.div: [620] sde dge_56_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ga_byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod/ le'u/ 6_shog_61_na3
[372] Bodhisattvapiṭaka, Toh 56 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ga, 61a3.

f.d:
'phags pa dkon mchog sprin las kyang /
sbyin pa ni byang chub sems dpa'i byang chub bo/[621] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Also the Clouds of Jewels Sutra says:
Generosity brings about the enlightenment of a bodhisattva.[373]

d.div: [621] sde dge_231_bka'/ mdo sde/ wa_dkon mchog sprin gyi mdo/ shog_12_na7
[373] Ratnameghasūtra, Toh 231 Kangyur, mdo sde, wa, 12a7.

f.d:
yang khyim bdag drag shul can gyis zhus pa'i mdo las/ byin pa'i yon tan dang ma byin pa'i skyon rnams spel mar gsungs te/ ji skad du/
gang byin pa de ni bdag gi yin no/ / gang khyim na bzhag pa de ni bdag gi ma yin no/ / gang byin pa de ni snying po can no/ / gang khyim na bzhag pa de ni snying po med pa'o/ / gang byin pa de ni bsrung mi 'tshal ba'o/ / gang khyim na gzhag pa de ni bsrung 'tshal ba'o/ / gang byin pa de ni 'jigs pa med pa'o/ / gang khyim na gzhag pa de ni 'jigs pa dang bcas pa'o/ / gang byin pa de ni byang chub kyi lam nye bar ston pa'o/ / gang khyim na bzhag pa de ni bdud kyi phyogs nye bar ston pa'o/ / gang byin pa de ni longs spyod chen por 'gyur ro/ / gang khyim na bzhag pa de ni longs spyod chen por mi 'gyur ro/ / gang byin pa de ni longs spyod zad mi shes pa'o// gang khyim na bzhag pa de ni zad par 'gyur ro/[622] / zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs so//

Further, we find a presentation of the drawbacks of a lack of generosity and the advantages of its practice interspersed in the Questions of the Layman Ugra Sutra:
What I have given is mine; what I have hoarded is not mine. What has been given has purpose; what is hoarded is pointless. That which has been given does not require protection; what is hoarded does. What has been given brings no anxiety; whatever is hoarded is accompanied by worries. What has been given shows the way to buddhahood; what is hoarded shows the quick way to evil. Giving will bring great wealth, and hoarding will not. Giving will never know the end of wealth; hoarding will exhaust it.[374]

d.div: [622] sde dge_63_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ nga _khyim bdag drag shul can gyis zhus pa'i mdo/ shog_264_ba5
[374] Gṛhapatyugraparipṛcchāsūtra, Toh 63 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, nga, 264b5.

f.d:
sbyin pa'i ngo bo ni ma chags pa'i sems kyis bdog pa yongs su gtong ba'o/ / de ltar yang byang sa las/
sbyin pa'i ngo bo nyid gang zhe na/ ma chags pa dang lhan cig skyes pa'i sems gang yin pa dang / des kun nas bslang ba sbyin par bya ba'i dngos po yongs su gtong ba'o/[623] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The second point is its nature. Generosity means to give completely, with an unattached mind. Bodhisattva Levels says:
What is the essence of generosity? It is to give what is appropriate to be given on the basis of being motivated by mental states that arise together with nonattachment.[375]

d.div: [623] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 9_shog_61_ba4
[375] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 61b4.

f.d: sbyin pa la dbye na gsum ste/ zang zing gi sbyin pa dang / mi 'jigs pa'i sbyin pa dang / chos kyi sbyin pa'o/ / de la zang zing gi sbyin pas ni gzhan gyi lus brtan par byed pa'o/ / mi 'jigs pa'i sbyin pas ni gzhan gyi srog brtan par byed pa'o/ / chos kyi sbyin pas ni gzhan gyi sems brtan par byed pa'o/ / yang sbyin pa dang po gnyis kyis ni gzhan la tshe 'di'i bde ba bsgrub pa yin la/ chos kyi sbyin pas ni phyi ma'i bde ba bsgrub pa yin no//

The third point concerns its different aspects. There are three: giving material necessities, giving freedom from fear, and giving the Dharma. Of these, giving material necessities strengthens others’ physical existence, giving freedom from fear strengthens the quality of other’s lives, and giving the Dharma strengthens their minds. Furthermore, the first two kinds of generosity bring well-being to others in this life, /151/ whereas the gift of Dharma brings well-being for [both this and] future lives.

de dag so so'i mtshan nyid bshad na/ dang po zang zing gi sbyin pa la gnyis te/ ma dag pa'i sbyin pa dang / dag pa'i sbyin pa'o/ / de yang dang po ni spang bar bya ba'o/ / gnyis pa ni nyams su blang bar bya ba'o/ /
The fourth point develops the essential characteristics of each aspect. Giving material necessities is itself of two kinds, proper and improper, the former to be cultivated and the latter abandoned.

de la yang ma dag pa'i sbyin pa ni bzhi ste/[624] bsam pa ma dag pa dang / dngos po ma dag pa dang / zhing ma dag pa dang / thabs ma dag pa'o/ / de la bsam pa ma dag pa ni/ log pa'i bsam pa dang / dman pa'i bsam pa'o/ / de la log pa'i bsam pas sbyin pa gtong ba ni/ gzhan la gnod pa'i phyir sbyin pa dang / tshe 'di'i grags pa 'dod pa'i phyir sbyin pa dang / gzhan dang 'gran pa'i phyir sbyin pa'o/ /

Improper material giving is discussed in terms of four aspects: improper motivation, inappropriate gifts, inappropriate receiver, and an improper way of giving. An improper motivation can be either a distorted motivation or an inferior one. Giving out of distorted motivation is giving in order to harm others, to gain fame, or because of competition.

d.div: [624] sbyin pa la/ dpal spungs/

f.d:
de gsum yang byang chub sems dpas spang ste/ ji skad du byang sa las/
byang chub sems dpa' ni gzhan dag bsad pa'am/ bcings pa'am/ chad pas bcad pa'am/ go rar gzhug pa'am/ bskrad pa'i phyir sbyin pa sbyin par mi byed do/[625] / zhes pa dang /
byang chub sems dpa' ni grags pa dang tshigs su bcad pa'i phyir sbyin pa sbyin par mi byed do/ / zhes pa dang /
byang chub sems dpa' ni gzhan la 'gran pa'i phyir yang sbyin pa sbyin par mi byed do/[626] / zhes gsungs so/ /

A bodhisattva should renounce all three. Bodhisattva Levels says:
Bodhisattvas should not give in order that others be killed, tied up, punished, imprisoned, or banished.[376] and
Bodhisattvas should not give in order to acquire fame or be praised.[377] and
Bodhisattvas should not give in order to compete with others.[378]

d.div: [625] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 9_shog_63_ba5
[626] gong mtshungs/ byang chub sems dpa'i sa/ le'u/ 9_shog_73_na6

f.d:
dman pa'i sbyin pa ni/ tshe phyi ma la dbul gyis dogs nas sbyin pa dang / lha mi'i lus dang longs spyod 'dod nas sbyin pa'o/ / de gnyis ka yang byang chub sems dpas mi bya ste/ ji skad du/
byang chub sems dpa' ni dbul por 'gyur du dogs pa'i 'jigs pas sbyin pa sbyin par mi byed do/[627]/ zhes pa dang /
byang chub sems dpa' ni brgya byin nyid dang / 'khor los sgyur ba nyid dang / dbang phyug la brten zhing sbyin pa sbyin par mi byed do/[628] / zhes gsungs so//

Giving through inferior motivation means practicing generosity through fear of poverty in future lives or through hoping for it to be the cause of future human or divine rebirth and future wealth. Bodhisattvas should not have these two types of motivation. It says:
Bodhisattvas should not give through fear of poverty.
Bodhisattvas should not give in order to gain the backing of Indra, a universal monarch, or Īśvara.[379]

d.div: [627] gong mtshungs/ byang chub sems dpa'i sa/ le'u/ 9_shog_65_ba3
[628] gong mtshungs/ byang chub sems dpa'i sa/ le'u/ 9_shog_66_na1

f.d: ma dag pa'i sbyin pa gzhan rnams kyang / byang sa las spang bar gsungs te/ de dag gi don bsdu na/ dngos po ma dag pa spang ba ni/ byang chub sems dpas dug dang me dang mtshon cha la sogs pa/ len pa po kho rang la gnod par bya ba'am/ pha rol la gnod pa'i phyir slong na sbyin par mi byed do/ /[629]

Bodhisattva Levels discusses other kinds of improper giving as well. To summarize, inappropriate giving that needs to be abandoned involves giving of fire, poison, weapons, and the like, which can harm either their receiver or someone else.[380] /152/

d.div:
[629] rin chen phreng ba las/
gang la dug ni phan gyur na/ / de la dug kyang sbyin par bya/ / kha zas mchog kyang mi phan na/ / de la de ni sbyin mi bya/ / sbrul gyis zin pa ji lta bur/ / sor mo bcad pa phan bshad pa/ / de ni thub pas gzhan phan la/ / mi bde ba yang bya bar gsungs/ / slong na sbyin par mi byed do/ / zhes gsungs so/ / [*] sde dge_4158_bstan/ spring yig_ge_mgon po klu sgrub/ rin chen phreng ba/ le'u/ 3_sh+loka_64_shog_116_ba7_slong na sbyin na sbyin par mi byed do/ /zhes gsungs so/ /zhes pa'i tshig 'di ma dpe dang mi rigs dpe skrun gnyis kar mi byung /

[380] There is the following in parenthetical passage in the Tibetan original, perhaps added by a later editor: “The Precious Garland says:
‘Should poison benefit someone, then poison should be given. If it is not beneficial to the person, even the best food should not be given. It is said that chopping off a finger bitten by a poisonous snake is beneficial; the Buddha taught that even unpleasant things should be done if they benefit others.’” Nāgārjuna, Ratnāvalī 3:63–64, Toh 4158 Tengyur, spring yig, ge, 116b7.

f.d: rgya dang rngon gyi 'khrul 'khor dang de'i thabs la sogs pa mdor na gnod par 'gyur ba dang sdug bsngal du 'gyur ba ci yang rung ba de dag thams cad slong ba rnams la sbyin par mi byed do/ /
Bodhisattvas should not respond to requests for snares, hunting devices, and so forth—in brief, for whatever may harm others.

pha dang ma sbyin par mi byed do/ / pha dang ma gta' mar 'jug par mi byed do// bu dang chung ma la sogs pa mi dga' bzhin du gzhan 'dod pa rnams la sbyin par mi byed do/ / longs spyod mang po yod bzhin du nyung ngu sbyin par mi byed do/ / bsags pa'i sbyin pa mi byed do/ /

They should not give away their parents or use them as collateral. They should not give away a nonconsenting spouse or offspring. A person of much wealth should not give little. Communal wealth should not be misused as charity.

zhing ma dag pa spang ba ni/ bdud rigs kyi lha mtho 'tshams pa'i bsam pas lus slong na yang / rang gi lus dang yan lag gse zhing sbyin par mi byed do/ / bdud kyis byin gyis brlabs pa'i sems can rnams smyos pa dang sems 'khrugs pa'i sems can rnams la yang lus sbyin par mi byed do/[630] / de dag ni 'dod pa'i dngos po med de/ sems la rang dbang med pa'i phyir bla brdol tsam du zad do/ / sems can 'grangs ngoms can la yang bza' btung sbyin par mi byed do/ /

Abandoning inappropriate recipients refers to the following. Even though demons with harmful intentions may beg you for your body, you should give neither it nor parts of it to them. Neither should you give your body to those who are under the sway of demons or to those who are mad or temporarily deranged. Their need is not real: they are irresponsible, and their words are for the most part nonsense. It is not generosity to give food and drink to those who are well sated.

d.div: [630] sems can nam/ dpal spungs/

f.d: thabs ma dag pa spang ba ni/ mi dga' ba dang khros pa dang 'khrugs pas sbyin pa sbyin par mi byed do/ / ngan pa la brnyas pa dang / ma gus pa dang sbyar te sbyin pa sbyin par mi byed do/ / slong ba la yang 'phya ba dang / bsdig pa dang /[631] spa bkong bas sbyin pa sbyin par mi byed do//

Abandoning an improper manner of giving means that it is not a correct generosity to give reluctantly, to be angry about the giving, or to give with a disturbed mind. A person should not give to the deprived in a state of contempt or disrespect for them; neither should he dishearten, threaten, or deride the person begging.

d.div: [631] sdigs pa dang / dpal spungs/

f.d:
dag pa'i sbyin pa nyams su blang ba la don gsum ste/ dngos po dang / zhing dang / thabs so/ / dang po la yang gnyis te/ nang gi dngos po dang / phyi'i dngos po'o/ / de la nang gi dngos po ni/ rang gi lus su gtogs pa ste/ de ltar yang sred med kyi bus zhus pa'i mdo las/
yod de yod na lag pa 'dod pa la lag pa sbyin no/ / rkang pa 'dod pa la rkang pa/ mig 'dod pa la mig / sha 'dod pa la sha/ khrag 'dod pa la khrag[632] / ces pa la sogs pa gsungs so/ /

As for the practice of proper [material] giving, [first] there are three points—the objects, the recipient, and the manner of giving. The first, in turn, is explained in terms of “inner” and “outer” objects. The inner ones are body-related. For example, the Questions of Nārāyaṇa Sutra says:
If it is beneficial to give and if a person’s attitude is pure, a hand can be given if a hand is required, a leg if a leg is required, an eye if an eye is required, flesh if that is what is needed, and blood if that is required.[381]

d.div: [632] sde dge_134_bka'/ mdo sde/ na_sred med kyi bus zhus pa'i mdo/ mtshan gzhan bsod nams thams cad bsdus pa'i ting nge 'dzin zhes bya ba'i mdo/ shog_85_na5
[381] The Questions of Nārāyaṇa Sutra is another title for the Sutra of the Absorption that Gathers All Merit (Sarvapuṇyasamuccayasamādhisūtra), Toh 134 Kangyur, mdo sde, na, 85a5.

f.d:
de yang byang chub sems dpa' las dang po pas bdag gzhan mnyam pa'i blo ma skyes pa'i dus su lus ril por btang gis/ lus bsel zhing mi btang ngo /[633] / de ltar yang spyod 'jug las/
snying rje'i bsam pa ma dag par// lus 'di btang bar mi bya ste/ / ci nas 'di dang gzhan don du/ / don chen 'grub pa'i rgyur btang ngo /[634] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Those bodhisattvas on the beginner’s stage who have not yet realized the mental state of equalizing and exchanging of self and others may give their body in its entirety, not through separating it into bits and pieces. The Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life says of this:
Without a pure mind of compassion do not give away your body; that would be to give up the basis for achieving very great goals in this life and the next.[382] /153/

d.div: [633] lus gse/ dpal spungs/
[634] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 5_sh+loka_87_shog_13_ba4
[382] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 3:87, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 13b4.

f.d:
phyi'i dngos po ni/ bza' ba dang btung ba dang / gso ba dang bzhon pa dang /[635] bu dang chung ma la sogs pa chos bzhin du sgrub pa rnams so/[636] / de ltar yang sred med kyi bus zhus pa'i mdo las/
phyi rol gyi dngos po 'di lta ste/ nor dang / 'bru dang / dngul dang / gser dang / rin po che dang / rgyan dang / rta dang / glang po che dang / bu dang / bu mo dang /[637] zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs so/ /

The outer objects are food, drink, or whatever else nourishes steeds, children, spouse, and so forth that have been acquired in a way that accords with Dharma. The Questions of Nārāyanā Sutra says:
What is “outer objects”? It is the likes of wealth, grain, silver, gold, jewelry, ornaments, horses, elephants, sons, daughters.[383]

d.div: [635] bgo ba/ dpal spungs/
[636] bsgrub/ dpal spungs/
[637] sde dge_134_bka'/ mdo sde/ na_sred med kyi bus zhus pa'i mdo/ mtshan gzhan bsod nams thams cad bsdus pa'i ting nge 'dzin zhes bya ba'i mdo/ shog_83_ba7
[383] A.k.a. Sutra of the Absorption that Gathers All Merit (Sarvapuṇyasamuccayasamādhisūtra), Toh 134 Kangyur, mdo sde, na, 83b7.

f.d:
de yang byang chub sems dpa' khyim pas ni phyi nang gi dngos po bdog tshad btang bar gnang ste/ mdo sde rgyan las/
byang chub sems dpa' lus dang longs spyod dag/ gzhan la mi sbyin pa ni yong med do/[638] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Lay bodhisattvas are permitted to give away whatever inner or outer gifts they possess. The Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
There is nothing that a bodhisattva would not give to others, be it his body, wealth and so on[384]

d.div: [638] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 9_sh+loka_16_shog_8_na5
[384] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 9:16, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 8a5.

f.d:
byang chub sems dpa' rab tu byung bas ni gzhan thams cad btang gi /chos gos gsum po de ni sbyin par ma gnang ngo / / de ltar yang spyod 'jug las/
chos gos gsum ma gtogs pa sbyin/[639] / zhes gsungs te/ chos gos rnams byin na gzhan don nyams par 'gyur bas so//

Ordained bodhisattvas are allowed to give everything except their three Dharma robes. In Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life, we read:
One should give everything except the three Dharma robes.[385] This is because giving away these three robes could undermine your work for the benefit of beings.

d.div: [639] sde dge_3871_bstan/ dbu ma/ la_zhi ba lha/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 5_sh+loka_85_shog_13_ba3
[385] Śāntideva, Bodhicaryāvatāra 5:85d, Toh 3871 Tengyur, dbu ma, la, 13b3.

f.d:
zhing ni bzhi las/ yon tan gyis khyad par du byas pa'i zhing ni/ bla ma dang dkon mchog la sogs pa'o/ / phan btags pas khyad par du byas pa'i zhing ni/ pha dang ma la sogs pa'o/ / sdug bsngal bas khyad par du byas pa'i zhing ni/ nad pa dang / mgon med pa la sogs pa'o/ / gnod pa byed pas khyad par du byas pa'i zhing ni dgra la sogs pa'o/ / de ltar yang spyod 'jug las/
yon tan dang ni phan 'dogs shing /[640] / zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs so//

As for the recepient, there are four types: (1) those particularly designated by their qualities—gurus, the Three Jewels, and so forth; (2) those particularly designated by the benefit they have brought—father, mother, and so forth; (3) those particularly designated by their sufferings—the sick, the unprotected, and so forth; and (4) those particularly designated by the harm they have done—enemies and so forth. The Guide to the Bodhisattva Way of Life says,
If one strives in the arenas of qualities, benefits, and suffering, great good will ensue.[386]

d.div: [640] gong mtshungs/ spyod 'jug_le'u/ 5_sh+loka_81_shog_13_ba1

f.d:
sbyin pa btang ba'i thabs ni/ bsam pa phun sum tshogs pas sbyin pa dang / sbyor ba phun sum tshogs pas sbyin pa'o/ / de la dang po ni snying rjes kun nas bslang nas byang chub dang sems can gyi don du sbyin pa'o/ / sbyor ba phun sum tshogs pas sbyin pa ni/ ji skad du/
byang chub sems dpa' ni dad pa dang / bkur sti dang / rang gi lag pa dang / dus la bab pa dang / gzhan la mi gnod par sbyin pa sbyin par byed do/[641] / zhes byang sa las gsungs so/ /

Concerning the way in which the gift is given, (1) there is the giving with the very best of intentions and (2) through the best act of giving. The first consists of giving with a compassionate motivation to attain enlightenment and to benefit beings. As for the second, giving through the best possible action, it is said in Bodhisattva Levels:
A bodhisattva should give joyfully, with respect, by one’s own hand, at the right time, and without harming others.[387]

d.div: [641] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ le'u/ 1_shog_71_ba7
[387] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 71b7.

f.d: de la dang po ni/ dus gsum du dga' ba dang ldan pa ste/ sbyin pa'i snga rol du yid dga' ba dang sbyin pa'i tshe sems dang ba dang / byin zin nas 'gyod pa med pa'o/ / bkur sti ni gus pas sbyin pa'o/ / rang gi lag pa ni gzhan la ma bcol bar sbyin pa'o/ / dus la bab pa ni rang gis thob pa'i dus su sbyin pa'o/ / gzhan la mi gnod pa ni/ rang gi 'khor dang yongs su 'dzin pa dang bcas pa rnams la mi gnod par sbyin pa'o/ / de yang rang gi rdzas yin yang rdzas sgrub pa'i 'khor rnams gdong mchi ma dang bcas par gyur na yang sbyin par mi byed do/ / yongs su 'dzin pa dang bcas pa'i nor 'phrog gam/[642] brkus sam/ bsnyon nas kyang sbyin par mi byed do/ /

The first of these means to be joyful about giving during all three periods of the act—that is, to be glad about it before giving, to give with clear-minded joy, and to have no regrets once the giving has been done. “With respect” means with respect for the receiver. “By one’s own hand” means not delegating the task to someone else. /154/ “At the right time” means when what is pledged has already been acquired. “Without harming others” means giving in a way that does not cause harm to your immediate circles or to their guardians. In this respect, even though the thing you are giving may be yours, if by doing so brings tears [of sadness] to the eyes of those within your immediate circles who helped acquire the article, you should not give it. Generosity should not be practiced by giving goods that have been embezzled, burgled, or misappropriated.

d.div: [642] 'phrogs sam/ dpal spungs/

f.d:
yang chos mngon pa kun las btus pa las/
phyir zhing sbyin pa dang / phyogs mi byed par sbyin pa dang / 'dod pa yongs su rdzogs par sbyin pa'i phyir ro/[643] / zhes gsungs te/

The Compendium of Higher Knowledge says:
Give again and again, give without bias, and give in order to fulfill wishes most perfectly.[388]

d.div: [643] sde dge_4049_bstan/ sems tsam/ ri_'phags pa thogs med/ mngon pa kun btus/ le'u/ 1 _9_shog_46_na1
[388] Asaṅga, Abhidharmasamuccaya, Toh 4049 Tengyur, sems tsam, ri, 16a1.

f.d: de la phyir zhing sbyin pa zhes pa ni/ sbyin bdag gi khyad par te yang dang yang du sbyin pa'o/ / phyogs mi byed par sbyin pa zhes pa ni/ zhing gi khyad par te zhing la phyogs ris med par sbyin pa'o/ / 'dod pa yongs su rdzogs par sbyin pa zhes pa ni/ dngos po'i khyad par te len pa po'i bsam pa dang mthun par ci 'dod pa sbyin pa'o/ /

In this quotation, “give again and again” is the particular quality of the donor, who should practice generosity repeatedly. “Give without bias” is the particular quality related to the receiver and means giving impartially. “Give in order to perfectly fulfill wishes” is related to the gift itself. It means giving what corresponds most closely to the expectations of the receiver.
zang zing gi sbyin pa bshad zin to/ /
This concludes the section on giving material necessities.

mi 'jigs pa'i sbyin pa ni/ chom rkun gyis 'jigs pa dang /[644] gcan zan gyis 'jigs pa dang / nad dang chu la sogs pas 'jigs pa dag gi skyabs byed pa'o/ / de ltar yang byang sa las/
mi 'jigs pa sbyin pa ni/ seng ge dang / stag dang / chu srin 'dzin 'khri dang / rgyal po dang / chom rkun dang / chu la sogs pa'i 'jigs pa las yongs su bskyab pa yin par rig par bya'o/[645] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Giving freedom from fear refers to giving protection to those who are afraid of robbers, thieves, beasts of prey, illness, water, and so forth. Bodhisattva Levels says:
The gift of fearlessness should be known as the provision of complete protection from lions, tigers, crocodiles, kings, robbers, water, and so forth.[389]

d.div: [644] dpal spungs dpar mar 'brel sgra gyi zhes byung /
[645] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ shog_72_na7
[389] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 72a7.

f.d: mi 'jigs pa'i sbyin pa bshad zin to//
This concludes the teachings on supportive generosity.

chos kyi sbyin pa la don bzhi ste/ sbyin pa'i yul dang / bsam pa dang / chos dngos dang / chos bstan pa'i thabs so/ / de la yul ni/ chos dang chos smra ba la gus pa chos 'dod pa rnams la sbyin pa'o/ / bsam pa ni ngan pa spangs shing bzang po brten pa ste/[646] de yang bsam pa ngan pa spang ba ni/ rnyed bkur dang bstod grags la sogs pa zang zing gi sems dang bral bas chos ston pa'o//

Giving the Dharma is explained through four points: (1) the person being taught, (2) the motivation, (3) giving authentic Dharma, and (4) the actual presentation. The first of these means explaining the Buddhist teaching to those who wish to hear it and who have respect both for it and for the person expounding it. As for motivation, wrong motivations are to be abandoned and only correct ones should be present. To give up wrong motivations means to teach Dharma without concern for honors, praise, or fame and to not have materialistic incentives.

d.div: [646] bsten/ dpal spungs/ 'og tu'ang skabs mang por ma dper/ brten/ zhes yod sar dpal spungs su/ bsten/ zhes byung /

f.d:
de ltar yang 'phags pa sdud pa las/
zang zing med par 'gro la chos ni rjes su ston/[647] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom says:
Without material gain one teaches the Dharma to beings.[390]

d.div: [647] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ le'u/ 17_sh+loka_3_shog_10_na5
[390] Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā, Toh 13 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 10a5.

f.d:
'od srungs kyis zhus pa'i mdo las kyang /
dag cing zang zing med pa'i sems kyis su// chos kyi sbyin byed rgyal bas rab tu bsngags/[648] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In the Kāśyapa Chapter Sutra it says:
The Buddha speaks highly of the gift of Dharma being given with a pure mind unconcerned with material gain.[391] /155/

d.div: [648] sde dge_87_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ cha_'od srung gis zhus pa'i le'u/ shog_125_ba4
[391] Kāśyapaparivartasūtra, Toh 87 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, cha, 125b4.

f.d:
bsam pa bzang po brten pa ni/ snying rjes kun nas bslangs nas chos ston pa'o/ / de ltar yang 'phags pa sdud pa las/
sdug bsngal zad par bya phyir 'jig rten chos sbyin byed/[649] / ces gsungs so/ /

Having correct motivation means that you should teach the Dharma motivated by compassion. The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom says:
One gives the Dharma to the world in order to extinguish suffering.[392]

d.div: [649] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ sh+loka_4_shog_15_na5
[392] Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā, Toh 13 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 15a5.

f.d:
chos dngos ni/ mdo la sogs pa'i don ma nor ba phyin ci ma log par ston pa ste/ byang sa las/
chos kyi sbyin pa ni/ phyin ci ma log par chos ston pa dang / rigs par chos ston pa dang / bslab pa'i gzhi yang dag par 'dzin du 'jug pa ste/[650] zhes gsungs so/ /

Giving authentic Dharma means teaching unerringly the unmistaken meaning of the sutras and other texts. Bodhisattva Levels says:
Giving the Dharma means to teach the unerring Dharma, to teach the appropriate Dharma, and to make sure that the fundamental points of training are well understood.[393]

d.div: [650] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ shog_72_ba1
[393] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 72b1.

f.d:
chos bstan pa'i thabs ni/ chos zhu ba la de ma thag tu bshad par mi bya ste/ zla ba sgron me'i mdo las/
chos kyi sbyin pa'i ched kyi phyir/ / gal te khyod la gsol 'debs na/ / rab rgyas bdag gis ma bslab ces/ / thog mar tshig de brjod par bya/[651] / zhes dang /
'phral du brjod par mi bya'o/ / snod la brtag pa byas nas bya/ / gal te snod ni shes gyur na// gsol ma btab kyang bshad par bya/[652] / zhes gsungs so//

d.div: [651] sde dge_127_bka'/ mdo sde/ da_zla ba sgron ma'i mdo/ le'u/ 25_sh+loka_44_shog_85_ba7
[652] gong mtshungs/ zla ba sgron ma'i mdo/ le'u/ 25_sh+loka_46_shog_86_na1
[394] A.k.a. King of Meditation Sutra (Samādhirājasūtra), Toh 127 Kangyur, mdo sde, da, 85b7.

f.d:
des na chos 'chad pa'i tshe yang sa phyogs gtsang ma yid du 'ong bar bshad par bya ste/ dam chos pad+ma dkar po las/
gtsang zhing yid du 'ong ba'i sa phyogs su/ / yangs pa'i gdan ni rab tu bshams bting ste/[653] / zhes gsungs so/ /

When teaching the Dharma, it should be in a clean and pleasant place. The Lotus Sutra says:
In a clean and pleasant place, arrange well a wide seat [for teaching]. . . [395]

d.div: [653] sde dge_113_bka'/ mdo sde/ ja_dam chos pad dkar gyi mdo/ le'u/ 13_sh+loka_26_shog_106_na3
[395] Saddharmapuṇḍarīkasūtra, Toh 113 Kangyur, mdo sde, ja, 106a3.

f.d:
der chos kyi khri la bsdad la bshad par bya ste/ ji skad du/
bcos bu ras rnams sna tshogs legs bting ba/ / rkang rten bcas pa'i khri la rab 'dug cing /[654] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In such a place, you should sit on a teaching throne and then expound [the Dharma]. It says:
Well seated on an elevated Dharma seat that is beautifully arranged with various pieces of cloth.[396]

d.div: [654] gong mtshungs/ dam chos pad dkar gyi mdo/ le'u/ 13_sh+loka_28_shog_106_na4
[396] King of Meditation Sutra (Samādhirājasūtra), Toh 127 Kangyur, mdo sde, da, 106a4.

f.d:
rang yang khrus bya/ gos legs par bgos/ gtsang sbra byas/ spyod lam gzabs pas chos bshad par bya'o/[655] / de ltar yang blo gros rgya mtshos zhus pa'i mdo las/
chos smra bas gtsang sbra dang / kun tu spyod pa gzobs pa dang / legs par bkrus pa dang / legs par gos bgo bar bya'o/[656] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The teacher should bathe, be properly dressed and tidy, and explain the Dharma in an appropriate demeanor. The Questions of Sāgaramati Sutra says:
One who teaches Dharma should be tidy and behave in a proper fashion. He should have bathed and be nicely attired.[397]

d.div: [655] gzob bas/ dpal spungs/ gzab pas/ mi rigs dpe skrun/
[656] sde dge_152_bka'/ mdo sde/ pha_blo gros rgya mtshos zhus pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 12_shog_110_ba7
[397] Sāgaramatiparipṛcchāsūtra, Toh 152 Kangyur, mdo sde, pha, 110b7.

f.d: de ltar 'khor ni 'khod/ khri la ni bsdad pa'i tshe thog mar bar chad kyis mi tshugs par bya ba'i phyir/ bdud kyi nus pa gzhom pa'i sngags brjod par bya ste/

When everyone has assembled and taken their seats and the person teaching is on the Dharma seat, the latter should recite the following mantra that overcomes the power of harmful influences (māra), so that their hindering power cannot obstruct the teaching.

blo gros rgya mtshos zhus pa'i mdo las/
'di lta ste/ tad+ya thA/ sha me sha me wa ti/ sha me ta sha truM/ aM ku re/ maM ku re/ mA ra dzi te ka ro Te/ ke yU re/ te dzo wa ti/ o lo ya ni/ bi shud+d+ha ni rma le ma lA pa na ye/ khu khu re/ kha kha gra se/ gra sa ne/ o mu khi/ pa raM mu khi/ a mu khi/ sha mi tA ni/ sarba gra ha b+han+d+ha nA ne/ ni gri hi twa/ sarba pA ra pra wA di na/ bi muk+ta mA ra pA sha/ s+thA pi twa/ bud+d+ha mu dra/ a nung+ga ti tA/ sarba mA re/ pu tsa ri ta pa ri shud+d+he/ bi gats+tshan+tu/ sarba mA ra karma Ni/
blo gros rgya mtsho/ sngags kyi tshig 'di dag sngon du byas te/ chos kyi gtam byas na/ de'i khor yug dpag tshad brgya tshun chad du bdud kyi rigs kyi lha rnams mtho 'tshams pa'i phyir 'ong bar mi 'gyur ro/ / gang dag 'ong ba de dag gis kyang bar chad byed par mi nus so/[657] / de nas chos kyi tshig 'brel ba gsal ba ran pa bshad par bya'o/ /

The Questions of Sāgaramati Sutra says:
It is this: Tatyathā śame śamevati śametaśatruṁ aṁkure maṁ-kure mārajite karoṭe keyūre tejovati oloyani viśuddha nirmale malāpanaye khukhure khakha grasane omukhi paraṁukhi amukhi śamitvani sarvagraha bhandhanāne nigrihitva sarva-pārapravādina vimukta mārapāśa sthāpitva buddhamudra anuṅgarirva /156/ sarva mare pucari tapari śuddhe vigacchantu sarvamāra karmaṇi
Sāgaramati! If someone recites the words of this mantra before-hand, no demons or negative forces within a radius of a hundred leagues will be able to come and harm the teaching. Even were they to manage to come, they would be unable to create an obstacle. Thereafter, the Dharma words should be explained clearly, articulately, and in just the right amount.[398]

d.div: [657] gong mtshungs/ blo gros rgya mtshos zhus pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 12_shog_111_ba1

f.d: chos kyi sbyin pa bshad zin to/ /
This concludes the explanation of Dharma generosity.

sbyin pa spel ba ni/ sbyin pa gsum po de dag nyung ngu yin yang mang por bsgyur ba'i thabs yod de/ byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod las kyang /
shA ri'i bu byang chub sems dpa' mkhas pa ni/ sbyin pa nyung ngu yang mang por byed de/ ye shes kyi stobs kyis lhag par byed do/ / shes rab kyi stobs kyis rgyas par byed do/ / bsngo ba'i stobs kyis dpag tu med par byed do/[658] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The fifth point is how generosity can be increased. There are ways of transforming even a small amount of the above three types of generosity into something much greater. In the Bodhisattva Collection it says:
Śāriputra! Skillful bodhisattvas transform a little generosity into a lot. Through the power of pristine awareness it is elevated, through the power of wisdom it is expanded, and through the power of dedication it is made immeasurable.[399]

d.div: [658] sde dge_56_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ga_byang chub sems dpa'i sde snod/ le'u/ 6_shog_60_ba6
[399] Bodhisattvapiṭaka, Toh 56 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ga, 60b6.

f.d: de la ye shes kyi stobs kyis lhag par byed pa zhes pa ni/ 'khor gsum yongs dag tu shes pa ste/ sbyin pa'i bsod nams mang po 'byung ba'i don du/ shes rab kyi stobs kyis rgyas par byed pa zhes pa ni/ sbyin pa gang gtong yang / dang por sems can thams cad sangs rgyas kyi+i sa la 'god pa'i ched du gtong / bar du sbyin pa'i dngos po la zhen pa med/ sbyin pa byed pa po yang sgyu ma lta bu/ sbyin pa'i dngos po yang sgyu ma lta bu/ sbyin par byed pa'i yul yang sgyu ma lta bu'o/ / mthar sbyin pa'i rnam smin la re ba dang bral na/ sbyin pa'i bsod nams rgyas par thob bo/ /

“The power of pristine awareness elevates it” signifies awareness of the utter purity of the three spheres [of the act of giving]. “The power of wisdom expands it” means that deep understanding is applied in order to give rise to a vast amount of merit, as follows. At the outset, whatever is given is done so in order to establish all beings in the state of buddhahood. During the giving there is no attachment to the gift itself. At the conclusion there is no expectation of good future-life consequences from giving.

'phags pa sdud pa las kyang /
sbyin pa byin nas dngos la gnas pa med par byed/ / de ni nam du'ang rnam par smin la re ba med/ / de ltar gtong ba mkhas pas thams cad gtong ba ste/ / chung ngu btang la mang por dpag tu med par 'gyur/[659] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom says:
Not making their giving something substantially existent and never practicing generosity in anticipation of its full karmic rewards—such is the way the wise and skillful practice generosity; so a little gift becomes much, to an inestimable extent.[400]

d.div: [659] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ le'u/ 22_sh+loka_14_shog_39_na3
[400] Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā, Toh 13 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 39a3.

f.d:
bsngo ba'i stobs kyis dpag tu med par byed ces pa ni/ sbyin pa de dag sems can thams cad kyi don du bla na med pa'i byang chub tu bsngos na dpag tu med par 'gyur ba'i don to/ / des na byang sa las/
'bras bu la blta zhing sbyin pa sbyin par yang mi byed do/ / sbyin pa thams cad bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu bsngo bar byed do/[660] / zhes gsungs so/ /

“The power of dedication makes it immeasurable” means dedicating such generosity to the ultimate enlightenment of every sentient being. Bodhisattva Levels says:
Do not be generous with a view to the specific results of that act of generosity. Dedicate all generosity to the ultimate, perfectly pure, and complete enlightenment of each and every sentient being.[401]

d.div: [660] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_byang chub sems dpa'i sa/ shog_65_ba1
[401] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 65b1.

f.d:
bsngo bas ni 'phel ba gcig pur ma zad kyis/ mi zad par yang 'gyur te/ 'phags pa blo gros mi zad pa'i mdo las/
btsun pa shA ra dwa ti'i bu/ dper na chu thigs pa gcig rgya mtsho chen por lhung ba ni bskal pa'i mthar thug pa'i bar du bar ma dor zad pa med do/ / de bzhin du dge ba'i rtsa ba byang chub tu bsngos pa ni/ byang chub kyi snying po la 'dug gi bar du bar ma dor 'ga' yang zad par mi 'gyur ro/[661] / zhes gsungs so//

Dedication not only increases [the results] but makes them inexhaustible. /157/ The Akṣayamati Sutra says:
Noble son Śāradvati! Should a drop of water be put in the ocean, it will not be consumed until the end of the eon. Likewise the roots of virtue dedicated to enlightenment will never become exhausted or in the least diminished until the very heart of enlightenment is reached.[402]

d.div: [661] sde dge_175_bka'/ mdo sde/ ma_blo gros mi zad pa bstan pa'i mdo/ shog_107_na1
[402] Akṣayamatinirdeśasūtra, Toh 175 Kangyur, mdo sde, ma, 107a1.

f.d:
sbyin pa dag par byed pa ni bslab pa kun las btus pa las/
stong nyid snying rje'i snying po can/ / spyod pas bsod nams dag par 'gyur/[662] / zhes gsungs te/

The sixth point concerns how generosity can be made pure. To quote the Compendium of Trainings:
Applying emptiness with compassion as its essence, virtue will be made pure.[403]

d.div: [662] sde dge_3939_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_rgyal sras zhi ba lha/ bslab btus/ sh+loka_21_shog_2_ba6
[403] Śāntideva, Śikṣāsamuccaya, Toh 3939 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 2b6.

f.d:
sbyin pa de dag stong pas zin pa ni 'khor ba'i rgyur mi 'gro la/ snying rjes zin pa ni theg pa dman pa'i rgyur mi 'gro ste/ mi gnas pa'i mya ngan las 'das pa 'ba' zhig gi rgyur 'gro bas na dag pa'o/ / de la stong pas zin pa ni/ gtsug na rin chen gyis zhus pa'i mdo las/ sbyin pa la stong pa nyid kyi rgya bzhis gdab par gsungs te/ ji skad du/
de rgya bzhis btab nas sbyin par byed de/ bzhi gang zhe na/ nang lus stong pa nyid kyi rgyas gdab pa dang / phyi longs spyod stong pa nyid kyi rgyas gdab pa dang / sems yul can stong pa nyid kyi rgyas gdab pa dang / chos byang chub stong pa nyid kyi rgyas gdab pa ste/ rgya bzhi po de dag gi rgyas btab nas sbyin pa sbyin par byed do/[663] / zhes gsungs so/ /

When the above-mentioned forms of generosity are supported by realization of emptiness, they will not become a cause for samsara. When they are supported by compassion, they will not become a cause for [attaining] the Hinayana. In such a way, generosity is made pure because it becomes a cause solely for attaining the nonabiding nirvana. In the Questions of Ratnacūḍa Sutra, it is taught that generosity is marked with four seals of emptiness. It says:
Practice generosity by applying four seals to it. What are these four? To apply the seal of emptiness of the inner, one’s body; to apply the seal of emptiness of the outer, the gift; to apply the seal of emptiness to the mind, the subject; and to apply the seal of the emptiness to the reality, enlightenment. Having applied those four seals, one engages in the act of giving.[404]

d.div: [663] sde dge_91_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ cha_gtsug na rin po ches zhus pa'i mdo/ le'u/ shog_215_ba2
[404] Ratnacūḍaparipṛcchāsūtra, Toh 91 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, cha, 215b2.

f.d: snying rjes zin pa ni/ sems can rnams kyi spyi'am bye brag gi sdug bsngal ma bzod nas sbyin pa'o//
“Being supported by compassion” means to engage in giving because one is unable to tolerate the suffering of other beings in general or more specific kinds.

sbyin pa'i 'bras bu ni/ mthar thug dang gnas skabs gnyis su shes par bya'o/ / de la mthar thug ni bla na med pa'i byang chub thob ste/ de ltar yang byang sa las/
de ltar byang chub sems dpa' rnams sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa yongs su rdzogs par byas nas/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ro/[664] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The seventh point concerns the fruits of generosity, which should be understood in both immediate and ultimate terms. Ultimately, generosity brings total enlightenment. Bodhisattva Levels says:
When bodhisattvas totally complete the perfection of generosity, they truly become perfect buddhas who have reached peerless, manifest, and perfect enlightenment.[405]

d.div: [664] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ shog_73_ba6
[405] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 73b6.

f.d:
gnas skabs su ni zang zing gi sbyin pa btang bas/ mi 'dod kyang rang la longs spyod phun sum tshogs par 'gyur/ gzhan yang sbyin pas bsdus nas mchog la sbyor bar byed nus so/ / de ltar yang 'phags pa sdud pa las/
byang chub sems dpa'i sbyin pas yi dwags 'gro ba gcod/ / dbul ba dang ni de bzhin nyon mongs thams cad gcod/ / spyod tshe longs spyod mtha' yas rgyas pa thob par 'gyur// sbyin pas sdug bsngal gyur pa'i sems can yongs smin byed/[665] / ces gsungs so/ /

The immediate results are that material giving brings the most perfect wealth even if one does not desire it. Furthermore, having attracted others through giving one can connect them with the supreme attainment as well. The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom says:
Bodhisattva generosity destroys the route to rebirth as a hungry spirit. It suppresses poverty and also cuts through affliction. While practicing, they will enjoy vast and limitless wealth. /158/ Through giving they will bring suffering beings to greater maturity.[406]

d.div: [665] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ le'u/ 32_sh+loka_1_shog_19_ba1
[406] Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā, Toh 13 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 19b1.

f.d:
byang sa las/
zas byin pas ni stobs can 'gyur/ / gos sbyin pas ni kha dog ldan/ / bzhon pa byin pas bde 'gyur brtan/ / mar me byin pas mig dang ldan/[666] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Bodhisattva Levels says:
Gifts of food will bring strength, gifts of clothes will bring a good complexion, gifts of steeds will provide the basis for happiness, and offering oil lamps will bring good eyesight.[407]

d.div: [666] sde dge_4037_bstan/ sems tsam/ wi_'phags pa thogs med/ byang sa/ shog_65_ba2
[407] Asaṅga, Bodhisattvabhūmi, Toh 4037 Tengyur, sems tsam, wi, 65b2.

f.d:
mi 'jigs pa'i sbyin pa btang bas ni bdud dang bar chad kyis mi tshugs par 'gyur ba'o/ / de ltar yang rin chen phreng ba las/
'jigs la mi 'jigs sbyin pa yis/ / bdud rnams kun gyis mi tshugs shing / / stobs po che yi mchog tu 'gyur/[667] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Giving freedom from fear brings immunity from harm by negative forces and obstacles. The Precious Garland says:
By giving giving freedom from fear to the fearful, you will not be harmed by any negative force and will become supreme among the mighty.[408]

d.div: [667] sde dge_4158_bstan/ spring yig_ge_mgon po klu sgrub/ rin chen phreng ba/ le'u/ 3_sh+loka_92_shog_118_na1
[408] Nāgārjuna, Ratnāvalī 3:91, Toh 4158 Tengyur, spring yig, ge, 118a1.

f.d:
chos kyi sbyin pa btang bas ni sangs rgyas dang myur du mjal nas 'grogs pa dang / 'dod pa thams cad myur du thob bo/ / de ltar yang rin chen phreng ba las/
chos nyan pa la sbyin pa dag / sgrib pa med par byas pa yis/ / sangs rgyas rnams dang 'grogs pa nyid/ / 'dod pa myur du thob par 'gyur/[668] / zhes gsungs so/ /

By giving the gift of Dharma, someone will soon meet the buddhas, be close to them, and attain everything wished for. The Precious Garland says:
Through giving the Dharma to those who listen, you eliminiate their obscurations, and by being a companion of the buddhas, you will swiftly attain what is longed for.[409]

d.div: [668] gong mtshungs/ rin chen phreng ba/ le'u/ 3_sh+loka_90_shog_117_ba6
[409] Nāgārjuna, Ratnāvalī 3:89, Toh 4158 Tengyur, spring yig, ge, 117b6.
