[614] A scriptural source of this and the previous quote from Tilopa has not been identified. Some pith advice belongs to the intimate instructions handed down orally (man ngag) and was only committed to writing generations after its originator.

f.d:
klu sgrub kyis kyang /
glang chen log nas sems tshugs tshud pa ltar/ / 'gro 'ong bcad na ngang gis dal ba ste/ / 'di ltar rtogs so nga la chos ci dgos/[977] /

Nāgārjuna has also said:
A mind that has stably relaxed within itself, like an elephant that has been trained, has stopped running to and fro, and remains naturally at ease. Thus have I realized, and hence what need have I of teachings?[615]

d.div: [977] ma dper/ klu sgrub kyis zhes drangs kyang / lung 'di sa ra ha'i do ha mdzod du bzhugs pa'i gsham gsal de min nam snyam pas brtag_glang chen lob nas sems tshags tshud pas na/ /der ni 'gro 'ong chad nas ngal ba ste/ /'di ltar rtogs na gang du'ang 'dri+i sa med/ /sde dge_2224_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ sa ra ha/ do ha mdzod kyi glu/ shog_74_ba3
[615] Although our author ascribes this quote to Nāgārjuna, most probably the verse is from Saraha’s Treasury of Spiritual Songs (Dohakoṣagīti), Toh 2224 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, wi, 74b3.

f.d:
zhes dang / yang de nyid kyis/
gar yang ma rtog cir yang ma sems shig / bcas bcos ma byed rang bzhin lhug par zhogs/ / ma bcos pa ni skye med rang bzhin mdzod/ / dus gsum rgyal ba kun gyi gshegs shul yin/[978] / zhes gsungs so//

And the same said:
Don’t adopt an attitude or think in any way whatsoever. Don’t interfere or contrive but leave mind loose in its natural state. The uncontrived is the unborn, true nature. This is of the trail set by all the victors of the three times.[616]

d.div: [978] klu sgrub kyi lung 'di'i gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[616] The source of this quote ascribed to Nāgārjuna has not been identified.

f.d:
ri khrod dbang phyug gis kyang /
gang la'ang skyon du mi lta zhing / / ci yang ma yin nyams su blang / / drod rtags la sogs 'dod mi bya/ / bsgom du med par bstan mod kyang / / le lo btang snyoms dbang mi gtong / / rgyun du dran par bsgom par bya/[979] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Lord of Hermits [i.e., the Indian mahasiddha Śavaripa] has also said:
Do not see fault anywhere. Practice that which is nothing whatsoever. Do not foster longing for signs of progress and the like. Although it is taught that there is nothing whatsoever to meditate on, do not fall under the sway of inactivity and indifference. In all circumstances, practice with mindfulness.[617]

d.div: [979] ri khrod dbang phyug gi lung 'di'i gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[617] The source of this quote from Śavaripa has not been identified.

f.d:
sgom don grub pa las/
bsgom pa'i tshe na ci yang mi bsgom ste/ / tha snyad tsam du de la sgom zhes bya/[980] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In the Achievement of the Very Point of Meditation it says:
When meditating, do not meditate on anything whatsoever. To call it “meditation” is simply use a convention.[618]

d.div: [980] sgom don grub pa zhes pa'i gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[618] The source of this quote has not been identified.

f.d:
sa ra ha pas kyang /
gang la zhen pa yod na de yang thong / / rtogs par gyur na thams cad de yin te/ / de las gzhan pa sus kyang shes mi 'gyur/[981] / zhes gsungs so/ /

d.div: [981] sde dge_2224_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ wi_grub chen sa ra ha/ do ha mdzod kyi glu/ shog_71_ba2
[619] Treasury of Spiritual Songs (Dohakoṣagīti) verse 16, Toh 2224 Tengyur, rgyud, wi, 71b2.

f.d:
jo bos kyang /
zab cing spros bral de nyid do/ / 'od gsal 'dus ma byas pa gang / / ma skyes mi 'gag gdod nas dag /
rang bzhin mya ngan 'das pa yi/ / chos dbyings mtha' dang dbus med pa/ / blo mig zhib mos rtog bral bas/ / bying rgod rab rib med par lta/[982] / zhes dang /
chos dbyings spros dang bral ba la/ / shes pa spros dang bral bar bzhag / ces gsungs so//

In the words of Atiśa:
This is suchness, profound and free of elaboration. Luminous and unconditioned, unborn and unceasing, it is primordially pure.
It is the natural nirvana, the ultimate, without middle or end; behold it with the fine eye of mind free of concept and without the bluriness of laxity or excitation.[620] And:
In the ultimate expanse free of conceptual elaboration, place your mind free of conceptual elaboration.[621]

d.div: [982] sde dge_2314_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ shi_mar me mdzad ye shes/ chos kyi dbyings su lta ba'i glu/ sh+loka_2_shog_255na1
[620] Song of Seeing Dharmadhātu (Dharmadhātudarśanagīti), verses 2–3, Toh 2314 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, shi, 255a1.
[621] Source unidentified.

f.d:
de ltar bzhag pa ni/ shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa la goms par bya ba'i thabs phyin ci ma log pa yin no/ / de ltar yang shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa bdun brgya pa las/
chos gang la yang blang ba'am/ gzung ba'am/ dor ba ma mchis pa de shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa bsgom pa lags so/ / gang ci la yang mi gnas pa de nyid shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa bsgoms pa lags so// gang la yang mi sems rnam par mi dmigs pa de shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa bsgom pa lags so/[983]/zhes gsungs so/ /

Placing the mind in the way described above is to employ an unerring method for cultivating the perfection of profound wisdom. The Perfection of Wisdom in Seven Hundred Lines says:
Not to engage in, hold onto, or reject anything—that is to meditate on the perfection of wisdom. Not dwelling on anything is to meditate on the perfection of wisdom. Not to think about anything and not to focus on anything whatsoever is to meditate on the perfection of wisdom.[622]

d.div: [983] sde dge_90_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ cha_sher phyin bdun brgya pa/ shog_186_na3
[622] Saptaśatikānāmaprajñāpāramitā, Toh 90 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, cha, 186a3.

f.d:
'phags pa brgyad stong pa las kyang /
shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa bsgom pa 'di ni chos gang yang mi bsgom pa lags so/[984] / zhes gsungs so/ / yang mdo sde de nyid las/
shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa bsgom pa ni nam mkha' bsgom pa lags so/[985] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines says:
To meditate on the perfection of wisdom is to meditate on no phenomena whatsoever. And:
To meditate on the perfection of wisdom is to meditate on space.[623] /204/

d.div: [984] sde dge_12_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_brgyad stong pa/ le'u/ 15_shog_167_ba5
[985] gong mtshungs/ brgyad stong pa/ shog_111_ba2
[623] Aṣṭasāhasrikāprajñāpāramitā, Toh 12 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 167b5.

f.d:
'o na nam mkha' ci ltar bsgom na/ yang mdo sde de nyid las/
nam mkha' rtog pa med pa nyid las shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa rtog pa med pa nyid do/[986] / zhes gsungs so/ /

How can one “meditate on space”? The same sutra tells us:
In that space is devoid of conceptualization, the perfection of wisdom, too, is devoid of conceptualization.[624]

d.div: [986] gong mtshungs/ brgyad stong pa/ shog_283_ba4

f.d:
'phags pa sdud pa las kyang /
skye ba med dang skye ba gnyis kar mi rtog pa/ / 'di ni shes rab pha rol phyin mchog spyod pa yin/[987] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom also says:
Not to be both in absence of arising as well as arising, this is to practice the perfection of wisdom.”[625]

d.div: [987] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ le'u/ 1_sh+loka_26_shog_3_na7
[625] Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā, Toh 13 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 3a7.

f.d:
slob dpon ngag gi dbang phyug gi zhal nas kyang /
bsam bya bsam par mi bya zhing / / bsam min pa yang mi bsam mo/ / bsam dang bsam min ma bsam na/ / de nas stong nyid mthong bar 'gyur/[988] / zhes gsungs so//

In the words of the great master Vāgīśvarakīrti:
Do not think about the thinkable. Do not think about the unthinkable either. By thinking neither about the thinkable nor the unthinkable, emptiness will be seen.[626]

d.div: [988] sde dge_1748_bka'/ rgyud 'grel/ sha_ngag gi dbang phyug grags pa/ 'chi ba bslu ba'i man ngag_shog_133_ba1
[626] Advice on Cheating Death (Mṛtyuvañcanopadeśa), Toh 1748 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, sha, 133b1.

f.d:
stong pa nyid ci lta bur mthong zhe na/[989] ji skad du/ chos yang dag par sdud pa'i mdo las/
stong pa nyid mthong ba ni mthong ba ma mchis pa'o/ / zhes pa dang /
bcom ldan 'das chos thams cad ma mthong ba ni yang dag par mthong ba'o/ / zhes pa dang /
'ga' yang mthong ba med pa ni/ de kho na nyid mthong ba'o/[990] / zhes gsungs so/ /

How does someone “see emptiness”? As it says in the Perfectly Gathering the Qualities [of Avalokiteśvara] Sutra:
To see emptiness is not to see [anything] at all. And:
Blessed One! Not to see any thing is to see excellently. And:
Without seeing any thing whatsoever, the one and only nature is seen.[627]

d.div: [989] stong nyid ji lta bu mthong zhe na/ dpal spungs/
[990] sde dge_238_bka'/ mdo sde/ zha_chos yang dag pa sdud pa'i mdo/ shog_68_ba5
[627] Dharmasaṃgītisūtra, Toh 238 Kangyur, mdo sde, zha, 68b5.

f.d:
dbu ma bden chung las kyang /
ma mthong ba ni de mthong bar/ / shin tu zab pa'i mdo las gsungs/[991] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Shorter Text on Middle Way Truths also says:
It says in some exceedingly profound discourses that not-seeing is to see that [truth].[628]

d.div: [991] sde dge_3902_bstan/ dbu ma/ a_mar me mdzad ye shes/ bden pa gnyis la 'jug pa/ 72_na6
[628] Atiśa, Penetrating the Two Truths (Satyadvayāvatāra), Toh 3902 Tengyur, dbu ma, a, 72a6. Gampopa refers to Satyadvayāvatāra as the Shorter Text on Middle Way Two Truths.

f.d:
'phags pa sdud pa las kyang /
nam mkha' mthong zhes sems can tshig tu rab brjod pa/ / nam mkha' ci ltar mthong ste don 'di brtags par gyis/ / de ltar chos mthong ba yang de bzhin gshegs pas bstan/[992] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom also remarks:
People commonly use the term “seeing space.” Consider carefully just how someone can see space. The Tathāgata taught the way to see phenomena as being like that.[629]

d.div: [992] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ le'u/ 12_sh+loka_9_shog_8_ba3
[629] Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā, Toh 13 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 8b3.

f.d:
rjes thob thams cad sgyu ma lta bur lta zhing sbyin pa la sogs pa'i bsod nams kyi tshogs ci nus su bsags pa'o/[993] [994] / de ltar yang 'phags pa sdud pa las/
gang zhig phung po lnga dag sgyu ma 'drar shes shing / / sgyu ma gzhan dang phung po gzhan du mi byed pa/ / sna tshogs 'du shes bral zhing nye bar zhi spyod pa/ / de ni shes rab pha rol phyin mchog spyod pa yin/[995] / zhes gsungs so/ /

(C) The third point concerns the [post-meditation or] between-sessions phase. While viewing everything that occurs in between meditation sessions as illusory, every wholesome merit possible should be established, through the practice of generosity and so forth. As the Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom says:
Whoever understands the five aggregates to be like an illusion but does not make the aggregates and the illusion as separate things and is free of the notion of multiplicity but experiences peace, that is to practice the excellent perfection of wisdom.[630]

d.div: [993] rjes thob la chos thams cad/ dpal spungs/
[994] bsag go/ dpal spungs/
[995] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ le'u/ 1_sh+loka_14_shog_2_ba4

f.d:
ting nge 'dzin rgyal po'i mdo las/[996]
sgyu ma byed pa dag gis gzugs sprul zhing / / rta dang glang po shing rta sna tshogs byas/ / de la ci bzhin snang ba gang yang med/ / chos rnams thams cad de 'drar shes par gyis/[997]/zhes gsungs so/ /

The King of Meditation Sutra says:
Although magicians conjure up forms— making horses, elephants, carts, and all sorts of things— they know that nothing of what appears is actually there. Recognize all phenomena to be likewise.[631]

d.div: [996] dpal spungs dpar mar ting nge 'dzin rgyal po'i mdo 'di'i lung cha tshang mi byung ba brtag
[997] sde dge_127_bka'/ mdo sde/ da_ting nge 'dzin rgyal po'i mdo/ le'u/ 9_sh+loka_16_shog_26_ba2
[631] Samādhirājasūtra, Toh 127 Kangyur, mdo sde, da, 26b2.

f.d:
spyod pa'i de kho na nyid las kyang /
mi rtog dran pa'i blo yod kyang // bsod nams tshogs ni rgyun mi bcad/[998] / ces gsungs so/ /

It is said in the Suchness of Conduct:
The mind is attentive to not conceptualizing, yet the amassing of merit never ceases.[632]

d.div: [998] spyod pa'i de kho na nyid kyi gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[632] Spyod pa’i de kho na nyid, *Caryātattva. The source of this quote has not been identified.

f.d:
de ltar goms pa dang / mnyam rjes gnyis kyang tha mi dad du 'gyur zhing rlom sems dang bral bar 'gyur ro/ / de ltar yang /
bdag nyid mnyam par bzhag ce'am langs zhes rlom sems med/ / ci phyir zhe na chos kyi rang bzhin yongs shes phyir/[999] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Through such familiarity, the meditation and post-meditation phases will become indistinguishable and one will become free of conceitedness. Thus it says: /205/
He will have no conceitedness in terms of “I am in meditative equipoise” or “I am arising from the equipoise.” Why? Because there is awareness of the very nature of things.[633]

d.div: [999] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ le'u/ 1_sh+loka_11_shog_2_ba2
[633] Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom (Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā), Toh 13 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 2b2.

f.d:
de ltar don dam stong nyid shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa de'i ngang la dar cig tsam gnas na'ang bskal pa'i bar du nyan pa'am/[1000] [1001] klog pa'am dge ba'i rtsa ba sbyin pa la sogs pa byas pa bas bsod nams dpag tu med pa che ba yin no// de ltar yang / / de kho na nyid bstan pa'i mdo las/
shA ri'i bu/ gang gis bskal pa gcig gi bar du nyan pa bas/ gang gis se gol gtogs tsam zhig tu de kho na nyid kyi ting nge 'dzin bsgom na bsod nams 'phel lo/ / shA ri'i bu de lta bas/ de kho na nyid kyi ting nge 'dzin gzhan la nan tan gyis gdams par bya'o/ / shA ri'i bu gang sangs rgyas su lung bstan pa'i byang chub sems dpa' thams cad kyang ting nge 'dzin 'di la gnas pa sha stag go[1002] / zhes gsungs so/ /

To be immersed, even for a short moment, in the perfection of wisdom—the ultimate, emptiness—constitutes an incomparably greater virtue than to spend eons receiving Dharma teachings, reciting scriptures, or planting roots of virtue in the form of generosity and similar wholesome actions. The Sutra Teaching Suchness states:
Śāriputra! Compared to someone listening [to the Dharma] for up to an eon, if another person were to practice meditative absorption on suchness even for the duration of a finger snap, his merits would increase far more greatly. Śāriputra! For this reason you should earnestly instruct others to practice meditative absorption on suchness. Śāriputra! All the bodhisattvas who have been predicted as being future buddhas also abide solely in that meditative absorption.[634]

d.div: [1000] dar cig tsam gnas kyang / sbyin pa bskal pa'i bar du btang ba bsod nams che bar bshad de/ de kho na nyid bstan pa'i mdo las kyang / zhes dpal spungs dpar mar tshig bsdus nas byung /
[1001] na'ang nas 'og tu de ltar yang / zhes pa'i bar gyi tshig rnams dpal spungs dpar mar mi byung /
[1002] de kho na nyid bstan pa'i mdo zhes pa'i gzhung ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[634] De kho na nyid bstan pa’i mdo. The sutra that is the source of this quote has not been found.

f.d:
rtogs pa chen po rgyas pa'i mdo las kyang /[1003]
thang cig bsam gtan thun zhugs na/ / khams gsum pa yi mi rnams la// srog byin pa bas 'di don che/[1004] / zhes gsungs so/ /

It is also stated, in the Sutra on the Full Development of Great Realization:
It is more meaningful to practice meditative concentration for a session than to give life to beings of the three dimensions.[635]

d.div: [1003] rtogs pa chen po rgyas pa'i mdo las kyang / zhes pa nas shog bu gsum tsam gyi rjes su/ jo bos kyang / cig tu mnyam bzhag sems brtan na/ /lus ngag dge la mi brtson bya/ /zhes pa'i bar gyi gzhung cha tshang dpal spungs dpar mar mi byu_nga bas brtag
[1004] sde dge_266_bka'/ mdo sde/ 'a_rtogs pa chen po rgyas pa'i mdo/ shog_287_ba5_'gyur khyad che/

[635] Mahāsamayavaipulyasūtra, Toh 265 Kangyur, mdo sde, ’a, 287b5. Intriguingly, a large part of the text, starting from this point up to the section relating to the signs of having cultivated wisdom (p. 337), is missing in the Palpung edition. This variance represents a significant difference between the texts, especially since the section missing in the Palpung edition deals specifically with an important standpoint of the simultaneist (gcig bcar ba) approach to the path—that all key elements of the path to buddhahood are embodied within the single practice of understanding the nature of your mind.

f.d:
gtsug tor chen po'i mdo las kyang /
bskal pa mang po'i bar du thos dang bsams pa bas ni/ nyin gcig chos kyi don bsgoms pas bsod nams che'o/ / de ci'i phyir zhe na/ des skye 'chi'i lam dang ring du bral bar byed pa'i phyir ro/[1005] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In the Great Uṣṇīṣa Sutra it states:
It is of greater merit to cultivate the true meaning of things for a day than to study and reflect for many cosmic eons. Why is this so? Because it takes one far away from the road of births and deaths.[636]

d.div: [1005] gtsug tor chen po'i mdo ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[636] Gtsug tor chen po’i mdo. The source of this quote has not been identified.

f.d:
dad pa la 'jug pa'i mdo las kyang /
khams gsum gyi sems can gyis ji srid 'tsho'i bar du 'tsho ba'i yo byad kyis tshogs bsags pa bas/ rnal 'byor pas stong pa nyid thun gcig bsgoms pas bsod nams che'o/[1006] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In the Sutra on Excellently Nurturing Faith [in the Mahayana], it says:
There is greater merit in a yogi’s session of emptiness meditation than there would be if all beings in the three dimensions spent their whole lives using their possessions to accumulate virtue.[637]

d.div: [1006] sde dge_144_bka'/ mdo sde/ pa_theg pa chen po la dad pa rab tu sgom pa'i mdo/ shog_32_ba6_tshig ji bzhin lung med/ mdo 'di la dad pa la 'jug pa'i mdo mtshan gzhan du brjod do//
[637] Approximation of Mahāyānaprasādaprabhāvanasūtra, Toh 144 Kangyur, mdo sde, pa, 32b6.

f.d:
stong pa nyid kyi don yid la mi gnas na/ gzhan dge ba de dag gis bdag grol ba mi thob par bstan te/ chos 'byung ba med par bstan pa'i mdo las/
yun ring dus su tshul khrims srung byed cing / bskal pa bye bar bsam gtan brtan byas kyang / / yang dag don gyi mtha' 'di ma rtogs na/ / brtan pa 'di la de dag grol mi 'gyur/ / ci yang med pa'i chos 'di sus shes pa/ / nam yang 'di ni chos kun chag mi 'gyur/[1007] / zhes gsungs so/ /

It is taught that if your mind is not dwelling on the key points of emptiness, then other virtues cannot deliver you to liberation. The Sutra Teaching the Nonorigination of All Things:
Someone may observe moral discipline for a long time and practice meditative concentration for millions of eons, but without realization of this highest truth, those things cannot bring liberation, according to this teaching. Whoever understands this “nothing whatsoever” will never cling to anything whatsoever.[638]

d.div: [1007] sde dge_180_bka'/ mdo sde/ ma_chos thams cad 'byung ba med pa bstan pa'i mdo/ shog_294_na5
[638] Sarvadharmāpravṛttinirdeśasūtra, Toh 180 Kangyur, mdo sde, ma, 294a5.

f.d:
sa'i snying po 'khor lo bcu pa las kyang /
ting 'dzin bsgoms pas the tshom gcod 'gyur gyi/ / de ma gtogs pa gzhan gyis nus ma yin/ / de bas ting 'dzin bsgom pa mchog yin gyi/ / mkhas pa dag gis de la nan tan bya/[1008]/zhes pa dang / yang de nyid las/
chos bri ba dang / klog pa dang / nyan pa dang / 'chad pa dang / kha ton bskal par byas pa bas/ nyi ma gcig bsgom pa bsod nams che'o/[1009] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In the Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sutra it states:
It is through cultivating absorption doubts will be cut. Other than that, nothing can. /206/ Hence the cultivation of absorption is supreme, and the wise practice it diligently.[639] Furthermore:
The positive result of meditating for a day far exceeds that of writing out, reading, studying, reciting, or explaining the teachings for eons.[640]

d.div: [1008] sde dge_239_bka'/ mdo sde/ zha_sa'i snying po 'khor lo bcu pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 3_shog_138_ba2
[1009] gong mtshungs/ sa'i snying po 'khor lo bcu pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 3_shog_139_ba5_tshig ji bzhin pa lung du med/
[639] Daśacakrakṣitigarbhasūtra, Toh 239 Kangyur, mdo sde, zha, 138b2.

f.d:
de lta bu'i stong pa nyid kyi don dang ldan na/ chos 'di la ma 'dus pa gcig kyang med do// skyabs su 'gro ba yang yin te/ ma dros pas zhus pa'i mdo las/
byang chub sems dpas chos thams cad ni bdag med pa/ sems can med pa/ srog med pa/ gang zag med par shes/ gzugs su ma yin/ mtshan du ma yin/ chos su ma yin par de bzhin gshegs pas yang dag par rjes su ma mthong ba de lta bu ni/ zang zing med pa'i sems kyis sangs rgyas la skyabs su song ba yin no/ / de bzhin gshegs pa'i chos nyid gang yin pa de ni chos kyi dbyings so/ / chos kyi dbyings gang yin pa de ni chos thams cad kyi rjes su song ba zhes bya ste/ de ltar chos thams cad kyi dbyings su song ba mthong ste/ de ltar mthong ba de lta bu ni zang zing med pa'i sems kyis chos la skyabs su song ba yin no/ / gang chos kyi dbyings 'dus ma byas par bsgom pa dang / nyan thos kyi theg pa 'dus ma byas par brten pa dang / 'dus byas dang / 'dus ma byas pa gnyis su med pa 'di lta bu ni/ zang zing med pa'i sems kyis dge 'dun la skyabs su song ba yin no/[1010] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Once you become endowed with the key point of emptiness, as described above, there is nothing at all that is not encompassed within it. This constitutes to take refuge as well. For example, the Questions of Nāga King Anavatapta Sutra states:
Bodhisattvas recognize all phenomena to be without a self, without a sentient nature, without life, and without personhood. To see quite correctly in the way the tathāgatas see—not as forms, not as names, and not as specific phenomena—is to have taken refuge in the Buddha with a mind unpolluted by material consideration. The essence of the tathāgatas is the ultimate expanse; that which is ultimate expanse is referred to as that which pervades every thing.Thus, seeing it as the domain of all phenomena is to take refuge in the Dharma with a mind unpolluted by material consideration. Whoever is familiar with the ultimate expanse as being unconditioned and with the fact that the śrāvakayāna is founded in what is unconditioned, and who also understands the nonduality of the conditioned and the unconditioned, takes refuge in the Sangha with a mind unpolluted by material consideration.[641]

d.div: [1010] sde dge_156_bka'/ mdo sde/ pha_klu'i rgyal po ma dros pas zhus pa'i mdo/ shog_250_na6
[641] Anavataptanāgarājaparipṛcchāsūtra, Toh 156 Kangyur, mdo sde, pha, 250a6.

f.d:
byang chub tu sems bskyed pa yang de nyid yin te/ sems bskyed chen po'i mdo las/
'od srung chos thams cad nam mkha' ltar mtshan nyid med cing / ye nas 'od gsal ba rnam par dag pa de ni byang chub tu sems bskyed par bya'o/[1011] / zhes gsungs so/ /

This constitutes the generation of bodhicitta as well. For example, the Sutra of Great Bodhicitta[642] says:
Kāśyapa! Every phenomenon is, like space, without specific characteristics and is primordial lucid clarity and utter purity. That is “to give rise to bodhicitta.”

d.div: [1011] sems bskyed chen po'i mdo brnyed son ma byung /
[642] Sems bskyed chen po mdo. This sutra has not been identified.

f.d:
bskyed rim lha bsgom pa dang sngags kyi bzlas brjod kyang 'di yod na tshang bar gsungs/ / de yang gang nas gsungs na/ kyai rdo rje las/
bsgom med sgom pa po yang med/ / lha med sngags kyang yod ma yin/ / spros pa med pa'i rang bzhin la/ / lha dang sngags rnams yang dag gnas/ / rnam snang mi bskyod don grub dang / / rin chen dpag med sems dpa'o/[1012] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The deity meditation and mantra recitation are all complete within this as well. In the Hevajra Tantra it says:
No meditation, no meditator as well; no deities and no mantra either; within the nature free of conceptual elaboration, the deities and mantras are truly present: Vairocana, Akṣobhya, Amoghasiddhi, Ratnasambhava, Amitābha, and Vajrasattva.[643]

d.div: [1012] sde dge_417_bka'/ rgyud/ nga _kye rdo rje/ le'u/ 1_shog_6_na7
[643] Hevajratantra, Toh 417 Kangyur, rgyud, nga, 6a7.

f.d:
sangs rgyas mnyam sbyor las/
gzugs brnyan lugs ma la sogs la/ / rnal 'byor 'byung bar mi 'gyur gyi/ / byang chub sems la rab brtson na/ / de las rnal 'byor lhar 'gyur ro/[1013]/zhes gsungs so/ /

The Union with All the Buddhas Tantra says:
From a cast image and the like a true union (yoga) will not emerge, whereas the yogi who strives excellently in bodhicitta will actually become the deity.[644] /207/

d.div: [1013] sde dge_366_bka'/ rgyud/ ka_sangs rgyas mnyam sbyor/ le'u/ 1_shog_152_na6

[644] Sarvabuddhasamayoga, Toh 366 Kangyur, rgyud, ka, 152a6. The term yoga means “fusion” or “union.” In the lines cited here, the term refers to a union with the deity during the completion stage of tantra, while “the yogi” here is the tantric meditator.

f.d:
rdo rje rtse mo las kyang /
sngags rnams kun gyi mtshan nyid ni// sangs rgyas kun gyi thugs yin te/ / chos kyi snying po sgrub byed yin/ / chos kyi dbyings dang yang dag ldan/ / sngags kyi mtshan nyid yin par brjod/[1014] / ces gsungs so/ /

The Vajra Peak Tantra says:
The intrinsic characteristic of every mantra is said to be the mind of all the buddhas; it is a means to cultivate the essence of Dharma. To be perfectly endowed with the ultimate expanse is said to be the intrinsic characteristic of mantras.[645]

d.div: [1014] sde dge_480_bka'/ rgyud/ nya_rgyud rdo rje rtse mo/ le'u/ 1_shog_155_ba1
[645] Vajraśekharatantra, Toh 480 Kangyur, rgyud, nya, 155b1.

f.d:
sbyin sreg byed pa yang de nyid la 'dus pa yin te/ gsang ba bdud rtsi rgyal po'i rgyud las/ /
gang gi phyir na sbyin sreg ni// dngos grub dam pa ster ba dang / / rnam rtog 'joms phyir sbyin sreg ste/ / shing sogs bsregs pas sbyin sreg min/[1015] / zhes gsungs so//

It also comprises fire offerings. As the King of Secret Nectar Tantra says:
What are fire offerings for? They are made to bestow the highest accomplishments and to overcome conceptualization. Burning wood and so forth is not a fire offering.[646]

d.div: [1015] sde dge_401_bka'/ rgyud/ ga_gsang ba bdud rtsi'i rgyal po'i rgyud/ le'u/ 1_shog_234_ba6
[646] Amṛtaguhyatantrarāja, Toh 401 Kangyur, rgyud, ga, 234b6.

f.d:
lam pha rol tu phyin pa drug kyang 'di nyid la tshang ste/ rdo rje ting nge 'dzin gyi mdo las/
stong pa nyid las ma g.yos na/ / pha rol phyin pa drug 'dus so/[1016] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The path in terms of the six perfections is also complete in it. The Diamond Meditative Absorption Scripture says:
If unwavered from emptiness, the six perfections are embodied.[647]

d.div: [1016] sde dge_135_bka'/ mdo sde/ na_rdo rje'i ting nge 'dzin gyi chos kyi yi ge_shog_125_ba7
[647] Vajrasamādhidharmākṣara, Toh 135 Kangyur, mdo sde, na, 125b7, but not identical to Gampopa’s quote.

f.d:
tshangs pa khyad par sems kyis zhus pa'i mdo las kyang /
mi bsam pa ni sbyin pa'o/ / tha dad la mi gnas pa ni tshul khrims so/ / bye brag mi 'byed pa ni bzod pa'o/ / blang dor med pa ni brtson 'grus so/ / ma chags pa ni bsam gtan no/ / mi rtog pa ni shes rab bo/[1017] / zhes gsungs so/ /

According to the Questions of Brahma Viśesacinti Sutra:
To be without intention is generosity. Not to dwell on the separatedness of things is moral discipline. Not to make differentiations is patience. Absence of adoption and rejection is diligence. Nonattachment is meditative concentration. Nonthought is wisdom.[648]

d.div: [1017] sde dge_160_bka'/ mdo sde/ ba_tshangs pa khyad par sems kyis zhus pa'i mdo/ bam po/ 3_shog_58_na2_'gyur khyad che/
[648] Brahmaviśeṣacintiparipṛcchāsūtra, Toh 160 Kangyur, mdo sde, ba, 58a2.

f.d:
sa'i snying po'i mdo las kyang /
mkhas pas stong nyid chos bsgom pa ni/ / 'jig rten kun la mi brten mi gnas/ / srid pa kun la gnas par ma yin/ / rnam par dag pa'i tshul khrims bsrung ngo /[1018] / zhes gsungs so//

The Ten Wheels of Kṣitigarbha Sutra also states:
The meditation of the wise and skillful on the teaching of emptiness does not resort to or dwell on anything of the world. It abides nowhere in any existence, and as such is the observance of pure moral discipline.[649]

d.div: [1018] sde dge_239_bka'/ mdo sde/ zha_sa'i snying po 'khor lo bcu pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 7_shog_224_na6
[649] Daśacakrakṣitigarbhasūtra, Toh 239 Kangyur, mdo sde, zha, 224a6.

f.d:
yang de nyid las/
chos rnams thams cad ro gcig mthun par/ / stong pa mtshan ma med pa'i zhi ba'i// sems ni ci la'ang mi gnas mi chags/ / bzod pa'i de ni phan yon che bar 'gyur ro/ / mkhas pas brtson 'grus brtsams pa dag ni/ / chags pa thams cad ring du spangs pa ste/ / sems ni ci la'ang mi gnas mi chags/ / yang dag bsod nams zhing zhes de la bya/ / sems can kun la phan dang bde ba'i phyir/ / ting 'dzin bsgom zhing khur lci yang lta ste/ / kun nas nyon mongs thams cad sel ba/ / de ni yang dag mkhas pa'i mtshan nyid/[1019] / ces gsungs so/ /

It is said in the same sutra:
All phenomena are of one taste, being equally empty and without any characteristics. The mind that does not dwell on or become attached to anything is [practicing] patience, and through this, benefit will increase greatly.[650] The wise who practice diligence have cast far away every attachment. The mind that neither dwells on nor clings to anything whatsoever should be known as a “field of finest virtue.”[651] To practice meditative concentration in order to bring happiness and well-being to all sentient beings is something that removes a great burden. To thus clear away every polluting affliction is the defining characteristic of the truly wise.[652]

d.div: [1019] gong mtshungs/ sa'i snying po 'khor lo bcu pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 7_shog_228_ba4

f.d:
phyag 'tshal ba yang 'di nyid yin te/ nam mkha' rin po che'i mdo las/
ci ltar chu la chu bzhag dang / / ci ltar mar la mar bzhag ltar// rang gis rang rig ye shes 'di/ / legs mthong gang yin 'dir phyag yin/[1020] / zhes gsungs so//

It also constitutes making prostrations. The Precious Space Sutra:
Like water poured into water and like butter poured into butter, he who sees this pristine self-cognizing awareness is also making prostration to it.[653]

d.div: [1020] nam mkha' rin po che'i mdo ngos 'dzin ma thub mod/ lung 'di klu sgrub kyi rim lngar bkod/ sde dge_1802_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ ngi _klu sgrub/ rim lnga/ le'u/ 2_shog_48_na4
[653] A Precious Space Sutra has not been identified, but this quote is found in Nāgārjuna’s Five Stages (Pañcakrama), Toh 1802 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, ngi.

f.d:
yang 'di nyid yod na mchod pa yang yin te/ yab sras mjal ba'i mdo las/
stong nyid chos la rten bgyid cing / / sangs rgyas spyod yul gang mos pa/ / de dag ston pa mchod pa de/ / mchod pa de ni bla na med/[1021] / ces gsungs so/ /

It also represents the making of offerings. The Meeting of Father and Son Sutra says: /208/
To resort to the Dharma of emptiness and aspire to that which is the domain of experience of the buddhas— such is to make offerings to the enlightened teacher, and such offerings are unsurpassable.[654]

d.div: [1021] sde dge_60_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ nga _yab sras mjal ba'i mdo/ le'u/ 24_bam po/ 9_shog_99_ba3
[654] Pitāputrasamāgamasūtra, Toh 60 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, nga, 99b3.

f.d:
bdud rtsi gsang ba'i rgyud las/
mnyes pa don gyi mchod pa ste/ spos sogs phul bas mnyes pa med/ / rang sems las su rung ba dag / mnyes pa'i mchod pa chen po'o/[1022] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Also, in the King of Secret Nectar Tantra it says:
Meaningful offerings are pleasing, but not so offerings of incense and the like. By making the mind perfectly workable, the great and pleasing offering is made.[655]

d.div: [1022] sde dge_402_bka'/ rgyud/ ga_gsang ba bdud rtsi'i rgyal po'i rgyud/ le'u/ 1_shog_234_ba7
[655] Amṛtaguhyatantrarāja, Toh 401 Kangyur, rgyud, ga, 234b7.

f.d:
yang 'di nyid dang ldan na/ sdig pa bshags pa yang 'di rang yin te/ las rnam par dag pa'i mdo las/
gang zhig bshags pa 'dod byed cing / / drang por 'dug la yang dag ltos/ / yang dag nyid la yang dag blta/ / 'di ni 'gyod tshangs mchog yin no/[1023] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Furthermore, if you possess this perfection of wisdom, this constitutes the purification of past errors as well. In the Sutra on Totally Purifying Karma it says:
You who are desirous of atonement! Sit straight and behold the perfect truth. Perfectly beholding the perfect truth is the most excellent form of repentence.[656]

d.div: [1023] sde dge_3910_bstan/ dbu ma/ ki_wi mal mi tra/ cig car 'jug pa'i rnam par mi rtog pa'i sgom don/ shog_13_ba1_lung 'di wi mala'i cig car 'jug par phyogs su rgyas pa'i mdo las drangs pa ra snang /

[656] Las rnam par dag pa’i mdo. This quotation is given by Vimalamitra as coming from the Great Liberation Sutra, in his Meditating on Nonthought, Penetrating Simultaneity (Sakṛtprāveśikanirvikalpabhāvanārtha), Toh 3910 Tengyur, dbu ma, ki, 13b1.

f.d:
yang don 'di nyid la tshul khrims dam tshig bsrung ba yang tshang ste/ lha'i bus zhus pa'i mdo las/
gang la sdom pa sdom pa ma yin pa'i rlom sems med pa de ni/ mya ngan las 'das pa'i tshul khrims yin te/ tshul khrims rnam par dag pa yin no/[1024] / zhes gsungs so/ /

It also comprises the observance of moral commitments. As is said in the Questions of the Devaputra Susthitamati Sutra:
When there is no longer the conceitedness of vow or no-vow, there is the moral discipline of nirvana; that is the purest moral discipline.[657]

d.div: [1024] sde dge_80_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ cha_lha'i bus zhus pa'i mdo/ shog_12_ba1
[657] Susthitamatidevaputraparipṛcchāsūtra, Toh 80 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, cha, 12b1.

f.d:
'khor lo bcu pa'i mdo las kyang /
khyim na gnas shing skra dang kha spu yang ma bregs/ chos gos kyang ma gon/ tshul khrims kyang ma mnos mod kyang / 'phags pa'i chos nyid dang ldan pa de nyid don dam pa'i dge slong zhes bya'o/[1025] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The Ten Wheels [of Kṣitigarbha] Sutra also says:
Someone may be considered to be a layperson, living at home with head and beard unshaven. He may not wear monk’s robes and may not even have taken [the precepts] of moral discipline. But if he is endowed with the suchness of the noble ones, that person is a true monk in the ultimate sense.[658]

d.div: [1025] sde dge_239_bka'/ mdo sde/ zha_sa'i snying po 'khor lo bcu pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 4_bam po/ 5_shog_170_ba3
[658] Daśacakrakṣitigarbhasūtra, Toh 239 Kangyur, mdo sde, zha, 120b3.

f.d:
yang don de nyid la thos pa dang / bsam pa dang / bsgom pa gsum yang tshang ste/ rab tu mi gnas pa'i rgyud las/
ma bcos rnal ma'i zas gcig zos gyur na// grub mtha' ma lus kun kyang tshim par 'gyur/ / byis pas ma rtogs tha snyad tshig la brten/ / thams cad rang gi sems kyi mtshan nyid yin/[1026] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Furthermore, it also comprises all three stages of wisdom—of study, of contemplation, and of meditation. As is said in the Tantra of Supreme Nonabiding:
If one has eaten the food of the uncontrived naturalness, it fulfills all the philosophical tenets, whatever they may be. The immature, lacking realization, rely on terminology. Everything is but a characteristic of one’s own mind.[659]

d.div: [1026] rab tu mi gnas pa'i rgyud ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[659] Rab tu mi gnas pa’i rgyud. This sutra has not been identified.

f.d:
sa ra ha pas kyang /
klog pa de yin 'dzin dang bsgom pa de yin te/ / bstan chos snying la 'chang ba'ang de yin no/ / de la mtshon pa'i lta ba yod min te/[1027] / zhes gsungs so/ / yang don de nyid gtor ma chos spyod kyang yin te/ gsang ba bdud rtsi rgyal po'i rgyud las/
mchod dang gtor ma la sogs pa/ / las dang bya ba sna tshogs kun// sems kyi de nyid rnyed gyur pas/ / thams cad 'di yis sdud par nges/[1028] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Saraha said, moreover:
It is to read, it is to seize the meaning, and it is to meditate. It is also to assimilate the meaning of the treatises. There is no view capable of demonstrating it.[660] It also comprises making torma offerings and similar Dharma activities. The King of Secret Nectar Tantra says:
When someone has encountered the nature of mind, all different types of activity and deed are contained therein: offerings, torma, and so forth.[661]

d.div: [1027] sde dge_2224_bstan/ rgyud 'grel/ wi_grub chen sa ra ha/ do ha mdzod kyi glu/ shog_71_ba
[1028] sde dge_402_bka'/ rgyud/ ga_gsang ba bdud rtsi'i rgyal po'i rgyud/ le'u/ 1_shog_234_ba2
[660] Treasury of Spiritual Songs (Dohakoṣagīti), Toh 2224 Tengyur, rgyud ’grel, wi, 71b.
[661] Amṛtaguhyatantrarāja, Toh 401 Kangyur, rgyud, ga, 234b2.

f.d:
'o na ngo bo'am sems nyid gcig pur bsgom pa la de dag thams cad 'dus na/ thabs kyi rim pa mang du gsungs pa dag 'byung ba ci ltar yin zhe na/ gnas lugs la rmongs pa'i skal pa dman pa rnams 'khrid pa'i phyir te/ ye shes snang ba rgyan gyi mdo las/
rgyu rkyen 'brel bar bshad pa dang / / rim par 'jug pa bstan pa yang / / rmongs pa rnams la thabs su gsungs/ / lhun gyis grub pa'i chos 'di la/ / rim gyis sbyong ba ci zhig yod/[1029] / ces gsungs so/ /

Well, if meditation on this essence or the nature of mind comprises all those things, what was the reason for teaching so many graduated techniques? These evolved to guide those less-gifted beings who are still confused about the nature of things. The Sutra That Adorns the Radiance of Pristine Awareness says: /209/
Explanations of causes, conditions, and interdependence, as well as the teaching of the graduated path, were given as skillful means for the confused. As for this spontaneous Dharma, what graduated training could there be?[662]

d.div: [1029] ye shes snang ba'i rgyan gyi mdo'i nang 'tshol zhib zhus kyang ma brnyed pas ma dper gang las drangs ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[662] Jñānālokālaṃkāra; Ye shes snang ba rgyan gyi mdo. This quotation does not appear in present versions of this sutra.

f.d:
bde mchog sdom pa 'byung ba las kyang /
'di ltar bdag nyid mkha' mtshungs ltar/ / rtag tu grol ba'i bdag nyid thob/[1030] / ces gsungs so/ /

In the Tantra of the Arising of the Supremely Blissful, it says:
Thus is attained an eternally liberated status— a status comparable to the vastness of space.[663]

d.div: [1030] sde dge_373_bka'/ rgyud/ kha_dpal bde mchog 'byung ba/ le'u/ 33_shog_309_ba3
[663] Śrīmahāsaṃbhārodayatantra, Toh 373 Kangyur, rgyud, kha, 309b3.

f.d:
nam mkha' rin po che'i mdo las kyang /
chos kyi dbyings kyi rgya mtshor ma zhugs kyi bar la/ sa dang lam tha dad mod kyi/ chos kyi dbyings kyi rgya mtshor phyin nas/ sa dang lam cung zad kyang bgrod du med do/[1031] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In the Precious Space Sutra, it is said:
Before dwelling in the ocean of the ultimate expanse, the stages and levels are held to be different. Once the ocean of the ultimate expanse has been entered, there is not even the slightest traversing of stages and levels.[664]

d.div: [1031] nam mkha' rin po che'i mdo zhes pa'i gzhung 'di ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[664] The source of this quote has not been established.

f.d:
jo bos kyang /
gcig tu mnyam bzhag sems brtan na/ / lus ngag dge la mi brtson bya/[1032] / zhes gsungs so//

Illustrious Atiśa has said:
When a mind is firmly settled in the one, do not strive in physical and verbal virtues.[665]

d.div: [1032] sde dge_3960_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_jo bo rje mar me mdzad ye shes/ spyod pa bsdus pa'i sgron ma/ shog_313_na5_spyir na mnyam gzhag sems brtan na/
[665] Atiśa, Lamp for the Summary of Conduct (Caryāsaṃgrahapradīpa), Toh 3960 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 313a5.

f.d: shes rab goms pa'i rtags ni/ dge ba la bag yod par 'gyur/ / nyon mongs pa bags chung bar 'gyur/[1033] / sems can la snying rje skye bar 'gyur/ / sgrub pa la nan tan byed par 'gyur/ / g.yeng ba thams cad spang bar 'gyur/ / tshe 'di la mi chags shing zhen pa med par 'gyur ro/ /

(D) The six signs of having cultivated wisdom are you become more heedful with respect to virtue, your afflictions decrease, compassion arises for sentient beings, you apply yourself earnestly to practice, you reject all forms of distraction, and you are no longer attached to and are free of clinging to the things of this life.

d.div: [1033] shas chung / dpal spungs/

f.d:
de ltar yang rin chen phreng ba las/
stong pa nyid la goms pa yis/ / dge ba dag la bag yod thob/[1034]/ces pa la sogs pa gsungs so//

Therefore it is said, in the Precious Garland:
Through familiarity with emptiness, heedfulness with regard to virtue is attained.[666]

d.div: [1034] sde dge_4158_bstan/ spring yig_ge_mgon po klu sgrub/ rin chen phreng ba/ le'u/ 3_sh+loka_88_shog_117_ba6_'gyur khyad che/
[666] Nāgārjuna, Ratnāvalī 3:88, Toh 4158 Tengyur, spring yig, ge, 117b6.

f.d:
shes rab kyi 'bras bu ni/ mthar thug dang / gnas skabs gnyis su shes par bya'o/ / de la mthar thug ni bla na med pa'i byang chub thob ste/ de ltar yang shes rab bdun brgya pa las/
'jam dpal shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa la spyad na/ byang chub sems dpa' chen po myur du bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub tu mngon par rdzogs par 'tshang rgya bar 'gyur ro/[1035] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The seventh point explains the fruits of the perfection of wisdom. These should be understood as being twofold: the ultimate result and the temporary consequences. The ultimate result is to attain enlightenment. Thus the Perfection of Wisdom in Seven Hundred Lines teaches:
Mañjuśrī! Through practicing the perfection of wisdom, bodhisattva mahāsattvas will rapidly and genuinely become perfectly enlightened in peerless, unsurpassable perfect buddhahood.[667]

d.div: [1035] sde dge_90_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ cha_sher phyin bdun brgya pa/ shog_203_ba7
[667] Saptaśatikānāmaprajñāpāramitā, Toh 90 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, cha, 203b7.

f.d:
gnas skabs su ni/ bde legs thams cad 'byung ste/ ji skad du/ 'phags pa sdud pa las/
sangs rgyas sras dang nyan thos rang rgyal lha rnams dang / / 'gro ba kun gyi bde skyid chos rnams ci snyed pa/ / de kun shes rab pha rol phyin pa mchog las byung /[1036] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In the short term, every good and excellent thing will occur. As it is said, in the Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom:
Whatever delightful, happy things are encountered by bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, gods, or any being, all derive from the supreme perfection of wisdom.[668]

d.div: [1036] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ le'u/ 28_sh+loka_4_shog_16_na7
[668] Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā, Toh 13 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 16a7.

f.d: dam chos yid bzhin gyi nor bu thar pa rin po che'i rgyan las/ shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i le'u ste bcu bdun pa'o// //
This concludes the seventeenth chapter, concerning the perfection of wisdom, in this Ornament of Precious Liberation, a Wish-Fulfilling Gem of Sublime Dharma. /210/
(byang chub sems dpa'i sa dang lam bshad pa/)
le'u bco brgyad pa/ lam gyi rnam bzhag
18. The Presentation of the [Five] Paths

de ltar dang po byang chub mchog tu sems bskyed nas/ bslab bya de dag la nan tan byas pas/ byang chub sems dpa'i sa lam rnams rim gyis bgrod par 'gyur ro/ / de la lam bshad na/ sdom ni/
tshogs kyi lam dang sbyor lam dang / / mthong ba'i lam dang sgom lam dang / / yongs su mthar phyin pa yi lam/ / lnga yis lam rnams yongs su bsdus/[1037] / zhes gsungs so//

Having first given rise to the intention to achieve supreme enlightenment and having earnestly engaged in the training presented ear-lier, a person will traverse the paths and levels of the bodhisattva in their respective sequence. To present the path, the following:
The paths are totally encompassed within these five: the path of accumulation, the path of application, the path of seeing, the path of cultivation, and the path of complete accomplishment.

d.div: [1037] shes pa'o/ dpal spungs/

f.d: de ltar lam lnga po de byang chub lam sgron gyi gzhung ltar na yang / dang po skyes bu chung 'bring gnyis kyi chos bsgoms nas gzhi brtan par bya ba dang / de nas smon 'jug gnyis kyi sems bskyed pa dang / de nas tshogs gnyis bsags pa la 'bad par bstan pa de rnams kyis tshogs lam legs par bstan pa yin no/ / rim gyis drod sogs thob byas nas/[1038] /zhes pas ni sbyor lam bstan pa yin no/ / rab dga' la sogs thob gyur te/[1039] /zhes pas ni mthong lam dang sgom lam dang mthar phyin pa'i lam bstan pa yin no/ /

According to the treatise Lamp for the Path to Awakening, these five paths are taught as follows. The first, the path of accumulation, lays the founda-tion through cultivating the Dharma instructions suited to a persons of initial and middling capacities. These are followed by development of the two aspects of bodhicitta—aspiration and engagement—and the amassing of the two accumulations. The text then teaches how the path of application occurs, “through an understanding acquired progressively through the sub-phases of heat and so forth.”[669] The paths of seeing, cultivation, and complete accomplishment are taught through “the Joyous and so on are attained.”[670]

d.div: [1038] sde dge_3947_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_dpal mar me mdzad ye shes/ lam sgron/ sh+loka_60_shog_240_ba4
[1039] gong mtshungs/ lam sgron/ sh+loka_60_shog_240_ba5

[669] Atiśa, Bodhipathapradīpa verse 59b, Toh 3947 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 240b4. As is explained below in the text, the “heat” here is metaphorical and has nothing to do with an experience of heat during meditation. The metaphor is one of approaching a blaze, such as a bonfire, and reaching that initial point where the heat can be felt. The “blaze” referred to is that of pristine awareness.
[670] Ibid. verse 59c, 240b5.

f.d: de la tshogs lam ni/ rigs dang ldan pa gcig gis dang por byang chub mchog tu sems bskyed/[1040] slob dpon las gdams ngag mnos nas/ drod kyi ye shes ma skyes kyi bar du dge ba la 'bad pa byed tshad rnams yin no/[1041] / de'i skabs su rtogs pa dang mos pa las gyur pa dang / lhag par 'dod pa las gyur pa dang / thob pa las gyur pa dang bzhir dbye'o/ /

First is the path of accumulation. It represents all the efforts that those endowed with the Mahayana potential will have to make in the practice of virtue, from the moment they first set their mind on supreme enlightenment and receive some advice and instruction from a teacher until such time as the attainment of the pristine awareness of the heat subphase [of the path of application]. This phase of the path is itself subdivided into four, according to whether it is informed by understanding, aspiration, longing for the sublime, or actual attainment.

d.div: [1040] sems bskyed la/ dpal spungs/
[1041] 'bad par/ dpal spungs/

f.d: de dag ci'i phyir tshogs lam zhes bya zhe na/ drod la sogs pa rtogs pa skye ba'i snod du rung bar bya ba'i phyir/ dge ba'i tshogs gsog par byed pas na tshogs lam zhes bya'o/[1042] / de dag la thar pa'i cha dang mthun pa'i dge ba'i rtsa ba zhes kyang bya'o/ / gnas skabs de na byang chub kyi phyogs kyi chos kyi dbang du byas na/ dran pa nye bar bzhag pa bzhi dang / yang dag par spong ba bzhi dang / rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa bzhi ste/ chos bzhi gsum bcu gnyis bsgom pa'o/ /

Why is it called the path of accumulation? It is so called because of its activities, which serve to gather and establish the accumulations of virtue and so forth in order to make a person a vessel suitable for realizations such as those of heat and so forth to arise. They are also referred to as “roots of virtue conducive to liberation.” During that particular period, one cultivates twelve—that is, three sets of four—[of the thirty-seven] factors conducive to awakening. They are: (1–4) the four foundations of mindfulness, (5–8) the four perfect endeavors, and (9–12) the four bases of magical powers.

d.div: [1042] gsog pas na/ dpal spungs/

f.d: de la dran pa nye bar bzhag pa bzhi ni/ lus dran pa nye bar bzhag pa dang / tshor ba dran pa nye bar bzhag pa dang / sems dran pa nye bar bzhag pa dang / chos dran pa nye bar bzhag pa ste/ de dag ni tshogs lam chung ngu'i dus so/ /

Of these, the four foundations of mindfulness, which constitute the lower stage of the path of accumulation, involve developing: (1) mindfulness of body, (2) mindfulness of feelings, /211/ (3) mindfulness of mind, and (4) mindfulness of phenomena.

yang dag par spong ba bzhi ni/ sdig pa mi dge ba'i chos skyes pa spong ba dang / ma skyes pa mi bskyed pa dang / gnyen po dge ba'i chos ma skyes pa bskyed pa dang / skyes pa 'phel par byed pa ste/ de dag ni tshogs lam 'bring gi dus su'o/ /

The four perfect endeavors, which constitute the middle stage of the path of accumulation, are: (1) relinquishing the existing evils and nonvirtues, (2) not giving rise to evils and nonvirtues currently absent, (3) giving rise to virtuous remedies not yet present, and (4) increasing virtues already developed.

rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa bzhi ni/ bdun pa'i ting nge 'dzin dang / brtson 'grus kyi ting nge 'dzin dang / sems kyi ting nge 'dzin dang / dpyod pa'i ting nge 'dzin te/ de dag ni tshogs lam chen po'i dus su'o//

The four bases of magical powers, which constitute the upper stage of the path of accumulation, are: (1) meditative absorption through aspiration, (2) meditative absorption through diligence, (3) meditative absorption through intention, and (4) meditative absorption through analysis. These above are emcompassed within the path of accumulation.

sbyor ba'i lam ni tshogs lam rab kyi mthar phyin pa'i rjes la/ bden pa bzhi rtogs pa dang rjes su mthun pa nges 'byed yan lag rnam bzhi zhes bya ba skye ba ste/ drod dang / rtse mo dang / bzod pa dang / 'jig rten chos mchog rnams so/ /

The second is the path of application. This follows on from the proper completion of the path of accumulation. It is the birth of “the four sub-phases of definite breakthrough in understanding” conducive to realization of the four noble truths. The four subphases are called: heat, the peak, fearless acceptance, and the highest worldly realization.

de dag la ci'i phyir na sbyor lam zhes bya zhe na/ bden pa mngon par rtogs pa la sbyor ba'i don gyis na sbyor lam zhes bya'o/ / de yang drod dang rtse mo'i gnas skabs na dbang po lnga dang ldan ste/ dad pa'i dbang po dang / brtson 'grus kyi dbang po dang / dran pa'i dbang po dang / ting nge 'dzin gyi dbang po dang / shes rab kyi dbang po'o/ / bzod pa dang / 'jig rten chos kyi mchog gi gnas skabs na stobs lnga dang ldan te/ dad pa'i stobs dang / brtson 'grus kyi stobs dang / dran pa'i stobs dang / ting nge 'dzin gyi stobs dang / shes rab kyi stobs so/ /

Why is it called the path of application? Here “application” refers to connecting with a direct realization of truth. During the subphases of heat and the peak, five faculties are employed: faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. In the subphases of fearless acceptance and highest worldly realization, these become five powers: faith, diligence, mindfulness, meditative absorption, and wisdom.

mthong ba'i lam ni/ 'jig rten chos kyi mchog gi rjes thog tu/[1043] 'phags pa'i bden pa bzhi la dmigs pa'i zhi gnas dang / lhag mthong mtshungs par ldan pa dang bcas pa ste/ de yang sdug bsngal la chos shes pa'i bzod pa dang / sdug bsngal la chos shes pa dang / sdug bsngal rjes su rtogs pa'i shes pa'i bzod pa dang / sdug bsngal la rjes su rtogs par shes pa la sogs pa bden pa bzhi po re re la bzhi bzhi ste/ bzod pa dang shes pa skad cig ma bcu drug gi bdag nyid can no/ /

The third is the path of seeing. This follows on from the highest wordly realization subphase. It is the combination of tranquility and insight focused on the four truths of the noble ones. In relation to [the first truth, that of] suffering, there are [aspects of insight known as]: (1) receptivity to knowledge of the nature of suffering, (2) knowledge of the nature of suffering, (3) receptivity to subsequent knowledge of the nature of suffering, (4) subsequent knowledge of the nature of suffering. There are four such aspects for each of the four noble truths. The insight embodies these sixteen instants of receptivity and knowledge.

d.div: [1043] thogs su/ dpal spungs/

f.d: de dag la ci'i phyir mthong ba'i lam zhes bya na/ sngon ma mthong ba'i 'phags pa'i bden pa mthong bas na mthong ba'i lam zhes bya'o/ / gnas skabs de na byang chub kyi yan lag bdun dang ldan te/ dran pa yang dag byang chub kyi yan lag dang /[1044] chos rnam par 'byed pa yang dag / brtson 'grus yang dag / dga' ba yang dag / shin tu sbyangs pa yang dag / ting nge 'dzin yang dag / btang snyoms yang dag byang chub kyi yan lag go /

Why are those referred to as the path of seeing? Because at that stage authentic insight into the [four] truths of the noble ones is gained for the first time. During that stage, a person is endowed with the seven aspects of enlightenment /212/: (1) right mindfulness, an aspect of enlightenment (2) right discernment, (3) right diligence, (4) right joy, (5) right pliancy, (6) right meditation, and (7) right equanimity, an aspect of enlightenment.

d.div: [1044] de bzhin du/ chos rnam par/ dpal spungs/

f.d: sgom lam ni/ mthong lam skyes pa'i rjes thog nas bzung ste/ / de la 'jig rten pa'i lam dang / 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam gnyis so/ /
The fourth is the path of cultivation. It is what follows the path of seeing. It has two aspects: the mundane path and the supramundane path.

de la 'jig rten pa'i sgom lam ni/ 'jig rten pa'i bsam gtan dang po dang / gnyis pa dang / gsum pa dang / bsam gtan bzhi pa dang / nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched dang / rnam shes mtha' yas skye mched dang / ci yang med pa'i skye mched dang / 'du shes med 'du shes med min gyi skye mched rnams so/ / 'di dag bsgom pa la dgos pa gsum yod de/ sgom spangs kyi nyon mongs rnams mgo gnon par byed pa dang / tshad med pa la sogs pa'i yon tan khyad par can sgrub par byed pa dang / 'jig rten las 'das pa'i lam gyi rten byed pa'o/ /

The mundane path of cultivation comprises the first, second, third, and fourth worldly meditative concentrations (dhyāna) and the [four formless meditative attainments in the form of] the spheres of (1) limitless space, (2) limitless consciousness, (3) nothing whatsoever, and (4) neither awareness nor absence of awareness. There are three purposes in cultivating these: (a) to overwhelm the afflictions that are to be removed at the level of the path of cultivation, (b) to enable achievement of exceptional qualities such as the four immeasurables (c) to provide a basis for the supramundane path of cultivation.

'jig rten las 'das pa'i sgom lam ni/ ye shes gnyis la dmigs pa'i zhi gnas dang lhag mthong rjes su 'brang ba dang bcas pa ste/ de yang mthong ba'i lam du bden pa bzhi po re re la bzod pa dang shes pa bzhi bzhi ste/ bcu drug tu mthong ba la bzod pa brgyad ni mthong lam du mthong ba des chog[1045] / shes pa brgyad po ni sgom lam du bsam gtan bzhi dang / gzugs med gsum gyi ting nge 'dzin dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i sgo nas zhi gnas dang lhag mthong goms par byed pa'o// de yang chos nyid rtogs pa rnams goms par byed pa ni chos shes pa'i phyogs yin la/ ye shes rtogs pa rnams goms par byed pa ni rjes su rtogs pa'i shes pa'i phyogs yin no/ / 'du shes med 'du shes med min gyi skye mched ni/ 'du shes kyi rgyu ba yongs su mi gsal ba'i phyir 'jig rten pa nyid do/ /

The supramundane path of cultivation consists of tranquility and insight—along with their accompanying qualities—focused on the two aspects of pristine awareness. Now, of the sixteen facets of insight—the two facets of receptivity and two facets of knowledge corresponding to each of the four noble truths—gained during the path of seeing, the eight receptivities are proper to the path of seeing, and the insight gained is all that is needed to complete them. The eight facets of knowledge, however, require ongoing familiarization, and this is what is being developed through the path of cultivation. It is achieved through continued familiarity with tranquility and insight on the basis of the four meditative concentrations and the first three of the four formless meditative attainments. Cultivating the realization of suchness belongs to the aspect [of the path] known as knowledge of phenomena, whereas cultivating the realization of pristine awareness belongs to the aspect known as subsequent knowledge. As [for the final formless meditative attainment], the sphere of neither awareness nor absence of awareness, given that the activity of awareness lacks clarity within this sphere, it remains entirely as a mundane sphere.

d.div: [1045] des go chod/ dpal spungs/

f.d: de dag la ci'i phyir sgom pa'i lam zhes bya zhe na/ mthong lam du rtogs pa'i de kho na nyid sgom pa goms par byed pas na sgom lam zhes bya'o/ / gnas skabs de ni 'phags pa'i lam yan lag brgyad ldan te/ yang dag pa'i lta ba dang / yang dag pa'i rtogs pa dang /[1046] yang dag pa'i ngag dang / yang dag pa'i las kyi mtha' dang / yang dag pa'i 'tsho ba dang / yang dag pa'i rtsol ba dang / yang dag pa'i dran pa dang / yang dag pa'i ting nge 'dzin no//

Why are the above called the path of cultivation? Because in it, the person cultivates familiarity with the realizations gained on the path of seeing. During this stage the meditator is endowed with the eightfold path of the noble ones: right view, right thought, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, /213/ right mindfulness, and right meditation.

d.div: [1046] rtog pa/ dpal spungs/

f.d: mthar phyin pa'i lam ni/ rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin gyi rjes la skyes pa zad pa shes pa dang / mi skye ba shes pa'i rang bzhin no/ /
The fifth is the path of complete accomplishment. This occurs subsequent to the diamond-like meditative absorption, and it consists of the knowledge of cessation and that of nonarising.

de la rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin ni/ sgom lam gyi mtha'i spong ba'i lam gyi gnas skabs te/ sbyor ba'i lam dang bar chad med pa'i lam gyis bsdus pa'o// ting nge 'dzin de yang bar chad med pa/ sra ba/ brtan pa/ ro gcig pa/ khyab pas na rdo rje lta bu zhes btags pa'o/ /

Diamond-like meditative absorption refers to the final stage of elimination on the path of cultivation and thus is encompassed within the preparatory and uninterrupted stages of the path of cultivation. Since this particular meditative absorption is unimpeded, durable, stable, of a single taste, and pervasive, it is called “diamond-like.”

de la bar chad med pa ni rkyen 'jig rten pa'i spyod pas mthar mi phyin pa'i phyir ro/[1047] / sra ba ni/ sgrib pa thams cad kyis mi shigs pas so/ / brtan pa ni rnam rtog gis mi bskyod pas so/ / ro gcig pa ni rnam par ro gcig pas so/ / khyab pa ni shes bya thams cad kyi spyi'i de bzhin nyid la dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ /

It is unimpeded because no worldly activity can be a cause which might unsettle it. It is durable because none of the obscurations can damage it. It is stable because no thought can trouble it. It is of a single taste because has one flavor. It is pervasive because it is focused on the ultimate nature common to each and every thing that is knowable.

d.div: [1047] 'phan / dpal spungs/

f.d: ting nge 'dzin de'i rjes la skyes pa'i zad pa shes pa ni/ rgyu kun 'byung zad pa'i dbang gis bden pa bzhi la dmigs pa'i ye shes so/ /

Subsequent to the diamond-like meditative absorption, there is the knowledge of cessation of generation. This is pristine awareness focused on the four noble truths in terms of the exhaustion of all causes [of suffering].

mi skye ba shes pa ni/ 'bras bu sdug bsngal spangs pa'i dbang gis bden pa bzhi la dmigs pa'i ye shes so/ / yang na rgyu zad pa dang 'bras bu mi skye ba la dmigs pa'i ye shes ni zad pa dang / mi skye ba shes pa'o/ /

There is also knowledge of nonarising. This pristine awareness is also focused on the four noble truths, but here in terms of the resultant sufferings themselves having been eliminated. In other words, pristine awareness related to the exhaustion of causes and the nonarising of results is the knowledge of cessation and nonarising.

de dag la ci'i phyir mthar phyin pa'i lam zhes bya zhe na/ bslab pa mthar phyin pa yin zhing / mya ngan las 'das pa'i grong khyer du 'gro bas na mthar phyin pa'i lam zhes bya'o/ / gnas skabs de na mi slob pa'i chos bcu yod de/ mi slob pa'i yang dag pa'i lta ba nas/ mi slob pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi bar dang / mi slob pa'i rnam par grol ba dang / mi slob pa'i yang dag pa'i ye shes so/ /

Why are those referred to as the path of complete accomplishment? Because training has been completed, and it is the stage where the journey to the citadel of enlightenment has reached its end. At that stage there are ten qualities of no-more training.[671] They are [the eight qualities of the eightfold path—namely,] right view through to right meditation of no-more training, plus total liberation and perfect pristine awareness of no-more training.

d.div: [671] Literally, “qualities without needing to train” or “qualities of the phase of no-more learning.” These spontaneous qualities are contrasted to the previous four phases of the path, where effort and training are needed for qualities to arise.

f.d: mi slob pa'i chos bcu po de yang zag med kyi phung po lnga'o dbang du byas pa ste/ de la mi slob pa'i yang dag pa'i ngag dang / las kyi mtha' dang / 'tsho ba dang gsum ni tshul khrims kyi phung po'o/ / yang dag pa'i dran pa dang / ting nge 'dzin dang gnyis ni ting nge 'dzin gyi phung po'o/ / yang dag pa'i lta ba dang / rtogs pa dang / rtsol ba dang gsum ni shes rab kyi phung po'o/ / yang dag pa'i rnam par grol ba ni rnam par grol ba'i phung po'o/ / yang dag pa'i shes pa ni/ rnam par grol ba'i ye shes mthong ba'i phung po'o//

These ten factors, in which there is no more training to be performed form five uncontaminated aggregates. Right speech, right action, and right livelihood of no-more training constitute the moral discipline aggregate; right mindfulness and right meditation of no-more training constitute the meditative absorption aggregate; right view, right thinking, and right effort of no-more training constitute the wisdom aggregate; total, utter liberation of no-more training constitutes the total liberation aggregate; and right pristine awareness of no-more training constitutes the aggregate of seeing the pristine awareness of total liberation.
dam chos yid bzhin gyi nor bu thar pa rin po che'i rgyan las/ lam gyi rnam par gzhag pa bstan pa'i le'u ste bco brgyad pa'o// //
This concludes the eighteenth chapter, concerning the presentation of the paths in this Ornament of Precious Liberation, a Wish-Fulfilling Gem of Sublime Dharma. /214/
le'u bcu dgu pa/ sa'i rnam bzhag
19. The Presentation of the Levels

lam lnga po de dag la sa du yod ce na/[1048] sdom ni/
las dang po dang mos spyod dang // byang chub sems dpa'i sa bcu dang / / sangs rgyas sa ste de ltar na/ / bcu dang gsum gyis sa rnams bsdus/ / zhes so/ /

With respect to those five paths, if one asks, how many levels are there? For this, there is the following synopsis:
The [presentation of] levels has thirteen points: the begin-ner’s level, the level of practice by means of aspiration, the ten bodhisattva levels, and the level of buddhahood.

d.div: [1048] de la/ dpal spungs/

f.d:
sa de rnams ni/ byang chub lam sgron las kyang /
rab dga' la sogs thob 'gyur te/[1049] / zhes gsungs te/ rab dga' ni sa dang po yin la/ la sogs kyis ni 'og gi sa gnyis dang gong gi sa bcu bsdus so//

With respect to these levels Lamp for the Path to Awakening states:
. . . the Joyous and so forth are attained.[672] Here, “the Joyous” is the name of the first bodhisattva level, and the words “and so forth” include the two levels below it and the ten above it.

d.div: [1049] sde dge_3947_bstan/ dbu ma/ khi_dpal mar me mdzad ye shes/ lam sgron/ sh+loka_59_shog_240_ba5
[672] Atiśa, Bodhipathapradīpa verse 59c, Toh 3947 Tengyur, dbu ma, khi, 240b5.

f.d: de la las dang po pa'i sa ni/ tshogs lam gyi gnas skabs te/ rang gi rgyud ma smin pa smin par byed pa yin pas so/ /
The first point concerns the beginner’s level. This applies to the stage when the person is on the path of accumulation. It is so called because it brings that which is immature to maturity.

mos pa spyod pa'i sa ni sbyor lam gyi gnas skabs te/ stong nyid kyi don la mos pa byed pa tsam yin pas so/ / de'i dus na pha rol tu phyin pa'i mi mthun pa'i phyogs ser sna la sogs pa dang / mthong spang gi nyon mongs pa dang / shes bya'i sgrib pa kun tu btags pa rnams mi 'byung bar mgo gnon pa yin no/ /

The second point concerns the level of practice by means of aspiration. This corresponds to the period of the path of application. It is so called because its activity aspires singly to the meaning of emptiness. During this phase the following are crushed so as never to reoccur: (1) factors incompatible with the perfections—avarice and so forth, (2) afflictions that will be eliminated through the path of seeing, and (3) the acquired levels of cognitive obscuration.

byang chub sems dpa'i sa bcu ni sa dang po rab tu dga' ba nas bcu pa chos kyi sprin gyi bar ro/ / de ltar yang 'phags pa sa bcu pa'i mdo las/
kye rgyal ba'i sras dag bcu po 'di ni byang chub sems dpa'i sa rnams yin te/ byang chub sems dpa'i sa rab tu dga' ba zhes bya ba dang /[1050] zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs so/ /

The third point concerns the ten bodhisattva levels. These are the levels from the Joyous through to the Cloud of Dharma. The Ten Levels Sutra says:
O child of good family! These ten are the bodhisattva levels: the bodhisattva level of the Joyous. [673]

d.div: [1050] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ kha_sa bcu pa'i mdo/ shog_170_na2
[673] Ten Levels Sutra (Daśabhūmikasūtra), Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, kha, 120a2.

f.d: de la sa dang po rab tu dga' ba ni/ mthong lam skyes pa'i gnas skabs te/ stong nyid kyi don dngos su rtogs pa'o/ / sa gnyis pa nas bzung nas bcu pa'i bar ni/ sgom lam gyi gnas skabs te/ sa dang por rtogs pa'i de kho na nyid de las goms par byed pa'o/[1051]/

The Joyous—the first of the ten levels—corresponds to the path of seeing, in which emptiness is directly realized. The second through tenth levels are the path of cultivation. During these, insight into the suchness realized during the first level is cultivated.

d.div: [1051] de la goms/ dpal spungs/

f.d: byang chub sems dpa'i sa bcu po de dag kyang spyi'i chos dang / bye brag gi chos gnyis kyis shes par bya'o/ / de la spyi'i chos ni gsum ste/ sa'i ngo bo dang / sa'i nges tshig dang / sa bcur dbye ba'i rgyu mtshan no/ /

These ten bodhisattva levels should be understood both in general and specifically. First, the general points concerning the ten bodhisattva levels are three: (1) their nature, (2) the etymology of level, (3) the reason for a tenfold division. /215/
de la sa'i ngo bo ni/ chos bdag med pa mngon sum rtogs pa'i shes rab grogs ting nge 'dzin dang mtshungs par ldan pa slob pa'i rgyud kyis bsdus pa'o/ /

As for the nature of the levels, they consist of the wisdom directly realizing the selflessness of phenomena accompanied by the meditative absorption that exists within the mental continuum on the trainer’s stage.
sa'i nges tshig ni/ sa de dang de'i gnas skabs kyi yon tan gyi chos kyi rten byed pa'am/ sa gong ma'i gong ma skyed par byed pas na/[1052] sa zhes bya'o/ /

Concerning their etymology: they are called levels, or grounds, because they each serve as bases for all the qualities associated with them as well as with the states they represent. Furthermore, each one serves as the foundation that gives rise to the subsequent level.

d.div: [1052] sa gong ma/ dpal spungs/

f.d: sa'i nges tshig gi dpe ni/[1053] ye shes de la gnas shing longs spyod pas na sa ste dper na ba glang gi lhas bzhin no/ / ye shes de nyid bgrod pas na sa ste/ dper na rta dkyus sa bzhin no/ / ye shes de yon tan gyi chos thams cad skye 'khrungs gi gzhir gyur pas na sa ste/ dper na zhing sa bzhin no/ /

The following are analogies for the etymology of the term level. It is called level (or ground ) because all [higher qualities] reside within that pristine awareness and partake in it just as, for example, [all the cattle] reside within and use the cattle yard. Also, it is called the level (or ground) because [all higher qualities] traverse that pristine awareness just as [horses run on] the running tracks. Lastly, they are like fields, since they are the foundations on which grow all the qualities proper to pristine awareness.

d.div: [1053] sa'i nges tshig ni/ mi rigs dpe skrun khang / sa'i nges tshig gi dpe ni/ zhes pa nas/ dper na zhing sa bzhin no// zhes pa'i bar dpal spungs dpar mar mi byung /

f.d: sa bcur dbye ba'i rgyu mtshan ni/ yongs su sbyong ba'i khyad par gyis sa bcur phye ba'o/ /
The reason for a tenfold division is their specific particularities of complete nurturing.

bye brag gi chos ni sa re re zhing khyad par dgu dgus bstan te/[1054] ming gi khyad par dang / nges tshig gi khyad par dang / yongs su sbyong ba'i khyad par dang / nyams su blang bya'i khyad par dang / rnam par dag pa'i khyad par dang / rtogs pa'i khyad par dang / spangs pa'i khyad par dang / skye ba'i khyad par dang / mthu'i khyad par ro//

Second, the specific points about each bodhisattva level will be presented through nine particularities for each level: (1) name, (2) etymology, (3) thorough preparation, (4) practice, (5) purity, (6) realization, (7) things abandoned, (8) state of birth, and (9) ability.

d.div: [1054] bzhin/ mi rigs dpe skrun/

f.d: de la sa dang po'i
ming gi khyad par ni/ rab tu dga' ba'o/ /
Its specific name is the Joyous.

nges tshig gi khyad par ni/ sa de thob pa dang byang chub la nye zhing sems can gyi don 'grub pas rab tu dga' bar 'gyur bas na rab tu dga' ba'o/[1055] / de ltar yang mdo sde rgyan las/
byang chub la ni nye ba dang / / sems can don grub mthong ba la/ / rab tu dga' ba skye 'gyur te/ / de phyir rab dga' zhes brjod do/[1056]/ zhes gsungs so/ /

Its specific etymology: Those who have achieved this level feel immense joy because enlightenment is close at hand and benefit for sentient beings is now really being accomplished: hence its name, the Joyous. Thus it says, in the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras:
On seeing that enlightenment is close and that the good of beings is accomplished, the most supreme joy will arise. For that reason it is called the Joyous.[674]

d.div: [1055] don grub/ dpal spungs/
[1056] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 21_sh+loka_32_shog_37_ba3
[674] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 21:32, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 37b3.

f.d:
yongs su sbyong ba'i khyad par ni/ gzhi thams cad la gya gyu med pa'i bsam pa la sogs pa/ chos bcu la sbyangs pas sa de thob pa yin no/ / de ltar yang mngon rtogs rgyan las/
yongs su sbyong ba rnam bcu yis/ / sa ni dang po thob 'gyur te/[1057] / zhes pa la sogs pa gsungs so/ /

The specific thorough preparation: This level is achieved through mastery of ten qualities, such as having intentions that are never deceitful, no matter what domain of action or thought [the bodhisattva] is engaged in. Thus the Ornament of Clear Realization says:
Through ten aspects of thorough preparations,[675] the first level will be attained.[676]

d.div: [1057] sde dge_3786_bstan/ sher phyin/ ka_byams pa mgon po/ mngon rtogs rgyan/ skabs/ 1_sh+loka_49_shog_3_ba7
[675] The list of various trainings needed for mastery of this and the following nine bodhisattva levels are to be found in Maitreya’s Ornament of Clear Realization and its commentaries.
[676] Maitreya, Abhisamayālaṃkāra 1:49, Toh 3786 Tengyur, shes phyin, ka, 3b7.

f.d:
nyams su blang bya'i khyad par ni/ sa 'di la gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpa' de/ spyir pha rol tu phyin pa bcu ka nyams su len yang khyad par du sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa shas che ste/ sems can thams cad tshim par byed 'dod do/[1058] / de ltar yang 'phags pa sa bcu pa'i mdo las/
sa dang po'i thad ka las pha rol tu phyin pa bcu po dag las/ de sbyin pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa ches shas che ba yin te/ lhag ma rnams kyang mi bsgrub pa ni ma yin no/[1059] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The specific practice: Although bodhisattvas at this level practice all ten perfections, it is said that they place particular emphasis on practicing the perfection of generosity because of their wish to bring contentment to all beings. Thus the Ten Levels Sutra says:
From the outset of the first level, among all ten perfections, the perfection of generosity is emphasized, /216/ although this does not mean that the others are neglected.[677]

d.div: [1058] tshims/ dpal spungs/
[1059] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ kha_sa bcu pa'i mdo/ shog_182_ba5
[677] Ten Levels Sutra (Daśabhūmikasūtra), Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, kha, 182b5.

f.d:
rnam par dag pa'i khyad par ni/ ji skad du sa bcu pa las/
sa rab tu dga' ba 'di la mthong ba rgya chen po dang / smon lam gyi stobs kyis sangs rgyas mang po snang bar 'gyur te/ sangs rgyas brgya phrag mang po dang / sangs rgyas stong phrag mang po dang / de bzhin du sbyar te/ sangs rgyas bye ba khrag khrig 'bum phrag mang po snang bar 'gyur ro/ / de dag mthong nas lhag pa'i bsam pa rgya chen pos mchod par byed/ bsti stang byed do/ / de bzhin du sbyar te/ de'i dge 'dun gyi tshogs la yang ri mor byed do/ / dge ba'i rtsa ba de dag kyang bla na med pa'i byang chub tu bsngo bar byed do/ / sangs rgyas de dag las kyang chos nyan pa dang / len pa dang / 'dzin par byed do/ / chos de dag kyang nan tan gyis sgrub par byed do/ / bsdu ba'i dngos po bzhis kyang sems can rnams yongs su smin par byed do/[1060] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The specific purity: As is said in the Ten Levels Sutra:
On the first level, the Joyous, there is vast vision. Through the power of prayers, many buddhas are seen, many hundreds of buddhas, many thousands of buddhas. . . [etc.;] many hundreds of millions of buddhas manifest. On seeing them, you make offerings with a great and noble intention and express great respect. . . [etc.;] you also make offerings to their Sangha. You dedicate all those roots of virtue to unsurpassable enlightenment. You receive teachings from these buddhas, take them to heart, and remember them. These teachings are practiced earnestly, and beings are brought to maturity through the four means of attraction.[678]

d.div: [1060] gong mtshungs/ le'u/ 1_sh+loka_33_shog_182_na7_sa thob gyur ma thag tu 'jigs pa lnga dang bral/ 'tsho ba med dang 'chi dang man bsngags ngan 'gro dang / 'khor gyi 'jigs bral de la bag tsha'i rkam pa med/

f.d:
de ltar na/ bskal pa mang por sangs rgyas dang chos dang dge 'dun gsum mchod cing rjes su bzung ba dang / sems can yongs su smin par byas pa dang / dge ba bla na med pa'i byang chub tu bsngo ba ste/ rgyu gsum po des de'i dge ba'i rtsa ba rgya cher rnam par dag par 'gyur ba yin no/ / de yang ji skad du/
dper na gser sa le sbram de nyid gser mgar dag gis ci tsam ci tsam du mer bsregs pas/ de tsam de tsam du byang ba dang / yongs su dag pa dang / ci dgar las su rung bar 'gyur ro/ / de bzhin du sa dang po la gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpa' de'i dge ba'i rtsa ba yang rab tu byang ba dang yongs su dag pa dang / ci dgar las su rung bar 'gyur ro/[1061] / zhes gsungs so//

In such a way, and for many eons, (1) they make offerings to the buddhas, Dharma, and Sangha and are cared for by them; (2) they bring beings to spiritual maturity; and (3) they dedicate virtue to highest enlightenment.[679] Thus, through these three causes, all their roots of virtue are made very great and very pure. It says:
For instance, the degree of refinement and purity of gold, and its ability to lend itself to any desired use, will depend on the amount of work the goldsmith has put into its smelting. Like this, the roots of virtue of bodhisattvas on the first level are perfectly refined, completely pure, and fit for any use.[680]

d.div: [1061] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ kha_sa bcu pa'i mdo/ shog_183_na2
[679] These three factors are important in their own right and often cited as the activities of great bodhisattvas. Reference will be made back to this list of three in the following nine levels.
[680] Ten Levels Sutra (Daśabhūmikasūtra), Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, kha, 183a2.

f.d: rtogs pa'i khyad par ni/ spyir sa bcu po 'di rnams mnyam bzhag la rtogs pa gcig tu mtshungs mod kyi/ rjes kyi nges pa 'dren pa'i bye brag la ltos nas so so yod do/ / so so po de bshad na/ sa dang po la chos kyi dbyings kun tu 'gro ba'i don du rtogs te/ des bdag gzhan mnyam pa nyid rab tu thob bo/ / de ltar yang dbus mtha' las/ kun tu 'gro don zhes gsungs so/[1062] /

The specific realization: In general, realization is one and the same during meditative equipoise throughout the ten levels. The differences are in respect to the phases subsequent to the equipoise periods, and it is this aspect that will be considered relevant to each level. On this first level, the expanse of suchness is [realized as being] all-pervading, and this provides full realization of the sameness of self and others. Therefore the Clear Differentiation of the Middle and Extremes speaks of the “all-pervading truth.”[681]

d.div: [1062] sde dge_4021_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa/ dbus mtha' rnam 'byed/ le'u/ 2_sh+loka_16_shog_42_na1
[681] Maitreya, Madhyāntavibhāga 2:16a, Toh 4021 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 42a1.

f.d:
spangs pa'i khyad par ni/ sa de la nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa'i dbang du byas na/ mthong spangs kyi nyon mongs pa brgyad cu rtsa gnyis yod pa las/ ma lus par spangs pa yin no/ / shes bya'i sgrib pa'i dbang du na rnam pa gsum yod pa las/ lpags shun la yod pa lta bu rnams spangs pa yin no/ / 'jigs pa lnga dang yang bral lo/ / 'phags pa sa bcu pa'i mdo las kyang /
sa rab tu dga' ba 'di thob ma thag tu 'jigs pa lnga po gang yin pa 'di lta ste/ 'tsho ba med pa'i 'jigs pa'am/ tshigs su bcad pa med pa'i 'jigs pa'am/ 'chi ba'i 'jigs pa'am/ ngan 'gro'i 'jigs pa'am/ 'khor gyi nang du bag tsha ba'i 'jigs pa de dag thams cad de la med pa yin no/[1063] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The specific things abandoned: In terms of the afflictions obscuration, all the eighty-two afflictions[682] to be overcome through the path of seeing have been eliminated. Of the three types of knowledge obscurations, /217/ the ones comparable to a rough outer skin are eliminated. Five types of fear or anxiety are absent. These are described in the Ten Levels Sutra:
What are the five fears present until the level of the Joyous is attained? They are fear of not gaining a livelihood, fear of not having a good reputation, fear of death, fear of the lower states of existence, and anxiety about being stuck among many worldly people. At that level these are all annihilated.[683]

d.div: [1063] sde dge_44_bka'/ phal chen/ kha_sa bcu pa'i mdo/ shog_186_na5

[682] The usual number is eighty-eight, based on Maitreya’s Ornament of Clear Realization. Eighty-two could have been an early slip, by Gampopa himself or by a copyist or woodblock carver, that has been reproduced ever since.
[683] Ten Levels Sutra (Daśabhūmikasūtra), Toh 44 Kangyur, phal chen, kha, 126a5.

f.d:
skye pa'i khyad par ni/[1064] sa 'di la gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpa' de phal cher 'dzam bu'i gling la dbang ba'i 'khor los sgyur ba'i rgyal por 'gyur te/ sems can rnams kyi ser sna'i dri ma sel lo// de ltar yang rin chen phreng ba las/
de yi rnam par smin pas ni/ / 'dzam gling dbang phyug chen por 'gyur/[1065] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The specific state of birth: Bodhisattvas on this level are mostly reborn as universal monarchs in Jambudvīpa. There they remove the pollution of beings’ avarice. The Precious Garland says:
As a full consequence of this, they become a mighty ruler of Jambudvīpa.[684]

d.div: [1064] ma dper/ skyes pa'i khyad par ni/ zhes byung yang dpar ma gzhan ltar/ skye ba'i khyad par ni/ zhes bcos/
[1065] sde dge_4158_bstan/ spring yig_ge_mgon po klu sgrub/ rin chen phreng ba/ le'u/ 5_sh+loka_42_shog_123_ba4
[684] Nāgārjuna, Ratnāvalī 5:42, Toh 4158 Tengyur, spring yig, ge, 123b4.

f.d: skye ba'i khyad par gsungs pa 'di dag kyang rang bzhin la bsams kyi/[1066] gzhan don ni gang la gang 'dul du rnam pa du mar yang kun tu ston te/ skyes pa'i rabs las gsungs pa bzhin no/ /

Although this is the special particularity of birth mentioned, through their pure intention to benefit others, they can manifest themselves anywhere and in any way needed to train beings, as was well taught in the Jātaka stories.

d.div: [1066] bsam gyi/ dpal spungs/

f.d:
mthu'i khyad par ni/ ji skad du/
