f.d:
yang de nyid kyi le'u nyer gcig pa las kyang /
bla na med pa'i sangs rgyas kyi ye shes yod do/ / chos kyi 'khor lo bskor ba yod do/ / sems can yongs su smin par byed pa yod do/[1149] / zhes gsungs so/ /

It also says, in the twenty-first chapter of the same work:
There is the pristine awareness of a perfect buddha. There is the turning of the wheel of Dharma. There is the bringing of beings to maturity.[748]

d.div: [1149] sde dge_8_bka'/ sher phyin/ ca_shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa stong phrag brgya pa/ le'u/ 21_shog_333_na7
[748] Śatasāhasrikāprajñāpāramitā, Toh 8 Kangyur, sher phyin, ’a, 333a7.

f.d:
mdo gzhan las kyang ye shes bshad pa mang po yod do// bstan bcos kyi dbang du byas na/ mdo sde rgyan las kyang /
ji ltar nyi ma'i 'od zer gcig / byung na 'od zer kun 'byung ba/ / de bzhin sangs rgyas rnams kyi yang / / ye shes 'byung bar shes par bya/[1150] / zhes sogs dang /
me long ye shes mi g.yo ste/ / ye shes gsum ni de la brten/ / mnyam pa nyid dang so sor rtogs/ / bya ba grub pa kho na'o/[1151] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Many statements on pristine awareness are also to be found in other sutras. Of the treatises, we find, in the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras:
You should know that just as when one sun ray shines all the others are shining too, so it is the case also with the pristine awareness of the buddhas.[749]. . . And:
The mirror-like pristine awareness is immovable and is the basis for the other three pristine awarenesses of equanimity, discernment, and activity.[750]

d.div: [1150] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 10_sh+loka_31_shog_10_na1
[1151] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 9_sh+loka_67_shog_11_ba4
[749] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 10:31, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 10a1.

f.d: bstan bcos gzhan las kyang sangs rgyas kyi ye shes bshad do/ / gzhung de dag la brten nas kha cig sangs rgyas la ye shes mnga' bar bzhed do// de yang mnga' lugs bshad na/ ye shes de mdor bsdu na ji lta ba mkhyen pa'i ye shes dang / ji snyed pa mkhyen pa'i ye shes gnyis yin la/

Buddha pristine awareness is also mentioned in other treatises. The opinion of those who say that buddhas possess pristine awareness is based on these authoritative texts. The following explains the way in which the buddhas possess pristine awareness. In brief, pristine awareness is twofold: (1) pristine awareness of the ways things are, and (2) pristine awareness of things in their manifoldnesss.

de la ji lta ba mkhyen pa'i ye shes ni/ don dam mkhyen pa ste/ sngar brjod pa ltar rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin gyi mthar thug pa de kho na nyid yongs su goms pa las/ yul gyi spros pa ma lus par bcad pa na/ blo'i 'jug pa mtha' dag rab tu zhi bas/ chos kyi dbyings spros pa med pa dang / ye shes spros pa med pa gnyis ro gcig pas/ chu la chu bzhag pa'am mar la mar bzhag pa ltar dbyer med pa'am/ gzugs ci yang ma mthong ba la nam mkha' mthong bar bsnyad pa ltar ram/ snang ba med pa'i shes rab chen po yon tan rin po che thams cad kyi rten du gyur pa ste/

Of these, the pristine awareness of the way things are is the perception of the ultimate truth. For, as mentioned above, when through complete familiarity with suchness in the culimination of the diamond-like meditative absorption, every single conceptual elaboration pertaining to objectification has been severed, every form of mental activity has come to cease. As such the ultimate expanse free of conceptual elaboration and pristine awareness free of conceptual elaboration have merged into a single taste, indivisible like water poured into water or butter mixed into butter. So, like referring to seeing no form as “seeing empty space,” the great wisdom devoid of any appearance had become the ground of all precious qualities.

de ltar yang /
ji ltar chu la chu bzhag dang / / mar la mar ni rjes zhugs ltar// shes bya spros bral de nyid dang / / dbyer med ye shes rnam 'dres pa/ / de ni sangs rgyas thams cad kyi// rang bzhin chos sku zhes byar brjod/[1152]/ces pa dang /
nam mkha' mthong zhes sems can tshig tu rab brjod pa/ / nam mkha' ji ltar mthong ste don 'di brtags par gyis/ / de ltar chos mthong ba yang de bzhin gshegs pas bstan/ / mthong ba dpe gzhan gyis ni bsnyad par nus ma yin/[1153]/ zhes gsungs so/ /

Therefore it is said:
Like water poured into water, like butter mixed into butter, /231/ the knowable free of elaboration and pristine awareness free of elaboration are totally fused. It is this that is called dharmakāya and that is the essential nature of all the buddhas.[751] And:
People talk of seeing space. Think about it and consider how they see space. The Tathāgatha taught that this is how to see phenomena. Such seeing cannot be expressed by any other example.[752]

d.div: [1152] spring yig bdud rtsi'i thigs pa/ rngog blo ldan shes rab/ bka' gdams gsung 'bum phyogs bsgrigs pod dang po/ shog_709_phreng / 6
[1153] sde dge_13_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_mdo sdud pa/ le'u/ 12_sh+loka_9_shog_8_ba3
[751] Although Gampopa does not name the source of this quote, these lines can be found in the famed translator Ngok Loden Sherap’s A Letter Entitled “Droplets of Nectar,” p. 709, line 6.
[752] Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom (Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā), Toh 13 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 8b3.

f.d: ji snyed pa mkhyen pa'i ye shes kun rdzob tha snyad pa'i don rnam pa thams cad du mkhyen pa yin te/ rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin la brten nas sgrib pa'i sa bon thams cad bcom pas shes rab chen por gyur/[1154] / de'i stobs kyis shes bya'i tshogs dus gsum gyis bsdus pa'i don mtha' dag skyu ru ra rlon pa lag mthil du bzhag pa ltar mkhyen zhing gzigs pa yin no/ /

The pristine awareness of things in their manifoldness is omniscience with respect to conventional, relative reality. All potential for obscuration has been destroyed by the diamond-like meditative absorption, and so there is great wisdom. Through its power, every aspect of the knowable throughout the three periods of time is seen and known, as clearly as if it were a fresh purple plum in the palm of the hand.

d.div: [1154] 'gyur/ dpal spungs/

f.d:
mdo las kyang sangs rgyas kyis kun rdzob mkhyen par bshad de/ ji skad du/
rma bya'i mdongs ni gcig pu yi/ / rgyu yi rnam pa tha dad pa/ / kun mkhyen min pa'i shes bya min/ / de shes pa ni kun mkhyen stobs/[1155]/ zhes gsungs so/ /

The sutras speak of the buddhas’ sublime awareness of what is relative in these terms:
All the various causes of a single eye in a peacock’s tail are unknowable by someone not omniscient, yet such knowledge is within the power of the Omniscient One.[753]

d.div: [1155] sde dge_4090_bstan/ mngon pa/ ku_dbyig gnyen/ chos mngon pa mdzod kyi rang 'grel/ gnas/ 1_shog_92_ba4
[753] Vasubandhu, Commentary on the Treasury of Higher Knowledge (Abhidharmakośabhāṣyam) 1:92, Toh 4090 Tengyur, mngon pa, ku, 92b4.

f.d:
rgyud bla ma las kyang /
thugs rje chen pos 'jig rten mkhyen/ / 'jig rten kun la gzigs nas ni/[1156] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Furthermore, the Uttaratantra says:
With great compassion he knows the world. Having seen everything in the world. [754]

d.div: [1156] sde dge_4024_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 2_sh+loka_53_shog_64_ba2
[754] Maitreya, Uttaratantra 2:53, Toh 4024 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 64b2.

f.d:
de yang ji ltar mkhyen zhing gzigs na dngos 'dzin lta bu ma yin te/ sgyu ma lta bu mkhyen zhing gzigs pa ni/ de ltar yang chos yang dag par sdud pa'i mdo las/
dper na sgyu ma mkhan po 'ga'/ / sgyu ma thar par bya phyir brtson/ / gang phyir de ni mngon shes pas/ / sgyu ma la ni de mi chags/ / de bzhin srid gsum sgyu ma ltar/ / rdzogs pa'i byang chub mkhas pas mkhyen/[1157] / zhes gsungs so/ /

When buddhas know and see as described above, it is not as though they perceive things as real. They see and know things as illusions. Thus it says, in Perfectly Gathering the Qualities [of Avalokiteśvara] Sutra:
An illusionist is not himself duped by his conjurations and thus, through his clear knowledge of what is happening, does not become attached to his illusory creations. Similarly, those skilled in perfect enlightenment know the three worlds to be like an illusion.[755]

d.div: [1157] sde dge_238_bka'/ mdo sde/ zha_chos yang dag pa sdud pa'i mdo/ shog_43_ba4
[755] Dharmasaṃgītisūtra, Toh 238 Kangyur, mdo sde, zha, 43b4.

f.d:
yab sras mjal ba'i mdo las kyang /
sgyu ma mkhan pos sgyu sprul pa/ / sgyu ma lags par 'tshal bas na/ / de la rmongs par 'gyur ma lags/ / khyod kyis 'gro kun de bzhin gzigs/ / thams cad gzigs la phyag 'tshal bstod/[1158] / ces gsungs so//

In the Meeting of Father and Son Sutra, it says:
By remaining conscious of the fact that conjurations are but illusions, a magician will not fall under their spell. I pay homage and praise you, the omniscient ones, who regard all beings like this.[756]

d.div: [1158] sde dge_60_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ nga _yab sras mjal ba'i mdo/ le'u/ 24_bam po/ 10_shog_111_na3
[756] Pitāputrasamāgamasūtra, Toh 60 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, nga, 111a3.

f.d: yang kha cig na re/ yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas la ji lta ba mkhyen pa'i ye shes zhes bya ba don dam mkhyen pa ni mnga' la/ ji snyed pa mkhyen pa'i ye shes zhes bya ba kun rdzob mkhyen pa mi mnga'o/ / de ltar mkhyen rgyu yod pa la ma mkhyen pa ni ma yin te/ mkhyen rgyu kun rdzob med pas de mkhyen pa'i ye shes med pa'o/ /

Now, some hold the view that perfectly enlightened buddhas do possess the pristine awareness of the way things are—the awareness of the ultimate truth—but do not possess the pristine awareness of things in their manifoldness—the awareness of the relative. Their point is not that there is something there to be known and that the buddhas are not aware of it but rather that, since there is nothing relative to be aware of in the first place, there could be no pristine awareness that is aware of it.

de yang kun rdzob ni nyon mongs pa can gyi ma rig pas rgyu byas pa'i byis pa so so skye bo rnams la snang /[1159] nyon mongs pa can ma yin pa'i ma rig pas rgyu byas pa'i 'phags pa gsum la snang ste/ dper na mig nad can la skra shad dang rab rib snang ba lta bu yin/ sangs rgyas ni rdo rje lta bu'i ting nge 'dzin gyi mjug tu ma rig pa spangs nas/ chos 'ga' yang mthong ba med pa'i tshul du de kho na'i don gzigs pas/ kun rdzob 'khrul pa 'di sangs rgyas la mi mnga' ste/ dper na mig nad dag pa'i gang zag la skra shad dang rab rib mi snang ba lta bu'o/ /

“Relative” or “conventional” reality is something that appears to immature beings conditioned by afflicted ignorance. as well to /232/ the three types of realized beings who are conditioned by ignorance that does not belong to the class of affliction. This is analogous to the appearance of falling hair and blurs to someone with impaired sight. As for a buddha, given that following the diamond-like meditative absorption he has totally eliminated ignorance and thus “sees” suchness in the way someone “sees” nothing whatsoever, for a buddha this illusion of the relative is not present. This is analogous to the fact that, to those with unimpaired sight, there is no perception of falling hair or the blurs.

d.div: [1159] de yang kun rdzob ji ltar med na/ kun rdzob ni/ dpal spungs/

f.d: des na kun rdzob snang ba 'di ma rig pa'i dbang gis yin pas/ 'jig rten la ltos nas bzhag par zad kyi/ sangs rgyas la ltos nas med pas de mkhyen pa'i ye shes kyang med pa yin no/ / gal te sangs rgyas la snang ba dang bcas pa'i blo yod na/ 'khrul pa'i yul snang bas sangs rgyas nyid kyang 'khrul bcas su 'gyur la/ thub pa chen po rnams rtag tu mnyam par bzhag pa la sogs pa'i lung dang yang 'gal lo/ / (rgya cher rol pa las/ yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas/ / dus thams cad mnyam par bzhag go / zhes gsungs so//)[1160] zhes zer ro//

Therefore this appearance of the relative occurs due to the power of ignorance and is posited only in relation to [the perspectives of] the worldly. In relation to buddhahood, they have no existence, and so there can be no buddha’s pristine awareness that perceives it. Were the buddhas to posses a mind that contained relative appearances, then by definition, buddhas would themselves have to be deluded due to the manifestation of such deluded fields of experience. This is in contradiction to the scriptures, which state that the great victors are constantly in a state of meditative equipoise and so forth. (As it says, for instance, in the Vast Manifestation Sutra: “Totally pure and perfect buddhas are at all times in meditative equipoise.”[757] So they say.

d.div: [1160] sde dge_95_bka'/ mdo sde/ kha_mdo rgya cher rol pa/ 'di'i nang 'tshol zhib byed kyang ma rnyed/ dpal spungs dpar mar rgya cher rol pa'i mdo'i yig chung gi lung cha tshang mi byung /
[757] Lalitavistarasūtra, Toh 95 Kangyur, mdo sde, kha. This sentence is in small font in the Tibetan original, indicating it to be an embedded annotation; it is missing in the Palpung edition.

f.d:
de la 'dod pa snga ma ba na re/ rjes thob yin pa tsam gyis g.yeng ba la sogs par mi 'gyur bas/ rtag tu mnyam par bzhag pa la sogs pa'i lung dang yang mi 'gal lo/ /zhes gsungs so/[1161] / 'khrul yul snang ba tsam 'khrul par brjod pa yang mi 'thad de/ gzhan gyi shes ngo'i 'khrul yul thams cad snang yang / de 'dzin pa'i blos ma lus pa 'khrul pa nyid du shes bzhin du/ 'gro ba rnams kyi mtho ris dang / byang grol gyi rgyud nyid du brten par zad pas 'khrul bcas su ga la 'gyur/ des na/
'khrul pa tsam du shes pa na/ / ma 'khrul nyid du nges par bzung /[1162] / zhes gsungs so/ / zhes zer ro//

Of these the proponent of the former viewpoint asserts this. It is not the case that just by virtue of being a subsequent-meditation state that it involves distraction and so forth. Therefore there is no contradiction with the scriptures such as the ones that state [that the buddhas] always remains in meditative equipoise. It is also incorrect to state a perception to be deluded simply because illusory objects appear to it. For although all the illusory phenomena that are the objects of other’s illusions do appear [to the buddhas], the mind perceiving them recognizes all of it to be illusions. Furthermore, they dispel them, using them as a cause for the higher rebirth, purity, and liberation of beings. So how could there be delusion? Thus:
When they are recognized as mere illusions, that which is not an illusion is perceived with certainty.[758]

d.div: [1161] dpal spungs dpar mar zhes gsungs so zhes pa 'di mi byung ba dag par snang na'ang ma dpe rang sor bzhag yod/
[1162] 'khrul pa tsam du shes pa na/ /ma 'khrul nyid du nges par bzung / /zhes pa 'di gang nas drangs ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[758] The source of this quote has not been identified.

f.d: yang kha cig na re/ bden zhen med pa'i kun rdzob yul du byas pa la tshad ma'i gnod pa med la/[1163] gnod pa med pa de/ sangs rgyas kyi yul du byas kyang 'khrul par mi 'gro /[1164] zhes kyang zer ro/ /

Yet others say that there is no great logical harm in holding the relative as a valid object, provided one does not cling to it as real. And if anything is free of logical harm, even if the buddhas were to perceive it, there would be no delusion.

d.div: [1163] mtshan mas/ zhes mi rigs dpe skrun khang du byung yang nor par nges/
[1164] sangs rgyas kyi yul byas kyang / dpal spungs/ sangs rgyas kyis yul du byas kyang / mi rigs dpe skrun khang /

f.d:
des na 'dod pa snga ma ni/ ji snyed pa zhes bya ba sangs rgyas la rjes thob kyi ye shes mnga' bar 'dod pa ste/[1165] ji skad du/
snga ma ji ltar mkhyen pa ni/ / 'khrul med mnyam bzhag blo 'jug med/ / phyi ma ji snyed mkhyen pa ni/ / 'khrul snang rjes thob blo 'jug can/[1166] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Those who hold the first view maintain that buddhas do possess subsequent pristine awareness, what is referred to as [pristine awareness of] things in their manifoldness. Thus they say:
The first, awareness of the way things are, is: undeluded, equipoised, and without mental activity. /233/ The next, awareness of multiplicity, is: with deluded appearance, subsequent knowledge, and with mental activity.[759]

d.div: [1165] ji snyed pa mkhyen pa/ dpal spungs/
[1166] 'di rngog blo'i spring yig bdud rtsi'i thigs pa'i nang byung / rngog blo ldan shes rab/ bka' gdams gsung 'bum phyogs sgrig pod dang po/ shog_709_phreng / 7
[759] Ngok Loden Sherap, Letter Entitled “Droplets of Nectar,” p. 709, line 7.

f.d:
'dod pa phyi ma ni/ sangs rgyas la rjes thob kyi ye shes mi mnga' bar 'dod pa ste/ 'phags pa sgo mtha' yas pa sgrub pa'i mdo las/
de bzhin gshegs pa mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas nas/ chos gang yang thugs su ma chud ma mkhyen no/ / de ci'i phyir zhe na/ mkhyen par bya ba'i yul gang yang med pa'i phyir ro/[1167] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Those who hold the second view that buddhas do not possess the pristine awareness of things in their manifoldness quote as their authority the Infinite Means of Purification Sutra:
Having reached true and perfect buddhahood, the Tathāgata neither knows nor has in mind any phenomenon whatever. Why is this? Because there exists no objective reality whatsoever to be known.[760]

d.div: [1167] sde dge_46_bka'/ dkon brtsegs/ ka_sgo mtha' yas pa rnam par sbyong ba bstan pa'i le'u'i mdo/ shog_59_ba7
[760] Anantamukhapariśodhananirdeśaparivartasūtra, Toh 46 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ka, 49b7.

f.d:
gzhan las kyang /
mu stegs byed pa kha cig ni/ / thar par 'gro dang ldan zhes smra/ / khyod ni zhi bar gshegs gyur nas/ / zhugs gum lta bu bgrang du med/[1168] / ces gsungs so/ /

Furthermore, it is said:
Some non-Buddhists say that you speak of going to liberation, yet when you have arrived at peace nothing remains, like something burned away.[761]

d.div: [1168] sde dge_1109_bstan/ bstod tshogs/ ka_mtho btsun grub rje/ khyad par 'phags bstod/ sh+loka_49_shog_3_ba6
[761] Udbhaṭasiddhasvāmin, Praise of the Excellence [of the Buddha] (Viśeṣastava), Toh 1109 Tengyur, bstod tshogs, ka, 3b6.

f.d: de ltar na 'dod pa tha dad pa rnams bshad zin to//
This concludes my review of the divergent standpoints around this particular issue.

dge bshes pa ni/ yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas dngos ni chos kyi sku yin la/ chos kyi sku zhes bya ba ni/ nor ba thams cad zad pa'am/ rang bzhin log pa tsam zhig la/ de skad du/ tha snyad byas pa tsam yin/ don la chos sku skye med spros bral yin no/[1169] /

A geshé’s position on buddha pristine awareness is as follows.[762] The actual pure and perfect buddha is the dharmakāya. The very term dharmakāya—“embodiment of Dharma”—is applied to the exhaustion of all errors, and thus its nature is that of the opposite of errors. It is expressed in this way merely in terms of conventional reality. In actual fact, dharmakāya itself is unborn and free of conceptual elaboration.

d.div: [1169] 'dir dge bshes pa ni zhes pa su yin ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[762] Although it is clear by the usage of the term geshé that it is referring to a Kadampa master, who that specific master is remained undetermined.

f.d: rje btsun mi la'i bzhed kyi/ ye shes bya ba yang / de lta'i shes pa bzo bcos ma phog pa 'di la yod med dam/ rtag chad tshig dang blo las 'das pa 'di rang yin/ 'di la ci ltar brjod kyang 'gal ba ma yin pas/ ye shes kyang de lta bu yin te/ mkhas su re ba'i blos byas pas/ sangs rgyas rang la zhus kyang phyogs gcig pa gcig gsung du yod mi snyam/ chos sku blo 'das skye med spros bral yin/ nga la ma dri/ sems la ltos dang / de 'dra zhig yin gsungs pas de ltar du bzhed pa med pa bzhin no/ /

Jetsun Milarepa’s position is as follows. “What we call pristine awareness is this very uncontrived awareness, beyond all such terms and intellections as ‘is’ or ‘is not,’ ‘eternal’ or ‘nothing.’ Therefore, no matter which terms are used to express it, there is no contradiction. Even if someone, with an ambition to become learned, were to ask the Buddha himself [about this topic], I do not think there is something definite that he can say about it. Dharmakāya is beyond the intellect; it is unborn and free of conceptual elaboration. So do not ask me; observe your own mind. That is the way it is.”[763] Thus he does not uphold a standpoint in [dichotomous] terms characterized above.

d.div: [763] Most probably the author is here citing his teacher Milarepa’s oral teaching, not a specific text.

f.d:
mdo sde rgyan las kyang /
thar pa nor zad tsam pa nyid/[1170] / ces gsungs so/ /

It says, in the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras:
Liberation is simply the exhaustion of error.[764]

d.div: [1170] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 6_sh+loka_2_shog_6_ba1
[764] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 6b1.

f.d: des na sangs rgyas ni chos kyi sku yin la/ chos sku ni skye med spros bral yin pas ye shes mi mnga'o/ /
Thus a buddha is the dharmakāya, and since the dharmakāya is unborn and free of conceptual elaboration, it does not possess pristine awareness.

'o na mdo las ye shes gnyis gsungs pa dang 'gal lo/ /zhe na/ mi 'gal te/ mig gi rnam par shes pa sngor snang du skyes pa la/ sngon po mthong zhes zer ba bzhin du/ ye shes nyid chos kyi dbyings su gyur pa la ji lta ba mkhyen par bzhed la/ ji snyed pa mkhyen pa kun rdzob yin pas gdul bya'i snang ba la 'jog pas na/ lugs 'di bde ba yin zhes gsungs so/ /

One might say that this [standpoint] contradicts the sutras that speak of twofold pristine awareness. In fact, it does not, for just as visual consciousness arises with the perception of the color blue and one says, “I see blue,” so the pristine awareness that is the ultimate expanse is pristine awareness of is the way things are, whereas the pristine awareness of manifoldness is the relative aspect [of that same pristine awareness] when it is triggered by whatever manifests to [the deluded minds of] beings. This position is taught to be the most convenient approach to the topic.

de ltar na spangs pa phun sum tshogs pa'am/ ye shes phun sum tshogs pa de sangs rgyas kyi ngo bo'am rang bzhin no/ / rgyud bla ma las kyang /
sangs rgyas nyid du dbyer med pa/ / dag pa'i chos kyis rab phye ba/ / nyi mkha' bzhin te spangs pa dang / / ye shes gnyis kyi mtshan nyid do/[1171] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Thus the very essence or the very nature of a buddha [can be viewed as] the most perfect purity and the most perfect pristine awareness. As is said in the Uttaratantra:
Buddhahood is indivisible yet can be categorized /234/ according to its qualities of purity: Like the sun and space the purity of the two pristine awarenesses are characterized.[765]

d.div: [1171] sde dge_4024_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 2_sh+loka_4_shog_62_ba2
[765] Maitreya, Uttaratantra 2:4, Toh 4024 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 62b2.

f.d:
mdo sde rgyan las kyang /
gang la nyon mongs shes bya'i sgrib pa'i sa bon dus ring rtag ldan pa/ / spong ba shin tu rgya chen rnam pa kun gyis rab tu bcom gyur zhing / / gnas 'gyur chos dkar yon tan mchog ldan thob pa sangs rgyas nyid/[1172] / ces gsungs so//

Also, it says in the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras:
Those who, through vast purification, have absolutely triumphed over the obscurations that have been consistently present for such a long time— the afflictions and knowledge obscurations, along with their latent potentials— and who possess the supreme good qualities through perfect transmutation: those are buddhas![766]

d.div: [1172] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 10_sh+loka_12_shog_9_na4
[766] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 10:12, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 9a4.

f.d:
sgra'i don bshad na/ ci'i phyir sangs rgyas zhes bya zhe na/ ma rig pa gnyid dang 'dra ba las sangs nas/ shes bya gnyis la blo rgyas pas na sangs rgyas zhes bya'o/ / de ltar yang /
ma rig gnyid las sangs phyir dang / / blo rgyas gnyis phyir sangs rgyas yin/[1173] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The second point is the etymology of buddha. Why buddha? The term buddha (Tib. sangs rgyas) is applied because they have awakened (sangs) from sleep-like ignorance and because the mind has fully expanded (rgyas) with respect to the two aspects of the knowable. As it says:
He has woken up from the slumber of ignorance, and his mind has fully expanded, so he is the buddha.[767]

d.div: [1173] sde dge_3971_bstan/ dbu ma/ gi_zla ba grags pa/ skyabs 'gro bdun cu pa/ shog_251_na2
[767] Candrakīrti, Seventy Stanzas on Going for Refuge (Triśaraṇasaptatī), Toh 3971 Tengyur, dbu ma, gi, 251a2.

f.d: de la ma rig pa'i gnyid las sangs shes pa'i don ni/ sngar bshad pa'i spangs pa phun sum tshogs pa yin no/ / shes bya la blo rgyas shes pa yang sngar bshad pa'i ye shes phun sum tshogs pa nyid do//

dbye ba bshad na/ sangs rgyas la dbye na sku rnam pa gsum ste/ chos kyi sku dang / longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku dang / sprul pa'i sku'o/ / de ltar yang / mdo gser 'od dam pa las/
de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad la sku gsum mnga' ste/ chos kyi sku dang / longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku dang / sprul pa'i sku'o/[1174] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The third point concerns its aspects. Buddhahood can be divided into three aspects, namely, its three bodies: dharmakāya, saṃbhogakāya, and nirmāṇakāya. It says, in the Sutra of Golden Light:
All tathāgatas possess three bodies: the dharmakāya, the saṃbhogakāya, and the nirmāṇakāya.[768]

d.div: [1174] sde dge_556_bka'/ rgyud/ pa_'phags pa gser 'od dam pa'i mdo/ le'u/ 3_shog_164_ba1
[768] Suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtra, Toh 556 Kangyur, rgyud, pa, 164b1.

f.d:
'o na lung kha cig las sku gnyis su bshad pa dang / sku bzhir bshad pa yang yod/ /sku lngar bshad pa yang yod do zhe na/ de ltar bshad kyang thams cad sku gsum po de rang du 'dus pa yin te/ mdo sde rgyan las kyang /
sku gsum dag gis sangs rgyas kyi/ / sku bsdus par ni shes par bya/[1175] / zhes gsungs so//

Someone might remark that some scriptures speak of two bodies, others of four bodies, and some of even five bodies. Although they are discussed as such, the bodies are all covered by this categorization in terms of three bodies. Thus the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
Be aware that all the buddha bodies are included within the three bodies.[769]

d.div: [1175] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams mgon/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 10_sh+loka_65_shog_11_ba3
[769] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 11b3.

f.d:
sku gsum gyi rnam par bzhag pa bshad na/ chos kyi sku ni sangs rgyas dngos yin te/ 'phags pa brgyad stong pa las/
de bzhin gshegs pa ni gzugs kyi skur mi blta ste/ de bzhin gshegs pa ni chos kyi sku'o/[1176] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The fourth point is a presentation [of the bodies]. The dharmakāya is what buddha really is. The Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines says:
Do not view the Buddha as the form body. The Buddha is the dharmakāya.[770]

d.div: [1176] sde dge_12_bka'/ sher phyin/ ka_brgyad stong pa/ le'u/ 31_shog_277_ba3
[770] Aṣṭasāhasrikāprajñāpāramitā, Toh 12 Kangyur, sher phyin, ka, 277b3.

f.d:
mdo ting nge 'dzin rgyal po las kyang /
rgyal ba'i dbang po gzugs kyi skur mi blta/[1177] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The King of Meditation Sutra says:
Do not view the King of Conquerors as the form body.[771]

d.div: [1177] sde dge_127_bka'/ mdo sde/ da_ting nge 'dzin rgyal po'i mdo/ le'u/ 17_shog_62_na7_de la dgongs pa yin na_ma/
[771] Samādhirājasūtra, Toh 127 Kangyur, mdo sde, da, 62a7.

f.d: gzugs sku gnyis ni chos kyi sku'i byin rlabs dang / gdul bya'i snang ba dang / sngon gyi smon lam las grub pa'i sku ste/ de gsum 'dzom pa las byung bar shes par bya'o/ /

The two form bodies are a consequence of the convergence of the following three factors: (1) the power of transmission of the dharmakāya (2) the subjective experience of the spiritual trainees, and (3) one’s past aspiration prayers.

de yang chos kyi dbyings kyi byin rlabs 'ba' zhig las byung ba yin na ni/ chos kyi dbyings kyis sems can kun la khyab pas/ kun 'bad pa med par grol bar rigs pa'am/ yang na sems can kun sangs rgyas dang zhal mjal bar rigs te/ de ltar yang mi 'dug pas chos kyi dbyings kyi byin rlabs gcig pu las byung ba ma yin no/ /

Were the form bodies due solely to the power of transmission of the ultimate expanse (dharmadhātu), /235/ the logical consequence would be that everyone would be effortlessly liberated, since the ultimate expanse pervades all beings. Were that the case, it would follow that all beings would come face to face with the buddhas. However, since this is not so, they do not come solely from the power of transmission of the ultimate expanse.

gdul bya'i snang ba 'ba' zhig yin na ni/ med pa snang ba de log shes yin la/ log shes la brten nas sangs rgyas na/ sems can rnams kyis thog ma med pa nas log shes la spyad nas/ de tsam kun sangs rgyas zin par rigs te/[1178] de ltar mi 'dug pas gdul bya'i snang ba gcig pu yang ma yin no/[1179] /

Were the form bodies to be solely due to the subjective experience of beings training on the path, buddhahood would be dependent on error, since to perceive something that is not there is an error. Also, since beings have been perceiving erroneously since time without beginning, all of them should already be buddhas. But this not the case either, so the form bodies are not just the subjective projections of beings still training.

d.div: [1178] de tsam na/ dpal spungs/
[1179] de ltar yang / dpal spungs/

f.d: smon lam 'ba' zhig las byung ba yin na ni/[1180] yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas smon lam la mnga' brnyes sam ma brnyes/ ma brnyes na thams cad mkhyen par yang mi 'gyur la/ brnyes na smon lam ni sems can thams cad kyi don du nye ring med par btab pas/ smon lam gyi sgo nas kun 'bad pa med par grol bar rigs te/ de ltar yang mi 'dug pas/ smon lam gcig pu las byung ba yang ma yin no/ /

Were the form bodies to be solely due to former prayers, then has a true and perfect buddha achieved power over prayer? If not, then that buddha has not reached omniscience. If a buddha has, then since his prayers are unbiased and for the benefit of all beings, the logical consequence would be for each and every being to be liberated. But this is not the case, so the form bodies do not come solely from former prayers.

d.div: [1180] yin na yang / dpal spungs/

f.d: des na gzugs sku gnyis ni/ gsum po de 'dzom pa'i mthu las byung ba yin no/ /
Therefore the form bodies are a consequence of the combination of these three factors.
sku gsum du grangs nges pa'i rgyu mtshan ni/ dgos pa la ltos pa'i grangs te/[1181] rang don du chos sku yin la/ gzhan don du gzugs sku rnam gnyis yin no//

The fifth point explains the reasons for a definite number. There are three bodies, and this number is determined by necessity, inasmuch as there is dharmakāya as benefit for yourself and the two form bodies as benefit for others.

d.div: [1181] grangs nges te/ dpal spungs/

f.d: de la chos skus rang don ci ltar byed na/ chos kyi sku de thob nas yon tan thams cad kyi gzhi rten yin pas/[1182] [1183] stobs dang mi 'jigs pa la sogs pa'i yon tan thams cad bos pa bzhin du 'du bar 'gyur ba'i phyir ro/ / gzhan yang chos sku de thob par ma zad de/ chos kyi sku de la mos pa byas pa dang / cung zad rtogs pa dang / phyogs gcig rtogs pa dang / phal cher rtogs pa rnams kyang yon tan rim pa ltar/ cung zad dang / mang po dang / du ma dang /[1184] dpag tu med pa dang ldan no/ /

How does the dharmakāya represent benefit for yourself ? Once the dharmakāya has been achieved, it is the basis for all other qualities, such as the [four] fearlessnesses, the [ten] powers, and so forth, which gather as though they had been summoned. Furthermore, even if someone has not achieved dharmakāya itself, those who aspire to dharmakāya, have a little realization of it, a partial realization, or nearly complete realization of it will have just a few qualities, many qualities, a great number of qualities, or an immeasurable amount of qualities, respectively:

d.div: [1182] thob na/ dpal spungs/
[1183] thams cad kyi rten/ dpal spungs/
[1184] du ma dang / zhes pa dpal spungs dpar mar mi byung ba ltar dag par snang yang ma dpe rang sor bzhag

f.d: de la 'jig rten chos mchog man chad kyi ting nge 'dzin dang / mngon shes dang / mthu phun sum tshogs pa thams cad ni chos kyi sku la mos pa byas pa'i yon tan yin no/ /
The qualities arising from aspiration to dharmakāya are those of the meditative absorptions, clear cognitions, and all the superb qualities up to and including the highest worldly realization.[772]

d.div: [772] The final stage of the path of preparation, just prior to transition into the ārya state.

f.d: 'phags pa nyan thos dgra bcom pa rnams kyi spangs pa dang /[1185] mngon shes dang / rdzu 'phrul la sogs pa thams cad ni chos kyi sku cung zad rtogs pa'i yon tan yin no/ /
The qualities emerging from a little realization of dharmakāya are all the qualities of purification, clear cognition, supernatural ability, and so forth of realized śrāvaka arhats. /236/

d.div: [1185] nyan thos chen po/ dpal spungs/

f.d: 'phags pa rang sangs rgyas dgra bcom pa rnams kyi spangs pa'i ting nge 'dzin dang /[1186] mngon par shes pa la sogs pa thams cad kyang chos kyi sku phyogs gcig rtogs pa'i yon tan yin no/ /
The qualities emerging from a partial realization of dharmakāya are all the qualities of purification, meditative absorption, clear cognition, and so forth of realized pratyekabuddha arhats.

d.div: [1186] spangs pa dang / dpal spungs/ ting nge 'dzin dang / dpal spungs dpar mar med/

f.d: byang chub sems dpa' sa la gnas pa rnams kyi spangs pa dang /[1187] ting nge 'dzin dang / mngon shes la sogs pa thams cad kyang / chos kyi sku phal cher rtogs pa'i yon tan yin no/ /

The qualities emerging from nearly complete realization of dharmakāya are the qualities of purification, meditative absorption, clear cognition, and so forth of bodhisattvas of the bodhisattva levels.

d.div: [1187] sa dang lam la/ dpal spungs/

f.d: gzhan don gzugs sku rnam gnyis yod pas bzhag pa yin te/[1188] dag pa'i gdul bya'i ngos la longs sku'o/[1189] / ma dag pa'i gdul bya'i ngos la sprul sku'o// des na sangs rgyas la sku rnam pa gsum du nges so//

The two form bodies are presented in this way as benefit for others, inasmuch as there is the enjoyment body (saṃbhogakāya) that appears to pure disciples and the emanation body (nirmāṇakāya) that appears to impure disciples. Thus there are definitely three bodies.

d.div: [1188] gzhan don du/ dpal spungs/
[1189] ngo la/ dpal spungs/

f.d: sku gsum po so so'i mtshan nyid 'chad pa la/ chos kyi sku zhes pa de yang / chos kyi dbyings stong pa nyid kyi don rtogs pas/ nor ba thams cad zad pa'am/ 'khrul ngor snang ba'i rang bzhin log pa tsam zhig la/ chos kyi sku zhes tha snyad btags pa tsam yin gyi/[1190] don gyi ngo bo la chos kyi sku dang / chos kyi sku'i mtshan nyid dang / mtshan gzhir grub pa gang yang mi mnga' ba'i phyir/ bla ma mi las gsungs pa de ka ltar yin no/[1191] /

The sixth point describes the characteristic properties of the three bodies. First, dharmakāya simply refers to the exhaustion of all error—the turning away from what is by nature delusory—once the meaning of emptiness (namely, the ultimate expanse) has been realized. However, as such, dharmakāya is simply a term representing a conceptual convention. In real essence, there is no dharmakāya whatsoever possessing true existence, either as dharmakāya, as characteristic properties of dharmakāya, or as anything that could serve as a basis for properties of dharmakāya. Since it is like that, this is how my guru Milarepa explained it.

d.div: [1190] tha snyad du/ dpal spungs/
[1191] mi mnga' 'o/ /dpal spungs dpar mar/ mi mnga' ba'i phyir/ bla ma mi las gsungs pa de ka ltar yin no/ /

f.d: ldog pa'i sgo nas bshad na chos kyi sku mtshan nyid brgyad dang ldan te/[1192] mnyam pa dang / zab pa dang / rtag pa dang / gcig pa dang / yang dag pa dang / gtsang ba dang / 'od gsal ba dang / longs spyod rdzogs pa dang 'brel ba'o/ /
Dividing it into its various aspects, dharmakāya has eight characteristic qualities—namely, being identical, profound, permanent, unitary, right, pure, lumionous, and linked to the enjoyment body.

d.div: [1192] sgo nas btsal na/ chos sku'i/ dpal spungs/

f.d: de la mnyam pa ni/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi sku la khyad par med pa'i phyir ro/ / zab pa ni/ spros pa thams cad dang bral bas rtogs par dka' ba'i phyir ro/ / rtag pa ni/ 'dus ma byas pas thog mtha' bar gsum du skye 'gag dang bral ba'i phyir ro/ / gcig pa ni/ dbyings dang ye shes tha mi dad pas dbyer med pa'i phyir ro/ / yang dag pa ni/ sgro skur gnyis kyi mtha' las 'das pas phyin ci ma log pa'i phyir ro/[1193] / gtsang ba ni/ sgrib pa gsum (nyon mongs shes bya snyoms 'jug gi/)[1194]gyi dri ma dang bral ba'i phyir ro/ / 'od gsal ba ni/ rtog pa med pa ste rnam par mi rtog pas mi rtog pa de nyid du dmigs pa'i phyir ro/ / longs spyod rdzogs pa dang 'brel ba ni/ yon tan rgya chen po'i bdag nyid kyi/ longs spyod rdzogs pa'i rten du gyur pa'i phyir ro/ /

It is identical inasmuch as there are no differences among the dharmakāyas of the various buddhas. It is profound because it is difficult to realize, having nothing to do with conceptual elaboration. It is permanent because it is not composite; it is without coming into being or cessation; and it is without beginning, middle, or end. It is unitary because it is indivisible, the ultimate expanse [i.e., emptiness] and its pristine awareness being inseparable. It is right because it is without error, since it transcends the two extremes of underestimation and exaggeration. It is pure because it is free from the pollution of the three obscurations (namely, the afflictions and knowledge obscurations and the impediments to meditative attainment). It is luminous clarity. Free of conceptuality, it is focused on nonconceptual suchness. It is linked to the enjoyment body. It is the basis for the enjoyment body (saṃbhogakāya), which is the very expression of its vast qualities.

d.div: [1193] sgro bskur/ dpal spungs/
[1194] yig chung 'di dpal spungs dpar mar med/

f.d:
de ltar yang rgyud bla ma las/
thog ma dbus mtha' med cing rnam dbyer med/ / gnyis med gsum bral dri med rnam rtog med/ / chos dbyings rang bzhin gang yin de rtogs pas/ / mnyam par bzhag pa'i rnal 'byor pa yis mthong /[1195] / zhes gsungs so//

The Uttaratantra says:
Beginningless, devoid of center and periphery, it is indivisible, without the two, free from the three, stainless, and nonconceptual— such is realized to be the nature of the ultimate expanse /237/ when seen by the yogi resting in meditative equipoise.[773]

d.div: [1195] sde dge_4024_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 2_sh+loka_38_shog_63_ba7
[773] Maitreya, Uttaratantra 2:38, Toh 4024 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 63b7.

f.d:
mdo sde rgyan las kyang /
rang bzhin sku ni mnyam pa dang / / phra zhing longs spyod rdzogs 'brel dang /[1196] / zhes gsungs so//

The Ornament of Mahayana Sutras also says:
Identical, the nature body (svabhāvakāya), subtle and linked with the enjoyment body (saṃbhogakāya).[774]

d.div: [1196] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 10_sh+loka_62_shog_11_ba1
[774] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 10:62, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 11b1.

f.d: longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku yang mtshan nyid brgyad dang ldan te/ 'khor dang / zhing dang / sku dang / mtshan dang / chos dang / mdzad pa dang / lhun gyis grub pa dang / rang bzhin med pa'o/ /
Second, the enjoyment body (saṃbhogakāya) also has eight characteristics—those of entourage, domain, form, marks, teaching, deeds, spontaneity, and absence of an own-being.

de la gang dang lhan cig tu spyod pa'i 'khor ni/ sa bcu la gnas pa'i byang chub sems dpa' sha stag go/ gang du longs spyod pa'i zhing ni/ zhing khams yongs su dag pa'o/ / gang gis longs spyod pa'i sku ni/ dpal rnam par snang mdzad la sogs pa'o/ / gang dang ldan pa'i mtshan ni/ sku de mtshan bzang po sum cu rtsa gnyis dang / dpe byad bzang po brgyad bcu dang ldan pa'o/ / gang la rdzogs par longs spyod pa'i chos ni/ theg pa chen po 'ba' zhig go / gang mdzad pa'i 'phrin las ni/ rgyal sras lung ston pa la sogs pa mdzad pa'o/ / lhun gyis grub pa ni/ mdzad pa la sogs pa de dag thams cad la 'bad pa dang bral te/ nor bu'i rgyal po ltar lhun grub tu 'byung ba'o/ / rang bzhin med pa ni/ sku la sogs pa sna tshogs su snang yang / shel gyi kha dog ltar sna tshogs kyi rang bzhin dang bral ba'o/ /

The entourage with which it is spontaneously experienced is composed solely of bodhisattvas abiding in the ten bodhisattva levels. The domain in which it is experienced is that of the utterly pure buddhafields. The form or way in which it is experienced is in the form of illustrious Vairocana and so forth. The marks with which it is endowed physically are the thirty-two marks of excellence and the eighty adornments. The Dharma teachings through which it is perfectly experienced are solely that of the Mahayana. The enlightened activity that forms its deeds is to predict the future enlightenment of the bodhisattvas and so forth. Its spontaneity is that those deeds and so forth are all accomplished without any effort, occurring spontaneously as in the example of the supreme [wish-fulfilling] gems. Its absence of own-being is that even though it manifests various sorts of form, they are not its true nature. They are like the colors picked up in a crystal.

de ltar yang mdo sde rgyan las/
longs spyod rdzogs pa khams kun tu/ / 'khor yongs sdud dang zhing dang mtshan/ / sku dang chos rdzogs longs spyod dang / / mdzad pa dag gis tha dad do/[1197]/zhes gsungs so/ /

Thus the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
Perfect experience: in every domain a complete entourage, the place, the marks, the form, the perfect use of Dharma teaching, and its deeds. These are the various characteristics.[775]

d.div: [1197] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 10_sh+loka_61_shog_11_na7

f.d:
mngon rtogs rgyan las kyang /
mtshan ni sum cu rtsa gnyis dang / / dpe byad brgyad cu'i bdag nyid ni/ / theg chen nye bar longs spyod phyir/ / thub pa'i longs spyod rdzogs skur bzhed/[1198] / ces gsungs so//

Also, in the Ornament of Clear Realization, it says:
That endowed with the thirty-two marks and eighty adornments and partakes of the Mahayana is known as the enjoyment body of the Buddha.”[776]

d.div: [1198] sde dge_3786_bstan/ sher phyin/ ka_byams pa mgon po/ mngon rtogs rgyan/ skabs/ 8_sh+loka_12_shog_11_ba7
[776] Maitreya, Abhisamayālaṃkāra 8:12, Toh 3786 Tengyur, shes phyin, ka, 11b7.

f.d: sprul pa'i sku yang mtshan nyid brgyad dang ldan te/ rten dang / rgyu dang / zhing dang /

Third, the emanation body (nirmāṇakāya) also has eight principal characteristics—those of its basis, its cause, its domain, its duration, its character, its role of encouraging, its maturing function, and its liberating function.

dus dang / rang bzhin dang / 'jug par byed pa dang / smin par byed pa dang / grol bar byed pa'o// de la rten ni/ chos kyi sku ste g.yo ba med bzhin du'o/ / rgyu ni/ 'gro ba mtha' dag la phan par bzhed pa'i snying rje chen po las byung ba'o/ / zhing ni/ yongs su dag pa'i zhing dang yongs su ma dag pa'i zhing yong ngo / / dus ni/ 'jig rten ji srid gnas kyi bar du rgyun mi chad pa'o/ /

Its basis is the dharmakāya, [from which it emanates] without there being any movement. Its cause is tremendous compassion aspiring to benefit every single being. Its domain embraces both the very pure lands and quite impure ones. Its duration is that it endures, without interruption, for as long as the world endures.

rang bzhin ni/ sprul pa gsum gyi gzugs kyis te/ bzo sprul pa po wang len pa la sogs pa bzo sna tshogs dpe med par mkhas shing sbyor ba dang / skye ba sprul pa ri bong la sogs lus dman pa sna tshogs kyang len pa dang / mchog gi sprul pa dga' ldan nas gshegs pa dang / lhums su 'jug pa nas/ zhi ba chen por gshegs pa'i bar ston pa'o/ /

Its character is /238/ to manifest forms as the three types of emanation: • Creative emanations endowed with outstanding skill in and mastery of a given art or craft, such as playing lute and so forth • Birth emanations that take birth in various inferior bodies as specific types of existence, for example, as a hare • Supreme emanations that manifest [the twelve deeds]—descent from Tuṣita Heaven, entering the mother’s womb, and so forth, and eventually entering great peace.

de ltar yang mdo sde rgyan las/
bzo dang skye dang byang chub che/ / mya ngan 'das pa rtag ston pas/ / sangs rgyas sprul pa'i sku 'di ni/ / rnam par grol ba'i thabs chen po/[1199]/zhes gsungs so/ /

As it says in the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras:
Constantly manifesting as an artist, a human birth, great enlightenment, and nirvana, the Buddha’s emanation body is a great expression of liberation.[777]

d.div: [1199] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 9_sh+loka_64_shog_11_ba2
[777] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 9:64, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 11b2.

f.d:
rgyud bla ma las kyang /
sprul pa'i rang bzhin sna tshogs kyis/ / skye ba mngon par skye ba dang / / dga' ldan gnas nas 'pho ba dang / lhums su 'jug dang bltams pa dang / / bzo yi gnas la mkhas pa dang / / btsun mo'i 'khor la dgyes rol dang / / nges 'byung dka' ba spyod pa dang / / byang chub snying po gshegs pa dang / / bdud sde 'joms dang rdzogs par ni// byang chub chos kyi 'khor lo dang / / mya ngan 'da' bar gshegs mdzad rnams/ / yongs su ma dag zhing rnams su/ / srid pa ji srid gnas par ston/[1200] / zhes gsungs so/ /

As is said in the Uttaratantra:
Through emanations of various kinds, he manifestly takes birth—(1) descends from Tuṣitā, (2) enters the womb, and (3) is born. (4) Skilled in all arts and crafts, he (5) enjoys the company of his consorts, (6) [renounces], (7) undergoes hardships, (8) goes to the seat of enlightenment, (9) vanquishes the armies of harmful forces, (10) attains perfect enlightenment, (11) turns the wheel of Dharma, and (12) passes away. In all those realms, quite impure, he shows these deeds for as long as worlds endure.[778]

d.div: [1200] sde dge_4024_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 2_sh+loka_53_shog_64_ba3
[778] Maitreya, Uttaratantra 2:53, Toh 4024 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 64b3.

f.d: 'jug par byed pa ni/ 'jig rten tha mal pa dag ci rigs par mya ngan las 'das pa rnam pa gsum la 'dun zhing 'jug par byed pa'o/ / smin par byed pa ni/ lam la zhugs pa rnams tshogs yongs su smin par byed pa'o/ / grol bar byed pa ni/ dge bas yongs su smin pa dag srid pa'i 'ching ba las grol bar byed pa'o/ /

The role of encouraging is that the emanation body makes ordinary, worldly beings long for and work toward whichever of the three types of nirvana corresponds to their mentality. The maturing function is that the emanation body brings to full spiritual maturity those already engaged in the path. The liberating function is that the emanation body frees from the fetters of existence those who have reached full maturity in virtue.

de ltar rgyud bla ma las/
'jig rten zhi ba'i lam la 'jug pa dang / / rab tu smin dang lung ston rgyu yi gzugs/[1201] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Thus it says, in the Uttaratantra:
It causes worldly beings to enter the path of peace, brings them to full maturity, and is that which gives rise to predictions.[779]

d.div: [1201] gong mtshungs/ rgyud bla ma/ le'u/ 2_sh+loka_41_shog

f.d:
de ltar brgyad po de sprul pa'i sku'i mtshan nyid do/ / mngon rtogs rgyan las/
gang gis srid pa ji srid par/ / 'gro la phan pa sna tshogs pa/ / mnyam du mdzad pa'i sku de ni/ / thub pa'i sprul sku rgyun mi chad/[1202] / ces gsungs so//

These are the eight characteristics of the emanation body. The Ornament of Clear Realization says:
The body that acts simultaneously and in all sorts of ways to help beings for as long as existence continues is the unceasing emanation body of the Sage.[780]

d.div: [1202] sde dge_3786_bstan/ sher phyin/ ka_byams pa mgon po/ mngon rtogs rgyan/ skabs/ 8_sh+loka_33_shog
[780] Maitreya, Abhisamayālaṃkāra 8:33, Toh 3786 Tengyur, shes phyin, ka, 12b6.

f.d: khyad par ni gsum ste/ /mnyam pa'i khyad par dang / rtag pa'i khyad par dang / snang ba'i khyad par ro/ /
The seventh point concerns the three particularities of the buddha bodies: those of identity, permanence, and manifestation.

de la dang po mnyam pa'i khyad par ni/ sangs rgyas thams cad kyi chos kyi sku ni rten chos kyi dbyings tha dad med pas mnyam pa'o/ / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku ni dgongs pa tha dad med pas mnyam pa'o/ / sangs rgyas thams cad kyi sprul pa'i sku ni 'phrin las thun mong du gyur pas mnyam pa'o/ / de ltar yang mdo sde rgyan las/
de dag rten dang dgongs pa dang / 'phrin las kyis ni mnyam pa nyid/[1203] / ces gsungs so/ /

The particularity of identity is that the dharmakāya of all buddhas is identical, being inseparable from its support, the ultimate expanse. The enjoyment body of all buddhas is identical since its noble disposition is the same. The emanation body of all buddhas is identical /239/ because their activity is common. Therefore the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
These are identical because of their support, intention, and activity.[781]

d.div: [1203] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 10_sh+loka_66_shog_11_ba3
[781] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 10:66ab, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 11b3.

f.d:
rtag pa'i khyad par ni/ chos kyi sku don dam par skye 'gag dang bral ba'i bdag nyid yin pas rang bzhin gyis rtag pa'o/ / longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku ni chos kyi longs spyod rgyun chad pa med pa'i phyir rgyun gyis rtag pa'o/ / sprul pa'i sku ni mi snang bar gyur nas kyang yang dang yang du ston pa ste/[1204] rigs mthun rgyun chad kyang mtshams pa'i dus las mi yol bar 'byung ba'i phyir bya ba byed pas rtag pa'o/[1205] / de ltar yang mdo sde rgyan las/
rang bzhin dang ni rgyun mi chad/ / rgyun gyis de dag rtag pa nyid/[1206] / ces gsungs so/ /

The particularity of permanence: The dharmakāya is permanent by its very nature because, being the ultimate, its very identity is that which is without coming into being or ceasing. The enjoyment body is permanent through being continuous, inasmuch as the experience of Dharma that it manifests is uninterrupted. The emanation body is permanent insofar as its deeds are permanent. Although its manifestations disappear, it shows itself over and over again. Although that which manifests in correspondence to a certain need will cease, there is a functional permanence since it arises appropriately, without delay. The Ornament of Mahayana Sutras says:
Permanence of nature, of uninterruptedness, and of continuity. [782]

d.div: [1204] kun tu ston pa ste/ dpal spungs/ 1205_'tshams/ dpal spungs/
[1206] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 10_sh+loka_66_shog_11_ba4
[1207] dpal spungs dpar mar skabs 'gar/ skur/ zhes par/ sku zhes rjes 'jug med pa byung /

f.d: snang ba'i khyad par ni/ chos kyi dbyings la shes bya'i sgrib pa dag pas ni chos skur snang ngo /[1207] / nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dag pas ni longs skur snang ngo / / las kyi sgrib pa dag pas ni sprul skur snang ngo / /

The particularity of manifestation: The dharmakāya manifests through the purification of the knowledge obscuration that clouds the ultimate expanse. The enjoyment body manifests through the purification of the afflictions obscuration. The emanation body manifests through the purification of karmic obscurations.

d.div: [1208] sde dge_4024_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 4_sh+loka_13_shog_67_ba7

f.d: dam chos yid bzhin gyi nor bu thar pa rin po che'i rgyan las/ 'bras bu rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas bstan pa'i le'u ste nyi shu pa'o// //
This concludes the twentieth chapter, on the result—perfect buddhahood—of this Ornament of Precious Liberation, a Wish-Fulfilling Gem of Sublime Dharma.
(spyi don drug pa sangs rgyas kyi phrin las bshad pa/)
VI. Enlightened Activities
le'u nyer gcig pa/ sangs rgyas kyi 'phrin las/
21. Enlightened Activities of the Buddhas

'phrin las rtog med 'gro don mdzad/ /ces pa la/ 'o na dang po byang chub tu sems bskyed pa dang / bar du lam nyams su len pa dang / mthar 'bras bu sangs rgyas 'dod pa thams cad ni sems can gyi sdug bsngal bsal zhing bde ba bsgrub pa'i don ched kho na yin na/ sangs rgyas pa'i tshe rnam rtog dang 'bad rtsol mi mnga' bar 'dug pas/ sems can gyi don cang 'byung ngam snyam na/ sangs rgyas la 'bad rtsol dang rnam rtog mi mnga' bzhin du/ 'gro don lhun grub dang rgyun mi chad par 'byung ngo / /

Here is explained the line, “The activity is to nonconceptually fulfill the welfare of beings.”[783] At first bodhicitta is developed, then the path is prac-ticed, and finally the fruition, buddhahood, is achieved. Because all these goals have been pursued solely to eliminate beings’ sufferings and ensure their happiness, you may wonder how in fact there can be any benefitting of beings when buddhahood is attained, since buddhas are without either conceptual activity or effort. There does nevertheless occur spontaneous and uninterrupted benefitting of beings, even though buddhas do not think or make effort.

d.div: [783] This is the final line of the six-line topical summary presented by the author in the opening section of the text on page 122.

f.d:
de yang ji ltar 'byung ba bshad na/ sdom ni/
sku ni rtog med 'gro don mdzad// de bzhin gsung dang thugs kyang ni/ / rtog pa med par 'gro don mdzad/ / gsum gyis sangs rgyas 'phrin las bsdus/ / zhes pa'o//

To explain this point, is the following is the synopsis:
Enlightened activity is summed up in three points: the noble bodies of the buddhas, without deliberate thought, accomplish benefit for beings, and likewise do the magnificent speech and the noble mind. /240/

de yang sku gsung thugs rnam rtog med pas sems can gyi don mdzad pa de dpe dang sbyar nas/ rgyud bla ma las gsungs te/ ji skad du/
brgya byin rnga sprin tshangs pa dang / / nyi ma nor bu rin chen bzhin/ / de bzhin gshegs pa sgra brnyan bzhin/ / nam mkha' dang ni sa bzhin no/[1208] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Examples of this nonconceptual performance of the welfare of beings—physically, verbally, and mentally—are given in the Uttaratantra:
Like Indra, the [divine] drum, a cloud, and Brahma, like the sun and a precious [wish-fulfilling] jewel is the Tathāgata; also like an echo, like space, and like the earth.[784]

d.div: [1209] zhugs pa/ dpal spungs/
[784] Maitreya, Uttaratantra 4:13, Toh 4024 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 67b7.

f.d: de la brgya byin du snang ba bzhin zhes pa ni/ sku rtog pa med pas 'gro don mdzad pa'i dpe ste/ dper na lha dbang brgya byin de/ lha'i bu mo'i tshogs dang bcas te rnam par rgyal ba'i khang bzang na bzhugs pa la/ khang bzang de baiDUR+ya'i rang bzhin dag cing dang ba yin pas/ brgya byin gyi gzugs brnyan khang bzang gi phyi rol du snang ba 'byung ngo / / der sa gzhi la gnas pa'i skyes pa dang bud med gzhan dag gis brgya byin gyi gzugs brnyan dang longs spyod kyi gzugs brnyan mthong nas/ nged kyang myur du 'di ltar gyur cig ces smon lam 'debs shing de'i don du dge ba la 'bad pas shi 'phos nas der skye'o/ / gzugs brnyan snang ba de la rnam rtog med cing g.yo ba med do/ /

First, we have examples of how the noble forms [or bodies] of the buddhas nonconceptually accomplish benefit for beings. The quotation “like the manifestation of Indra” gives the example of how the nonconceptualizing bodies can bring benefit to sentient beings. In this example, Indra, lord of the gods, dwells in his palace called the House of Victory in the company of a host of young goddesses. The palace is made of vaidūrya jewel[785] so pure and lustrous that Indra’s reflected image appears on the walls and can be seen from the outside. Were humans living on Earth able to behold this image of Indra and his divine enjoyments in the heavens above them, they would long and pray to live like that. With such a goal in mind, they would make sincere efforts to be virtuous, and through such virtue they might be reborn in such a state after death. The vision that inspires them takes place without any effort of intention on the part of Indra.

d.div: [785] Vaidūrya has been translated as “lapis lazuli” and as “beryl.” Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoché explains that it is in fact a gem found only in the god realms.

f.d: de bzhin du don chen po la nye bar zhugs pas dad pa la sogs pa bsgom pa la/[1209] rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas rnams kyi sku mtshan dpes brgyan pa/ 'chag pa dang bzhengs pa dang bzhugs pa dang gzims pa dang chos gsung ba dang mnyam par bzhag pa la sogs pa cho 'phrul sna tshogs pa re mdzad pa mthong bar 'gyur la/[1210] de snang bas de la dad cing 'dun te/[1211] de thob par bya ba'i phyir de'i rgyu sems bskyed pa la sogs pa 'jug pas/ mthar sangs rgyas thob par 'gyur ro/ / skur snang ba de ni rnam rtog med cing g.yo ba med do/ /

In a similar way, those who have entered the path of highest good and who cultivate faith and similar virtues will see the forms of the perfect buddhas adorned with their special marks and signs; they will see them walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, teaching the Dharma, meditating, and accomplishing all sorts of miracles. As a result they will experience faith and yearn to attain such a state. To become like that, they will practice the virtues that are its cause: bodhicitta and all the other requisite practices. As a result, they will eventually become buddhas. The manifestation of the buddhas’ form bodies takes place without any deliberate thought and without any movement [on the buddhas’ part].

d.div: [1210] sna tshogs pa mdzad pa/ dpal spungs/
[1211] snang ba de la dad cing 'dun te/ dpal spungs/
[1212] sde dge_4024_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 4_sh+loka_shog_68_ba2

f.d:
de ltar yang /
ji ltar baiDUR+ya sa gzhi gtsang ma la// lha dbang lus kyi gzugs brnyan snang ba ltar/ / de bzhin 'gro sems sa gzhi gtsang ma la/ / thub pa'i dbang po'i sku yi gzugs brnyan 'char/[1212] / zhes gsungs so/ /

Thus it is stated:
Just as, on the clear surface of vaidūrya jewel, there appears the reflected form of the lord of gods, so on the clear surface of beings’ minds here appears the reflected form of the King of Conquerors.[786]

d.div: [1213] yig chung de rnams dpal spungs dpar mar mi gsal/
[786] Maitreya, Uttaratantra 4:14, Toh 4024 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 67b2.

f.d: des na sku rnam rtog med pas 'gro don mdzad pa'o// lha'i rnga bzhin zhes pa ni/ gsung rnam rtog med pas 'gro don mdzad pa'i dpe ste/ dper na rnam par rgyal ba'i khang bzang gi steng na/ lha'i rnga chos kyi shugs 'chang zhes bya ba/ lha rnams kyi sngon gyi dkar po'i las kyi mthu yis grub pa zhig yod de/ rnam par rtog pa med bzhin du/ 'dus byas thams cad ni mi rtag pa'o/ /zhes pa la sogs pa'i skad kyis bag med pa'i lha rnams bskul lo/ /

The line “like the divine drum” gives the example of how the buddhas’ speech can accomplish the welfare of beings without forethought. In the example, a drumbeat sounds in the realm of the gods. It resounds as a result of the gods’ former beneficial actions. The drumbeat does not have thought or intention, /241/ yet its sound conveys messages such as “All conditioned things are impermanent!” that stimulate the gods, who are inclined to neglect virtue in the present.

de ltar yang /
ji ltar lha nang lha rnams kyi/ / sngon gyi dkar po'i mthu yis ni/ / 'bad dang gnas dang yid gzugs dang / / rnam par rtog pa med bzhin du/ / mi rtag sdug bsngal bdag med dang / zhi ba'i sgra yis bag med pa'i/ / lha rnams thams cad yang nas yang / / chos kyi rngas ni bskul byed ltar/[1214] [1215] / ([1213])zhes gsungs so/ /

Thus it is stated:
Just as through the power of the gods’ former virtue, the Dharma drum in the divine realms— without any thought, effort, location, mind, or form— stimulates all the carefree gods over and over again with the words “impermanence,” “suffering,” “no self,” and “peace.”[787]

d.div: [1213] bka' rtags kyi phyag rgya bzhi ni 'dus byas thams cad ni mi rtag pa'o/ / chos thams cad ni bdag med pa'o/ / zag bcas thams cad ni sdug bsngal ba'o/ / mya ngan las 'das pa thams cad zhi ba'o//
[1214] skul/ dpal spungs/
[1215] sde dge_4024_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 4_sh+loka_31_shog_68_ba4

[787] Ibid. 4:31–32, 67b4. In the Tibetan original, embedded in the above quotation in verse is the following parenthetical sentence in smaller type: (That is, with the four seals that are the sign of the buddhas’ teachings: “All conditioned things are impermanent,” “All phenomena are devoid of self-entity,” “All tainted phenomena are in the nature of suffering,” and “Nirvana is peace.”) Incidently, this parenthetical sentence is not found in the Palpung edition.

f.d:
de bzhin du 'bad rtsol dang bral zhing rtog dpyod med kyang /[1216] sangs rgyas kyi gsung gis skal ldan rnams la ji ltar 'tshams pa'i chos ston to/[1217] / de ltar yang /
de bzhin khyab bdag 'bad sogs dang / / bral yang 'gro ba ma lus pa/ / sangs rgyas gsung gis khyab mdzad de/ / skal ldan rnams la chos ston to/[1218] / zhes gsungs so/ /

As in the example, it is without any effort or deliberation that the speech of the buddhas transmits suitable teachings to those who are ready. So it is stated:
Likewise, without effort and so forth, the omnipresent embraces all beings, without exception, with the speech of the enlightened ones, teaching the Dharma to those who are ready.[788]

d.div: [1216] rtog pa/ dpal spungs/
[1217] 'tsham/ dpal spungs/
[1218] sde dge_4024_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 4_sh+loka_33_shog_68_ba5

f.d: des ni gsung rnam rtog med pas 'gro don mdzad pa'o/[1219] /
In the above way, the speech of the buddhas accomplishes the welfare of beings without any [need for] conscious deliberate thought.

d.div: [1219] des na/ dpal spungs/

f.d:
sprin bzhin zhes pa ni/ thugs rnam rtog med pas 'gro don mdzad pa'i dpe ste/ dper na dbyar gyi dus na 'bad rtsol med par nam mkha' la sprin tshogs te/ rnam rtog med par char sa la babs nas lo thog la sogs pa phun sum tshogs pa skyed do/ / de ltar yang /
ji ltar dbyar gyi dus na sprin/ lo thog phun sum tshogs pa'i rgyu/ / chu yi phung po 'bad med pa/ / sa la mngon par 'bab pa ltar/[1220] / zhes gsungs so/ /

The line “Like a cloud. . . ” presents the analogy of how the perfect mind of the buddhas nonconceptually accomplishes the good of beings. During the monsoon, clouds gather effortlessly in the sky, and their rain, falling on the earth without any deliberation on the clouds’ part, causes the growth of perfect crops and many other things to happen. It is stated:
Just as from monsoon clouds falls down to earth effortlessly a mass of water, the condition for plentiful crops. . . [789]

d.div: [1220] sde dge_4024_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 4_sh+loka_42_shog_69_na5

f.d:
de bzhin du thugs kyi 'phrin las rnam rtog med par chos kyi char gdul bya la babs pas/ dge ba'i lo thog smin par byed do/ / de ltar yang /
de bzhin thugs rje'i sprin las ni/ / rgyal ba'i dam chos chu yi char/ / 'gro ba'i don du lo thog rgyun/ / rnam par rtog pa med par 'bebs/[1221] / zhes gsungs so/ /

In a similar way, the activity of the buddha mind, without requiring any deliberation, pours down the rain of Dharma onto beings training in virtue and ripens their crop of wholesomeness. Thus it is stated:
Similarly, the clouds of great compassion cause, without any need of deliberation, a rainfall of the sublime teachings of the victorious ones.[790]

d.div: [1221] sde dge_4024_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 4_sh+loka_43_shog_69_na6

f.d: des na thugs rnam rtog med pas 'gro don mdzad do//
Thus the buddha mind accomplishes the welfare of beings without any need for conscious thought.

tshangs pa bzhin zhes pa ni/ dper na lha'i rgyal po tshangs pa de/ tshangs pa'i gnas nas ma 'phos bzhin du/ lha'i gnas thams cad du gnas par ston to/ / de bzhin du sangs rgyas kyang chos kyi sku las ma bskyod bzhin du/ gdul bya rnams la mdzad pa bcu gnyis la sogs par sprul nas don mdzad do/ / de ltar yang /
ji ltar tshangs pa tshangs pa yi/ / gnas nas 'pho ba med bzhin du/ / lha yi gnas ni thams cad du/ / snang ba 'bad med ston pa ltar/ / de bzhin thub pa chos sku las// bskyod pa med par khams kun tu/ / skal ldan rnams la 'bad med par/ / sprul pa dag ni ston par mdzad/[1222] / ces gsungs so//

Regarding the line, “like Brahma. . . ,” Brahma, lord of the gods, manifests his presence in all the heavens yet never leaves his own Brahma heaven. In a similar way, without ever moving from the dharmakāya, the buddhas manifest the twelve deeds and other similar emanations to those training in virtue, thereby bringing them benefit. /242/ So it is stated:
Just as Brahma, without ever moving from the Brahma heaven, effortlessly shows his manifestations in all the other heavens, so also does a victorious one, without ever moving from the dharmakāya, effortlessly show his emanations everywhere to those whose karma makes them ready.[791]

d.div: [1222] gong mtshungs/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 4_sh+loka_53_shog_69_ba7

f.d:
nyi ma bzhin zhes bya ba ni/ dper na nyi ma'i 'od zer gyis rtog pa med par dus gcig car du/ pad+ma la sogs pa me tog gi bye brag dpag tu med pa'i kha 'byed par byed do/ / de bzhin du sangs rgyas kyi chos kyi 'od zer gyis rnam rtog dang 'bad rtsol med bzhin du/ gdul bya rigs dang mos pa dpag tu med pa'i blo'i pad+ma dkar po'i phyogs su kha 'byed par mdzad do/ / de ltar yang /
ji ltar nyi ma rtog med par/ / rang 'od cig car spros pa yi/ / pad+ma rgyas par byed pa dang / / gzhan dang smin par byed pa ltar/ / de bzhin de bzhin gshegs pa yi/ / nyi ma dam chos 'od zer dag / gdul bya'i skye bo'i pad+ma la/ / rnam par rtog pa med par 'jug[1223] / ces gsungs so/ /

In the example of the sun, the sun’s rays, without any need for deliberation, cause lotuses and innumerable other kinds of flowers to blossom simultaneously. Similarly, without any thought or effort, the rays of the buddhas’ teachings cause the lotuses that are the minds of infinitely varied disciples, with their different aspirations, to open toward that which is wholesome. Thus it is stated:
Just as the sun, without any deliberation, through the simultaneous radiation of its sunbeams, brings the lotuses to full bloom and ripens other plants, so do the sunrays of the buddhas’ sublime teachings, without any need for deliberation, pour into the lotus-like beings training in virtue.[792]

d.div: [1223] gong mtshungs/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 4_sh+loka_59_shog_69_ba7

f.d:
yang dper na/ nyi ma de'i gzugs brnyan snod dwangs pa thams cad du gcig tu 'char ba ltar/ sangs rgyas gdul bya snang ba dag pa thams cad la gcig tu 'char ro/ / de ltar yang /
gang phyir gdul bya dag pa yi/ / chu yi snod ni thams cad la/ / bde gshegs nyi ma'i gzugs brnyan ni/ / dpag tu med pa gcig car 'char/[1224] / zhes gsungs so//

Taking this example of the sun another way, just as the reflection of the sun appears simultaneously on all surfaces that are sufficiently clear and smooth, so does the Buddha appear simultaneously to all disciples of sufficiently pure inner disposition:
In all the water vessels that are those pure disciples, countless reflections of the buddha sun appear simultaneously.[793]

d.div: [1224] gong mtshungs/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 4_sh+loka_62_shog_70_na6

f.d:
yid bzhin nor bu zhes pa ni/ dper na yid bzhin gyi nor bu rin po che la rnam rtog med kyang / gsol ba btab pas ci dgos 'bad pa med par 'byung ba ltar/ sangs rgyas la brten nas nyan thos la sogs pa bsam pa tha dad pa rnams kyi don 'grub pa'o/ / de ltar yang /
ji ltar yid bzhin nor bu ni/ / rtog pa med kyang cig car du/ / spyod yul gnas pa rnams kyi ni/ / bsam pa so sor rdzogs byed ltar/ / de bzhin sangs rgyas yid bzhin la/ / brten nas bsam pa tha dad rnams// sna tshogs chos ni thos gyur kyang / / de ni de la rnam mi rtog[1225] / ces gsungs so/ /

In the example of the wish-fulfilling gem, just as a wish-fulfilling gem does not think yet effortlessly produces whatever is requested by the person who calls on it, so the goals corresponding to the various motivations of the śrāvakas and other disciples are accomplished because of the buddhas. Thus it is stated:
Just as a wish-fulfilling gem, without thought and spontaneously, completely fulfills the wishes of those within its sphere of influence, so also, on account of the wish-fulfilling buddha, those of various motivations hear different kinds of teachings, without any deliberation on [the Buddha’s part].[794]

d.div: [1225] gong mtshungs/ rgyud bla ma/ skabs/ 4_sh+loka_67_shog_70_ba3

f.d: de bzhin du sgra brnyan dang / nam mkha' dang / sa gsum gyis kyang rnam rtog med par 'gro don mdzad pa'i dpe bstan to/ /

Similar to the above, there are three more examples—those of an echo, of space, and of the earth—showing how beings can be benefitted by the buddhas without requiring any conscious thought on their part.
dam chos yid bzhin gyi nor bu thar pa rin po che'i rgyan las/ sangs rgyas kyi phrin las bstan pa'i le'u ste/ nyi shu rtsa gcig pa'o// //
This was the twenty-first chapter, on nonconceptual enlightened activity, of this Ornament of Precious Liberation, a Wish-Fulfilling Gem of Sublime Dharma.
mjug gi don/
[Colophon]

dam chos yid bzhin gyi nor bu thar pa rin po che'i rgyan zhes bya ba/ theg pa chen po'i lam gyi rim pa bshad pa 'di ni ban+de dar ma skyabs kyis bskul ba'i ngor/[1226] lha rje bsod nams rin chen gyis bkod pa rdzogs so/ / yi ge pa yang dar ma skyabs kyis bgyis pa'o/ /

This concludes this Ornament of Precious Liberation, a Wish-Fulfilling Gem of Sublime Dharma, progressively explaining the Mahayana path, composed by the physician Sönam Rinchen at the instigation of Darma Kyap and transcribed by the latter.

d.div: [1226] 'di ni ban+de dar ma skyabs kyis bskul ba'i ngor/ zhes pa'i tshig 'di dpal spungs dpar mar mi byung /

f.d: dam chos yid bzhin nor bu yi/[1227] / rtog med 'gro ba'i don 'byung ba/ / khyod nyid bris pa'i bsod nams kyis/ / 'gro kun byang chub mchog thob shog[1228] / dge'o// //
May whatever merit there be in your transcription in terms of nonconceptual benefit for beings through the wish-fulfilling sacred Dharma help all beings attain supreme enlightenment. Virtue!

[1228] smon tshig 'di dpal spungs dpar mar gzhung rdzogs pa'i mjug mdzad pa pa'i mtshan byang gi gong du byung /

f.d: @#/ /thub pa'i dgongs pa rab tu gsal ba zhes bya ba'i bstan bcos bzhugs so//
Part III. Clarifying the Sage’s Intent: An Exposition of the Stages for Embarking upon the Excellent Path of the Bodhisattva
sa paN kun dga' rgyal mtshan/
Sakya Paṇḍita Kunga Gyaltsen (1182–1251) Translated by David P. Jackson

@#/ /rgya gar skad du/ munimataprakAshanAmashAs+t+ra/ namogurush+tsamany+dzug+hoShAyAdareN/ saMhitayorAkaR+yas+saMbung+ng+ha_dzinaHputrAdz+dzAto/ dzit+sutakAruN+yesh+shUnyatwAt+makabong+hish+tsit+tAdz+dzaH bod skad du/ thub pa'i dgongs pa rab tu gsal ba zhes bya ba/[1]

d.i: The title in Sanskrit: Munimataprakāśanāmaśāstra The title in Tibetan: Thub pa’i dgongs pa rab tu gsal ba

d.div: [1] thub pa'i dgongs pa gsal ba zhes bya ba/ gser bris/ glo mon thang dbu med/

f.d: 1. Spiritual Potential
bla ma dang 'jam pa'i dbyangs la gus pas phyag 'tshal lo/ /
Reverent homage to the guru and Mañjuśrī! /247/

d.div: phan bde'i 'byung gnas rdzogs pa yi/ / sangs rgyas rgyal ba'i sras las 'khrungs/ / rgyal sras stong nyid snying rje yi/ / bdag nyid byang chub sems las 'khrungs/ /
de phyir 'gro la phan don du/ / byang chub sems la phyag 'tshal nas/ / rgyal sras rnams kyi lam bzang la/ / 'jug pa'i rim pa bsdus te bshad//

The completely awakened Buddha, the source of benefit and lasting happiness, arose from a Conqueror’s son (a bodhisattva).[1] The Conqueror’s son arose from the thought of awakening (bodhicitta), which is in nature emptiness and compassion.[2]
Therefore, to benefit living beings, I pay homage to the thought of awakening and briefly explain here the stages for embarking upon the excellent path of the Conqueror’s sons.

[1] I completed my translation of this treatise before the Institute of Tibetan Classics (ITC) Tibetan edition was published, and thus I did not have access to the 427 endnotes of that edition (pp. 453–72). The references to passages or works in the Dergé edition of Kangyur and Tengur canons that were traced by the ITC editors were kindly added to my endnotes by Lea Groth-Wilson and thus can now be consulted. In my original notes I had gathered a number of my own source identifications, mainly to the Peking (P) editon of the canon.
[2] Cf. Candrakīrti’s Entering the Middle Way (Madhyamakāvatāra) 1:1, Toh 3861 Tengyur, dbu ma ’a, 202a2, quoted by Sapaṇ at the end of his text. See page 498.

f.d:
blo dang ldan pas byang chub kyi mchog tu sems bskyed de/ bla na med pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i byang chub thob par 'dod pas/ theg pa chen po mdo sde rgyan las 'byung ba'i lam gyi rim pa ni/
rigs dang chos la mos pa dang / / de bzhin du ni sems bskyed dang / / sbyin la sogs pa bsgrub pa dang / / sems can rnams yongs smin byed dang / / skyon med pa la 'jug nyid dang / / zhing ni yongs su dag pa dang / / mi gnas mya ngan 'das pa dang / / byang chub mchog dang ston pa'o/[2] / zhes gsungs pa de nyams su len par 'dod na/ thog mar skal ba dang ldan pa'i gzhi rigs nges par bya'o/ /

If an intelligent person has produced the thought of highest awakening and aspires to unsurpassable, perfect, and complete awakening, the folllowing are the stages of the religious path as taught in [Maitreya’s] Ornament of Mahayana Sutras:
(1) [Recognizing] spiritual potential, (2) appreciating Dharma,[3] (3) generating the thought [of awakening], (4) accomplishing the perfections of generosity and the rest, (5) bringing sentient beings to maturity, (6) entering into the faultless [levels of an ārya] and the pure fields [and into] (7) nonsituated nirvana, highest awakening, and the displaying” [of a buddha’s deeds].[4] If one wishes to practice as taught here, then such a person should first determine his or her spiritual potential (gotra), which is the basis for being suitably endowed to practice Dharma.

d.div: [2] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 20_sh+loka_61_shog_35_na4_sde dge bstan 'gyur du/ skyon med pa la 'jug nyid dang / /sems can rnams yongs smin byed dang / /

[3] Chim Jampaiyang (Detailed Abhidharma Commentary, 74a) defines “appreciating” (mos pa) as “to desire or to hold an object as possessing valuable qualities” (’dod pa’am dmigs pa la yon tan can du ’dzin pa).

[4] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 20:61–62, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 35a4; P 5521, sems tsam, phi. Numbering for themes in this citation have been added in accord with Sapaṇ’s presentation to assist the reader. These lines are supposed to be at least a little cryptic, a terse list of themes requiring a whole book to explain. Later Sakya scholars discuss this ordering and whether it accords exactly with Sapa-ṇ’s topics. The verse is quoted by Vasubandhu, Commentary on the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras (Sūtrālaṃkārabhāṣya); Toh 4026 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi; P 5527 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi. In the TG version of these verses, the fifth topic, “bringing sentient beings to maturity” (sems can rnams yongs smin byed dang), has been moved up to fourth in the list, with “entering into the faultless [levels of an ārya]” turned into the fifth. This change in ordering is discussed in the introduction to this volume.

f.d:
de yang mdo sde rgyan las/
rang bzhin dang ni rgyas pa dang / / de ni rten dang brten pa ste/ / yod med nyid dang yon tan ni/[3] / sgrol ba'i don du rig par bya/[4] / zhes gsungs pa ltar/ rang bzhin gyi rigs sems can thams cad la yod/

Concerning “spiritual potential,” the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras teaches:
The natural and developed are the support and the supported. As existence and nonexistence, know spiritual potential in the sense of liberating excellent quality.[5] Accordingly, natural spiritual potential is present in all sentient beings.

d.div: [3] ma dpe dang dpar ma gzhan la/ yod med gnyis dang / zhes byung yang sde dge bstan 'gyur ltar/ yod med nyid dang / zhes bcos/
[4] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 4_sh+loka_4_shog_4_na2
[5] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 4:4; Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 4a2.

f.d: rgyas pa'i rigs byang chub tu sems bskyed nas yod/ ma bskyed pa la med/ rang bzhin gyi rigs rten/ rgyas pa'i rigs brten pa'o/ / rigs la saM skr-i ta'i skad du go tra zer la/ o'i sgra ur bsgyur/ rkyen Na byin pas gu Na/ tra so sor phral na tA ra ste/ de ltar yon tan la brten nas 'khor ba'i rgya mtsho'i pha rol tu sgrol bas yon tan sgrol zhes bya bar 'gyur ro//

Developed spiritual potential is present in those who have produced the thought of gaining awakening.[6] It is absent in those who have not produced this thought. Natural spiritual potential is “the support”; developed spiritual potential is that which is supported. [The words “liberating excellent quality” are explained by the following Sanskrit tradtitional explanatory] etymology:[7] “Spiritual potential” in Sanskrit is gotra. By changing the o of go to u, and by adding the element na, you arrive at guṇa (“excellent quality”). If you divide the syllable tra, the result is tāra (“liberating”). Thus, because it liberates you to the far shore of the ocean of cyclic existence (samsara) on the basis of excellent qualities, it is a “liberating excellent quality.”

d.div: [6] On the developed spiritual potential (rgyas pa’i rigs), see also Ngawang Chödrak, Setting Exquisite Gems, 30.6, where he gives Gorampa’s interpretation in the context of Abhisamayālaṃkāra exegesis—that is, Perfection of Wisdom scholastics.
[7] Sthiramati similarly explains the etymology of the Sanskrit term gotra in his Detailed Exposition of the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras (Sūtrālaṃkāravṛttibhāṣya), P 5531, sems tsam, mi, 48a.

f.d: rigs de'i rtags ni/

d.i: The marks of possessing the spiritual potential of the Mahayana

f.d: sbyor ba'i sngon du snying rje dang / / mos pa dang ni bzod pa dang / /dge ba yang dag spyod pa rnams/ / rigs kyi rtags su nges par bshad/[5] / ces gsungs pas/

These are stated in the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras to be:
Before you have set out, to have compassion, to have appreciation and patience, and to practice virtue—these are specified[8] as signs of spiritual potential.[9] /248/

d.div: [5] gongs mtshungs/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 4_sh+loka_5_shog_4_na3
[8] Nges par bshad: nirūpyate (nirūp), “ascertained, determined,” or even “defined”?

[9] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 4:5, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 4a3. As quoted by Vasubandhu, Sūtrālaṃkārabhāṣya, P 5527, sems tsam, phi, 146a: sbyor ba’i sngon du snying rje dang// mos pa dang ni bzod pa dang// dge ba yang dag spyod pa ni// rigs kyi rtags su shes par bya//. Cf. Guenther, Jewel Ornament, 7.

f.d: chos la ma zhugs pa'i sngon nyid nas snying rje che ba dang / dkon mchog gsum la mos pa dang / gzhan gyis gnod pa byas pa la bzod pa che ba dang / /dge ba'i rtsa ba byed pa la rang bzhin gyis mos pa ste/ 'di lta bu su la yod kyang / sangs rgyas kyi rigs yod pa'i rtags so//

Thus there are four signs [needed] from the beginning, before commencing the practice of Dharma: great compassion, appreciation of the Three Jewels, great forbearance when others harm you, and pleasure in planting the roots of virtue. Whoever has these displays the buddha potential.
rigs de'i skyon ni/

d.i: The impediments to that spiritual potential

f.d: nyon mongs goms dang grogs ngan dang / / phongs dang gzhan gyi dbang nyid de/ / mdor na rigs kyi nyes pa ni/ / rnam pa bzhir ni shes par bya/[6] / zhes gsungs pa ltar/

These are stated in the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras to be:
Habituation to the afflictions, having harmful friends, living in poverty, and being dominated by others— in brief, know the impediments to the spiritual potential as fourfold.[10]

d.div: [6] gongs mtshungs/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 4_sh+loka_6_shog_4_na4
[10] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 4:6, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 4a4. Quoted also in Vasubandhu, Sūtrālaṃkārabhāṣya, P 5527, sems tsam, phi, 144b.
