(6) [The ninth power,] the divine eye,[571] is the very complete result of the four meditative concentrations in the god realms, and it is “extremely pure” because it is based on completely perfected and pure meditative concentration. The gods of the desire realm possess [an eye] that conforms to the above in name only, whereas since humans lack even that, it is called “superhuman.” The objects of that [divine eye] are two: sentient beings who are dying, and those who are being reborn in the intermediate state. [In the latter, some beings have a vision of] “bad color,” which is to pass into darkness, like a black blanket or like entering pitch darkness, and “good color,” which is to go into light, something like moonlight or Varanasi white cotton cloth. “Bad” and “good” are because those beings go to lower miserable destinies and happy destinies, respectively.

d.div: [571] Divine eye is knowing the future deaths and rebirths of yourself and others. Chim Jampaiyang, Detailed Abhidharma Commentary, (618): “The knowledge of death, transference, and intermediate state refers to knowing the future existence of oneself and others” (’chi ba dang ’pho ba bar do dang skye ba mkhyen pa ni rang gzhan gyi ma ’ongs pa’i srid pa mkhyen pa ste).

f.d: lus dang ngag dang yid kyi nyes pa spyod pa dang ldan pa'i tshul khrims 'chal ba kun slong dang bcas pa'o// log par lta ba la ni gnyis te/ thams cad la skur ba 'debs pa dang / 'phags pa la skur ba 'debs pa'o/ / des log pa'i las kyi rgyu dang 'bras bu la mngon par zhen pas log pa'i las mngon par 'du byed de/ chos yang dag blangs pa dag da lta bde la/ phyi mar sdug bsngal ba dang / gnyis kar sdug bsngal bar 'gyur ba gnyis len to/ /

Having committed the evil acts of body, speech, and mind is to have impure moral discipline together with its motivations.[572] Two kinds of perverse views are denying everything and denying āryas. Those whose erroneous attachment to the cause and effect of wrong acts leads them to accumulate wrong deeds bring upon themselves two types of cause and effect in terms of feeling: a pleasant present life but a miserable future one, and miserable experiences in both lives.[573]

d.div: [572] I read here ldan pa (emendation), or ldan pa ni (Drolungpa, Great Tenrim), instead of ldan pa’i (Dergé).

[573] “Four causes and results in terms of feeling” (catvāridharmasamādānāni) are listed in the Great Sanskrit and Tibetan Glossary (Mahāvyutpatti), P 5832: see Sakaki, Mahāvyutpatti, no. 1560. The remaining two are presumably a miserable present life but a pleasant future one, and pleasant experiences in both lives.

f.d: ngan 'gro'i rgyu'i gtso bo yin pas rgyu dang rkyen des zhes bya ba'o/ / lus zhig pa ni ming dang gzugs phan tshun 'brel zhig pa'o/ / 'chi ba'i 'og nas 'chi ba thams cad las 'di tha chad yin pas so/ /

Because [perverse views] are the main cause for the lower miserable destinies, it is taught, “By that cause and condition. ” The “destruction of body” is the destruction of the mutual connection between the mental aggregates (nāma) and the physical aggregate (rūpa). The words “after death” (literally, “beneath death”) are used because this is the worst of all deaths.

ngan song ni chos ngan pa dang / ya nga bar spyod pas ngan par song bas so/ / ngan 'gro ni sdug bsngal drag po dang yun ring ba dang bar ma chad pa dang / mang po myang bar 'gyur bas so/ / log par ltung ba ni 'og na gnas shing / g.yang sa che la nyam nga ba dang / snying rje ba'i sgra cher 'byin pas so/ / sems can dmyal ba ni rang bzhin dang / lus dang dngos po bstan pa'o/ / de kho na smos pa ni shas cher skyid lug pa'i gnas yin pas te ngan song kun mtshon pa'o/ /

“Lower miserable destiny” (apāya) is so called because, having done evil and frightful things, you have gone to an evil place. “Evil state” (durgati) is so called because you will experience there much fierce, long-lasting, and uninterrupted suffering. “Fallen state” (vinipāta) is so called because it rests below, it has great and terrifying abysses, and because you utter there great pitiful cries. The term “hell existence” (naraka) reveals the nature, body, and reality of the hells. Only hell is mentioned because it is the predominate occasion for depression, so it exemplifies all three of the lower miserable destinies.
dge ba'i phyogs ni thams cad de las zlog pa ste/ bde 'gro legs par spyod pa sngon du 'gro bas so/ / mtho ris ni bde ba la longs spyod pa mchog yinapas so/ /

The virtuous factors are entirely the opposite of the above. “Pleasant states” (sugati) are so called because they are preceded by excellent conduct. “Higher destinies” (svarga) are so called because they are the highest enjoyment of pleasures.[574]

d.div: [574] See also Jackson, Entrance Gate, 382n40, on the term mtho ris (svarga). For the Buddhist, svarga includes the three higher realms of existence—not only the heavens of the gods and the demigods but also the realm of humans. Hence, my translations “higher destinies” or “fortunate realms of existence.” It is often opposed to ngan song.

f.d: zag pa zad pa mkhyen pa ni thams cad kyi bag la nyal ma lus pa spangs pa/ gnyen po zag pa med pa'i sems dang shes rab mchog tu gyur pa'i sems dang / lhag pa'i shes rab kyis bsdus pa ste/ zag pa med pa'i sems rnam par grol ba dang / shes rab rnam par grol ba'o/ /

(7) [The tenth power,] knowledge of the extinction of the impurities, /384/ is the elimination of every latent disposition of all the afflictions. The antidotes are the pure mind and discerning wisdom. These are included within the mind that has reached supremacy and surpassing discerning wisdom, that is, the emancipation of the pure mind and the emancipation of discerning wisdom.

de'ang sngar lam bsgom pa la brten te srid pa tha ma de nyid la thob nas/[409] bdag gis thob bo zhes mngon par shes pa drug pos rang gis ji lta bar shes pas 'dod na gzhan la yang ston pas na tshe 'di la rang gi mngon par shes pas mngon sum du byas te/ rjod par byed ces bya'o//

Moreover, after you have attained this power in that final existence itself based on previous meditative cultivation of the path, you will exactly know, through the sixth superknowledge, “I have won it.” And consequently you will reveal it also to others if they desire. Therefore it is explained, “In this life, having made it manifest through superknowledges, it is expressed to others.”

d.div: [409] mtho ris de'ang sngar lam bsgom pa la/ zha lu/

f.d: mi 'jigs pa bzhi ni/

d.div: rang gzhan don du ye shes dang / / spangs dang nges 'byung gegs byed la/ / ston mdzad mu stegs gzhan dag gis/ / mi brdzi khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/[410] /
Homage to you who teach, for the benefit of self and others, gnosis, elimination, salvation, its obstacles, and who are not overwhelmed by the heterodox tīrthikas![575]
[410] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 21_sh+loka_53_shog_38_ba1

[575] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 21:52, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 38b1. On the “four modes of fearlessness” (mi ’jigs pa bzhi, vaiśāradya), see Vasubandhu, Abhidharmakośa 7:32, Toh 4089 Tengyur, mngon pa, ku, 22b7.

f.d: rang gi don dang gzhan gyi don dang spangs pa dang nges par 'byung ba'i gegs byed pa'i chos bzhi ston pa la 'jig rten pa'i nga rgyal can rnams kyi nang du 'jigs pa dang / yang ba dang bag tsha ba med par de dag zil gyis gnon pa ste/ skye ba'i gnas la nga rgyal ba lha dang / rdzu 'phrul gyis nga rgyal ba bdud dang / tshad med pas nga rgyal ba tshangs pa dang / yon tan gyis nga rgyal ba dge sbyong dang / rigs kyis nga rgyal ba bram ze dang / de lta bu'i nga rgyal can rnams kyis chos dang mthun par brgal ba ni/ skyon yod pa la skyon yod do zhes drang por tshogs su sun 'byin pa yin la/ de mi mnga' zhing brdzun gyis sun 'byin pa ni/ chos dang mi mthun par rgol ba ste/ de rang gi skyon yin gyi gzhan gyi skyon ma yin pas de lta bus rgol yang skyes bu dam pa'i skyon du mi 'gyur ba'i phyir ro//

In teaching the four instructions of (1) [gnosis], (2) elimination [of the afflictions], (3) salvation, and (4) that which obstructs it—[the first two] pertaining to his own benefit and [the last two] for the benefit of others—[the Buddha], lacking fear, fright, and timidity amid proud people of the world, overawes those in the assembly: proud individuals such as gods who are puffed up about their place of birth, demons (māra) who are conceited about their magical powers, Brahma who is proud of his immeasurable attainments, ascetics who are proud of their excellent qualities, and brahmans who are proud of their lineage. Religiously principled disputation is to refute truthfully, amid an assembly, another person who possesses faults, with the words: “He possesses such and such faults.” But the Buddha does not possess those faults. To refute through falsehood is unprincipled disputation. For even though someone disputes in such a way, that will not be a fault for a noble person because such a procedure is the disputant’s own fault but not the fault of the other.[576]

d.div: [576] See also Sapaṇ, Entrance Gate for the Wise 3:13; Jackson, Entrance Gate, 378n26.

f.d: bsrung ba med pa gsum ni/

d.div: bsrung med bsnyel ba mi mnga' bas/ / 'khor gyi nang du bag brkyang gsung / / kun nas nyon mongs gnyis spangs pas/ / 'khor sdud khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/[411]/

Homage to you who, without the need for guardedness and because of your unforgetfulness, speak in a relaxed way in an assembly, and because you have eliminated the twin afflictions, attract a circle of followers![577]
[411] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 21_sh+loka_54_shog_38_ba2
[577] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 21:53, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 38b2. This verse is also quoted above, page 436; “absence of guardedness” (bsrung ba med pa gsum).

f.d: sku gsung thugs kyi spyod pa yongs su dag pa'i phyir la las skyon 'dogs su 'ong zhes bcab pa mi mnga' bas 'khor gyi nang du bag brkyang nas thams cad zil gyis mnan te chos gsung pa'o/ /

The Buddha lacks any furtive thoughts, such as “Some may censure me for this,” because he is perfectly pure in his bodily, verbal, and mental conduct. Therefore he is unreserved in the midst of assemblies, and he teaches the doctrine in a way that overawes everyone.

dran pa nyer bar gzhag pa gsum ni/ gdul bya rnams la chos gsung pa na/ 'khor 'ga' zhig legs par sgrub/ 'ga' zhig log par sgrub/ 'ga' zhig gnyis kar sgrub pa la chags pa dang / sdang ba spangs pa ste/ 'khor legs par sdud pa'o/ /

[The verse also refers to] three applications of mindfulness. When he gives religious instructions to his disciples, he is free from attachment and aversion toward those of his followers who correctly accomplish it, accomplish it incorrectly, or accomplish it both both ways. Thus he attracts disciples in an excellent way. /385/
bag chags yang dag par bcom pa ni/

d.i: The thorough destruction of the propensities toward the afflictions

d.div: kun mkhyen khyed ni gshegs pa dang / / bzhugs pa kun la thams cad du/ / kun mkhyen min spyod mi mnga' bas// yang dag don ldan khyod phyag 'tshal/[412] /
Homage to you, Omniscient One, who are truly meaningful because you do not possess anything but omniscient conduct at all times and in [all activities, such as] going and dwelling![578]
[412] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 21_sh+loka_55_shog_38_ba3

f.d: dgra bcom pa la ni 'gro ba dang gnas pa dang smra ba la sogs pa la/ nyon mongs pa zad kyang bag chags ma spangs pa'i phyir kun mkhyen ma yin pa'i spyod pa glang po cher 'khrul pa dang / shing rta la thug pa la sogs pa lta bu srid la/ 'di la ni de mi mnga' bas thams cad mkhyen pa yang dag pa'i don dang ldan pa'o//

Even though for the arhat the afflictions have been extinguished, in such activities as his going, dwelling, and speaking, it is still possible for him to engage in nonomniscient conduct, such as [having accidents through] wrongly handling a mad elephant, a collision with a chariot, and so forth, because he has not eliminated the latent propensities toward the afflictions. But since the Buddha does not possess those latent propensities, his omniscience is truly what it claims to be.
bsnyel ba mi mnga' pa'i chos nyid ni/

d.div: 'jig rten kun gyi bya ba la/ / khyod ni dus las mi 'da' bas/ / mdzad pa rtag tu don mnga' ba/ / mi bsnyel khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/[413] /
In your activities for all beings in the world you are never untimely, and therefore your deeds are always meaningful. Homage to you who are not forgetful![579]
[413] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 21_sh+loka_56_shog_38_ba3

[579] Ibid. 21:55, 38b3; dran pa nye bar gzhag pa, smṛtyupasthāna/-upasthiti, Vasubandhu, Abhidharmakośa 7:16, 7:44, Toh 4089 Tengyur, mngon pa, ku, 22a6. This verse is also quoted above at the end of chapter 7.

f.d: nyan thos dang rang sangs rgyas ni bsnyel na sems can gyi don yal bar 'dor srid la/ 'di la ni yul gang na sems can gang la dus gang gi tshe/ don gang zhig rnam pa ji ltar bya ba la dus las mi 'da' bar de'i thabs ston pa la bsnyel ba mi mnga' bas mdzad pa rtag tu 'bras bu yod pa'o/ /

It is possible that śrāvaka [arhats] and pratyekabuddhas may abandon the welfare of sentient beings if they become forgetful. But the Buddha is always timely and never forgetful, when revealing the skillful means for accomplishing that welfare of others, of what place, for what sentient beings, at what time, for what purpose, and in what manner an action is to be done. Therefore his deeds are always fruitful.
thugs rje chen po ni/

d.div: 'jig rten kun la nyin mtshan du/ / lan drug tu ni so sor gzigs/ / thugs rje chen po dang ldan pa/ / phan dgongs khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/[414] /
At six times during day and night, you gaze over the whole world of living beings. Homage to you who possess great compassion and are of beneficial intent![580]
[414] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 21_sh+loka_57_shog_38_ba4
[580] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 21:56, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 38b4; thugs rje chen po, mahākṛpā, Vasubandhu, Abhidharmakośa 7:33, Toh 4089 Tengyur, mngon pa, ku, 22b7.

f.d: lan drug tu ni nye bar mtshon pa ste/ dus thams cad du sems can su ni nyams/ su ni 'phel/ su ni ngan song las drang bar bya zhes pa la sogs pas phan par dgongs pa'o//

The “at six times” mentioned here is merely an illustration. The Buddha at all times has thoughts of beneficial intent, such as “Who among sentient beings are experiencing setbacks?” “Who are flourishing?” and “Who are to be led out from the lower miserable destinies?”
sangs rgyas kyi chos ma 'dres pa bco brgyad ni/

d.i: The eighteen characteristics unique to the Buddha

d.div: spyod pa dang ni rtogs pa dang / / ye shes dang ni phrin las kyis/ / nyan thos rang sangs rgyas kun gyi/ / bla ma khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/[415] /
Homage to you who are superior to the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas by virtue of your conduct, realization, gnosis, and activities![581]
[415] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 21_sh+loka_58_shog_38_ba4
[581] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 21:57, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 38b4.

f.d: spyod pas bsdus pa drug ni/ sku la 'khrul ba mi mnga' ste/ dgra bcom pa dag la shing rta dang glang po che la thug pa dang / tsher ma'i 'obs su lhung ba dang / sbrul rkang pas brdzis pa dang / bud med kyis sdod pa'i gnas su 'jug pa la sogs pa yod pa la sangs rgyas la mi mnga' ba'o/ /

The six special characteristics included within “conduct.”[582] (1) Physically he is without mistake. For arhats there may occur such things as accidentally colliding with chariots or elephants, falling into a pit of thorny brambles, stepping on a snake, or entering into an occasion for being seduced by a woman. But the Buddha is free from such things.

d.div: [582] The division of the enlightened qualities into shared and special is also treated by Chim Jampaiyang in his Detailed Abhidharma Commentary, 616, and lists the eighteen special qualities of a buddha as the ten powers of the buddha, the four modes of fearlessness, plus three foundations of mindfulness, and great compassion. Chim specifies that this list, according to Abhidharmakośa, is not the same as the four-fold Mahayana classification of eighteen special buddha-qualities taught in the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra. He then quotes the same Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra verse 21:57 as a representative of this alternative Mahayana list.

f.d: gsung la ca co mi mnga' ste/ dgra bcom pa dag lung stong du ca co dang / gnas ma yin par rta bgad 'byin pa lta bu yod la/ sangs rgyas la mi mnga' ba dang / thugs mnyam par ma gzhag pa mi mnga' ba ni/ dgra bcom pa la mnyam gzhag las langs nas rjes thob la 'jug pa lta bu 'di la mi mnga' ste/[416] mnyam gzhag dang rjes thob zung du 'jug pa'i phyir ro/ /

(2) His speech is free from nonsensical utterances. Arhats may do such things as utter gibberish in a desolate place or inappropriately emit horse laughs. But the Buddha does not possess such verbal behaviors. (3) His mind never possesses nonmeditative states. The Buddha does not possess behavior such as that of the arhat who engages in nonmeditative activities after arising from meditative states. /386/ This is because the Buddha’s meditative state and postmeditative activities are integrated.

d.div: [416] yod la/ lu phu/

f.d: dran pa nyams pa mi mnga' ba ni/ dgra bcom pa la dran pa nyams pa srid pa las/ sangs rgyas la mdzad pa dang gsungs pa la bsnyel ba mi mnga' ba dang / tha dad pa'i 'du shes mi mnga' ba ni/ dgra bcom pa 'khor ba la gcig tu sdug bsngal ba dang / mya ngan las 'das pa la bde bar 'dzin pa lta bu 'di la mi mnga' ste/ 'khor 'das mnyam par rtogs pa'i phyir ro/ /

(4) He never has lapses of memory. While it is possible for an arhat to have memory lapses, the Buddha is not forgetful in his physical acts and speech. (5) He does not perceive cyclic existence and nirvana as different. The arhat takes cyclic existence to be solely misery and takes nirvana to be bliss. But the Buddha does not have such perceptions, for he has realized that cyclic existence and nirvana are equivalent.

so sor ma brtags pa'i btang snyoms mi mnga' ba ni/ dgra bcom pa dag so sor ma brtags par sems can gyi don yal bar 'dor ba srid la/ 'di la de mi mnga' ste so sor brtags nas btang snyoms su 'jog pa'i phyir ro/ /

(6) He does not pass over things without individual consideration. It is possible for arhats to abandon the welfare of sentient beings because of not considering each matter, but the Buddha does not possess such conduct, for he passes over a thing only after considering it.

rtogs pas bsdus pa drug ni/ dgra bcom pa dag shes bya'i sgrib pa ma spangs pas 'dun pa la sogs pa drug yongs su nyams pa srid la/ 'di la mi srid pas 'dun pa dang / brtson 'grus dang / dran pa dang / ting nge 'dzin dang / shes rab dang / rnam par grol ba nyams pa mi mnga' 'o/ /

The six special characteristics included within “realization.” Because they have not eliminated the knowledge obscurations, it is possible for arhats to experience reverses in the six realizations, beginning with resolve. But for the Buddha this is impossible because his (7) resolve, (8) endeavor, (9) mindfulness, (10) meditative absorption, (11) discerning wisdom, and (12) emancipation do not fail.
ye shes gyis bsdus pa gsum ni/ dgra bcom pa dus gsum la thogs pa dang chags pa yod la/ 'dir de dag mi mnga' ba'i ye shes brnyes pa'o//

The three special characteristics included within “gnosis.” The arhat is hindered and impeded in his knowledge of the three times, but the Buddha has acquired gnosis that is without either [hindrance or impediment concerning (13) past, (14) present, or (15) future].

'phrin las kyis bsdus pa gsum ni/ sku gsung thugs kyi phrin las gsum po nyan thos kyi dge ba la 'jug kyang skabs su lung ma bstan yang srid la/ 'dir ye shes kyis kun nas bslangs pa'i ye shes sngon du 'gro zhing ye shes dang lhan cig spyod pas ye shes kyi rjes su 'brang ba'o/ /

The three special characteristics included within “activities.” These are the activities of (16) body, (17) speech, and (18) mind. While it is possible for the activities of the śrāvaka [arhat] on occasion to become neutral deeds even though he applies himself to doing the virtuous, for the Buddha, all activities are preceded by gnosis because their motivating factor is gnosis, and they follow gnosis because they are practiced simultaneously with gnosis.
des na bco brgyad po 'dis ma 'dres pa'i chos dang ldan pas 'phags pa'i gang zag thams cad kyi yang bla mar 'gyur ba'o//
Therefore, because he is endowed with these eighteen characteristics unique to him, the Buddha becomes the superior even of [other] āryas.
rnam pa thams cad mkhyen pa nyid ni/

d.i: His being omniscient in every respect

d.div: sku gsum dag gis byang chub che/ / rnam pa kun brnyes thams cad du/ / sems can kun gyi the tshom dag / gcod pa khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/[417] /
Homage to you who through the three bodies have acquired the great awakening in every respect and who resolve the doubts of all sentient beings![583]
[417] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 21_sh+loka_59_shog_38_ba5
[583] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 21:58, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 38b4.

f.d: chos kyi sku rang bzhin gyis rnam par dag pa spang bya glo bur gyi dri ma las grol ba dang / longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku 'og min na byang chub sems dpa' sa bcu pa la theg pa chen po rgyun mi 'chad par gsung pa dang / sprul pa'i sku skye ba dang / mchog dang / bzo'i sprul pa'i sgo nas rgyun mi 'chad par sems can gyi don mdzad cing the tshom thams cad gcod pa'o/ / chos kyi sku zab la/ gzugs kyi sku gnyis rgya che bas shes bya ji lta ba dang ji snyed pa mkhyen cing / rang gzhan gyi don grub pas sems can thams cad kyi the tshom gcod pa'o//

The Dharma body (dharmakāya) is by nature pure and also free from what is to be removed, the adventitious stains of the afflictions. The enjoyment body (sambhogakāya) teaches continually the Mahayana in the Akaniṣṭha pure realm to bodhisattvas on the tenth level. And the emanation body (nirmāṇakāya) continually achieves the benefitting of sentient beings through “born” emanations, “highest” emanations, and artificial emanations. Thus the Buddha resolves doubts. By the profundity of the Dharma body and the vastness of the two form bodies, the Buddha understands knowable things exactly as they are and in their full variety and extent. /387/ And because the purposes of self and others are achieved, he resolves the doubts of all sentient beings.
pha rol tu phyin pa drug ni/

d.div: 'dzin pa med cing nyes pa med/ / rnyog pa med cing mi gnas pa// mi g.yo chos rnams thams cad la/ / spros med khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/[418] /
Homage to you who are without grasping, without moral fault, undisturbed, not [lazily] remaining, unagitated, and without discursive elaborations about all factors of existence![584]
[418] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 21_sh+loka_60_shog_38_ba6

f.d: sbyin pa la longs spyod kyi 'dzin pa med/ tshul khrims la ltung ba'i nyes pa med/ bzod pa la khong khro'i rnyog pa med/ brtson 'grus la le lo'i gnas med/ bsam gtan la rnam par g.yeng bas mi g.yo/ shes rab la chos thams cad kyi spros pa med pa'o/ /

The Buddha’s generosity is without grasping for wealth. His moral discipline has no fault of the moral offences. His patience lacks the disturbance of anger. His diligence is without any dwelling in laziness. His meditative concentration is not agitated by distraction. And his discerning wisdom lacks discursive elaborations about all factors of existence.[585]

d.div: [585] Here begins Sapaṇ’s addenda to the verses of praise from the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras. The final three verses of the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra (20:60–62) were not included or commented on.

f.d: don gnyis grub pa las ni/

d.i: His accomplishment of the two purposes

d.div: thob bya'i yon tan kun brnyes pas// rang dang gzhan gyi phrin las bsgrubs/ / mkhyen par bya ba'i chos rnams kun/ / ma lus gzigs pa khyod phyag 'tshal/[419] /
Through your acquisition of all obtainable excellent qualities, you have accomplished the activities for benefitting yourself and others. Homage to you who see all knowable things without exception!

[419] 'di ni sa paN gyis gong du/ sangs rgyas kyi yon tan mdo sde rgyan du tshigs bcad du ma bsdebs pa rnams 'dir tshigs bcad du mdzad de kha skong bar gsungs pa'i gras yin/ gsham du'ang tshigs bcad du bkod pa mchan ma btags pa rnams kyang 'di dang mtshungs par sa paN rang nyid kyi kha skong tshigs bcad du ngos 'dzin dgos par snang /

f.d: thob par bya ba'i yon tan thun mong dang thun mong ma yin pa mtha' dag brnyes pas/ rang dang gzhan gyi don ma lus pa bsgrubs pa mkhyen par bya ba'i chos ma lus pa gzigs pa'o/ /

By the Buddha’s acquisition of all shared and unique excellent qualities that are to be obtained, he has accomplished absolutely all purposes of self and others and sees all knowable things without exception.
byang chub kyi phyogs ni/
[The thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening]

d.div: dran dang brtson 'grus ting nge 'dzin/ / rmad du byung ba'i dbang po stobs/ / byang chub yan lag 'phags pa'i lam/ / legs sgrub khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
Homage to you who have accomplished well the ways of mindfulness, the diligences, meditative absorptions, wonderful moral faculties, powers, the limbs of awakening, and the path of the ārya!

f.d: [The Buddha is to be praised because he possesses the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening, which are:][586]

d.div: [586] Sapaṇ explains these thirty-seven factors according to the Mahayana system not Vasubandhu’s Abhidharmakośa.

f.d: lus la sogs pa nam mkha' lta bur mkhyen pa dran pa nye bar gzhag pa bzhi dang / nyes pa'i tshogs spangs pa dang / mi skye ba dang / yon tan gyi tshogs ma skyes pa skyed pa dang / skyes pa 'phel ba'i phyir/ brtson 'grus te yang dag par spong pa bzhi dang / 'dun pa dang / brtson 'grus dang / sems pa dang / spyod pa'i ting nge 'dzin rgya chen po rdzu 'phrul gyi rkang pa bzhi dang / dad pa la sogs pa'i dbang po lnga dang / stobs lnga yongs su rdzogs pa dang / chos rnam par 'byed pa la sogs pa byang chub kyi yan lag bdun dang / yang dag pa'i lta ba la sogs pa 'phags pa'i lam yan lag brgyad de/

• The four foundations of mindfulness: the knowledge of the body, [feelings, mind, and phenomena] as being like space • The four perfect endeavors: diligence for eliminating the host of moral faults, diligence to make sure they do not arise again, endeavor to produce the host of excellent qualities that have not arisen, and endeavor to increase those that have arisen • The four bases of magical powers: the vast meditative absorptions of aspiration, diligence, intention, and analysis • The five moral faculties, including faith and the others • The five moral powers, perfectly complete • The seven limbs of awakening, such as the penetration of Dharma • The eight branches of the ārya path, such as right view
'di dag grub pa tsam nyan thos dang rang sangs rgyas la'ang yod mod kyi/ legs par grub pa sangs rgyas kho na la mnga' bas so//
The minimal accomplishment of these is possessed also by the śrāvaka [arhat] and the [pratyekabuddha], yet only the Buddha possesses its excellent accomplishment.
snyoms par 'jug pa las ni/[420]

d.div: [420] snyoms par 'jug pa dgu ni/ zha lu/
khams gsum gtogs pa'i rnam par rtog / spangs pa'i snyoms 'jug rnam dgu yis/ / sems kyi tha ba 'joms pa'i dbang / / mthar son khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/ /

Homage to you who have brought to perfect completion the power that crushes the hard, fallow soil of mind through the nine absorptions that have eliminated the discursive thinking that belongs to the three cosmic realms! /388/

f.d: snyoms par 'jug pa dgu ni/ khams gsum du gtogs pa'i rnam par rtog pa phra rags dgu spong ba ste/ 'dod khams kyi rnam rtog spangs ba bsam gtan dang po dang / de bzhin du gnyis pa dang / gsum pa dang / bzhi pa la snyoms par 'jug pa dang / gzugs khams kyi rnam rtog spong ba nam mkha' mtha' yas skye mched dang / de bzhin du rnam shes mtha' yas dang / ci yang med pa dang / yod min med min gyi skye mched bzhi dang / rnam rtog mtha' dag spong ba 'gog pa'i snyoms 'jug ste dgu'o/ / 'di dag la rim gyis snyoms par 'jug na/ seng ge rnam par bsgyings pa zhes zer la/ dkrugs nas 'jug na thod rgal gyi snyoms 'jug zhes bya ba thod rgal 'di la

The nine absorptions are the elimination of the nine relatively coarser and subtler types of conceptual thinking that are included within the three cosmic realms. The elimination of the conceptual thinking of the realm of desire is the first meditative concentration, and likewise it is the absorptions of the second, third, and fourth concentrations. The elimination of the conceptual thinking of the form realm consists of the four meditative attainments: the attainment of infinite space, and likewise that of infinite consciousness, nothingness, and neither existence nor nonexistence. The elimination of all conceptual thought is the meditative attainment of cessation, thus bringing the total number of absorptions to nine. If you engage in meditating on these successively, it is called “the majestic lion.” If you engage in them out of their normal sequence, it is called “entering the absorptions by skipping over.” With respect to this skipping-over procedure,

nyan thos kyi lugs mdzod las/
sa brgyad rnam gnyis 'brel ba dang / gcig rgal song zhing 'ongs nas ni/ / rigs mi mthun pa gsum par 'gro/ / thod rgal gyi ni snyoms 'jug yin/[421] / zhes gsungs la/ theg chen gyi lugs ni mngon rtogs rgyan las/
'gog dang bcas pa'i snyoms 'jug dgur/ / rnam pa gnyis su song 'ongs nas/ / 'dod par gtogs pa'i rnam par rtog / mnyam gzhag min pa'i mtshams bzung ste/ / gcig dang gnyis gsum bzhi dang lnga/ / drug dang bdun dang brgyad brgal nas/ / 'gog pa'i bar du mi 'drar 'gro/ / thod rgal gyi ni snyoms 'jug yin/[422] / zhes gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

the Treasury of Higher Knowledge teaches the śrāvaka tradition as follows:
Interspersing the eight levels [of absorptions] in two ways, consecutively and by jumping over one [level at a time], to advance to a third state of a different class is to enter the absorptions by skipping over.[587] But the Mahayana tradition is as taught in the Ornament of Clear Realization:
Having advanced up and returned down in two ways through the nine absorptions including cessation, to take as an endpoint a nonconcentrated conceptual thought of the desire realm and to pass over one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight levels up to cessation differently is to engage in the absorptions through skipping over.[588]

d.div: [421] sde dge_4089_mngon pa/ ku_dbyig gnyen/ chos mngon pa mdzod/ gnas/ 8_sh+loka_18_shog_24_na7
[422] sde dge_3786_bstan/ sher phyin/ ka_byams pa mgon po/ mngon rtogs rgyan/ skabs/ 5_sh+loka_24_shog_8_na5
[587] Vasubandhu, Abhidharmakośa 8:18c–19b, Toh 4089 Tengyur, mngon pa, ku, 24a7.
[588] Maitreya, Abhisamayālaṃkāra 5:24–25, Toh 3786 Tengyur, shes phyin, ka, 8a5.

f.d: 'di gnyis mi 'dra ba ni/ nyan thos dang theg pa chenapo'i lugs yin pas mi 'gal lo/ /
The difference between these two does not amount to a contradiction because they are traditions of the śrāvaka and Mahayana, respectively.[589]

d.div: [589] See Lamotte, Le Traite, 1048.

f.d: 'di dag la nyan thos ni sems las su rung ba dang / snang bas skyo ba dgag pa'i phyir 'gog pa la snyoms par 'jug la/ byang chub sems dpa' ni ting nge 'dzin la dbang 'byor bar bya ba'i phyir yin zhing / sangs rgyas ni ting nge 'dzin la dbang 'byor ba nyid kyis lhun gyis grub pa yin no/ / de'ang nyan thos kyi rtsol ba la ltos/ byang chub sems dpa'i rtsol ba chung / sangs rgyas la rtsol ba med par lhun gyis grub pa/ sems kyi tha ba 'joms pa'i dbang 'byor pas so//

Regarding these meditative attainments, the śrāvakas engage in these absorptions of cessation for the sake of making their minds supple and serviceable, and to put an end to their despair at the various appearances [such as feeling and so on of ordinary existence], whereas the bodhisattva practices them for the sake of gaining mastery over meditative absorptions, and the Buddha spontaneously achieves them precisely through his mastery of meditative absorptions. Moreover, the śrāvaka’s engaging in those is dependent on effort. The bodhisattva attains them through small effort. For the Buddha, they are spontaneously achieved without effort, for he has sovereign mastery that crushes [the afflictions:] the “hard, fallow soil” of mind.
rnam par thar pa'i sgo gsum la/

d.div: gnyis su 'dzin pas rab stong nyid/ / nye bar len la smon mi mnga'/ / mtshan ma thams cad rab zhi bas/ / rnam thar mchog brnyes khyod phyag 'tshal//

Homage to you who have acquired the highest liberation because you are completely devoid of dichotomizing, to you who have no wish for appropriating [the defiled aggregates], to you for whom all phenomenal marks are pacified!

f.d: gzung ba dang 'dzin pa gnyis mi mnga' bas rnam par thar pa'i sgo stong pa nyid dang / nye bar len pa'i phung po lnga la chags pa dang bral bas smon pa med pa dang / dmigs pa'i mtshan ma thams cad zhi bas mtshan ma med pa'o/ / nyan thos dang rang sangs rgyas la'ang 'di mnga' mod kyi/ bag chags kyi sgrib pa ma spangs la/ 'dis spangs pas phul du byung ba yin no//

Because he possesses neither apprehended object nor apprehending subject, the Buddha has attained the door of liberation, “emptiness.” /389/ Because he is free from attachment toward the five impure appropriating aggregates, he has attained “the wishless.” And since for him all objectivized phenomenal marks are pacified, he has attained “the markless.” While these are also possessed by the śrāvaka [arhat] and pratyekabuddha, nevertheless those two have not eliminated the obscurations of the latent propensities. But since the Buddha has eliminated those, he is supreme.
bdud bzhi bcom pa la/

d.i: The destruction of the four māras

d.div: ye shes dang ni thugs rje la/ / bskal pa du mar thugs sbyangs pas/ / nye bar 'tshe ba'i bdud sde rnams/ / legs 'dul khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
Homage to you who have well subdued the harmful hosts of māras through having trained your mind for many eons in gnosis and compassion!

f.d: ye shes phun sum tshogs pa'i rtsa ba shes rab yin la/ des nyon mongs pa'i rgyu bdag 'dzin rang bzhin med par rtogs pas 'bras bu nyon mongs pa rang grol du 'gyur bas na nyon mongs pa'i bdud dang / gzhi des phung po nye bar grub pa med pas phung po'i bdud dang / phung po ma grub pa la nying mtshams sbyor ba med pas 'chi bdag gi bdud bcom/ thugs rje'i rtsa ba byams pa'i stobs kyis sems can thams cad la bu gcig pa ltar gzigs pas gnod pa thams cad nye bar zhi bas lha'i bu'i bdud bcom mo/ /

The root of consummate gnosis is discerning wisdom. And by the realization through that discerning wisdom that the cause of the afflictions—the postulating of a self—is without own-nature, there ensues the spontaneous liberation of its result, the afflictions. And as a consequence the māra of the afflictions is destroyed. The māra of the aggregates is destroyed because on the basis of the above, the aggregates are realized as not established. Since there is no joining [that is, no entering of consciousness into a womb] for one whose aggregates are realized as not established, the māra of death is vanquished. And the māra of the lesser deities (devaputra) is destroyed by the pacification of all harms through the Buddha’s viewing all sentient beings as though they were his only son by virtue of the power of his loving kindness, which is the root of his great compassion.

'di la nyan thos dag rdo rje'i gdan du nyon mongs pa dang lha'i bu'i bdud btul/ yangs pa can du 'chi bdag gi bdud brtul/ rtsa mchog tu phung po'i bdud btul zhes gsungs la/ theg chen pa dag ni/
khyod kyis dang po lha yi bu'i/ / bdud kyi me tog rgyal mtshan bsnyil/ / de nas nyon mongs bdud kyi ni/ / nga rgyal ri bo mthon po bsnyil/ /
khyod kyis byang chub ma brnyes par/ / 'dod khams dbang phyug las rgyal te/ / byang chub bar chad med lam la/ / khams gsum dbang phyug las rgyal lo/ / zhes gsungs pa ltar/ sangs rgyas pa'i snga logs su 'dul bar bzhed do//

Regarding all this, the śrāvakas teach that the Buddha subdued the māra of the afflictions and of the lesser deities in Bodhgaya. At Vaiśālī he subdued the māra of death. And at Kuśīnagarī he subdued the māra of the aggregates. But those of the Mahayana teach:
First you destroyed the flower victory-banner of the māra of the deities. Then you destroyed the high mountain of pride of the māra of the afflictions.
You conquered the lord of the desire realm even without attaining awakening, and on the immediate path [of the vajra-like absorption], you conquered the lord of the three cosmic realms.[590] Accordingly, they maintain that the Buddha subdued the māras prior to his attainment of buddhahood.

d.div: [590] Unnamed Mahayana source. Not located.

f.d: dbang bcu la/

d.div: phyi dang nang dang gnyis ka dang / / 'dun dang mkhyen dang 'doms pa la// dbang bcu dag gis 'jig rten gyi/ / bya ba kun sgrub khyod phyag 'tshal/ /
Homage to you who accomplish all affairs the world through the ten controlling powers over inner, outer, both [inner and outer], resolution, knowledge, and instruction!

f.d: tshe la dbang ba ni/ tshe bzhed tshad bzhugs pa ste longs spyod sbyin pas/ sems can gyi tshe'i rgyur gyur pas so/ / sems la dbang ba ni/ ci ltar 'dod pa sems ting nge 'dzin la 'jug pa las su rung ste/ sbyin pas gzhan gyi sems tshim par byas pas so/ / yo byad la dbang ba ni/ bsam pa ji lta bar yo byad 'byor pa ste gzhan yo byad kyis tshim par byas pas so/ /

Controlling power over life. This is the ability to live for whatever lifespan is desired, and it is the outcome of having prolonged the lives of sentient beings through generous gifts of wealth. Controlling power over mind is the serviceability of a buddha’s mind for entering into any meditative absorption exactly according to his wishes. It is the outcome of having satisfied the minds of others through generosity. Controlling power over material goods is receiving material goods exactly according to his wishes, and it is the outcome of having satisfied others with material goods.
'di gsum sbyin pa'i 'bras bu'o/ /
The above three powers are the results of generosity.

las la dbang ba ni/ sgo gsum gyi las ji ltar 'dod pas bsgrub pa ste/ tshul khrims kyis gzhan lus ngag yid kyi las gsum kha na ma tho ba med pa la bsam pa ji lta bar bskul ba'i 'bras bu'o/ / skye ba la dbang ba ni/ gang 'dod pa'i 'gro ba dang lus la sogs pa 'grub pa ste tshul khrims dang ldan pa'i smon lam grub pa de'i rgyu can no/ /

Controlling power over deeds is the ability to achieve deeds of body, speech, and mind just as he wishes. /390/ It is the result of having impelled others to faultless deeds of body, speech, and mind by means of his own moral discipline. Controlling power over rebirth is the ability to achieve whatever forms of existence, body, and so forth that he desires in a new rebirth. His realization of the aspirations that are endowed with moral discipline is their causal condition.
'di gnyis tshul khrims kyi 'bras bu'o/ /

mos pa la dbang ba ni/ sa'ang gser du bsgyur ba la sogs pa ste/ bzod pas sems can gyi mos pa'i rjes su zhugs pa'i 'bras bu'o/ / smon lam la dbang ba ni/ ji ltar smon pa'i don 'grub pa ste/ brtson 'grus kyis sems can gyi don ji ltar 'dod pa bsgrubs pa'i 'bras bu'o/ / rdzu 'phrul la dbang ba ni/ bsam gtan gyis dgongs pa ji lta ba la zhugs pa'i 'bras bu'o/ /

Controlling power over whatever he wishes is such things as transforming even earth into gold. It results from acting in accord with the wishes of sentient beings by means of his patience. Controlling power over aspirations is the accomplishment of whatever goal he aspires to. It is the result of having accomplished the benefit of sentient beings in exact agreement with their wishes through his diligence. Controlling power over magical powers is the result of having engaged in meditative absorptions exactly in accord with enlightened intentions through meditative concentration.

ye shes la dbang ba ni/ shes rab kyis sems can gyi gang 'dod pa la sbyar ba'i 'bras bu'o/ / chos la dbang ba ni/ mdo la sogs pa'i chos 'dod pa ji ltar ston pa ste/ shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pas chos thams cad bshad pas thob pa'o/ /

Controlling power over gnosis is the result of having applied himself to whatever sentient beings desire through discerning wisdom. Controlling power over Dharma teachings is the teaching of instructions such as the sutras just as sentient beings desire. It is acquired by the teaching of all Dharma instructions through the perfection of wisdom.
'di gnyis shes rab kyi 'bras bu'o/ /
These last two controlling powers are the results of discerning wisdom.

yo byad dang skye ba ni phyi'o/ / sems ni nang ngo / / tshe dang las dang mos pa dang / /rdzu 'phrul ni phyi nang gnyis kas bsdus pa'o/ / 'dun pa dang / ye shes dang / chos la dbang ba ni/ rim ba bzhin mos pa dang / mkhyen pa dang / 'doms pa la dbang ba'o/ /

Material goods and rebirth are the “outer.” Mind is the “inner.” Life, deeds, likes, and magical powers are included within “both inner and outer.” Aspiration, gnosis, and Dharma teachings are “resolution,” “knowledge,” and “instruction,” respectively.
tshe dang sems dang yo byad dang / / las dang skye ba mos pa dang / / smon lam rdzu 'phrul ye shes chos/ / 'di dag thub pa'i dbang bcur bzhed/ / bsdu ba'i tshigs bcad do//

To summarize in a verse:
Life, mind, and material goods, deeds, rebirths, and wishes, aspirations, magical powers, gnosis, and Dharma teaching: these are the ten controlling powers of the Buddha.
ting nge 'dzin ni/

d.div: rmad byung lhun gyis grub pa can/ / shes bya kun la thogs med pa/ / sgrub dang spong ba'i ting 'dzin la/ / mnga' brnyes khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/[423] /
Homage to you who have attained mastery over the meditative absorptions that accomplish and eliminate and that are wonderful, spontaneously realized, and unhindered about all objects of knowledge!
[423] sde dge_4020_bstan/ sems tsam/ phi_byams pa mgon po/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 21_sh+loka_51_shog_38_na5

f.d: gzhan las khyad par du 'phags shing / 'bad pa la mi ltos par phrin las thogs pa med pa'i ting nge 'dzin dpa' bar 'gro ba dang / rin chen phyag rgya dang / seng ge rnam par bsgyings ba la sogs pa bzhed pa sgrub pa'i ti nge 'dzin yin la/ rdo rje lta bu dang / nyon mongs pa thams cad spong ba la sogs pa spang bya spong ba'i ting nge 'dzin te/ rgyas par rgyal ba'i yum las ji skad gsungs pa bzhin no//

The meditative absorptions that are superior over others, not dependent on effort, and unimpeded in their activities [include both the “accomplishing” and “eliminating” absorptions]. Absorptions such as valiant progress (śūraṅga), jewel seal (ratnamudrā), and majestic lion (siṃha vijṛmbhita) accomplish something desired, whereas absorptions such as the vajra-like and elimination of all afflictions eliminate the things that are to be eliminated. You should understand them in more detail as they are explained in the Mother of the Conquerors [i.e., the Perfection of Wisdom sutras].
gzungs kyi sgo ni/

d.div: 'dzin dang chad pa chos kyi sgo/ / nyung ngus chos rnams bde blag tu/ / ston mdzad gzungs kyis chos kyi gter/ / kha 'byed khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/ /

Homage to you who open up the treasure deposits of Dharma teachings through your dhāraṇīs that are the door [granting unimpeded] retention and teaching and that with few syllables easily reveal the teachings! /391/

f.d: zad mi shes pa'i za ma tog bkod pa la sogs pa gzungs kyi sgos/ chos thams cad kyi kha 'byed pa ste/ de yang yi ge bsam gyis mi khyab pa ye ge bzhi bcu rtsa gnyis su sdud pa dang / bzhi bcu rtsa gnyis po yi ge gcig tu 'du ba la mkhas pas gzhan gyis smras pa 'dzin pa dang / rang gis 'chad pa la thogs pa med pa ste/ 'di'ang yum las yi ge gcig gis byang ba'i rang bzhin la mkhas par bya ba la sogs pa gsungs pa ltar ro/ /

Through the doors of dhāraṇī, such as the inexhaustible Jewel Casket,[591] he opens the door of all Dharmas. Moreover, since he is expert in summarizing inconceivably many syllables into forty-two syllables, and in summarizing those forty-two into one syllable, he is unimpeded in retaining what others say and in his own imparting of teachings. This also is as taught in the Mother [the Perfection of Wisdom sutras] as becoming, through a single syllable, learned in the purified nature and so forth.

d.div: [591] Za ma tog bkod pa, Skt. karaṇḍavyūha.This does not refer to the sutra of the same name but to a long dhāraṇī, a.k.a. the zad mi shes pa’i za ma tog, in the Sutra of Golden Light (Suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtra), Toh 556 Kangyur, rgyud, pa, 197b.

f.d: spangs pa phun sum tshogs pa la/ /

d.i: Consummate elimination of the afflictions and obscurations

d.div: chags sogs dgag dka'i dri ma dang // 'khor gsum rnam par rtog pa'i gzhi/ / bag chags bcas pa gtan spangs pa/ / sgrib pa kun grol khyod phyag 'tshal/ /

Homage to you who have completely eliminated the stains that are difficult to remove—desire and the other [afflictions]— and the basis of conceptual constructions of the spheres of an action, together with the propensities toward them, and who are freed from all obscurations!

f.d: 'dod chags dang zhe sdang la sogs pa zag pas bsdus pa/ nyon mongs pa'i sgrib pa dang / bdag dang gnas dang longs spyod la sogs pa 'khor gsum gyis bsdus pa shes bya'i sgrib pa bag chags dang bcas pa spang pas sgrib pa thams cad las grol ba'o//

He is liberated from all the obscurations because he has eliminated both the affliction obscurations, which are desire, anger, and so forth, included within the category of the impurities (āsrava), and the knowledge obscuration, which is the conceptual postulation of “self,” “place,” “wealth,” and so forth, included within the category of the “three spheres” [of an action] (trimaṇḍala)—together with all propensities toward those obscurations.
ye shes ni/

d.div: gsal dang dri med yon tan gter/ / phrin las rten dang brten pa yis/ / rang gzhan don gyi ye shes la/ / rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas khyod phyag 'tshal/ /

Homage to you who have attained complete buddhahood with respect to the gnoses that relate to self and others by means of the support and the supported, luminous, stainless, a treasure lode of excellent qualities, and activities!

f.d: me long lta bu'i ye shes me long la gzugs brnyan shar ba ltar shes bya'i dkyil 'khor ma lus pa gsal ba dang / mnyam pa nyid kyi ye shes nga dang nga yir 'dzin pa'i dri ma dang bral ba dang / so sor rtog pa'i ye shes stobs dang mi 'jigs pa la sogs pa yon tan thams cad kyi gter dang / bya ba grub pa'i ye shes/ rang gzhan gyi phrin las thams cad lhun gyis grub pa'o/ /

The mirror-like gnosis is the illumination of the complete mandala of knowable things, like a reflection appearing clearly in a mirror. The gnosis of equality is the freedom from the impurities of the postulation of “I” and “mine.” The gnosis of discrimination is the treasure lode of all excellent qualities such as the powers and the ways of fearlessness. The gnosis of the accomplishment of works is the spontaneous realization of all beneficial activities for yourself and others.
de'ang me long lta bu rten yin la/ ye shes phyi ma gsum/ de la brten pa dang / snga ma gsum ni rang don gtso che ba yin la/ phyi ma gnyis ni gzhan don gtso che'o//

Moreover, mirror-like gnosis is the support, while the latter three gnoses are the supported. The former three pertain predominately to the benefits of the Buddha himself, while the latter one[592] relates predominately to the benefitting of others.

d.div: [592] The Dergé edition, 97a, reads gnyis; correct to gcig.

f.d: gsung gi yon tan ni/

d.div: gsung dbyangs mi 'jigs seng ge'i sgra/ / yan lag drug cu dang ldan pas/ / lhar bcas 'jig rten thams cad la/ / legs sgrogs khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
Homage to you who excellently sound forth to the whole world of men and gods your speech, which is a fearless lion’s roar possessing sixty aspects!

f.d: gsung 'jam pa dang / rna bar snyan pa dang / rgyang du grags pa la sogs pa dbyangs kyi yan lag drug cu ste/ rgyas par gsang ba bsam gyis mi khyab pa las gsungs pa lta bu'o/ /

The sixty aspects of [a buddha’s] speech are those such as softness, sweetness, and audibility over long distances. For a more detailed description, they are as explained in the Inconceivable Secret Sutra.[593] /392/

d.div: [593] Tathāgatācintyaguhyanirdeśasūtra, Toh 47 Kangyur, dkon brtsegs, ka. Quote not located.

f.d: gnas gyur pa la ni/

d.div: khyod kyis zag bcas 'gro ba'i rgyun/ / gang lags lam gyi bden pas bsgyur/ / 'gro ba kun 'jug ye shes su/ / mkhyen pa khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
You have changed that which is the defiled stream of ordinary existence through realizing the truth of the path. Homage to you who know as gnosis the [impurities] that operate in all living beings!

f.d: zag pa dang bcas pa'i phung po khams dang / skye mched gnas gyur pa las zag pa med pa'i ye shes kyi sku 'grub ste/ 'gro ba'i las dang nyon mongs pa ji snyed yod pa gnas gyur pa'i ye shes bsam gyis mi khyab par 'gyur ba mdo sde rgyan dang theg pa chen po bsdus pa las 'byung ba bzhin no/ /

The body of gnosis that possesses no impurities is achieved from the transformation of the aggregates, elements, and sensory bases that possess impurities. The occurrence of the inconceivably great gnosis that is the transformation of all the karma and afflictions of living beings is as taught in the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras and the Compendium of the Mahayana.
'byor pa'i khyad par la/

d.div: 'jig rten slob ma bse ru sras/ / ston pa'i 'byor pa phul byung ba/ / gang lags de 'dra mnga' brnyes pas/ / legs 'byor khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/ /

Homage to you who are consummately endowed through your having attained control of such endowments as those of the worldly, the śrāvakas, the rhinoceroses, and the sons and the supreme endowments of the Great Teacher!

f.d:
brgya byin dang tshangs pa la sogs pa 'jig rten pa'i 'byor pa mtha' dag slob pa ste/ dgra bcom pa gcig gi zil gyis gnon la/ de bse ru ste rang sangs rgyas kyis/ de sras te byang chub sems dpas/ de ston pa ste sangs rgyas kyi zil gyis gnon te/ mdo sde rgyan las/
'jig rten pa yi 'byor pa ni/ / nyan thos rnams kyi zil gyis gnon/ / nyan thos rnams kyi 'byor pa yang / / rang sangs rgyas kyi zil gyis gnon/ /
de yis byang chub sems dpa' yi/ / 'byor pa'i char yang mi phod do/ / de yis rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas kyi/ / 'byor pa'i char yang mi phod do/[424] / zhes gsungs pa lta bu ste/

All the endowments of such gods of the mundane sphere as Śakra and Brahma are eclipsed by those of the śrāvaka—that is, the arhat. That one is eclipsed by the rhinoceros—that is, the pratyekabuddha. That one is eclipsed by the [Conqueror’s] son—that is, the bodhisattva. And that one is eclipsed by the Great Teacher, that is, the Buddha. As the Ornament of Mahayana Sutras teaches:
The endowments of the person of the mundane sphere are eclipsed by those of the śrāvakas. Those of the śrāvakas are eclipsed by those of the pratyekabuddha.
Those cannot measure up to even a fraction of those of the bodhisattva. And those cannot measure up to even a fraction of the endowments of the perfect Buddha.[594]

d.div: [424] gong mtshungs/ mdo sde rgyan/ le'u/ 10_sh+loka_38_shog_10_na6
[594] Maitreya, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra 10:38–39, Toh 4020 Tengyur, sems tsam, phi, 10a6.

f.d: dper na 'phags pa nyer sbas bsam gtan la mnyam par gzhag pa na/ bdud sdig can gyis co 'dri ba'i phyir me tog gi phreng ba dbu la bkris pa na/ 'phags pas bdud sdig can gyi mgrin par khyi ro bam pa 'bu 'dzag pa cig dkris pa lta bu dang /[425] 'jig rten gyi khams dpag tu med pa 'dab chags su mes 'jigs pa na 'jam dpal gyis smras pa shA ri'i bu/ khyod kyi rdzu 'phrul la brten nas 'gro'am/ kho bo'i rdzu 'phrul la brten nas 'gro bar bya/ shA ri'i bus bsams pa/ rang gi rdzu 'phrul gyis 'gro na yun ring du thogs pa zhig pas/ 'jam dpal gyi rdzu 'phrul yang blta'o snyam ste khyod kyi rdzu 'phrul gyis 'gro bar bya'o/ / de lta na mig cung zad tshums shig_shA ri'i bus mig btsums par brtsams pa na da phye shig_shA ri'i bus phye ba na bton zin par gyur to/ / shA ri'i bus smras pa/ khyod kyi rdzu'aphrul bsam gyis mi khyab bo/ / 'jam dpal gyis smras pa de de bzhin te/ kho bo'i rnam par thar pa khyed nyan thos mos pa dman pa rnams kyi yul ma yin no zhes gsungs pa lta bu'o/[426]/

For example, when Ārya Upagupta was sitting engaged in meditative concentration, Māra the evil one placed over his head a garland of flowers in order to mock him. At that the ārya placed around the evil one’s neck the putrid, worm-infested corpse of a dog. Also, for example, when infinitely many world systems were being successively destroyed by fire, Mañjuśrī said: “O Śāriputra, shall we go there by means of your magical powers or shall we go by means of mine?” Śāriputra thought, If we go by means of my magic powers, it will take a long time. Let’s see how strong Mañjuśrī’s magical powers are. “Let’s go by means of yours.” “In that case, close your eyes for just a bit.” When Śāriputra was just beginning to close his eyes, [Mañjuśrī said:] “Now open them!” When Śāriputra opened them, they had already arrived. Śāriputra said, “Your magical power is inconceivable!” “Just so,” Mañjuśrī said. “My liberated conduct is not within the domain of those of inferior aspiration, including śrāvakas such as yourself.” /393/

d.div: [425] gtam brgyud 'di'i khungs mdo ngos 'dzin ma thub/
[426] gtam brgyud 'di'i khungs mdo ngos 'dzin ma thub/

f.d: skyabs mchog tu gyur pa ni/

d.i: His status as the supreme refuge

d.div: thun mong ba dang phul byung chos/ / rlabs chen shin tu rmad byung ba/ / brnyes pas 'jig rten thams cad kyi/ / skyabs gyur khyod la phyag 'tshal lo/ /
Homage to you who are the refuge of all living beings in the world because of your acquisition of the shared and preeminent qualities that are powerful and extremely wondrous!

f.d: de dag las tshad med rnam thar zil gnon/ zad par mngon par shes pa lnga 'jig rten pa dang thun mong ba/ zag pa zad pa'i mngon shes nyon mongs pa med pa smon gnas shes pa/ so so yang dag par rig pa/ byang chub kyi phyogs snyoms 'jug dgu/ rnam thar gsum la sogs pa ni slob ma dang thun mong ba/ gzhan rdzu 'phrul dang / ting nge 'dzin dang gnas gyur 'ga' zhig la sogs pa ma dag pa'i sa bdun po dang thun mong pa'o/ / nyon mongs pa can gyi yid gnas gyur pa dang / mtshan dpe la sogs pa 'ga' zhig gis brgyad pa dang thun mong ba'o/ / gzungs kyi sgo dang / so so yang dag par rig pa chen po la sogs pa 'ga' zhig sa dgu pa dang thun mong ba'o/ / ting nge 'dzin dang dbang bcu pa la sogs pa 'ga' zhig sa bcu pa dang thun mong ba'o/ / nyan thos ni byang chub sems dpa'i sa bcu mi bzhed pas sras dang thun mong ba zhes ming 'dogs so/ / gzhan sangs rgyas kyi chos ma 'dres pa bco brgyad dang / mi 'jigs pa bzhi dang / bsrung ba med pa gsum la sogs pa sangs rgyas kho na'i khyad par gyi chos so// 'di lta bu'i yon tan brnyes pas lha dang bcas pa'i 'jig rten thams cad kyi skyabs kyi dam par gyur pa yin no/ /

From among those [qualities of the Buddha explained above,] the infinite states, emancipations, bases of mastery, bases of totality, and five of the superknowledges are qualities shared with some beings of the mundane sphere. His superknowledge of the extinction of impurities, his absence of afflictions, knowledge from aspiration, analytical knowledges, factors conducive to awakening, nine absorptions, three doors of liberation, and so forth are shared with the śrāvaka [arhat]. The remaining magical powers and some meditative absorptions and transformations are shared with bodhisattvas of the seven impure levels. Some qualities, such as the transformation of defiled mind and the physical characteristics are shared with the bodhisattva of the eighth level. The door of dhāraṇī and the great analytical knowledges are shared with the ninth level. Some attainments, such as certain meditative absorptions and the ten powers, are held in common with the tenth level. Since the śrāvakas do not maintain the ten levels of the bodhisattva, these qualities are called “held in common with the sons.” The others, such as the eighteen unique qualities of the Buddha, the four ways of fearlessness, and the three types of unguardedness, are specific qualities of the Buddha alone. Because he has acquired such excellent qualities, he is the supreme refuge of the entire animate world, including the gods.

d.i: Dedicating the merit of the praises

f.d:
de ltar bstod pa'i skabs bsgrubs nas/ bsgrubs pa'i dge ba bsngo ba ni/
de lta'i dngos bstod ston pa yis/ / bstan pa rin chen gsal mdzad pas/ / 'gro ba kun gyis shes bya yi/ / de nyid legs par mthong bar shog / de lta bu'i yon tan gyi dngos po dang ldan pa'i ston pa ni sangs rgyas bcom ldan 'das kho na yin la/ de'i bstan pa ni dgos 'dod thams cad 'byung bas rin po che'i gter dang 'dra'o/ / de legs par phye zhing gsal bar byas pa'i dge ba 'dis/ 'gro ba thams cad kyis shes bya ji lta ba dang ji snyed pa ma lus pa gsal bar mthong bar gyur cig ces bstod pa'i bsngo ba'o// //

Having thus completed the section consisting of praises, I dedicate the merit thereby achieved:
By illuminating the precious jewel-doctrine of the Buddha whose possessions have thus been praised, may all living beings perfectly see the ultimate reality of knowable things![595] The Great Teacher who has the “possessions” of such excellent qualities is the Lord Buddha alone. And his doctrine is like a treasure cache of jewels since it grants all that you need or want. By this merit resulting from having opened up and illuminated that treasure, may all living beings clearly see all knowable things exactly as they are and in their full variety and extent! /394/

d.div: [595] The Dergé edition, 98b, reads: yis (“by”), but I emend to yi (“of ”).

f.d: brtsams pa mthar phyin pa mjug gi don/
The Conclusion of the Treatise

d.div: bdag gis thub pa'i dgongs pa ji lta bar/ / zab dang rgya che'i mdo don legs gzigs pa/ / rgyal pa'i sras po byams pa'i gsung rab bzhin/ / 'gro la phan pa'i yid kyis gsal bar byas/ /

With the idea of benefitting living beings, I have illuminated the Sage’s intent exactly as it is according to the teachings of Maitreya, the son of the Conqueror, who correctly perceives the sense of the profound and vast sutras.
spyod pa rgya chen shin tu rgyas pa'i mdo/ / lta ba'i de nyid shes rab pha rol phyin/ / mi 'gal gsal bar ston pa kho bo'i gzhung / / rigs pas bsgrubs pa bla ma'i gsung bzhin bshad/ /

Clearly establishing as noncontradictory through reason the vast conduct of the “extremely vast” sutras and the ultimate reality of the theory of the Perfection of Wisdom [sutras], I have expounded this treatise of mine according to the teaching of my master.
deng sang shAkya thub pa'i bstan pa ni/ / bud shing zad pa'i me bzhin nyam chung bas/ / blo ldan skye bo sangs rgyas sgrub 'dod rnams/ / legs par soms la thub pa'i gsung bzhin zung / /

Nowadays the doctrine of the Śākya Sage has become weak, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted, so those intelligent people who desire to realize buddhahood should ponder well and uphold it according to the teachings of the Sage.
chos rnams de nyid shin tu lkog gyur la/ / so so'i skye bo'i spyod pa 'khrul gyur pas/ / 'di yi legs bshad bla ma dam pa'i drin// nyes pa snang gang bdag blo'i nyes par zad/ /

The ultimate reality of phenomena is completely hidden and ordinary persons’ engagement[596] with it erroneous. So whatever excellence of this work is due to the grace of my masters; what faults there may be are solely of my own mind.
[596] Possibly correct spyod to dpyod, “discernment”?
sangs rgyas 'jig rten sgron ma nub gyur cing / / mkhas pa'i skye bo phal cher 'das pas na/ / blo ngan ma sbyangs gzu lum smra rnams kyis/ / bde gshegs bstan pa deng sang 'dir dkrugs so/ /

The Buddha, the lamp of the world, has vanished, and most learned people have already passed away. So unintelligent, uneducated people propounding spurious opinions are nowadays mixing up the Sugata’s doctrine here in Tibet.
chos 'di log par bshad na sdig pa lci/ / legs par bshad na skye po phal cher khro/ / snyigs ma'i dus kyi chos smra dka' mod kyi/ / 'on kyang 'gro la phan snyam 'di brtsams so/ /

If you teach this Dharma wrongly, it would be a great moral fault. If you teach it well, most people become angry. Though teaching Dharma in the degenerate age is indeed difficult, I have composed this with the thought of benefitting living beings.
dge ba 'di dang dge ba'i rtsa ba gzhan/ / ma lus blo yis gcig tu bsdom byas te/ / nam mkha'i mthas gtugs sems can don bsgrub phyir/ / kun mkhyen rgyal po'i go 'phang thob par shog /

Having mentally gathered together all the merit of this [composition] and all other roots of virtue, may I attain the station of omniscient king, so that I may achieve the welfare of sentient beings reaching to the limits of the sky!

f.d: byang chub sems dpa'i lam la 'jug pa'i rim pa/ thub pa'i dgongs pa gsal ba zhes bya ba sde snod 'dzin pa dpal ldan sa skya paN+Di tas sbyar ba'o/ / rdzogs so// //

The stages for entering into the path of the bodhisattva called Clarifying the Sage’s Intent was composed by the illustrious Sakya Paṇḍita, an upholder of the Buddhist scriptures. Here it is completed.
tshogs chos 'di dbus gtsang khams gsum du ngas thams cad la bshad pa yin pas/ nga'i slob ma thams cad kyis lung thob pa yin pas yi ge 'di la ltos la shod/ 'di bzhin nyams su long //[427] //

Since I have taught this assembly discourse to all in Ü, Tsang, and Kham provinces, all my disciples have received its textual transmission. Therefore may you refer to this text and teach it! And may you practice according to it!

d.div: [427] 'di mdo smad du yongs su rdzogs nas dbus gtsang du dpe bskur ba'i tshe slob ma rnams la springs pa yin no/ / zha lu dgon/
